api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Ability.html.summary: Class Ability Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll An ability: one thing an entity can do, as a fireball, a dash or a heal. An entity learns it from its Entity asset's Starting Abilities, from an equipped item's Active Ability or from code (AbilitySystemComponent.GiveAbility), and keeps it in a slot with a level of its own, between its StartingLevel and MaxLevel, kept under its asset tag. An activation passes its caster's tag requirements and its Caster Checks (SourceActivationRules), lets its Behaviour's targeting task pick its target, which its Target Checks (TargetActivationRules) then check, applies its Cost and Cooldown effects to its caster and spends its AttributeCosts, as it starts or in the stage that takes them, and runs its stages of tasks. Its Definition says how it activates, its Tags what it is, grants and requires, and its Components add features with hooks into its life; its WorkerGroup, OnHit and Modifiers hold on its entity while the entity knows it. Each is handed the activation's data: Prepare as its stage starts, Activate, the work its stage waits on, and Clean as the stage ends; IsCriticalSection says whether it's critical work, which commits its ability to its stage and keeps out another ability's critical work while it runs. One task object serves every activation of its ability, so what it keeps for one belongs in the activation's data, not in its fields. Read gives one of its numbers at its ability's level, EntityOf its caster or its first target, and ApplyTo applies an effect from the ability with the activation's magnitudes. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.AbstractMonoPro.summary: Class AbstractMonoProcess Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll The base of every MonoBehaviour process: a component, on a prefab or a scene object, that ProcessControl registers, steps and ends, as a GAS hub or a projectile. Its lifecycle, step timing and step priority are fields of its inspector, Synchronous in Update and LateUpdate at the first priority by default, and as it initializes it takes the parent, position and rotation its packet gives. ProcessControl registers those already in a scene as it starts. Derive from it, or from LazyMonoProcess for a run that lasts until it's paused or ended, and override RunProcess, the run ProcessControl awaits, and the hooks you need: WhenInitialize; WhenUpdate, WhenLateUpdate and WhenFixedUpdate at its timing; WhenWait, WhenTerminate and WhenDestroy; and TryHandlePause and TryHandleResume to keep a run through a pause. An override of WhenInitialize or WhenTerminate calls the base's, and WhenDestroy stands in for OnDestroy, which a class of its own would hide. Its object comes from its registration's instantiator, its handler's or its own Instantiator, or is cloned from its prefab, and is given back or destroyed as the process ends. Processes on its child objects pause and end with it, as ProcessControl cascades by default. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.AssetPartKind.h.summary: Class AssetPartKind Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll A part of an effect, an ability or an item on the caster or the target, found by a tag: a Poison effect's stacks, how many Fire effects are on the target, what every Burn there has dealt, the time left on a shield, an ability's level or whether it's cooling down, how many potions are in a stack, whether a ring is equipped. An effect matches by its asset tag, a context tag or a tag it grants; an ability or an item by its asset tag or a context tag; a tag under the one given matches too. Where several match, Among says how they read as one: added up, the first, the highest or the lowest. A count reads 0 where none matches; any other part reads Default. A true-or-false part reads 1 or 0, so added up it's how many are so. An effect's Worker Value asks that effect's workers for a key (INumberWorker), about that application of it, and counts only the effects whose workers answer. Sets, effects, workers and conditions name the asset itself, and some lookups compare attributes by name, so give each its own. Each AttributeSetElement exposes Current and Base configs; this blueprint resolves both sides independently and assembles the resulting AttributeValue. Per-side resolution rules (applied identically for Current and Base): If the side's scaler is null OR its RealMagnitude is UseMagnitude → return Magnitude. Otherwise call the cached scaler (Initial vs Active path) and project the side's slot from the returned AttributeValue (Current → CurrentValue, Base → BaseValue), then combine with the side's Magnitude via its RealMagnitude operation. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.AttributeOverfl.summary: Struct AttributeOverflowData Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll Bounds policy for an attribute's Current and Base slots. The same instance is used both at runtime (via ApplyBounds()) and authoring time (the AttributeSetElement drawer clamps user input live) — all clamping flows through Clamp(AttributeValue) / the per-slot min/max helpers so policy semantics are defined once. Per-policy semantics: • Unlimited — no bounds. • ZeroToBase — Current ∈ [0, Base]; Base unbounded. • FloorToBase — Current ∈ [Floor.Current, Base]; Base ∈ [Floor.Base, +∞). • ZeroToCeil — Current ∈ [0, Ceil.Current]; Base ∈ [0, Ceil.Base]. • FloorToCeil — Current ∈ [Floor.Current, Ceil.Current]; Base ∈ [Floor.Base, Ceil.Base]. An entity names one, and as its GAS initializes each element becomes its attribute's root value, the value before any effect, which a cached scaler can tie to the entity's level or to another attribute. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.CachedAttribute.summary: Class CachedAttributeValue Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll Per-attribute runtime state under the two-kind impact model: Modifiers (transient, derived) — registered via RegisterModifier(IAttributeImpactCarrier, IReadOnlyList<IAttributeImpacter>, IReadOnlyDictionary<IAttribute, CachedAttributeValue>) while their carrier lives, re-evaluated on every Recompute(IReadOnlyDictionary<IAttribute, CachedAttributeValue>), reversed exactly by UnregisterModifier(IAttributeImpactCarrier, IReadOnlyDictionary<IAttribute, CachedAttributeValue>). Commits (permanent) — applied via CommitImpact(IAttributeImpactCarrier, IReadOnlyList<IAttributeImpacter>, IReadOnlyDictionary<IAttribute, CachedAttributeValue>); the post-bounds delta is recorded per retention group in FarEmerald.PlayForge.CachedAttributeValue.committedByGroup and NEVER reversed. The formula (EFFECT_PIPELINE.md §2.1): ActiveValue = ConstrainValue( Override( FlatBonus( Multiply( Add( root ) ) ) + Σ committedByGroup ) ). Committed history lands where it was measured, after the % modifiers, so they don't scale it: 50 base × 1.5 aura + 10 tome = 85, and a 30 hit under the aura takes 30. Reproducibility invariant: ActiveValue is always exactly what Recompute(IReadOnlyDictionary<IAttribute, CachedAttributeValue>) produces from current state — every mutation path ends in a recompute. There is no second bookkeeping system to drift. Guide: Attributes Named in: Effect & Attribute Pipeline: 2. Attribute state (CachedAttributeValue) · Effect & Attribute Pipeline: 2. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAbilityActivat.summary: Enum EAbilityActivationPolicy Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll What an activation does while another ability holds its claim, the When Busy the inspectors show. Activate Anyway (AlwaysActivate) starts at once; Refuse (ActivateIfIdle) is refused, as Busy, while another ability asked under Refuse holds its claim; Queue (QueueActivationIfBusy) waits in the input buffer, for up to its Buffer Window, while a Queue ability holds its claim or a running stage blocks it. Whatever the choice, an ability with critical tasks can't start while another with critical tasks holds its claim. An entity's When Busy is one, and so is each activation request's Policy. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.EActivationRefu.summary: Enum EActivationRefusal Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll Why an activation was refused, or None where it wasn't: it activated, waits in the input buffer, or starts next frame. A refused activation said only false. Guide: Abilities public enum EActivationRefusal Fields None = 0 Not refused: it activated, waits in the input buffer, or starts next frame. NotKnown = 1 The entity doesn't know the ability, or knows none that carries the tag. Disabled = 2 The ability system is off, as an ended entity's is. Locked = 3 The ability system is locked. NoNewProcesses = 4 ProcessControl takes no new processes, and an ability runs as one. LevelZero = 5 The ability's level is 0, and it's set to ignore activation there. Requirements = 6 The caster's tags fail the ability's source requirements, or its While active group. Cooldown = 7 The ability's cooldown is on. Cost = 8 The ability's cost would take an attribute it spends below 0. Dead = 9 The caster is dead. Rule = 10 Another of the ability's caster checks refused it, which Rule names. Blocked = 11 A running ability's stage blocks it, and the request doesn't wait. Busy = 12 Another ability holds the claim and the request doesn't wait, or the ability's own activation still holds it, or the input buffer has no window to wait in. Critical = 13 Another ability's critical section holds its claim, and this ability has one too, so it's kept out, whatever policy either was asked under. Under Queue, it waits in the input buffer instead. Chance = 14 Its chance to activate didn't come up. CrowdControl = 15 A crowd control rule its caster is under stops it, as a stun stops every ability. Range = 16 The target or the point it was handed lies beyond its Cast Range, so an AI can walk closer and ask again. Target = 17 After its targeting, its target failed one of its Target Checks, which Rule names, or its target tag requirements, where it names none. The activation had started, and ends there with nothing of it paid; the ability system tells it as it tells any refusal.

Started = 1 It started: its claim, its targeting and its first stage ran inside the call until one of its tasks waited, so an ability whose tasks all finish at once has ended by now. Buffered = 2 It waits in the input buffer, as its Queue policy lets it, until the claim or the block that holds it lifts. It starts then, or is let go as its window runs out. NextFrame = 3 It was asked for while its own activation call still ran, from its own callbacks or from another ability's that it started, so it starts in the next frame instead. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.Attribut.title: Class AttributeSetElementDrawer | PlayForge
api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.Attribut.summary: Class AttributeSetElementDrawer Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.dll An attribute set element: a foldout row with the attribute, and while it's folded one line of what it starts at; open, what it starts at at each level, then Base and Current, each a magnitude field as an effect's are, then its bounds, its constraints, its retention group and its collision. What it starts at is worked out by the runtime (AttributeStartValues): a stand-in entity at each level of the set it's previewed in, with the set's sub-sets. A note says when another element's value is the one used, and a message when a scaler reads an attribute the set doesn't give. The element showed its magnitudes as a formula, as "10 + Level", and Current and Base one at a time on a switch. It writes nothing while it draws, and only a typed magnitude is kept within the bounds, as part of the same edit. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.Attribut.summary: Class AttributeStartValues Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.dll What each attribute an entity built from an attribute set starts at, at each of the set's levels, worked out as the runtime works it out: a stand-in entity at the level, whose attribute system is set up from the set as the GAS sets one up, with the set's sub-sets and collisions, and each element's scalers, bounds and rounding. Nothing else acts on the stand-in, no worker, effect or item, so a value is the one the set gives before anything changes it. A set that another holds starts as part of it, so its values can be worked out in each set that holds it, and the attribute set inspector previews a set in one of them (PreviewIn(AttributeSet, AttributeSet)). api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeRen.summary: Class ForgeRenames Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.dll Renames an asset as its inspector does, from The Forge or an asset's header: a PlayForge asset's name, with the tag its name gives, as one Undo step; a Scaler asset's scaler and a Requirement template's requirements, whose names its lists show; and for an asset with no name of its own, as a Value Pipeline, its file alone. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeSpr.summary: Class ForgeSpreadsheets Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.dll Numbers by level and item stats, to and from CSV, so a game is balanced in a spreadsheet. A sheet of numbers by level has a row for each number of an asset that reads a Table or By Level: the asset's tag and name, the field as the inspector labels it, its kind, and what it reads at each level, its values times its number, as Laguna Blade's -450/-600/-750. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeTem.title: Class ForgeTemplatePush | PlayForge
api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeTem.summary: Class ForgeTemplatePush Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.dll Templates as prefabs work. A template's changes reach its children when it's pushed to them, as an explicit step: each child, and each of theirs, takes the template's fields but those it overrides, and one Undo takes the push back. An edit to a child's field makes the field the child's own, an override, which its inspector marks, and Revert to Template takes back. Saving a template opened a dialog in the middle of the save, loaded every asset of its type, and changed the children with no Undo. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeVal.title: Class ForgeValidator | PlayForge
api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeVal.summary: Class ForgeValidator Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.dll PlayForge's one validator. It runs every ForgeValidationRule on each PlayForge asset in the project and keeps what they find, which the Problems view lists and an inspector's header counts. It follows the project, so nothing polls: an edit checks its asset again, an import checks what it brought, and a deleted asset has every asset checked again, since another may have read it. In batch mode, LogAll() writes each problem to the Console. Validate All checked four things, flagged every effect with no workers, and showed 15 problems in a dialog. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.RuntimeD.title: Class RuntimeDebugger | PlayForge
api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.RuntimeD.summary: Class RuntimeDebugger Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.dll The Debugger: one window for the game as it plays, in place of the GAS Debugger, Process Control and the Tag Debugger. Its Entities view lists the hubs ProcessControl registers, of either kind, beside one hub's attributes, effects, abilities and tags, which it can change. Its Processes view lists every process, with what it's doing and how long its steps take, and its Tags view every tag the entities hold, as a tree, beside who holds the one selected. Its Timeline view shows what the entities' abilities and effects did over time, as a recorder heard it. The lists follow ProcessControl as processes join and leave, and the values change in place, at the rate the window menu sets, while the game plays. Outside Play mode it offers Play Mode. The GAS Debugger scanned the scene for MonoBehaviour hubs and rebuilt its details every 0.25 s; Process Control and the Tag Debugger were IMGUI windows of their own. A read finds what the scaler asks for, each attribute on its side and each caller's key, and adds a row for each the first time, filled from its side's entity where it has one. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ValuePip.summary: Class ValuePipelineTry Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.dll A Value Pipeline tried in the editor: a value put through its stages at each level of a range, against the stand-ins a Scaler asset's try reads against, a caster's and a target's attributes, typed or filled from an entity, and the values a caller sets. Each chance a stage rolls comes up where it can, or misses where it can, as ChancesComeUp says, so a read gives the same each time. A Block or Evade stage rolls first, as it does as an effect lands, and one that comes up stops the hit before the pipeline runs: nothing of it lands. No effect is behind a try, so a stage that reads the hit's carrier reads none, and what an Absorb stage soaks comes off no one. A pipeline's try, from For(ValuePipeline), is kept for the session with Keep(), and never written into the asset. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.html.title: Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor | PlayForge
api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.html.summary: Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor Classes AbilityBehaviourDrawer An ability's behaviour drawn whole, as an asset or a component of the user's own holds one: Unity's foldout of the fields the ability inspector shows of it, its targeting, its asset loaders, what cancels it and what it blocks, and its stages. The lists are Unity's, where a new loader starts empty and each stage keeps its fold as one is removed or dragged; Implicit Tag shows under Use Implicit Targeting while it's on. It drew colored sections that folded, lists of its own, and badges. AbilityComponentDrawer An ability's component: its kind, never None and named without "AbilityComponent", as "Cast Range" for a CastRangeAbilityComponent, then its fields, folding to a line of their values. A kind an ability may hold only once isn't offered while its list holds one. AbilityDrawer A reference to an ability: Unity's object field, with Open or New beside it. It was a button that opened a dropdown list of its own. AbilityEditor The Ability inspector: Identity, Leveling, Tags, the ability's Activation and Stages, Requirements, Workers and Local Data, then Used By. A collapsed section shows one line, and the inspector takes its look from the style sheet. AbilityStageConditionDrawer A stage's condition: its tag, a tag field in the label column, and, once it names one, where the stage looks for it and whether it runs while the tag is missing instead, each indented under it. With no tag, the stage always runs, and Unity's foldout showed all three. AbilityTagRequirementsDrawer An ability's tag requirements, as the same table: the caster's, the caster's while the ability runs, and the target's, each with what it requires and what it must not have. AbilityTaskBehaviourStageDrawer An ability's stage: a foldout row named by its place, as "Stage 1", with Critical on its right while a task commits the ability to it; folded, one line of what it holds, as "2 tasks · All · Applies usage effects"; open, its completion policy, its usage effects, its condition, what cancels it and what it blocks, then its tasks in Unity's reorderable list, where a new task starts empty. The stages' own list removes a stage. It drew a colored badge for the stage's number, its policy, its usage effects, its task count and a critical task, ▶ and ▼ as text, a delete button, and a list of its own with ▲, ▼ and × buttons, from 163 styles set in C#; and it grew that list as an array, which gave a new task the last one's object, so the two were one. AbilityTaskDrawer An ability task: its kind, as "Delay" for a DelayTask, then the kind's own fields. The base drawer names a kind without "AbilityTask" or "Task", and builds the fields again as the kind changes, which this drawer did itself. AbilityValidationRuleDrawer An ability's validation rule: its kind, as its [ForgeMenu] names it or named without "ValidationRule" or "Validation", then the kind's own fields. A rule is always of some kind, so the picker offers no None. Each list is offered the kinds of its side, the Caster Checks a caster's and the Target Checks a target's, with those of either; a check a component stands behind, as Check Range, is offered to neither, as it comes with its component. AbstractComponentDrawer<T> A component: its kind, always of some kind, then its fields. A kind that allows one is offered while the list it's in holds none of it, the element that holds it still naming it. AbstractForgeObjectDrawer<T> A reference to a PlayForge asset, or to a Value Pipeline, Crowd Control Rules or Effect Modifier: Unity's object field, with its type's icon, and beside it a plain button, Open while it names an asset, which shows the asset in a window of its own, or New while it's empty, which asks for a new one's name in The Forge's New dialog, makes it where The Forge makes its type and uses it. A drawer adds its own actions to the field's right-click menu. It was a button that opened a dropdown list of its own, with hover colors and Clear and Open icon buttons set in C#. AbstractGenericDrawer<T> A kind field that folds, as an attribute set element does: a row with the arrow and the kind field, then the kind's fields; folded, one line of their values in secondary text, as "Strength 2 · Duration 0.5". Whether it's folded is kept with the object the field holds, so it follows the object through its list. It drew colored badges for a folded field's values, and its arrow and its look from styles set in C#. AbstractMonoProcessEditor A Mono Process's inspector: a Process section of Unity's fields, its lifecycle, its timing, how it's ordered as it steps, how it's made, and whether it follows its siblings, each choice saying what it does in its field's tooltip; then the component's own fields. Priority Method shows while the process steps, and Priority under it while the method is Manual. It drew a tinted box, a gray hint in 10 px under each field, set 50 ms after it drew, and a gray rule. Every field is a PropertyField bound to its property, so a multiple selection edits each process, and a prefab instance's edits show as overrides. Without [CanEditMultipleObjects] the Inspector never offered one. AbstractTypeRefDrawer<T> A [SerializeReference] field of an abstract type: Unity's field, its label in the label column, the kind it holds named in its box, which opens Unity's searchable dropdown of the kinds it can hold; then the kind's own fields, each Unity's, indented under it. A pick makes a new object of the kind for each selected asset, by the kind's constructor so its initializers run, as one Undo step; drawing writes nothing. Every element of a list shares one drawer, so each field keeps its state in its own elements. The drawer kept the last element's fields and kind in fields of its own, so an edit to one element could fill another with its fields. It drew a button that opened a list in tinted boxes, and the kind's fields in a box with an orange left border. AbstractWorkerDrawer<T> A worker: its kind, always of some kind, then its fields, folding to a line of their values. AlignedFoldoutDrawer Each class PlayForge serializes in a field with no drawer of its own, drawn as a foldout of its fields, its arrow in line with the rows around it, as a list's is: an attribute read's retention groups, as an × Attribute scaler's Groups, a turn to face's settings, an asset's definition and tags, a list's entries. Unity hangs an inspector foldout's arrow 12 px into the margin, to the left of a list's arrow and, in a scaler's block, out to the block's edge; this one keeps the lists' column, as pf-foldout--aligned sets in PlayForge.uss. A class opts in with a CustomPropertyDrawer of its type here. A field marked ForgeShowWhenAttribute shows only while the field it names says so, as a read's Groups shows only for the reads that name groups. An inspector drawn with IMGUI gets the same foldout. AnalysisWorkerDrawer An analysis worker, as a worker group's Analysis list holds one: its kind, picked from the analysis workers or None, then its fields, folding to a line of their values. AssetSetterDrawer An asset loader, as an ability's Asset Loaders list holds one: its kind, picked from the Set tasks, as "Set Effects" for a SetEffectsTask, then the kind's own fields. AttributeConstraintsDrawer An attribute's constraints: Auto Clamp, Scale With Base and Rounding, Unity's fields in the label column, with Snap Interval indented under Rounding while it snaps. They sat in a tinted, rounded box with a yellow left border, under a 10 px bold heading with colored letter badges, from styles set in C#. AttributeCostDrawer An ability's attribute cost: the attribute it spends, or, where it names none, the role whose attribute it spends, and how much. AttributeDrawer A reference to an attribute: Unity's object field, with Open or New beside it. It was a button that opened a dropdown list of its own. AttributeEditor The Attribute asset's inspector, which edits several attributes at once: its header, then Identity (Name, Abbreviation, Description, Role and, for a Barrier, what it absorbs for and how it decays, Gains Scaled By, the roles it plays in its project, and Textures), Local Data, and Used By, the assets that refer to it. AttributeImpactEntryDrawer One of an effect's additional impacts: a foldout row with its attribute and a Remove button, and while it's folded one line such as "Mana −10 · Continuous"; open, its operation, magnitude and delivery, then its order, retention group and impact types. Its Delivery offers what the effect's duration can make, and a help box says when the one it names can't happen. An impact entry had no drawer, so an effect couldn't be given a second impact. AttributeOverflowDataDrawer An attribute's bounds: the policy, then the floor and the ceiling it reads, each indented under it, as a field that depends on another is. A bound's right-click menu sets it to no limit. It drew the floor and ceiling with 10 px labels and buttons in an accent color, from styles set in C#, and showed them 50 ms after it drew. AttributeRoleDrawer A project's role on one row: its tag, then the attribute that plays it. AttributeSetDrawer A reference to an attribute set: Unity's object field, with Open or New beside it. It was a button that opened a dropdown list of its own. AttributeSetEditor The Attribute Set inspector: Identity, Leveling, the set's Attributes, Sub-Sets and Collision Settings, then All Attributes, the table of what the set gives an entity, then Workers, Local Data and Used By. A collapsed section shows one line, and the inspector takes its look from the style sheet. AttributeSetElementDrawer An attribute set element: a foldout row with the attribute, and while it's folded one line of what it starts at; open, what it starts at at each level, then Base and Current, each a magnitude field as an effect's are, then its bounds, its constraints, its retention group and its collision. What it starts at is worked out by the runtime (AttributeStartValues): a stand-in entity at each level of the set it's previewed in, with the set's sub-sets. A note says when another element's value is the one used, and a message when a scaler reads an attribute the set doesn't give. The element showed its magnitudes as a formula, as "10 + Level", and Current and Base one at a time on a switch. It writes nothing while it draws, and only a typed magnitude is kept within the bounds, as part of the same edit. AttributeStartValues What each attribute an entity built from an attribute set starts at, at each of the set's levels, worked out as the runtime works it out: a stand-in entity at the level, whose attribute system is set up from the set as the GAS sets one up, with the set's sub-sets and collisions, and each element's scalers, bounds and rounding. Nothing else acts on the stand-in, no worker, effect or item, so a value is the one the set gives before anything changes it. A set that another holds starts as part of it, so its values can be worked out in each set that holds it, and the attribute set inspector previews a set in one of them (PreviewIn(AttributeSet, AttributeSet)). AttributeStartValues.Result What a set's attributes start at, over its levels. AttributeStartValues.Start One attribute's start: its value at each level, and the elements that give it. AttributeTransferDrawer An effect's transfer: when it moves, who gives and of what, who gets and in what, which of the values, and how much, each a field of its own as an attribute cost's are. AttributeValueDrawer An attribute value: its label in the label column, then its Current and Base side by side. It drew "Cur" and "Base" in 9 px text with a slash between them, from styles set in C#. AttributeWorkerDrawer An attribute worker, as a worker group's Attribute list holds one: its kind, picked from the attribute workers and never None, then its fields, folding to a line of their values. AuraEntryDrawer An aura's fields, drawn where it's held, as an Aura component's own. AvoidRequireTagGroupDrawer A requirement group of its own, as a targeting task's or a template's: the same table, of one row named by the field, with what it requires and what it must not have; a cell opens its list, with the group's name and template under it. It drew a tinted box with green and red stripes, colored count badges, a Name and an Import of its own, and rebuilt itself as it opened. BasePlayForgeEditor Base class for all PlayForge asset inspectors: a header with the asset's name and type, and the content below it. The content scrolls in the Inspector's own scroll view, and the header stays at its top. BuildVerification Headless player-build verification (asset-store readiness / CI): Unity -batchmode -nographics -projectPath <proj> -executeMethod FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.BuildVerification.BuildWindowsPlayer Exit codes: 0 = build succeeded, 1 = build failed, 3 = exception. Proves the runtime assembly compiles and links in a real player (no editor-only leaks). CachedMagnitudeModifierGroupMemberDrawer A Scaler Group's member, cached or not, as Unity's fields: how its result combines with the members' before it, then its scaler, whose own drawer shows its kind and its settings. It drew a stripe and a symbol in the operation's color, the scaler's kind beside them, and, for a cached member, a "CACHED" badge. ChanceRollDrawer How a chance rolls, as Unity's foldout of its fields: Pseudo-Random, Own Luck, and Luck while Own Luck is on, where it's read; without it the project's Luck role is read, so Luck is hidden. ChargeRechargeDrawer An ability's Recharge: its kind, named without "Recharge", as Each Charge or All At Once, or one of your own, then the kind's own fields. A recharge is always of some kind, so the picker offers no None. ClockChoiceDrawer A clock picked in an inspector, as an ability's Run Sequence task's Clock: its kind, Caster's, Game's, Unscaled or Scaled, or one of your own, then the kind's own fields, as Scaled's Scale and the clock it scales. None leaves the run the clock it would have had. ConditionDrawer A condition field, as a Conditional scaler's When, drawn as a scaler field is: its name and its kind, picked from the conditions there are, a project's own among them, its one line, as "Target's Health < 0.3 × Target's Health (base)", then the condition's own fields on a block under it, each as Unity draws its type, so its numbers are number fields. It writes nothing while it draws. ContainedEffectPacketDrawer A contained effect, on one row: when it's applied, then the effect. It drew a tinted, rounded box with a stripe in its policy's color, set 50 ms after it drew. ContextImpactWorkerDrawer A context impact worker, one made from AbstractContextImpactWorker: its kind, picked from those workers or None, then its fields, folding to a line of their values. CrowdControlRuleDrawer A crowd control rule: its tag, what it stops, and, where it stops the abilities carrying one of its tags, those tags. A stun stops every ability, so its row names none. CrowdControlRulesDrawer A Crowd Control Rules field as a reference to an asset, with New and Open beside it. CrowdControlRulesEditor A Crowd Control Rules asset's inspector: the shared header, then its rules. CueHandlerDrawer A cue handler, picked by its kind, as a worker is. CueLibraryEditor A cue library's inspector: its routes, each a cue tag and the handlers it plays; then each cue tag the project's assets raise through it, by a Cue Tag cue, with the route that plays it, or that none does, and the assets that raise it, each a row that opens its asset in The Forge. It follows the project as it changes, and its routes as they're edited. DataWrapperDrawer A Local Data row: its key, its value's kind and its value, each a column of its own, laid out by the style sheet. A value's kind is a class, Float to ScriptableObject or one of your own: a kind that holds one Value draws it in the row, and one of your own with more fields draws each under its name. Each row holds a value of its own, so a row added as a copy of the last edits its own. EffectAreaDrawer An effect's area's fields, drawn where it's held, as an Area component's own. EffectChangeDrawer A modifier's change: its kind, always of some kind, then its fields, as a worker is drawn. EffectComponentDrawer An effect's component: its kind, never None and named without "EffectComponent", as "Aura" for an AuraEffectComponent, then its fields, folding to a line of their values. A kind an effect may hold only once isn't offered while its list holds one. EffectModifierDrawer An Effect Modifier field as a reference to an asset, with New and Open beside it. EffectModifierEditor An Effect Modifier's inspector: what it's for, its rule, the effects it picks and its changes, each of a kind with its fields, and a line that says them. Unity's own fields. EffectPurgeDrawer An effect's Purges, a foldout of its fields, its arrow in line with the lists' around it in the Tags section. Unity hangs an inspector foldout's arrow 12 px into the margin, to the left of a list's arrow; this one keeps the lists' column, as pf-foldout--aligned sets in PlayForge.uss. EffectTagRequirementsDrawer An effect's tag requirements on one side, the target's or the source's, as a table: Applying, While On and Removed By, each with what it requires and what it must not have. The drawer drew a tinted box with colored subsections, a type badge, a Name and import buttons of its own, and rebuilt itself as it opened. EffectTemplateRegistry The effects a new Cost or Cooldown effect copies, by "Cost" or "Cooldown". Project Settings → PlayForge holds them, with the project; they lived in EditorPrefs, which every project on the machine shares. EffectWorkerDrawer An effect worker, as an effect's Workers list holds one: its kind, picked from the effect workers or None, then its fields, folding to a line of their values. EntityComponentDrawer An entity's component: its kind, never None and named without "EntityComponent", as "Respawn" for a RespawnEntityComponent, then its fields, folding to a line of their values. A kind an entity may hold only once isn't offered while its list holds one. EntityDrawer A reference to an entity: Unity's object field, with Open or New beside it. It was a button that opened a dropdown list of its own. EntityIdentityEditor The Entity inspector: Identity, Leveling, Tags, the entity's Attributes, Abilities and Items, Workers and Local Data, then Used By. A collapsed section shows one line, and the inspector takes its look from the style sheet. FocusedAttributeWorkerDrawer A focused attribute worker, one made from AbstractFocusedAttributeWorker: its kind, picked from those workers and never None, then its fields, folding to a line of their values. ForgeAssetLines One line for each asset, which its inspector's header and The Forge's list show: an ability's numbers by level, then its costs and cooldown, as "-450/-600/-750 Health; 280/420/680 Mana; 70/60/50 s"; an item's what it changes while equipped and the ability it grants, as "+20 Armor; Blink"; an entity's first attributes as it starts and its abilities, as "Health 500, Mana 300, Armor 5; Fireball, Blink"; an effect's first impact by level, as its Levels section reads it. Numbers that read what an editor can't give, as the target, are marked with a *. ForgeComponentRule<TComponent> A check of one kind of component, wherever an asset holds it: an ability's, an effect's, an item's or an entity's. The validator finds it as it finds every rule, and it hears each component of its kind the asset holds, with the component's place in its list, which a problem names as its property path; an ability's inspector says its problems under the Components list. Derive from it, with a public constructor that takes nothing, for a component of your own, as PlayForge's components' rules do. ForgeDrawerStyles Comprehensive UI building utilities for PlayForge editors. Provides all necessary methods to create custom editors programmatically. ForgeDrawerStyles.Colors The colors PlayForge's editors draw with: accents and section tints, backgrounds, text and borders, status colors, and a color for each kind of PlayForge asset, which GetAssetColor gives for a type, gray for any it doesn't name. ForgeDrawerStyles.HeaderConfig Configuration for main header creation. ForgeDrawerStyles.HeaderResult Result from CreateMainHeader containing references to update. ForgeDrawerStyles.Icons Characters PlayForge's editors show as small icons in labels and buttons, each a string constant, as Check (✓), Cross (✗) and ArrowDown (↓). ForgeDrawerStyles.SectionConfig Configuration for collapsible section creation. ForgeDrawerStyles.SectionResult Result from CreateCollapsibleSection containing references. ForgeFlagsDrawer A flags field of PlayForge's, which writes only what's picked. Unity's own flags field stores a value that holds every flag as Everything, -1, as it binds: an asset only looked at changed, as every effect's Purges' Applied By, Any by default; a template's child took the change as an override; and the inspector's SerializedObject moved while its bindings were still being made, which Unity asserted on (IsInSyncWithParentSerializedObject). This field shows the value without writing it, stores the flags picked of those its type has, so Everything is every flag it has now and not one it gains later, and follows an Undo. ForgeImportWindow The one Import window: choose a source, choose the fields that differ, each pre-checked, and import them as one Undo step. A list is replaced, unless its row asks to add to it. It serves a section's Import, a whole asset's, and a single property's, such as a worker group. A whole asset keeps its name, description, icons, asset tag, template and level link. Six windows did this before, each its own way: section import copied every field with no choice, and the Effect's Duration and Impact couldn't import. ForgeImportWindow.Field One field the window can import, by its property path. ForgeLint What the project's assets give each other, which the content linter's checks read: the impact types its effects and impact workers deal, the gameplay events its thresholds and stop stages send, and the effects its items apply. It's gathered from every PlayForge asset, and the shared Value Pipelines and Effect Modifiers, as a check first asks, and forgotten as the validator checks the project afresh, or as an asset changes what it gives, which has every asset checked again against what's now true. ForgeLogSettingsBridge Keeps the ForgeLog level chosen in Preferences → PlayForge and applies it to MinimumLevel on every domain reload, since static fields reset on reload and EditorPrefs lasts. ForgeNewAssetWindow A new asset's name and folder, then Create, as The Forge's Create menu asks. It makes the asset through the one factory a field's New uses too, CreateNew(Type, string, string): a copy of the type's New Asset default, named, with the tag its name gives, in the folder Project Settings names. The Create tab's dialog set type settings that did nothing, and logged each asset it made. ForgePreset A way to start a new asset: one of PlayForge's presets, which fills the new asset's fields, or one of the project's own template assets, which the new asset starts as a copy of. ForgePresetMaking What a preset reaches as it fills a new asset: its name, the project, and a way to make the assets it needs, each saved in its type's folder, or in the one the new asset was asked for where that isn't its type's. ForgePresets The presets The Forge's Create menu lists for each type: PlayForge's, then the project's templates. ForgeProblem One problem the validator found in a PlayForge asset: the asset, how serious it is, and what's wrong. ForgeProblemsWindow The Problems view: every problem the validator finds in the project's PlayForge assets, each with its severity and its asset, and a click selects the asset. It follows the validator, so it has no Refresh. It replaces Validate All, which showed 15 problems in a dialog nothing in could be selected, and the Audit, which wrote to the Console. By Rule, its other view, groups the problems under the rule each breaks, and where a simple step fixes a problem, gives it a Quick Fix, and its rule a Fix All, each one Undo step. It lists the linter's notes too, which may be meant, as a trigger on an event that code sends, under their own filter, and its counts leave them out. ForgeProjectEditor A Forge Project's inspector: the shared header, then its settings; its catalog a line saying how many assets it names for saves and how it keeps them, where it drew each entry, a list of GUIDs as long as the project. ForgeQuickFix A problem's quick fix: what it does, as its button says, and the step itself. The step writes through a SerializedObject, or records Undo, so the Undo step the Problems view opens around it takes it back; and the validator, which follows each edit, checks the asset again. ForgeRenameWindow Rename, from an asset's menu in The Forge's list or its header, or F2 on The Forge's list: the asset's name, to type over, then Rename, which renames it as its inspector does (ForgeRenames). Enter renames and Escape cancels. ForgeRenames Renames an asset as its inspector does, from The Forge or an asset's header: a PlayForge asset's name, with the tag its name gives, as one Undo step; a Scaler asset's scaler and a Requirement template's requirements, whose names its lists show; and for an asset with no name of its own, as a Value Pipeline, its file alone. The file takes the name, with its type's prefix and suffix from Project Settings, leaving out its spaces as a new asset's file does, and follows the name back through Undo and Redo. A file that is its asset's only name keeps the spaces, and its rename Unity doesn't undo. ForgeSpreadsheetWindow A sheet's changes before they're made: each number it changes, its asset, what it reads now and what it will, each chosen until it's unticked; what of the sheet can't be read; and Import, which makes the chosen changes as one Undo step. ForgeSpreadsheets Numbers by level and item stats, to and from CSV, so a game is balanced in a spreadsheet. A sheet of numbers by level has a row for each number of an asset that reads a Table or By Level: the asset's tag and name, the field as the inspector labels it, its kind, and what it reads at each level, its values times its number, as Laguna Blade's -450/-600/-750. A sheet of item stats has a row for each item and a column for each attribute its granted effects add to: a number, or one for each level, as 10/15/20. A sheet read back finds each row's asset by its asset tag, or by its name where it gives none; a name two assets share, an asset that isn't there and a field it hasn't got are problems, not guesses. Its changes, listed, apply as one Undo step, each number's values set so it reads what the row says. ForgeTagLibraryEditor A Tag Library's inspector: the shared header, then its entries and its contexts. ForgeTagRegistry Central registry for tracking tag usage across all PlayForge assets. Provides context-aware tag filtering and usage statistics. ForgeTagRegistry.ContextUsage Tracks usage within a specific context. ForgeTagRegistry.FieldUsageInfo Tracks a single usage of a tag - which asset and which field path. ForgeTagRegistry.TagContext Represents a unique context where tags are used. Uses string-based context identifiers (from ForgeContext constants). ForgeTagRegistry.TagUsageRecord Tracks usage of a single tag across contexts. ForgeTemplateConfig Defines which property paths are excluded from template propagation for each asset type. Excluded fields are identity fields (name, tags, textures), linking fields (link mode, linked source), and template system internals. ForgeTemplatePropagator Core engine for template propagation. Handles: Propagating template field changes to child assets (non-overridden, non-excluded) Merging list properties (additions and removals from template) Detecting and recording field overrides by comparing child against template Cascading propagation through template chains (A → B → C) Finding all child assets of a given template via project scan ForgeTemplatePush Templates as prefabs work. A template's changes reach its children when it's pushed to them, as an explicit step: each child, and each of theirs, takes the template's fields but those it overrides, and one Undo takes the push back. An edit to a child's field makes the field the child's own, an override, which its inspector marks, and Revert to Template takes back. Saving a template opened a dialog in the middle of the save, loaded every asset of its type, and changed the children with no Undo. ForgeValidationRule A check the validator runs on each PlayForge asset. Derive from it, with a public constructor that takes nothing, to add a check of your own: the validator finds every one. A problem a simple step fixes can carry the step as its Fix. ForgeValidator PlayForge's one validator. It runs every ForgeValidationRule on each PlayForge asset in the project and keeps what they find, which the Problems view lists and an inspector's header counts. It follows the project, so nothing polls: an edit checks its asset again, an import checks what it brought, and a deleted asset has every asset checked again, since another may have read it. In batch mode, LogAll() writes each problem to the Console. Validate All checked four things, flagged every effect with no workers, and showed 15 problems in a dialog. GameplayEffectDrawer A reference to an effect: Unity's object field, with Open or New beside it, and under it a line that says how the effect takes its levels, with Link to make it take them from the asset that holds the field. Its right-click menu holds the field's template, a pick of the effects nothing links, and New Linked Effect. Setting the field asked in a dialog whether to link the effect, and the template, the link filter and a create button sat beside the field as tinted buttons. GameplayEffectDurationDrawer An effect's duration: Policy, then what the policy uses: Duration and its ticks for a Durational effect, Tick Every for an Infinite one, then Tick On Application, execute ticks, the clock, Re-application and Then, and stacking for Stack Existing. It drew its parts in tinted boxes with colored headings, under sentences that explained them, and showed or hid them 50 ms after it drew. It follows the policy as it changes, an Undo among them. GameplayEffectEditor The Effect inspector: Identity, Leveling, Tags, Duration, Impact, Requirements, Workers and Local Data, then Used By. A collapsed section shows one line, and the inspector takes its look from the style sheet. Requirements shows the target's table, then the source's, on a two-button switch. GameplayEffectImpactDrawer An effect's impact: the attribute, the operation, the magnitude, then how the impact is delivered, which the duration gives it, and what a periodic one commits. Then its impact types and who it affects, its additional impacts, each with a delivery of its own, with Add Impact, and its contained effects. It no longer draws Reverse On Removal, which the impact model removed, and it takes its look from the style sheet: it drew tinted boxes with colored headings. IProxyStagePolicyDrawer A proxy stage's policy: its kind, named without "ProxyStagePolicy" or "Policy", always of some kind. ImpactWorkerDrawer An impact worker, as a worker group's Impact list holds one: its kind, picked from the impact workers or None, then its fields, folding to a line of their values. InlineFieldsDrawer A field's own fields, drawn where it's held, as a component's own: a field of its whole drew a foldout inside the component. ItemComponentDrawer An item's component: its kind, never None and named without "ItemComponent", as "Uses" for a UsesItemComponent, then its fields, folding to a line of their values. A kind an item may hold only once isn't offered while its list holds one. ItemDrawer A reference to an item: Unity's object field, with Open or New beside it. It was a button that opened a dropdown list of its own. ItemEditor The Item inspector: Identity, Leveling, Tags, the item's Effects and Abilities, Workers and Local Data, then Used By. A collapsed section shows one line, and the inspector takes its look from the style sheet. LevelProviderDrawer A [LinkedSource] field, the asset whose levels this one takes: Unity's object field of level providers, whose picker lists them, and under it a line of the levels it gives. It was any asset's field that warned at a wrong pick, with a tinted box, a colored type badge, a × and a "..." that opened a browser window of its own, which Unity's picker does. LevelThresholdDrawer A Threshold scaler's threshold: the level it holds from and the tier's name on one row, Unity's fields bound to them, so an Undo shows in them, and under them what the scaler reads from there, a number field of any kind. In a list it needs no label of its own. It drew a tinted row with "Lv" in blue and an arrow as text, and its fields wrote as they changed and followed nothing after. MagnitudeModifierGroupMemberDrawer A Scaler Group's member, cached or not, as Unity's fields: how its result combines with the members' before it, then its scaler, whose own drawer shows its kind and its settings. It drew a stripe and a symbol in the operation's color, the scaler's kind beside them, and, for a cached member, a "CACHED" badge. NumberFields What the number field's inspector and its Problems rule know of numbers: which properties are numbers, what a field's context provides and its unit, what a kind needs and where the kind menu files it, and what a number's kind reads, inside other scalers too. NumberSiblingFieldDrawer The field a relative number reads, picked from a menu of the other number fields of the object that holds the number, each by its name as the inspector writes it. The number's own field and any field that reads it back stay out, so a loop can't be picked. A name the object no longer has, as after a rename, shows as missing. PlayForgeGASProfilerModule The PlayForge GAS module in Unity's Profiler: the GAS's counters, charted: its entities by hub, its effects, impacts, activations and refusals, and its tag compiles and recomputes. PlayForgePreferences PlayForge's view toggles, which belong to each user rather than to the project, so they stay in EditorPrefs, as Unity's own preferences do, and the Preferences page edits them. The settings the project shares are PlayForgeSettings. PlayForgeProcessesProfilerModule The PlayForge Processes module in Unity's Profiler: ProcessControl's and TaskSequence's counters, charted, and in its details the selected frame's costliest processes, which PlayForge puts into the capture as the frame's metadata while the Profiler records. PlayForgeSettings PlayForge's authoring settings, a Forge Project's, so they travel with the project under version control: where each type's new assets go, the defaults a new asset copies and Import lists first, and the effects a new Cost or Cooldown copies. A new asset's file is its name alone. The Project Settings page edits them; the view toggles stay in Preferences (PlayForgePreferences). The file and the EditorPrefs a project took them from once are gone with that taking. ProcessInstantiatorDrawer A process's instantiator: its kind, or None, then its fields. PropertyFieldExtensions Extensions to UI Toolkit's PropertyField: OnPopulated runs a callback once the field has built its children, at once where it has, or else on the field's scheduler, asking again until it has. PurgeFilterDrawer A purge's filter: its kind, named without "Purge Filter", as Except Tagged, or one of your own, then the kind's own fields. QuickFillWizard Quick Fill, from a scaler field's menu: what it fills, the scaler's levels or its points; a pattern and its values; rounding; and a preview of the values as the scaler's table shows them, with their curve, and, for a scaler spread over levels, what each level reads between its points. Apply writes them, and the curve a spread scaler reads, as one Undo step. It drew a look of its own, a purple bold title, a green Apply, 10 px hints and tinted boxes, from styles set in C#, with its fields outside the label column, and wrote through a property it kept from when it opened. RelativeAttributeWorkerDrawer A relative attribute worker, one made from AbstractRelativeAttributeWorker: its kind, picked from those workers or None, then its fields, folding to a line of their values. RequirementTemplateEditor A Requirement Template's inspector: the shared header, then its fields. RespawnPlaceDrawer A Respawn's place: its kind, Home, Where It Died or Point, or one of your own, named without "Respawn Place", then the kind's own fields, as Point's point. RuntimeDebugger The Debugger: one window for the game as it plays, in place of the GAS Debugger, Process Control and the Tag Debugger. Its Entities view lists the hubs ProcessControl registers, of either kind, beside one hub's attributes, effects, abilities and tags, which it can change. Its Processes view lists every process, with what it's doing and how long its steps take, and its Tags view every tag the entities hold, as a tree, beside who holds the one selected. Its Timeline view shows what the entities' abilities and effects did over time, as a recorder heard it. The lists follow ProcessControl as processes join and leave, and the values change in place, at the rate the window menu sets, while the game plays. Outside Play mode it offers Play Mode. The GAS Debugger scanned the scene for MonoBehaviour hubs and rebuilt its details every 0.25 s; Process Control and the Tag Debugger were IMGUI windows of their own. SaveScalerAssetWindow Save as Scaler Asset, from a magnitude field's menu: a name and a folder, then Save and Use, which saves the field's scaler as a Scaler asset and makes the field share it. ScalableFloatDrawer A number field: its name, then its kind, Constant or another, and either its number or its range, as in "6–8 s", and its field menu. Another kind adds a one-line summary of what it reads, how the field combines its number with the kind, then the kind's own content: its values per level and their curve, its Scaler asset, or its fields. The kind menu files kinds by category and offers only those the field's context resolves (NumberContextAttribute), and a field whose unit is "%" shows and takes its number as a percentage. Its constant keeps the field's limits, on a slider where it has a range, and its label shows the field's tooltip. ScalableIntDrawer A whole-number field, such as Ticks: the same field, with its rounding. ScalerActions What a magnitude field's kind menu and field menu do, each as one Undo step that reaches every selected asset. Each asset's field changes from its own values, through a SerializedObject of its own. ScalerAssetEditor A Scaler asset's inspector: its name, kind and how many fields use it, its Description, its values, and the fields that use it, each a row that selects its asset. Its Name names it, as menus and The Forge list it; it could only be read, so a Scaler asset couldn't be renamed in The Forge. ScalerBehaviourDrawer A scaler's behaviour: its kind, named without "ScalerBehaviour" or "Behaviour", then the kind's own fields. The picker offers no None: a list's "−" removes a behaviour. An empty slot stays empty as it's drawn. ScalerDrawer A scaler field drawn on its own, such as an effect's Delta Time Scaler or an attribute set element's Scaling: its name and kind, the range it gives, then its content: its values per level with their curve, Stretch Over Levels, the kind's own fields and its behaviours, or a Shared scaler's asset. It drew a tinted box with a colored border, a collapse arrow, Quick Fill tabs and an import button, and rebuilt itself on a copy of the first selected asset, so an edit after a rebuild reached that asset alone. It writes nothing while it draws. Its kinds file by category, as a number field's do, and its field menu is a number field's: Save as Scaler Asset, the Scaler assets, Import Values, Quick Fill and Make Constant. ScalerTry A scaler tried in the editor: read at each level of a range against stand-ins for its caster and its target, which hold the values typed for them or filled from an entity's attribute set, and with the values a caller sets. A read finds what the scaler asks for, each attribute on its side and each caller's key, and adds a row for each the first time, filled from its side's entity where it has one. A row it lacks reads as an entity without the attribute does, and a caller's key not set reads as a caller that didn't set it. A stand-in holds attributes alone: a number that reads an effect on a side, an item, a tag, a retention group's part or Local Data reads as it would on an entity with none of them. A Scaler asset's try, from For(ScalerAsset), is kept for the session with Keep(), and never written into the asset. ScalerTry.AttributeRow An attribute a side holds for a read: whether it has it, and its current and base values. ScalerTry.CallerRow A key a caller sets for a read, with its value, or not set. ScalerTry.Reading What a read gave: its levels, the value at each, and the parts behind each. ScalerTry.Side The caster or the target: the attributes the read asked of it, and the entity they were filled from. ScalerValuesWindow Import Values, from a magnitude field's menu: choose a Scaler asset or another asset's field, compare their values level by level, with both curves, and Copy Values into the field as one Undo step. A shorter table's last value holds for the levels past its end. It replaces the scaler import window, which ignored the kinds a field allows and kept its list for 120 s. SectionClearUtility Clears a section's properties to a new asset's values, and empties its lists. Each field took its type's default, 0 or the first choice, so a cleared Impact allowed no target and had no chance to apply. SequenceInjectionDrawer An Inject task's injection: its kind, named without "Injection", always of some kind. SerializedPropertyExtensions Extensions that find the C# field behind a SerializedProperty: GetFieldInfo walks the property's path, going on into the object a [SerializeReference] field holds, and GetAttribute<T> and HasAttribute<T> read an attribute the field is marked with. SpreadsheetChange One change a sheet makes: a number of an asset, what it reads now, and what it will. SpreadsheetImport What a sheet would change in the project's assets, and what of it can't be read. StackBehaviourDrawer A stack behaviour, as an effect's Stack Behaviours list holds it: its kind, picked from the behaviours there are, then its fields, folding to a line of their values, as a worker is drawn. The behaviours configure a stacking container, a type apart from the one the effect behaviour drawer takes, so they had no drawer: Unity's own field gave a new element no kind to pick, and none could be added. Each is named for what it does. StandardWorkerGroupDrawer A worker group: its four lists of workers, each Unity's reorderable list, where a new worker starts empty for its kind to be picked. The Workers section it's drawn in folds, counts and imports it. Its name, which nothing reads, it doesn't draw. It was a box of its own, with a colored border, colored count badges, a type tag and an Import of its own, from 90 styles set in C#, inside a section whose header already counted and imported it. StartingItemDrawer A starting item on one row: the item, then an Equip checkbox, which equips it as it's given. It drew as a foldout holding Item and Equip On Init. TagDrawer A tag field: Unity's field, its label in the label column, the tag's parents in secondary text and its leaf in strong text, by its display name (FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeTagField). Pressing it opens the tag picker, Unity's searchable dropdown of the tags its context offers (ForgeTagContext), with None and, where the field may make one, New Tag… (FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeTagPicker). Its right-click menu clears it, makes a new tag, makes its tag a child of another, or copies its path. It was a button with a colored left border, a 120 px label it dropped for any field inside a list, text that changed as the pointer passed, and a picker drawn under it in tinted boxes in code, with a button that showed only on hover. TagQueryDrawer A tag query, in Unity's aligned fields: its tag, which tags match it, then how many it counts, as its comparison and its number on one row, "Count Greater Than 0" for has the tag. It drew a tinted box with labels of its own size and color. TagRegistryAssetPostprocessor Marks the tag registry, ForgeTagRegistry, out of date whenever a .asset file is imported, deleted or moved, so what reads it next, as a tag field's picker, scans the project's tags again. TagWorkerDrawer A tag worker, as a worker group's Tag list holds one: its kind, picked from the tag workers or None, then its fields, folding to a line of their values. TagWorkerRequirementPacketDrawer One of a tag worker's tag requirements, in a row: its tag, Require or Avoid, and the weight, a number of any kind. Require holds while the entity's weight of the tag is at least the weight, and Avoid while it's below. TagWorkerRequirementsDrawer A tag worker's Requirements: its list of tag requirements alone, labelled Tag Requirements. TargetingTaskDrawer An ability's targeting task: its kind, named without "TargetTask" or "Task", then its fields. TaskSequenceReferenceDrawer A sequence reference: a field as a kind field is, the sequence's name in its box, which opens a searchable dropdown of the project's sequences, the static methods marked [TaskSequenceMethod] that take nothing and return a sequence, by their names, None first, each class's under its name where more than one class holds them. A pick is one Undo step. A method the reference names that the project no longer has shows as missing until another is picked. It was Unity's popup, one long list, and before that an IMGUI popup, which wrote "(None)", and which searched every type of every assembly for the methods. TextureItemDrawer A row of an asset's Textures: its tag, then its texture, a project asset, side by side on one line. TheForge The Forge, PlayForge's main window: a list of the project's PlayForge assets beside a detail pane that holds the selected asset's inspector, under a summary of what it does and what uses it. The toolbar holds Create, the type filters, Tags, the search, the problem count and the help button, which opens the editor tools guide's section on The Forge; the status bar holds the counts. It follows the project, with no Refresh and no timer, and the validator's problems with it. One click selects a row and shows its asset. It had Create, View, Analysis and Settings tabs: the Analysis tab's power scores stay hidden until Items and Entities score too, and the Settings tab's settings are on the two settings pages. TypePickerCache The concrete classes a type allows, by name, kept per type for the editor session; a kind field's picker lists them. Its own picker window, the field that opened it and the TypeRef it wrote went unused, and went. ValuePipelineDrawer A Value Pipeline field as a reference to an asset: New beside it while it's empty, which makes one where The Forge makes assets and uses it, and Open once it names one. It was Unity's bare object field. ValuePipelineEditor A Value Pipeline's inspector: what it's for, its stages in order, each of a kind with its fields, and a line that says them; then its Try section, a value put through its stages at each level, as a Scaler asset's Try reads its scaler. Unity's own fields. ValuePipelineTry A Value Pipeline tried in the editor: a value put through its stages at each level of a range, against the stand-ins a Scaler asset's try reads against, a caster's and a target's attributes, typed or filled from an entity, and the values a caller sets. Each chance a stage rolls comes up where it can, or misses where it can, as ChancesComeUp says, so a read gives the same each time. A Block or Evade stage rolls first, as it does as an effect lands, and one that comes up stops the hit before the pipeline runs: nothing of it lands. No effect is behind a try, so a stage that reads the hit's carrier reads none, and what an Absorb stage soaks comes off no one. A pipeline's try, from For(ValuePipeline), is kept for the session with Keep(), and never written into the asset. ValuePipelineTry.Reading What a read gave: the value it put in, its levels, and the run at each. ValuePipelineTry.Run A level's run: each stage's step and what came out, or the stop that stopped the hit. ValueStageDrawer A pipeline stage: its kind, always of some kind, then its fields, as a worker is drawn. VarianceDrawer A Randomized scaler's variance: its kind, Percentage, Flat or Multiplier, or one of your own, named without "Variance", then the kind's own numbers, as Multiplier's Min and Max. Structs NumberLimits The limits a number field's constant keeps in the inspector, from its NumberMinAttribute, NumberMaxAttribute and NumberRangeAttribute, in what the field stores. Interfaces IForgeComponentRule A rule about one kind of component, whose problems an asset's inspector shows under its Components list. Enums ForgeProblemSeverity How serious a problem is: a Warning is likely a mistake, and an Error stops something working. A Note may be meant, as a trigger on an event that code sends: the Problems view lists it, and the counts and an inspector's header leave it out. NumberFields.Walk How far ScalersIn(object, Walk) walks into the numbers a value holds. QuickFillWizard.EFillPattern The shape the values take from the first to the last. QuickFillWizard.ERounding How the values are rounded once made.

api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.EntityClock.htm.summary: Class EntityClock Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll An entity's own time: the game's, as ForgeTime reads it, scaled by the entity's TimeScale: the scale code sets, as a hit-stop's, times the one its Time Scale attribute gives, as a slow's or a haste's, so the two compose. The entity's effects tick by it, its cooldowns among them, and so do its abilities' sequences and waits. Every entity ran on Unity's one clock, so nothing could slow one entity and not the rest. A scale of 0 holds the entity's time still; it isn't a pause, which ProcessControl's is, and processes keep their own bookkeeping on the game's clock. It's a clock as any other is, so a sequence that isn't an ability's runs on an entity's time with its packet's Clock set to it. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.EntityDeath.htm.summary: Class EntityDeath Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll What an entity does as it dies and as it revives: a MOBA hero, or anyone who dies and comes back, keeps its entity while its body goes. A frame's counts start from 0 each frame, and count every world's work, a headless run's within the frame among them. A level holds until it changes: the scene's ProcessControl gives the process levels as its LateUpdate loop ends, and the others follow what starts and ends. The markers time PlayForge's work; these say how much of it there is. Each message is of a system, effects, abilities, workers, numbers, processes, sequences and the rest, and a system can take a level of its own, SetLevel(ESystem, ELevel?), as the Creator Lab's log does; Logged hears each message let through, with the entity it's about where it names one. Its methods are marked to hide in the Console's stack, as the Console's Strip Logging Callstack hides them, and a double-click on a message it wrote opens the code that logged it, not this file. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeSave.html.title: Class ForgeSave | PlayForge
api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeSave.html.summary: Class ForgeSave Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll Saves an entity at rest and loads it back. Nothing captured an entity's state, so a game couldn't keep a battle between sessions. Capture(IGameplayAbilitySystem, ForgeAssetCatalog, IForgeEntityIds) takes what lasts on an entity into a ForgeSnapshot: its attributes' permanent commits, its levels, the abilities it knows, its items with their stacks, worn or not, its effects with their time left, its loose tags and its time scale. Modifiers aren't saved: they come back with the effects that carry them. Restore(IGameplayAbilitySystem, ForgeSnapshot, ForgeAssetCatalog, IForgeEntityIds) ends what's running, lets go of what the entity has, and puts back what the save had, on the entity it was taken from or a fresh one of its kind. A restore tells nothing as it goes. No effect is told as applied or removed, no attribute as changed, and nothing of an effect's application runs again: its workers, its commits on application, its contained effects. It tells OnRestored once, as it ends, for a listener to read the entity afresh. Returns ForgeSnapshot Copy(IGameplayAbilitySystem, IGameplayAbilitySystem) Copies what lasts on one entity onto another, as a mirror clone takes its original's state: what Capture(IGameplayAbilitySystem, ForgeAssetCatalog, IForgeEntityIds) takes, put back as Restore(IGameplayAbilitySystem, ForgeSnapshot, ForgeAssetCatalog, IForgeEntityIds) puts it, with no catalog and no IDs, as both entities are in this session. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.ForgeTick.html.summary: Class ForgeTick Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll The fixed-rate tick. With ProcessControl's tick rate set, the game steps in ticks, each a fixed step of its time, a number of them a frame: every process steps once a tick, its end of frame with it, and a sequence waits for the next tick where it waited for the next frame. So a run comes out the same at any frame rate. Off, as it is by default, a wait is Unity's next frame, as it was. A world of its own has a tick of its own, in force while it steps or moves a process, so its sequences wait on its steps. The ticks run on the game's time and stand with it, so a sequence on a clock that runs while it stands, as UnscaledClock does, waits for Unity's frames. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.GameplayConditi.summary: Class GameplayCondition Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll A condition read against a number's context: whether something holds where the number is read, as "the target's Health is below 0.3 of its base". A Conditional scaler reads one to choose its branch. It is a class, so a project adds its own as it adds a kind of number: override Evaluate(in NumberContext), and name it, file it and say what it reads with GameplayConditionAttribute: [Serializable] [GameplayCondition("Target Is Caster", Reads = NumberReads.Caster | NumberReads.Target)] public class TargetIsCaster : GameplayCondition { protected override bool Evaluate(in NumberContext context) => ReferenceEquals(context.Caster, context.Target); public override string Describe() => "the target is the caster"; } Where the context lacks what a condition reads, as a target's tag where there's no target, it doesn't hold, and it logs once. A condition's own numbers read with the condition as their owner. Its fields draw in the inspector with no editor code, with [Tooltip] and [ForgeShowWhen]; it is saved by its class's name, as a [SerializeReference] value is, so renaming the class needs Unity's [MovedFrom]. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.GameplayEffect..summary: Class GameplayEffect Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll A Gameplay Effect asset: a change to an entity, as damage, a heal, a timed buff, a poison, a cost or a cooldown. Abilities, items and code apply it to a target: Generate, through the target's GenerateEffectSpec, makes a GameplayEffectSpec for one application, which ApplyGameplayEffect lands. Its duration's Policy decides how long it lives: an Instant effect makes its change once, and a Durational or Infinite one goes on the target's effect shelf until its time runs out or something removes it. Its impacts change attributes, each a commit that stays or a modifier reversed as the effect ends; it can also grant tags and abilities, apply contained effects, run workers and carry components, and its requirements and conditions say whether it lands, goes on and comes off. It has no level of its own: it takes its origin's. It took the generic IValidationRule, which nothing else took; it declares its own Validate. A rule is a question, asked as often as the activation needs it answered: as it's requested, each frame a buffered request waits, and again once targeting has found its target, as the caster may have changed meanwhile. So a rule changes nothing and draws nothing: one that rolled a chance rolled it each time it was asked. Validate checks the entity getSource hands it: the caster among an ability's Caster Checks, the target among its Target Checks. Refused, it says why in error, as "Hale's Health, 80, isn't < 50". A kind says which of the two it belongs among with ValidationSideAttribute. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.IAttributeImpac.summary: Interface IAttributeImpacter Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll A single magnitude-evaluation unit owned by an IAttributeImpactCarrier. One carrier may expose many impacters; the cached attribute aggregator walks them and applies their contributions in op-precedence order: Add — summed first → DirtyValue. Multiply — composed via MultiplyBehaviour. FlatBonus — added after multiplies. Override — wins (resolved by SortOrder). Reversal under recompute model — retained carriers reverse automatically when removed (Recompute simply walks the new shorter retention list). One-shot committed contributions persist via CachedAttributeValue.committedOneShotDelta and are reversed only by an explicit synthetic-carrier rollback (see GameplayEffectImpact.ReverseImpactOnRemoval). Guide: Effects public interface IAttributeImpacter Properties AddBehaviour Only meaningful when Operation is Add: how this add combines with the others on the attribute, as its role says, a plain sum, or diminishing. EAddBehaviour AddBehaviour { get; } Property Value EAddBehaviour Group Retention group this impacter's contribution is attributed to (per-group value breakdown — base vs bonus health, etc.). Attribution only; never changes the math. Default: unattributed. Tag Group { get; } Property Value Tag MultiplyBehaviour Only meaningful when Operation is Multiply. Controls how this multiply impacter composes with other multiply impacters acting on the same attribute slot. EMultiplyBehaviour MultiplyBehaviour { get; } Property Value EMultiplyBehaviour Operation How this impacter's magnitude folds into the aggregate. ECalculationOperation Operation { get; } Property Value ECalculationOperation Pipeline The calculation its value goes through as it commits, once for each hit: an instant impact's, each tick of a periodic one's. None, it lands as it's evaluated. ValuePipeline Pipeline { get; } Property Value ValuePipeline SortOrder Tiebreaker within an operation. Lower runs first. For Override, the lowest sort wins; for Add / Multiply / FlatBonus the order is theoretically irrelevant but the field is kept so authoring can pin determinism (e.g. across reorders of effects that produce floating-point drift). int SortOrder { get; } Property Value int Stages The stages its holders' modifiers add, run after its pipeline as it commits and kept in the hit's breakdown; a lasting impact runs them on its magnitude itself. None by default. IReadOnlyList<AbstractValueStage> Stages { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<AbstractValueStage> TargetSlot Which slot of the AttributeValue the impact lands on. EAttributeTarget TargetSlot { get; } Property Value EAttributeTarget Methods Evaluate(IAttributeImpactCarrier) Evaluate the impacter's magnitude. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.Editor.html.summary: Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.Editor Classes CreatorLabMenu Window → PlayForge → Creator Lab: the lab in a new scene, played. The scenes open first are saved if the author wants. In the editor the lab lists every asset of the project, and opens one in The Forge. EditorLabLibrary The library in the editor, by kind: the active Forge Project's assets, as The Forge's pickers offer them, or every asset of the project's own folders while it has no Forge Project; it switches the active project, as The Forge does, and follows as The Forge switches it. Given folders, it plays those folders' assets alone. LabDriverEditor A Lab Driver's inspector, a project's own among them: the shared header, then its fields. LabRulesEditor The Creator Lab's rules' inspector: the shared header, then their fields.
