api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.ILabRules.h.summary: Interface ILabRules Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.dll What the lab needs to know of a project to play its units: the attribute that is a unit's health, the one it walks at, the tags that stop, hide or shield it, where its attack range is kept, and which of its abilities is its attack. PlayForge has no movement or health of its own, so a project says which of its attributes are these. The Demo's roster says the same of the Demo. Guide: The Creator Lab public interface ILabRules Properties AttackRange How near a unit stands to attack where its Local Data gives no range. float AttackRange { get; } Property Value float AttackRangeKey The Local Data key a unit's attack range is under, or none to stand at AttackRange. Tag AttackRangeKey { get; } Property Value Tag AttackSlot Which of an entity's starting abilities is its attack, from 0, or -1 where none is. int AttackSlot { get; } Property Value int CastOrderKey The Local Data key an entity's bot casting order is under, as "W Q E", or none to cast each in turn. Tag CastOrderKey { get; } Property Value Tag CastWhenKey The Local Data key for when a bot casts an ability: InRange, Hurt, Low (away from its foe), Stunned or FoeLow; or none to cast each in range. Tag CastWhenKey { get; } Property Value Tag Driver The driver the author's unit is ordered about through, a project's own movement and casting, or null for the lab's. ILabUnitDriver Driver { get; } Property Value ILabUnitDriver Health A unit's health: its bar, what a dummy counts, and what a bot reads to know it's hurt. Attribute Health { get; } Property Value Attribute Hides A unit with any of these can't be seen or targeted by the other side, as while it's invisible. IReadOnlyList<Tag> Hides { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<Tag> MovementSpeed What a unit walks at, in units a second, or null to walk at WalkSpeed. Attribute MovementSpeed { get; } Property Value Attribute ReachKey The Local Data key an ability's reach for a bot is under, 0 for anywhere, or none for anywhere. Tag ReachKey { get; } Property Value Tag Shields A unit with any of these can't be targeted by anyone. IReadOnlyList<Tag> Shields { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<Tag> Stops A unit with any of these can't move, as while it's stunned or channeling. IReadOnlyList<Tag> Stops { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<Tag> WalkSpeed How fast a unit walks where it has no movement speed. float WalkSpeed { get; } Property Value float

api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.LabBot.html.summary: Class LabBot Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.dll A bot's mind, the Demo's AI and the Battle sample's fighters made general: it takes the nearest foe it can target, casts what's ready in its order when its moment fits, handing its target in the activation's data, which click targeting takes with no click, and otherwise attacks. Low, it backs off a moment once in a while. Its order is its entity's Local Data under the rules' cast order key, as "W Q E", the letters its casts in its entity's order; with none, each in turn. An ability's moment is its Local Data under the rules' cast-when key: InRange, the default, within its Cast Range, or else its Local Data reach, 0 for anywhere; Hurt, below 60% health; Low, below 35%, cast away from its foe, as an escape; Stunned, while something stops it; FoeLow, with its foe below half. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.html.title: Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab | PlayForge
api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab.html.summary: Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab Classes CreatorLab The Creator Lab: a space where an author puts units down, gives them their project's abilities, effects and items, casts, and watches the numbers move. It builds what it needs as it wakes: PlayForge, where the scene has none; the ground, a light and its camera; a world of its own, which it steps by its own time; its own caster, a neutral source for what the author drops; and its panels. Window → PlayForge → Creator Lab opens it in a new scene. A test makes one with Create(ILabLibrary, LabRules, bool) and drives it through the same calls the panels make. LabAssets What the lab knows of an asset of each kind: its kind, its name, its color. LabBodyDriver The lab's own driver: its units walk in straight lines, set on a target, and cast as the lab's do. LabBot A bot's mind, the Demo's AI and the Battle sample's fighters made general: it takes the nearest foe it can target, casts what's ready in its order when its moment fits, handing its target in the activation's data, which click targeting takes with no click, and otherwise attacks. Low, it backs off a moment once in a while. Its order is its entity's Local Data under the rules' cast order key, as "W Q E", the letters its casts in its entity's order; with none, each in turn. An ability's moment is its Local Data under the rules' cast-when key: InRange, the default, within its Cast Range, or else its Local Data reach, 0 for anywhere; Hurt, below 60% health; Low, below 35%, cast away from its foe, as an escape; Stunned, while something stops it; FoeLow, with its foe below half. LabCamera The lab's camera: it looks down at an angle at a point on the ground, from the distance and tilt it's set to. Scroll pulls it back, a middle drag pans it, and ResetView() puts it back as it started. It follows a unit when given one, as the Demo's follows its hero, and shakes as a cue asks, as the game's camera shaker PlayForge's cues reach through ForgeCues. LabControls A player's controls for one unit, as a MOBA's: right-click the ground to move, right-click a foe it can target to attack it, Q, W, E and R for its abilities past its attack, 1 to 6 for its items' abilities, S to stop, Escape to cancel a cast. An ability that needs a target waits for a left-click, as its own click targeting reads it; meanwhile a ring on the ground shows the ability's reach, another ability's key casts that one instead, and a right-click order lets go of it. It reads PlayForge's input, ForgeInput, so a test or a game's own input stands in, and gives its orders through a driver: its own, its unit's rules', or the lab's. The Creator Lab's take its controlled unit; the Demo's player is these, its hero's. LabDriver A project's driver as an asset: each order a virtual that does as the lab's does, so a project overrides those its game gives its own way, and names the asset on its Lab Rules. Create → PlayForge → Lab Driver. LabDummy A test dummy, and the Demo's training dummy: a unit that stands and counts what it takes. It shows its damage a second over a window, the last blow with its types, and a short history of blows. It doesn't die unless asked: falling, it's revived where it stands at once. Left alone a few seconds, it mends to full, by the mend effect given, or else one of the lab's own. LabEffects The effects the lab makes for itself, as an asset's inspector would fill one in: a dummy's mend, where the project gives none. Each lives in memory alone and goes with what made it. LabPanels The lab's panels, UI Toolkit over the space: the library on the left, the mode on the right with the selected over it, shown as something is selected and set aside by its tab, and the log at the bottom; each other panel collapses to a tab at its edge. The middle stays the space's. Over the space, each unit's bar, and a status at the top that clicks go through: what a cast waits for, what's selected, whom the author controls, and the keys for what can be done now. An asset dragged from the library and dropped on the space is the lab's to apply, cast or give. Neutral panels, Unity's own controls, and a type's color in its icon alone. LabRules A project's rules for the Creator Lab, as an asset. An attribute left empty is the one playing its role in the project, Health or Movement Speed, or else found by its name among the project's: Health, and Movement Speed or Move Speed. With no asset, the lab makes one and finds both. LabRulesExtensions The checks a unit's rules answer, in one place for the lab, its bots and the Demo. LabSeat A bot's place in a battle: what it's made of, its side, its level and where it starts, and what the author gave it since, which a reset gives again as it makes the bot anew. LabShowing What the lab watches its units for, and the journals it keeps while it does: its effect journal over every unit, its stops, which pause its world as one fires and say which, and its watches, sampled over the last minute of its time. The lab steps it after each step of its world. LabSides The lab's sides: Blue and Red for a fight, Green and Gold for more teams, and Neutral, the side of no one, which the lab's own caster stands on. Each is an affiliation tag of the lab's own, made as it's first asked for. LabStop A stop: what it watches for, on the selected unit or any, and what it names, an effect, an ability, a tag, or an attribute and a value. The lab's world pauses as one fires, and says which. LabSummary The selected panel's lines: an asset's numbers level by level, as "−80/−120/−160 Health", and a unit's attributes and effects as they are now. LabUnit A unit in the lab, and the Demo's hero: a GameplayAbilitySystem on a body of its own, which walks where it's sent, attacks what it's set on, casts its abilities and its items', and holds its items. Its attributes, tags, levels and Local Data are the GAS's; this is the space's side of it. Movement is the lab's, a straight line on the ground at its speed, as a project's own body would be for a game. LabUnitSpec What a unit is made from, and where it stands. LabWatch A watch: a unit's attribute, a tag's count, an effect's stacks or time, or a number read on it, pinned, and its values over the last minute of the lab's time, one each tenth of a second. ListLibrary A library of the assets given, as a test or a build gives them. Structs LabBlow A blow a dummy took: when, how much, of what types, and from which effect. LabSide A side a unit stands on in the lab: an affiliation tag, as its registration's data gives it, a name and the color of its ring. Interfaces ILabLibrary The assets the lab plays: in the editor every PlayForge asset of the project or of its active Forge Project, in a build those a project names. The library panel lists them by kind. ILabRules What the lab needs to know of a project to play its units: the attribute that is a unit's health, the one it walks at, the tags that stop, hide or shield it, where its attack range is kept, and which of its abilities is its attack. PlayForge has no movement or health of its own, so a project says which of its attributes are these. The Demo's roster says the same of the Demo. ILabUnitDriver How a unit the author controls is ordered about: moved to a point, set on a unit to attack, made to cast, stopped. PlayForge has no movement of its own, so a project whose units move and cast their own way gives its own driver, on its Lab Rules, and the lab's controls and the Demo's give their orders through it. Without one, the lab's: a unit walks in a straight line and casts as the lab's units do. Enums ELabStopKind What a stop watches for. ELabWatchKind What a watch reads. LabAssetKind The kinds of asset the lab's library lists, in its order. LabMode What the lab's space holds.

api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.LifestealImpact.summary: Class LifestealImpactWorker Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll The Lifesteal worker: it heals its holder a share of each workable loss it deals another, the value of its holder's Share, the attribute it names, which an effect on the holder raises while it should. The losses that count are to its Receives attribute, and it heals its Heals attribute, each the Health role's where it names none. An effect has no lifesteal of its own. Only hits of the impact types it names count, as attacks, so a second worker on another attribute makes a spell vamp. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.NumberContext.h.title: Struct NumberContext | PlayForge
api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.NumberContext.h.summary: Struct NumberContext Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll What a number is read against: what its site has. A kind of number reads it; it is the whole of a kind's API, so adding to it later breaks no kind. It offers the caster, the target and the level; the carrier, where there is one, and what it has dealt; the caller's magnitudes and Local Data, each by key; an attribute's value or a retention group's part of it, on either side, and through SystemOf(NumberSide) the effects there; the activation's data, where a task reads it; and the owner, the object the field belongs to. Has(NumberReads) says which of these this site provides. A site builds one with Of, from an effect spec, a container, an activation's data, a worker's context, an entity, a cue or a process, and reads its numbers through it: Range.Evaluate(NumberContext.Of(data)). A test builds one with For(ISource, ITarget, int, int). It is a struct, and a number read through it allocates nothing. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.NumberKind.html.summary: Class NumberKind Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll A kind of number of your own: one class with one method. Override Evaluate(in NumberContext) to work out the kind's value from what the context offers, and Describe() for the field's one-line summary. Name it, file it and say what it reads with NumberKindAttribute, and the kind menu offers it in every number field whose context provides what it reads: [Serializable] [NumberKind("Distance to Target", Reads = NumberReads.Caster | NumberReads.Target)] [ForgeMenu("Space", Description = "How far the target is from the caster")] public class DistanceToTarget : NumberKind { [Tooltip("Along the ground, leaving height out")] public bool Flat = true; protected override float Evaluate(in NumberContext context) { var from = context.Caster.GetTargetingPacket().position; var to = context.Target.GetTargetingPacket().position; if (Flat) from.y = to.y = 0f; return Vector3.Distance(from, to); } public override string Describe() => "the distance to the target"; } A kind is a scaler, so it also works wherever a scaler does: inside a Group, a Conditional or a Clamped, and in an effect's magnitude. The base answers the scaler's carrier methods by building a NumberContext and calling yours. It reads no values per level. Its fields draw in the inspector with no editor code, as a scaler's do, with [Tooltip] and [ForgeShowWhen]. A kind is saved by its class's name, so renaming the class needs Unity's [MovedFrom], as any [SerializeReference] value does. Test one without an effect through For(ISource, ITarget, int, int). A charged hit reads −180 because its Group adds its caster's Attack Damage, 100, to a Conditional that gives 80, as the caster's Combo Charges, 4, are above 0. A part whose context lacks what it reads says what it needs, "the target", and gives its fallback, so a read in the editor with no entities says where it would change in play. A trace allocates, and is for the editor, tools and tests. A kind or a condition of a project's own explains its parts by overriding Explain(in NumberContext, NumberTrace) or Explain(in NumberContext, NumberTrace) and adding them: trace.Add(Min, context, this, "Min"). api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.ProcessControl..summary: Class ProcessControl Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll The scene's scheduler of processes: every process, a GAS, a projectile, an ability's sequence, registers with it, and it steps each from Unity's player loop, in Update, LateUpdate or FixedUpdate as the process's timing asks, moves it between its states as its lifecycle says, and ends it. A Bootstrapper brings it up as the one Instance, and it then registers the scene's own mono processes, as its Collect On Awake says. ProcessControl.Register(process).HandledBy(handler).With(data).Run() registers a process and starts it, and its result holds the process's relay, which pauses, resumes and ends it; RegisterGroup and RegisterWithGroup hold runtime processes in a group by a tag. Its control state (SetControlState) pauses, closes or ends every process at once; its Fixed Tick Rate, above 0, steps every process at fixed steps of game time, so a run comes out the same at any frame rate; and its Callbacks hear every process register, change state and go. Its bookkeeping is its World, a ProcessWorld, which code can also own and step with no scene. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.ProcessRegistra.summary: Struct ProcessRegistration Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll A process's registration with ProcessControl, built a step at a time: what handles the process, the packet it carries, the ProcessControl that takes it, and, for a MonoBehaviour process, what makes its object. Register(AbstractRuntimeProcess) and its siblings start one, and Run() registers the process and starts it, as registering always has: var result = ProcessControl.Register(projectile).HandledBy(gas).With(data).Run(); if (!result) Debug.Log(result.Refusal); What isn't given takes its default. The handler follows the packet's run-time type: an ability's packet hands the process to its source, and any other to GameRoot, or to none in a world of its own, which reaches for nothing of the scene's. Those overloads are wrappers of this now, marked obsolete, and go before the first Asset Store submission. It is a plain number by default, and it can also be one of the kinds the inspector's kind menu offers: a value by level, a multiple of an attribute, a value its caller sets, any scaler, or a kind a project writes (NumberKind). It is the magnitude field it grew from, under a new name, with the same saved fields: its number (Magnitude), its scaler, and how the two combine (RealMagnitude). api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.ScalerGroup.htm.summary: Class ScalerGroup Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll Several numbers joined as one: each member is a scaler or a kind of number, and says how it joins the others. Members that add are added up; that sum is multiplied by each member that multiplies and divided by each that divides; then each flat bonus is added on. So (5 + Caster's Strength) × 2 + 3 is one number, a wind-up's 1.7 ÷ Caster's Attack Speed another, and a curse's 5 + what its worker answers is one magnitude. A member that overrides gives the group's value alone. Where several override, OverrideMemberCollisionPolicy picks among them: the highest, the lowest, their average, the first or the last; Ignore sets them aside, and the other members join as they would without them. Each member reads in the number's own context, so a member that is a kind reads all the field's context gives, and a member that is a scaler evaluates against the effect, or against the carrier the context fills where there's no effect. Joining its members allocates nothing. It reads its members alone, so it has no values per level. With no members, or none that holds a kind, it is no kind at all (IsEmpty): its field reads its number, as a field with no kind does. It read values per level of its own, which its inspector hid. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.SequenceAnnotat.summary: Class SequenceAnnotation Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll Declarative annotation of what a sequence DOES — the introspection channel for code-driven sequences. Sequence bodies are opaque async lambdas; annotations let the author state gameplay intent so AbilityInspector can decipher abilities built on RunSequenceTask (tooltips, the Forge analysis tab, debugging). The load-and-apply pattern: an asset-loader task (e.g. SetEffectsTask) puts effects into the data packet under a tag, and the sequence applies them via data.TryApplyEffects(target, tag). Annotating with that tag (AppliedEffectsTag) lets the inspector connect the loaded effect assets to this sequence's application — including how many times (MaxApplications, e.g. Chain Lightning's 4 jumps). api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.SequenceTaskLib.summary: Class SequenceTaskLibrary Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll Reusable async building blocks for common gameplay operations. Designed to be awaited inside TaskSequence .Task() lambdas where the caller has access to the data packet and cancellation token. Usage: .Task(async (d, t) => { var target = d.GetPrimary<Transform>(Tags.TARGET); await Seq.MoveTo(target, Vector3.zero, 1.5f, t, easeCurve); }) All timed methods: Accept an optional AnimationCurve for easing (null = linear) Snap to the final value after completion to avoid float drift Respect CancellationToken for interrupt/skip/timeout support Handle zero/negative duration by snapping immediately Hold while their sequence is paused, given the token the task was handed. ArcForce can't: physics moves the body whatever the sequence is doing Guide: Task Sequences Named in: Task Sequences: Waiting · Task Sequences: The libraries · Extending PlayForge: Ability tasks: Stage tasks · Task Sequences: Building one · Time, Input and Logging: Which clock a run takes · Time, Input and Logging: Pointer input: What reads it · Extending PlayForge: Sequence tasks, injections and stage policies: A sequence the inspector lists public static class SequenceTaskLibrary Inheritance object SequenceTaskLibrary Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Methods ArcForce(Rigidbody, Vector3, float, float, CancellationToken, bool) Launches a Rigidbody in a parabolic arc from its current position to the destination using physics forces. The body interacts with colliders during flight. Temporarily disables standard gravity and applies a computed custom gravity to achieve the exact arc shape. On completion (or cancellation), the body is snapped to the destination and original gravity settings are restored. A context holds the values set on what it was built from: an effect's spec (spec.SetByCaller(tag, value), before it's applied), an ability activation's data (data.SetByCaller(tag, value), which each effect the ability makes takes as it's made, and which the ability's tasks read), or the data that spawned a process. It is a number kind, so it reads from any context that holds values: it read only an effect spec's, so a task's or a process's number read its default. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Testing.Allocat.title: Class AllocationProbe | PlayForge
api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Testing.Allocat.summary: Class AllocationProbe Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge.Testing Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.Testing.dll Measures allocation with Unity.Profiling.ProfilerRecorder, because the GC API returns 0 under Mono. Unity's "GC Allocated In Frame" counter reads live within a frame, so an operation is the counter's change across it. Dispose it as the test ends. A frame takes more care, because the counter's own total for a frame is noisy: 450 to 532 bytes with nothing running, shifting at random. Sampling every player loop stage shows why. All of that lands outside the player loop, in the editor's work between frames, except 40 bytes from the test runner's coroutine tick. So a frame here is the counter's change from the player loop's first stage to its last, less that tick, measured on the same frame. A clean frame reads exactly 0, with no baseline to calibrate, and a baseline would be worse than noise: taken while the noise ran high, it would hide real allocation. The cost is that anything allocated in a coroutine goes unmeasured with the test runner's. PlayForge's stepping runs in Update and its async work in UniTask continuations, which are measured. Now and then a burst of a kilobyte or so landed on a few frames at random, whatever was running. It was the editor's Build Report REST service, which listens on a port of its own: where another editor holds that port, as one open beside a batch run does, it tries again about once a second on a thread of its own, and each try allocates about 4 KB, which the counter takes as the frame's. Most frames are short, so a try rarely landed in one, but among 500 entities, whose frames fill most of a second, nearly every measure took one. A probe ends those tries (FarEmerald.PlayForge.Testing.AllocationProbe.EndRestServiceRetries()). Other noise may still land, and it doesn't repeat, where real allocation does, so a measure that isn't clean is taken again and the cleanest stands. A leak fails every attempt. It makes what a test needs, entities on either hub, from an identity asset or from attributes, and plays them as a game does: Hit(IGameplayAbilitySystem, IGameplayAbilitySystem, GameplayEffect) applies an effect, Cast(IGameplayAbilitySystem, Ability, IGameplayAbilitySystem, int) gives an ability and starts it, Use(IGameplayAbilitySystem, Ability, IGameplayAbilitySystem) starts one the entity has, and Hold(IGameplayAbilitySystem, Item, int) equips an item. Audit() first says what broke of its Invariants. ForgeTest makes one for each test, audits it and ends it. Step frames, and let ProcessControl step what runs: never call a process's update by hand. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.Testing.html.summary: Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge.Testing Classes AllocationMarker Runs after every other Update, so it marks where ProcessControl's stepping has finished and the test runner's coroutine tick is about to begin. AllocationProbe Measures allocation with Unity.Profiling.ProfilerRecorder, because the GC API returns 0 under Mono. Unity's "GC Allocated In Frame" counter reads live within a frame, so an operation is the counter's change across it. Dispose it as the test ends. A frame takes more care, because the counter's own total for a frame is noisy: 450 to 532 bytes with nothing running, shifting at random. Sampling every player loop stage shows why. All of that lands outside the player loop, in the editor's work between frames, except 40 bytes from the test runner's coroutine tick. So a frame here is the counter's change from the player loop's first stage to its last, less that tick, measured on the same frame. A clean frame reads exactly 0, with no baseline to calibrate, and a baseline would be worse than noise: taken while the noise ran high, it would hide real allocation. The cost is that anything allocated in a coroutine goes unmeasured with the test runner's. PlayForge's stepping runs in Update and its async work in UniTask continuations, which are measured. Now and then a burst of a kilobyte or so landed on a few frames at random, whatever was running. It was the editor's Build Report REST service, which listens on a port of its own: where another editor holds that port, as one open beside a batch run does, it tries again about once a second on a thread of its own, and each try allocates about 4 KB, which the counter takes as the frame's. Most frames are short, so a try rarely landed in one, but among 500 entities, whose frames fill most of a second, nearly every measure took one. A probe ends those tries (FarEmerald.PlayForge.Testing.AllocationProbe.EndRestServiceRetries()). Other noise may still land, and it doesn't repeat, where real allocation does, so a measure that isn't clean is taken again and the cleanest stands. A leak fails every attempt. EffectConfig What Effect(string, EffectConfig) builds. Each field is the plain default unless a test needs otherwise. ForgeTest The base of a test that plays PlayForge content: a live ForgeTestWorld before each test, and after it the world's invariants audited and the world ended. A test is a PlayMode [UnityTest] whose body runs through Live(Func<UniTask>), from a frame's end: [UnityTest] public IEnumerator Burn_ticks_twice() => Live(async () => { var health = Make.Attribute("Health"); var target = World.Entity(Hub.Runtime, Make.Set(Make.Pool(health, 100f, 100f))); var burn = Make.Effect("Burn", new EffectConfig { Policy = EEffectDurationPolicy.Durational, Target = health, Magnitude = -10f, Duration = 1f, PeriodicTicks = true, Ticks = 2 }); World.Hit(World.Entity(Hub.Runtime), target, burn); await Frames.Until(() => World.Value(target, health) <= 80f, 90, "two ticks land"); }); A test with a base class of its own makes a world with Start(float) instead. ForgeTestWorld One live PlayForge for one test: a real ProcessControl and GameRoot brought up by the real Bootstrapper, stepped by Unity's player loop a frame at a time. It makes what a test needs, entities on either hub, from an identity asset or from attributes, and plays them as a game does: Hit(IGameplayAbilitySystem, IGameplayAbilitySystem, GameplayEffect) applies an effect, Cast(IGameplayAbilitySystem, Ability, IGameplayAbilitySystem, int) gives an ability and starts it, Use(IGameplayAbilitySystem, Ability, IGameplayAbilitySystem) starts one the entity has, and Hold(IGameplayAbilitySystem, Item, int) equips an item. Its Clock(float) and Rolls(params float[]) make time and chance the test's. It ends as a test asks, or as it's disposed (await using): every process it began, every object and asset it made, and the framework's static state, so tests run in any order. Audit() first says what broke of its Invariants. ForgeTest makes one for each test, audits it and ends it. Step frames, and let ProcessControl step what runs: never call a process's update by hand. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.ValuePipeline.h.title: Class ValuePipeline | PlayForge
api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.ValuePipeline.h.summary: Class ValuePipeline Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll A value through ordered stages as it lands. An effect names one as its impact's calculation, as an Unreal effect names its execution calculation, so each hit goes through the stages a project writes once: the caster's bonuses, those that read the target, a critical roll, the target's reductions, a barrier; and what comes out lands. A new item that changes every hit is a stage, not an edit to each attack. Generic: the value is any number an impact lands with, a blow, a heal, a drain. It isn't a Scaler asset. A scaler is a number worked out from its context, read wherever a number is; a pipeline transforms a value it's given, once, as it lands, with both sides known, and its stages can do what a number can't: roll once for the hit and keep it, route a part of it into a barrier, say what each did. It runs for what an impact commits: an instant impact's hit, each tick of a periodic one. A lasting impact's value is read again as its attribute changes, so nothing runs it. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.WorkerNumberKin.summary: Class WorkerNumberKind Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Assembly FarEmerald.PlayForge.dll A value a worker answers under a key: the number asks, and a worker that implements INumberWorker answers from what it knows, as how much health its effect's target has lost since the effect began. So work a number can't do alone goes to a worker, and the number reads the result: a curse whose every fourth tick deals a share of the damage its target took since it landed is one effect, with one worker. It asks the workers of the effect whose number it is, about that application of the effect, or the caster's or the target's own workers. The first worker that answers the key gives the value. Where none answers, as where the number isn't an effect's or the entity has no such worker, it reads its Default. api/FarEmerald.PlayForge.html.summary: Namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge Classes Ability An ability: one thing an entity can do, as a fireball, a dash or a heal. An entity learns it from its Entity asset's Starting Abilities, from an equipped item's Active Ability or from code (AbilitySystemComponent.GiveAbility), and keeps it in a slot with a level of its own, between its StartingLevel and MaxLevel, kept under its asset tag. An activation passes its caster's tag requirements and its Caster Checks (SourceActivationRules), lets its Behaviour's targeting task pick its target, which its Target Checks (TargetActivationRules) then check, applies its Cost and Cooldown effects to its caster and spends its AttributeCosts, as it starts or in the stage that takes them, and runs its stages of tasks. Its Definition says how it activates, its Tags what it is, grants and requires, and its Components add features with hooks into its life; its WorkerGroup, OnHit and Modifiers hold on its entity while the entity knows it. AbilityActivationHandle One activation of an ability as it runs, which its slot, an AbilitySpecContainer, keeps from its claim to its end: its Data, the compiled Proxy that runs it, the tokens that cancel its targeting and its stages, whether it's targeting or running its stages, and whether it has let its claim go. HandleId numbers it among its entity's activations, from 0. AbilityBehaviour Abilities are separated into groups by activation policy. Depending on the policy, activation can proceed or is blocked. Even if the policy allows simultaneous activation, additional validation steps are taken before activation actually proceeds. If an ability has no targeting proxy (TargetingProxy is null) AbilityBreakdown The full static description of an ability. AbilityCharges An ability's charges on its caster: several uses, each spending a charge that comes back as the ability's Recharge says, by default on a cooldown of its own. An ability of 1 charge, with a recharge of PlayForge's own, is an ordinary cooldown. Its Charges component keeps them with the ability as its caster holds it, and is the ability's cooldown model through them. AbilityDataPacket Data packet for ability execution. Extends SequenceDataPacket so that abilities run through the TaskSequence system natively — the same packet flows through targeting, execution stages, callbacks, and ProcessControl. IMPORTANT: Ability tasks must be stateless. All per-activation data flows through this packet, NOT as fields on the task itself. AbilityDefinition An ability's Definition: its Name, Description and Textures, and how it activates: its When Busy (ActivationPolicy) and WhileTargeting; under Queue, its input buffer's BufferWindow and BufferPriority; Activate At Start (ActivateImmediately), for a Starting Ability; its Triggers, the gameplay events and gained tags that set it off on its own; its ChanceToActivate and how that rolls (ActivationRoll); the ProcCoefficient its effects' hits carry where an effect sets none of its own; and the crowd control it ignores (IgnoresCrowdControl). AbilityEffectUsage One effect's participation in an ability, with per-level numbers and contained effects. AbilityInspector Reads what an ability does without running it, for tooltips, the editor's summaries and the Creator Lab: Build gives its AbilityBreakdown, each effect it applies, in what role (a stage's task, its cost or cooldown, or contained in another) and on whom, with its numbers at each of its levels read through their scalers, and its components, triggers, chance to activate and attribute costs. BuildEffectSeries reads one effect across a range of levels, against a caster and a target where it's given them, and EvaluateAtLevel one number at a level; a number that reads what the read wasn't given, as the target, is marked dynamic. AbilityLevelValidation A Caster Check that compares the ability's level on its caster with Level, by Comparison, as a form it unlocks at a rank; by default, 2 or more. AbilityProxy Bridge between ability activation and sequence-based execution. AbilityProxy compiles the AbilityBehaviour into reusable TaskSequences at construction time — one for targeting and one for execution stages. Both phases register with ProcessControl for full visibility. Since AbilityDataPacket extends SequenceDataPacket, the same packet flows through targeting, execution, callbacks, and ProcessControl. Injection, callbacks, and usage effects are handled transparently: Injections go to the compiled sequence, its callback heard either way AbilitySystemCallbacks fire from sequence stage hooks Usage effects apply at configured stage boundaries AbilityReader A reader of an ability's cooldown: Assign(Tag) names the tag, and each Update step it finds the GAS's longest effect duration under it. It shows nothing of what it finds. AbilitySave An ability the entity knows, in its slot. AbilitySequenceCompiler Compiles an AbilityBehaviour into a reusable TaskSequence. Each AbilityTaskBehaviourStage becomes a SequenceStage with: Ability tasks wrapped via AbilityTaskAdapter Stage policy mapped from IAbilityProxyStagePolicy to ISequenceStagePolicy Usage effects wired into stage OnTerminate callbacks AbilitySystemCallbacks wired into stage event hooks The compiled TaskSequence is reusable: each Run() creates a fresh TaskSequenceRuntime, so the immutable definition is safe to share. IMPORTANT: Ability tasks must be stateless. All per-activation data flows through the AbilityDataPacket, not as fields on the task. AbilitySpec An ability as one entity knows it, made as the entity learns it: the Ability (Base) and its caster (Source), with its level kept on the caster under the ability's asset tag (GetLevel). It's the origin of the effects the ability applies, so they take its level and context tags, and an activation's data holds it as its EffectOrigin. It applies the ability's cost and cooldown (ApplyUsageEffects, PayCosts, SpendCooldown), reads the ability's numbers at its level (Read), finds its components (Find<T>), and keeps what they hold for this entity (ComponentStates) and its cooldown model (CooldownModel), which a HUD reads. AbilitySpecContainer One slot of an entity's ability system: the AbilitySpec it holds (Spec), its slot (Index), and the ability's activations as they run. It says whether the ability runs (IsActive), holds its claim (IsClaiming), is choosing its target (IsTargeting), is cooling down (IsCooldown) and which stage it's in (ActiveStageIndex); Cancel interrupts its runs, but one in a critical stage, and Inject sends an injection into each. AbilitySystemComponent.TryGetAbilityContainer finds one by slot or by ability. AbilityStageCondition When an ability's stage runs: always, or only while a tag is there, or only while it's missing, in the activation's data, on the caster or on the target. The compiler emitted no branch, so there was no on-hit or on-miss stage. AbilitySystemCallbacks Callbacks for ability system events. Used for monitoring ability lifecycle without modifying behavior. AbilitySystemComponent Manages abilities for an entity. Integrates with the worker system for impact processing. AbilityTagRequirements Tag requirements for ability activation. Specifies what tags the source (caster) and target must have or avoid. AbilityTags An ability's Tags: its AssetTag, made from its Name, which its entity carries while it knows the ability and keeps the ability's level under; its ContextTags, which describe it and which the changes its effects make carry as context; its Passive Tags (PassiveGrantedTags), on its entity while it knows the ability, and its Active Tags (ActiveGrantedTags), while an activation runs; and its TagRequirements of its caster, to activate and while it runs, and of its target. Names says whether a list of tags names an ability, its asset tag or a context tag being one of them or under one, as Cancelled By and Blocks name abilities. AbilityTaskAdapter Adapts an AbstractAbilityTask to the ISequenceTask interface. Since AbilityDataPacket extends SequenceDataPacket directly, the adapter simply casts the incoming data to AbilityDataPacket and delegates to the underlying ability task. IMPORTANT: Ability tasks must be stateless — all per-activation state must flow through the AbilityDataPacket, not as fields on the task. Shared [SerializeReference] instances are reused across activations. AbilityTaskBehaviourStage One of an ability's stages, which run one after another: the Tasks it starts together, and its Completion (StagePolicy), which ends it as its last task ends (All) or its first (Any), cancelling the rest. ApplyUsageEffects applies the ability's cost and cooldown in it, as it starts or, with ApplyUsageAtStageStart off, as it ends well, once an activation; its Condition skips it unless a tag is there, or missing; and its own CancelledBy and Blocks, where it names any, hold while it runs in place of the ability's. A stage that holds a critical task is critical (IsCritical): it commits the ability, so Cancelled By doesn't cancel it. AbilityTrigger What activates an ability on its own: a gameplay event sent to its entity, or a tag its entity gains. An ability activated only when code asked for it. The core sends events of its own to an entity where an ability listens for them: IMPACT_DEALT and IMPACT_TAKEN as an impact lands between two entities, KILL to the killer and DIED to the one who died, and REVIVED. Their data hold the instigator as SOURCE, the entity it was done to as EVENT_SUBJECT, and an impact's ImpactData as EVENT_IMPACT. A trigger can take only some impacts, roll a chance, and target the instigator or the subject. AbsorbStage A loss taken first from another attribute of the one hit, as a barrier or a shield takes a blow before health: what it soaks comes off that attribute, unworkable so no worker reads it again, at the frame's end, and the rest goes on. A gain passes it by. AbstractAbilityComponent A component of an ability: it hears the ability granted and removed, may refuse an activation, and hears an activation start, wind up, which the activation waits on, commit its cost and cooldown, and end, by how it did. AbstractAbilityRelatedTask The base of every task an ability runs: its targeting task, an AbstractTargetingAbilityTask, and its stages' tasks and asset loaders, each an AbstractAbilityTask. Each is handed the activation's data: Prepare as its stage starts, Activate, the work its stage waits on, and Clean as the stage ends; IsCriticalSection says whether it's critical work, which commits its ability to its stage and keeps out another ability's critical work while it runs. One task object serves every activation of its ability, so what it keeps for one belongs in the activation's data, not in its fields. Read gives one of its numbers at its ability's level, EntityOf its caster or its first target, and ApplyTo applies an effect from the ability with the activation's magnitudes. AbstractAbilityTask The base of a task in an ability's stage, as Apply Effects, Delay or Run Sequence: a stage starts its tasks together and ends as its Completion says, as its last task's Activate ends or its first's. A task of your own derives from it and overrides Activate, the work, and IsCriticalSection, with Prepare and Clean for what it does as its stage starts and ends; [ForgeMenu] files it in the stage's task picker. What it keeps for one activation goes in data.GetTaskState<T>(this), as one task serves every activation of its ability. AbstractAccumulatingEffectWorker Effect worker that tracks accumulated impact and performs work on removal. Useful for effects like "explode for accumulated damage when removed". AbstractAccumulatingEffectWorker.AccumulationData Per-effect instance data for tracking accumulation. AbstractAnalysisWorker Analysis workers run at end-of-frame after all other work is complete. Used for death checks, state evaluation, and other post-frame analysis. Analysis workers can either: Return actions to be queued (preferred for deferred execution) Perform direct actions via the legacy Activate() method AbstractAttributeValidationRule The base of an ability check that reads one of the checked entity's attributes, as Attribute does: it holds the Attribute, and a kind made from it overrides Validate, which checks the entity its list hands it, and GetName. Without [ValidationSide], either list offers it. AbstractAttributeWorker Base class for attribute change workers. Workers can be Inline (modify change value synchronously) or Deferred (queue actions for end-of-frame). AbstractCachedScaler Base class for cached scalers that participate in attribute modification rules. Used for derived/computed attributes that depend on other attributes. AbstractChargeRecharge How an ability's spent charges come back: what's in hand, and what a use spends. Extend it for a recharge of your own; each hook has a default, so a recharge overrides only what it changes. By default, each spent charge's cooldown runs alone and holds that charge back. AbstractClockChoice A clock picked in an inspector, for what runs a sequence: an ability's Run Sequence task, or a component of your own. Each kind gives the clock for a run on a packet as the run starts; a [Serializable] class of your own made from this one is offered beside them. The field left empty, None, leaves the run the clock it would have had. AbstractComponentValidationRule<TComponent> A check an ability's component stands behind, as Check Range is the Cast Range component's: shown among the ability's checks while the ability holds the component, and tied to it. The component enforces what it says, so the rule passes; no list holds it and the picker doesn't offer it, as it comes with its component and goes with it. A component of your own brings one with its TargetCheck or CasterCheck. AbstractContextImpactWorker Impact worker with standard context validation options. Most impact workers should inherit from this class. AbstractCreateProcessAbilityTask The base of an ability task that creates processes, as Create Mono Process spawns a projectile: a kind made from it sits under the Process submenu of a stage's task picker. A GameRoot's CreateProcessTasks take them too, each run once, with the GameRoot's own data, as the Bootstrapper brings the game up. AbstractCueHandler A gameplay cue: what something shows and sounds, apart from what it does. An effect's, an ability's, an entity's and an item's Cues components list their cues, each a list for each of its moments, and ForgeCues plays them all. A burst plays as a moment comes; a lasting cue begins as its moment comes and ends as it's over, as an effect that lands and later comes off, and a restore ends it and begins it again, playing no burst. Each hook is a no-op until a handler overrides it. An effect changed attributes and tags and nothing else, so what it showed was each game's own code. AbstractEffectChange One change a modifier makes to an effect as it's made. Each writes into the application's EffectChanges, which the effect's own reads take in; a project adds its own by deriving one. AbstractEffectComponent A component of an effect: it hears the effect land, tick, hit and end, at the moments its workers do, and a lasting effect lend and take back what it gives while it lasts. AbstractEffectConfig<T> A behaviour of an effect's containers of type T: GetCorrectContainer picks, among the target's containers of the effect, the one an application goes to, the last behaviour by priority having its way. An effect's stack behaviours derive from it through AbstractStackingConfig. AbstractEffectContainer One lasting application of an effect on its target's shelf: its spec; its clock, the total duration, the time left, the period and the time to its next tick; whether its ongoing requirements hold; and whether it's still active. A Durational or Infinite effect's duration makes one as it lands, of the kind its re-application and stacking choose; while it's on the shelf it grants the effect's asset tag and granted tags, and as it comes off it reverses the effect's lasting impacts and lands its On Remove effects. Code finds one with TryGetEffectContainer on the entity. AbstractEffectWorker Base class for effect lifecycle workers. Effect workers are attached to specific effects and react to their lifecycle events. All actions from effect workers are scoped to the effect's lifetime. AbstractEffectingMonoProcess A gameplay mono process that applies effects, as a projectile does as it lands. Its effects come from its origin, and take the set-by-caller magnitudes of the data that spawned it, as an ability's other effects do. AbstractEntityComponent A component of an entity: it hears its entity register, die, revive and end, and an activation of one of its abilities wind up, which the activation waits on. AbstractEntityService A per-entity object its components share, as the auras an entity runs, AuraSet, or the wait a Respawn counts down, RespawnTimer: made the first time it's asked for, with GetService<T>(); stepped each frame by its entity's own time; told as its entity revives; and ended with its entity. Each hook is a no-op a service overrides as it needs, so a heat meter or a combo counter of your own lives beside PlayForge's. AbstractFocusedAttributeWorker Attribute worker focused on a specific target attribute with standard validation options. Most attribute workers should inherit from this class. AbstractForgeComponent A component of a PlayForge asset: a feature it carries, added in its Components section, a class with hooks into its asset's life, each a no-op a kind may override. An effect's, an ability's, an entity's and an item's components each hear their own asset's moments, beside its workers. A component is its asset's, shared by every entity the asset reaches, so what it keeps for one of them it keeps through its context's state, never on itself. AbstractGameplayMonoProcess A mono process that takes part in gameplay, as a projectile an ability spawns. It knows its origin, the ability or entity that spawned it, and it carries attributes of its own: a projectile's speed is the projectile's, set on its prefab, by the level of what spawned it, or from the caster, and its code can change it as it flies. A role, as ProjectileSpeed, names the attribute a process reads for a purpose. AbstractGasTargetingAbilityTask The base of a targeting task that picks entities, as Select GAS Target and the Auto Target tasks do: its Requirements, tag queries a target must pass and tag queries it must not, decide which entities it takes, through TargetIsValid. AbstractImpactWorker Base class for impact workers that react to attribute impacts. Impact workers run on the source system after an impact is calculated. Can be either Inline (for simple transformations) or Deferred (for system modifications). AbstractItemComponent A component of an item: it hears the item given, equipped, unequipped and removed. AbstractMonoProcess The base of every MonoBehaviour process: a component, on a prefab or a scene object, that ProcessControl registers, steps and ends, as a GAS hub or a projectile. Its lifecycle, step timing and step priority are fields of its inspector, Synchronous in Update and LateUpdate at the first priority by default, and as it initializes it takes the parent, position and rotation its packet gives. ProcessControl registers those already in a scene as it starts. Derive from it, or from LazyMonoProcess for a run that lasts until it's paused or ended, and override RunProcess, the run ProcessControl awaits, and the hooks you need: WhenInitialize; WhenUpdate, WhenLateUpdate and WhenFixedUpdate at its timing; WhenWait, WhenTerminate and WhenDestroy; and TryHandlePause and TryHandleResume to keep a run through a pause. An override of WhenInitialize or WhenTerminate calls the base's, and WhenDestroy stands in for OnDestroy, which a class of its own would hide. Its object comes from its registration's instantiator, its handler's or its own Instantiator, or is cloned from its prefab, and is given back or destroyed as the process ends. Processes on its child objects pause and end with it, as ProcessControl cascades by default. AbstractMonoProcessInstantiator What makes a mono process's object and takes it back, as a pool hands out an idle object and keeps it again as its process ends. Derive from it and override PrepareNew, which makes or hands out an object of the prefab registered, PrepareExisting, which readies one already in a scene, and CleanProcess, which takes the object back as its process ends. A registration's InstantiatedBy, a process's own Instantiator or its handler's gives one; with none, the object is cloned and destroyed. AbstractProcessWrapper How ProcessControl holds a registered process of either kind: its relay, its data packet and its handler, with the process's hooks and steps passed through to it and its lifecycle, timing and priority read from it. MonoWrapperProcess holds a mono process and RuntimeWrapperProcess a runtime one; a relay's Wrapper is it, and TryGetProcess finds the process inside. AbstractProxyTaskBehaviour AbstractPurgeFilter A purge's filter of a project's own: whether the purge takes an effect, beside its strength, kinds and relation. AbstractReader The base of a mono process that shows a GAS's state: Assign gives it the GAS and calls SubscribeIfOnChangePolicy, which a reader overrides to hear the changes it shows. AbstractRelativeAttributeWorker Attribute worker that operates relative to another attribute. Useful for workers that need to compare or compute based on multiple attributes. AbstractRespawnPlace Where a Respawn brings its entity back: its home, where it stood as it registered; where it died; a point; or a place of your own, as a checkpoint or its side's base, a [Serializable] class made from this one, which is offered beside them. Each says where from its entity as it dies, its killer among what it knows, and its home. AbstractRuntimeProcess The base of every runtime process: a plain C# class, with no GameObject, that ProcessControl registers, steps and ends, as a runtime GAS, a task sequence's process or a group's member. Its name, step priority, step timing and lifecycle go to its base constructor; the one with none gives its type's name, the first priority, no step timing and SelfTerminating. Only a runtime process joins a group. Derive from it, or from LazyRuntimeProcess for a run that lasts until it's paused or ended, and override RunProcess, the run ProcessControl awaits, and the hooks you need: WhenInitialize; WhenUpdate, WhenLateUpdate and WhenFixedUpdate at its timing; WhenWait and WhenTerminate; and TryHandlePause and TryHandleResume to keep a run through a pause. An override of WhenInitialize or WhenTerminate calls the base's: the process is IsInitialized from registration until it ends, so it can be registered again once ended, and what it handles ends with it. AbstractScaler Base class for all magnitude scalers. Scalers determine how a value changes based on level (relative level = (level-1)/(maxLevel-1)). Level Configuration Modes: LockToSource: Automatically uses the owning Ability/Entity's level range. No extra setup needed. The source is determined at runtime from the IAttributeImpactDerivation spec. Unlocked: Uses its own MaxLevel setting, independent of the source. Partitioned: Uses the minimum of MaxLevel and the source's current level. AbstractScalerBehaviour A rule in a scaler's Behaviours, which adjusts the value the scaler works out, in the list's order: at each read, a behaviour is handed the carrier the value is read for (Initialize), then the value so far, and gives back the value after it (Evaluate). Derive from it and override both. AbstractSetAssetsTask The base of an asset loader, a Set task: it puts assets in the activation's data under a key as it's prepared, for the tasks after it to read, as a Run Sequence's sequence reads them with data.GetLoadedAssets<T>(tag); its own run ends at once. An ability's Asset Loaders run once an activation, after its targeting and before its first stage, and one among a stage's tasks loads as the stage starts. A loader of your own overrides Prepare and IsCriticalSection. AbstractStackingConfig The base of an effect's Stack Behaviours, the rules its stacking containers follow: Stack Bounds, Scaled Stack Amount and Starting Stacks. A behaviour of your own derives from it and overrides InitializeContainer, to set a new container up, and GetStacks, to settle how many stacks an application adds from the amount the behaviours before it settled on; GetCorrectContainer picks the container an application stacks into, the first by default. AbstractStackingEffectContainer The base of the containers that count stacks, the kind an effect lives in when its Re-application isn't Add Another, as its Stacking says: its Stacks, and Stack, which adds to them, each kind keeping its clock its own way. An Effect Stacks number reads its count, and Tick On Application executes once for each stack, unless a kind says otherwise. AbstractStopStage A stage that can stop a hit: it rolls its chance once as the effect lands, before anything of it does, and on a roll that comes up nothing of the effect lands, its damage, tags, contained effects and on-hits, and each side hears it. A lasting effect's ticks aren't rolled again. As the hit commits it passes the value on. AbstractTagRequirements Base class for tag requirement groups. Provides common functionality for requirement validation and property access. AbstractTagValidationRule A rule that reads a tag, as Tag Weight does: its weight on the entity it checks, the caster among the Caster Checks and the target among the Target Checks, or, where that entity holds none of it, the ability's Local Data under it. AbstractTagWorker Base class for tag-based workers that activate/deactivate based on tag state. Tag workers run as long as their tag requirements are met. Lifecycle: Activate() called once when requirements become met Tick() called periodically while active (based on TickPause) Resolve() called once when requirements are no longer met Common use cases: Show fire particles when Fire tag weight >= 3 Play warning sound when LowHealth tag is present Grant temporary ability while Empowered tag is active AbstractTargetedMonoProcess The base class for following/tracking projectiles. AbstractTargetingAbilityTask The base of an ability's targeting task, the one task that picks what an activation acts on before its stages run, as a click picks an entity or a search takes the enemies in range. Its Activate files the targeting packet of what it picks under the activation's Target key, whose entity becomes the activation's target, or calls WhenTargetingInvalid, which ends the activation where BreakRuntimeOnInvalid is on. Targeting holds the activation's claim while it runs, and its slot's IsTargeting says while it chooses. A task of your own overrides Activate; Prompt, the words a game shows while it waits for the player; TargetIsValid, which targets it takes; and ConnectInputHandler and DisconnectInputHandler, to hook an input handler of its own as it's prepared and unhook it as it's cleaned, an override of Prepare calling the base's last. TryGetDataTarget and TryGetDataPoint take a target or a point the activation's data already holds, as an AI's does, and WaitForPointerPress waits for a press of the game's input. AbstractTargetingPacket Where something is, for targeting: its position, rotation and scale, the entity it is (target) and its transform where it has them, and the direction it was aimed along, as Select Direction sets. Each entity gives one (ITarget.GetTargetingPacket), and a targeting task files the packet of what it picks under the activation's Target key, each packet's entity becoming one of the activation's targets. TargetingPacket follows a transform, and StaticTargetingPacket holds its own values. AbstractValueStage One stage of a ValuePipeline: it takes the value and gives what goes on. A project writes its own by deriving from it; each built-in one reads its numbers in the hit's context, as any number field is read. AbstractVariance How a Randomized scaler varies its value with its roll, from 0 to 1: by a share of it, by an amount, between two multipliers, or a way of your own, as dice or a bell curve, a [Serializable] class made from this one, which is offered beside them. Its numbers are read for the carrier with the variance as their owner. AbstractWaitTask A wait's own: what it waits on, its timeout and what it records where what it waits for comes. A wait holds its stage until what it waits for comes or its timeout runs out, in its caster's time, and with no timeout as long as its stage runs. ActionPriority Standard priority levels for IRootActions. Higher values execute first. ActionProcess A runtime process that calls an action in each of its Update steps, until it's ended. Made with the action alone, it's named Action, SelfTerminating, and stepped in Update at the first priority; the longer constructor gives its name, priority, timing and lifecycle. ActionProcess<T> An ActionProcess whose action is handed the same object, its source, each time it's called. ActionQueue An entity's queue of deferred actions, which its end of frame runs. Actions run by priority, higher first, and in the order queued within a priority; one queued as the queue runs takes its place by its priority in the same pass. Each is heard as it's queued, then once more as it's done with: run, dropped unrun, or failed. AddContainedEffectChange Adds a contained effect to it, landing on its target as it lands, each tick, or as it ends. AddOverflowChange Adds an overflow effect to it, landing as an application would take it past its most stacks; it needs a stack bound of the effect's own to overflow. Clear Stacks takes its stacks off as it overflows, as its bound can. AddStage A number added to the value's size, read for the hit: a flat bonus of 10 makes a blow of −100 a blow of −110 and a heal of 50 one of 60, as the value's sign has it. AffiliationValidation Affiliation: the target stands to its caster as it says, by the sides they hold, as an area's or an aura's filter takes them: an enemy shares none of the caster's sides, an ally shares one. A caster with no sides takes anyone as either. AllAtOnceRecharge No cooldown until the last charge is spent; its end brings every charge back at once. AllCondition Whether every one of its conditions holds; with none, it holds. A member that can't be worked out where it's read doesn't hold, so neither does this. AllProxyStagePolicy The stage ends as its last task does. AlwaysCondition A condition that always holds. AnalysisWorkerCache An entity's analysis workers: each analyzes the entity and its frame's summary at its end of frame, after its tag workers, and the actions it returns join the entity's action queue. A worker given by more than one source, as two copies of an item, runs once, and stays until the last of them takes it back. AnimationUtility Sets the tangent mode of a curve's key, on its left or its right, as UnityEditor.AnimationUtility does, from code that builds into a player: in the editor it calls Unity's, and in a player it does nothing, so the keys keep Unity's default tangents. A scaler shapes its curve with it. AnyCondition Whether any one of its conditions holds; with none, it doesn't. A member that can't be worked out where it's read doesn't hold, and the others still can. AnyProxyStagePolicy The stage ends as its first task does. ApplyEffectAction Deferred action to apply an effect. ApplyEffectsAbilityTask A stage task that applies its Effects to each of the activation's targets, from the ability at its level and with the magnitudes the caller set on the activation's data, in the project's resolve order unless UseResolveOrder is off. DelayBetweenApplicationMs waits between one effect and the next, and RecordLandedAs tags the activation's data as an effect lands, for a later stage's Condition. ApplyRemoveEffectsAbilityTask A stage task that puts its Effects on each of the activation's targets as its stage starts, with the caller's magnitudes, in the project's resolve order unless UseResolveOrder is off, and takes those effects off the targets as the stage ends, whoever applied them. Its own run ends at once, so it holds its stage no longer than the stage's other tasks do. ApplyToCasterTask Applies effects to its caster, whatever the ability targets, as the empowerment Shadow Step leaves its caster or the untargetable moment of Tumble's roll. An Apply Effects task applies to the ability's targets alone. AreaEffectComponent Area: as its effect lands on its target, it lands on each the area takes near that target too, as Storm Hammer stuns everyone near the one it hits. Without one, an effect lands on its target alone. An effect holds one at most. AreaEffectTask Applies effects to each entity within a radius of its caster, its activation's target or its point, of the sides it takes, as Volley's arrows, Rallying Cry's armor or Thunderclap's stun. Each is found by its position on either hub, or with physics on its layers, and takes the effects from the activation's origin with its caller's magnitudes, the dead left out. AssetLoaderInfo An asset-loader task and the effects it loads into the data packet. AssetPartKind A part of an effect, an ability or an item on the caster or the target, found by a tag: a Poison effect's stacks, how many Fire effects are on the target, what every Burn there has dealt, the time left on a shield, an ability's level or whether it's cooling down, how many potions are in a stack, whether a ring is equipped. An effect matches by its asset tag, a context tag or a tag it grants; an ability or an item by its asset tag or a context tag; a tag under the one given matches too. Where several match, Among says how they read as one: added up, the first, the highest or the lowest. A count reads 0 where none matches; any other part reads Default. A true-or-false part reads 1 or 0, so added up it's how many are so. An effect's Worker Value asks that effect's workers for a key (INumberWorker), about that application of it, and counts only the effects whose workers answer. AttenuateScalerBehaviour A scaler behaviour that turns the value into a factor, as its Policy says: as it is, one plus it, or one minus it, so a 30% bonus reads 1.3 and a 30% reduction 0.7. Attribute An Attribute asset: one number an entity can have, as Health, Mana or Strength. It holds no value: an entity takes its starting Current and Base from its attribute set, and effects change them from there. Sets, effects, workers and conditions name the asset itself, and some lookups compare attributes by name, so give each its own. Its Role says what it is, how bonuses to it add up and how a number reads it: a Value, a Bonus Share, a Multiplier, a Resistance, or a Barrier, which takes each workable loss to the attribute it absorbs for first and can decay. Gains Scaled By names an attribute that multiplies each workable gain to its Current, as Health's by Healing Received. AttributeBackedScaler Scales based on an attribute value from source or target. The attribute value is used as input to the scaling curve. AttributeBlueprint Describes the basest definition of an attribute's value on an entity — analogous to "base stats" before items, effects, or other transient sources contribute. Each AttributeSetElement exposes Current and Base configs; this blueprint resolves both sides independently and assembles the resulting AttributeValue. Per-side resolution rules (applied identically for Current and Base): If the side's scaler is null OR its RealMagnitude is UseMagnitude → return Magnitude. Otherwise call the cached scaler (Initial vs Active path) and project the side's slot from the returned AttributeValue (Current → CurrentValue, Base → BaseValue), then combine with the side's Magnitude via its RealMagnitude operation. AttributeChangeEffectWorker Answers how far an attribute has moved since its effect began, for a number of the Worker kind to read: how much health the target has lost since the curse landed, from every source. It notes the attribute as each application of its effect begins, and answers under its Key: the amount lost, gained or changed, or the attribute as it was. With EveryTicks above 0, it answers only on each Nth tick of its effect, and 0 on the others, so an impact that reads it lands every Nth tick: a curse dealing 5 a second, and every fourth second a quarter of what its target has lost since it began, is one periodic effect with a second impact of −0.25 × this worker's answer. Its tick is counted before the tick's impacts are worked out, so on its Nth tick the amount lost is the amount before that tick lands. AttributeChangeEffectWorker.State What it keeps for one application of its effect. AttributeChangeMomentHandler Handles attribute change events (pre-change and post-change). Routes workers to appropriate execution mode (Inline vs Deferred). AttributeCondition Whether an attribute of the caster or the target compares with a number: "Target's Health < 0.3 × Target's Health (base)". The number is any kind, read with the condition as its owner. An entity without the attribute doesn't hold. AttributeConstraints How an attribute set element holds its attribute's values: Auto Clamp applies its bounds, Auto Scale With Base changes Current by the same share as Base whenever Base changes, and Rounding, with its Snap Interval for Snap To, rounds both values after the bounds each time they change. AttributeCost What an ability spends of an attribute as it's used: the attribute it names, or the one playing the role it names in the project, and how much, a number that can scale by level. It's paid beside the ability's Cost effect. AttributeImpactEntry One authored impact: WHAT attribute, HOW (operation/slot/magnitude), WHEN (Delivery), and WHO it belongs to (retention group, for the per-group attribution surface). A GameplayEffectImpact holds a list of these — one effect can carry e.g. a Continuous "+10% speed" AND a Periodic "5 HP per tick" without contained-effect workarounds. AttributeMagnitudeSpec A magnitude + cached-scaler + real-magnitude triplet used for ONE side of an attribute's root value (either Current or Base). Held by AttributeSetElement twice — once per side. The scaler returns an AttributeValue; the blueprint projects to the slot this spec represents (Current → CurrentValue, Base → BaseValue). AttributeParts The part of an attribute's value a number reads: its current, its base, what's missing of it (base − current), or its share (current ÷ base). × Attribute, the cached attribute scaler and the Attribute condition read through it. AttributeReader A reader that shows one of a GAS's attributes in UI: its current and base values in CurrentText and BaseText, and its current value's share of its base on ValueSlider. AssignAttribute names the attribute and Assign the GAS; it shows them each Update step, and as the attribute changes. AttributeRegistry Every attribute the game's entities use, by name, for code that finds one by its name, with GetByName or TryGetByName. Names match in capitals with underscores for spaces, so Attack Speed and ATTACK_SPEED find the same attribute, and the first attribute registered under a name stands. An entity's attribute system registers each attribute it's given, as a Bootstrapper does the sets it names; the registry is cleared as play starts, and by Reset. AttributeRegulationCache Tracks attribute dependencies for cache invalidation. When an attribute changes, this tells us which other attributes need recalculation. AttributeRole An attribute's part in a project: a role, by its tag, and the attribute that plays it. PlayForge's features read the roles it ships, as death at 0 reads ROLE_HEALTH; a game's code reads its own. AttributeSave An attribute's permanent commits: each retention group's total, in the order the groups first committed. AttributeSet An Attribute Set asset: the attributes an entity starts with, and how each starts, its Current and Base, its bounds and its rounding, with those of its sub-sets. An entity names one, and as its GAS initializes each element becomes its attribute's root value, the value before any effect, which a cached scaler can tie to the entity's level or to another attribute. Where an attribute appears in more than one element, the elements' Collision and the Resolution Policy of the set the entity names decide its root. The entity carries the set's tag and its sub-sets', and holds their worker groups' workers as it lives. The set's level range is its own, or a level provider's while it's linked, and its cached scalers can size their values per level by it. AttributeSetElement One element of an attribute set: an attribute and how it starts, its Current and its Base, each a number or a cached scaler, Current able to follow Base; its bounds; its constraints, which clamp, scale and round it; the retention group its root counts toward; and its Collision, for an attribute that appears more than once across the set and its sub-sets. As the entity's GAS initializes, it becomes the attribute's root value, the value before any effect. AttributeSetMeta The attributes an attribute set gives an entity, worked out as the entity's attribute system takes the set: each element of the set and its sub-sets, by attribute and by its Collision. InitializeAttributeSystem then gives the attribute system each attribute, with the root the set's collision settings pick. AttributeSystemCallbacks Callbacks for attribute system events. Used for monitoring attribute changes without modifying behavior. AttributeSystemComponent Component for managing attributes and their modifications. It supports WorkerContext and deferred execution. AttributeTransfer One impact that moves an amount from one attribute to another, each side its own: the target's Agility to the caster's, as Essence Shift steals it, or one entity's Agility to its Strength, as Attribute Shift moves it. Only what the giver has moves, so nothing is made from nothing. As its Delivery says, it moves once as the effect lands, each tick, or for as long as the effect lasts, a modifier on both that gives back as it ends. AttributeValidation A check that compares the checked entity's current value of its Attribute with Value, read at the ability's level, by Comparison; with ShareOfBase, its share of its base, from 0 to 1, as "below half its health". An entity without the attribute fails it. Either list offers it. AuraAbilityComponent An aura an ability holds while its holder knows it, on those near its holder. AuraEffectComponent An aura an effect holds while it lasts, on those near the one it's on. AuraEntityComponent An aura an entity holds while it lives, on those near it. AuraEntry An aura: an effect that holds on each it takes near its holder, and comes off as they leave, as Mekansm's or a captain's command aura does. An item's holds while it's equipped, an ability's while it's known, an effect's while it lasts on the one it's on, an entity's as it lives. It checks who's near every so often. AuraItemComponent An aura an item holds while it's equipped, on those near its holder. AuraSet An entity's running auras: each checks who's near at its interval, by its holder's time, holds its effect on each it takes, from an origin of its own, and takes it off as they leave, die or end, as its holder dies, or as the aura goes. Two of one aura, as two of an item, are two runs, each holding its own. It's a service of its entity, gas.GetService<AuraSet>(), which the entity steps by its own time and ends as the entity ends. AutoTargetByAffinityTask Auto-targeting task that filters by affiliation (ally, enemy, neutral). Uses OverlapSphere to gather ITarget candidates, then filters by matching or opposing affiliation tags relative to the caster. Common use cases: Heal nearest ally AoE damage to enemies only Buff all allies in range AutoTargetFromDataTask Auto-targeting task that reads an ITarget from the data packet using a configurable tag key. Useful when a previous system (event, trigger, or another ability) has already determined the target and stored it in the data packet. If no target is found under the specified key, falls back to targeting invalid behavior. AutoTargetSelfTask Auto-targeting task that explicitly targets the caster (self). Useful when UseImplicitTargeting is disabled but you still need self as a target, or when you want to explicitly validate the self-target against tag requirements. AutoTargetTask Auto-targeting task that finds targets automatically based on spatial queries, tag requirements, and optional attribute conditions. Uses Physics.OverlapSphere to find candidate colliders, then filters for ITarget components that pass tag and attribute validation. AvoidRequireTagGroup Represents a group of tag requirements with Avoid (must NOT have) and Require (must HAVE) conditions. Supports hierarchical tag matching via TagQuery.MatchMode on individual queries. AvoidRequireTagGroupColor Marks an AvoidRequireTagGroup field with a color, given as red, green, blue and alpha from 0 to 1, as the tag requirements of abilities and effects mark their groups. The package's own drawers don't read it. BaseForgeAsset The base of every PlayForge asset, a ScriptableObject: attributes directly, and abilities, effects, items, attribute sets and entities through BaseForgeLevelProvider. It holds the asset's Local Data rows, read by key with TryGetLocalData, and its template, an asset of the same type whose fields it takes when the template is pushed, apart from those it overrides (SetTemplate, IsFieldOverridden). A type made from it gives its name, description, default icon and the tags it grants. BaseForgeLevelProvider The base of the PlayForge assets with a level range: abilities, effects, items, attribute sets and entities. It gives the asset's starting and max level, its name as a provider and its asset tag, and its link to another provider whose range it takes, as an effect linked to its ability (LinkToProvider, LinkedProvider); HasCircularDependency says whether a link would come back round to it. BasicEffectOrigin The base of the effect origins an entity holds, an ability's spec and an item's: an origin with a source, the entity it belongs to, whose level system it registers its level with, under its asset tag, as it's made. A class made from it implements the rest of IEffectOrigin. BlinkTask Puts its caster at its ability's target at once, as a blink: at the point, no farther than its reach, or behind the entity targeted, as Shadow Step does. Its reach and how far behind are read as it starts, at its ability's level; its caster's own mover, where it has one, is stopped after. BlockStage A block: on its chance, nothing of the effect lands, as Tougher Times blocks a hit outright. Bootstrapper Brings PlayForge up as a scene starts: ProcessControl, then the GameRoot, which runs as the Game Root entity of the Forge Project the Bootstrapper names. It names prefabs for both, which code makes in the PlayForge folder's Bootstrap folder as the first Forge Project is made; without them it makes each itself, so a scene needs nothing but a Bootstrapper. PlayForge ships no prefab. BountyEntityComponent Bounty: an effect an entity's killer takes as it dies, from it, so the effect reads its level, as gold or experience; and the killer's allies near it too, where it shares, as an assist. A death no one dealt gives none. An entity holds as many as it gives, each its own. BranchBuilder Builds a branch, a stage that picks one stage as it starts: the first whose If condition holds of the run's data packet, else its Default, else none. It's handed to the action given to a builder's or a stage's Branch. A synced runner can't run one. BranchCase A condition-stage pair for branching. BranchStage A stage that branches based on conditions. BreakStageRepeatInjection Breaks out of a stage's repeat loop (for WithRepeat or RepeatUntilSkippedPolicy). Does not skip the stage - just stops repeating and continues normally. CachedAttributeBackedScaler Cached scaler that combines a captured attribute value with a level-based scaling curve.
