The curve is evaluated at the owner's relative level, then folded with the captured attribute value via RelativeOperation. Returned as a symmetric AttributeValue (same float on Current and Base) — the blueprint projects the slot it needs. CachedAttributeScaler Cached scaler that mirrors a captured attribute's value. Registers a regulation relation so the owning attribute is recomputed whenever the captured attribute changes. Initial value reads from the captured attribute's RootValue (its base definition); active value reads from its current ActiveValue. CachedAttributeValue Per-attribute runtime state under the two-kind impact model: Modifiers (transient, derived) — registered via RegisterModifier(IAttributeImpactCarrier, IReadOnlyList<IAttributeImpacter>, IReadOnlyDictionary<IAttribute, CachedAttributeValue>) while their carrier lives, re-evaluated on every Recompute(IReadOnlyDictionary<IAttribute, CachedAttributeValue>), reversed exactly by UnregisterModifier(IAttributeImpactCarrier, IReadOnlyDictionary<IAttribute, CachedAttributeValue>). Commits (permanent) — applied via CommitImpact(IAttributeImpactCarrier, IReadOnlyList<IAttributeImpacter>, IReadOnlyDictionary<IAttribute, CachedAttributeValue>); the post-bounds delta is recorded per retention group in FarEmerald.PlayForge.CachedAttributeValue.committedByGroup and NEVER reversed. The formula (EFFECT_PIPELINE.md §2.1): ActiveValue = ConstrainValue( Override( FlatBonus( Multiply( Add( root ) ) ) + Σ committedByGroup ) ). Committed history lands where it was measured, after the % modifiers, so they don't scale it: 50 base × 1.5 aura + 10 tome = 85, and a 30 hit under the aura takes 30. Reproducibility invariant: ActiveValue is always exactly what Recompute(IReadOnlyDictionary<IAttribute, CachedAttributeValue>) produces from current state — every mutation path ends in a recompute. There is no second bookkeeping system to drift. CachedScalerGroup Combines multiple cached scalers using the active AttributeValue interface. Members are evaluated component-wise (Current and Base independently) and combined per the member's ECalculationOperation. Override members short-circuit other operations and resolve via OverrideMemberCollisionPolicy. Regulation propagates to all members so any captured-attribute change triggers a refresh. With no members, or none that holds a kind, it is no kind at all, so its element's side reads its number, as the Group does. Its Ignore policy threw; it sets overriding members aside. CachedSimpleScaler Simple cached scaler based on the owning system's relative level. Has no attribute dependencies, so RegulateContactWith is a no-op (inherited from base). Returns the same scalar on both Current and Base sides — the blueprint will project whichever slot it needs. CameraShakeCue Shakes the camera as its moment comes, in whichever list it's in, through the shaker the game gives Shaker. CancelAbilitiesTask Cancels its caster's running abilities by tag, as a dodge cancels a cast: each running ability tagged with one of its tags, or a child of one, by its asset tag or a context tag, is interrupted, but a run in a critical stage, which is committed, and never the ability it runs in. CantFallBelowAttributeWorker Can't fall below a value: a loss that would take its attribute below its Floor takes it to the floor, and no further, as Shallow Grave keeps its target at 1 Health while it lasts, in a buff's worker group. CastRangeAbilityComponent Cast Range: how far from its caster an ability's target may be, the one range it has, read at its level: the ability's reach, an IAbilityReach. An activation handed a target or a point beyond it is refused as Range, and targeting that picks one beyond it ends the activation there, told as Range too; a targeting task with a range of its own searches within it, from the caster; and the lab's bots cast it only once their foe is within it, each asking the ability's reach through ForgeReach. 0 reaches anywhere. An ability holds one at most. Its ability's Target Checks show its Check Range while it holds the component, which this enforces. CasterClockChoice An ability's caster's own time: its time scale times the game's; the game's for anything else. ChainInterruptInjection Marker injection for chain-level interrupts. ChanceChange Changes its chance to apply: multiplied, then added to. ChanceCondition Holds on a roll of its chance: a number, so it can be an attribute, as a critical strike chance, or an item's stacks through a curve. Read in a hit, it rolls once for the hit and keeps the roll, so a hit read twice, its preview and its commit, reads the same; read with no hit, it rolls each time. Pseudo-random and luck as its roll says. ChanceRoll How a chance rolls: pseudo-random, so each miss raises the next roll's odds and a hit starts them again, each caster keeping its own streak for the chance; and its luck, the attribute playing the project's Luck role, read on the caster, unless the chance gives its own. ChanceStage On a chance, the value times a number: a critical hit. It rolls once for the hit, as it lands, and its step in the breakdown says so. ChangeImpactChange Changes the numbers of its impacts on an attribute, of some impact types where it names any, by a Value Pipeline stage: one that commits, after the effect's own pipeline, kept in the hit's breakdown; a lasting one, on its magnitude. ChangeValue A change on its way through the attribute pipeline, which workers and listeners may adjust. The attribute system reuses it once the commit it belongs to is done, so read it during the call you're handed it in, or copy its Value. A deferred worker's actions may keep it: a change handed to one is left to them. ChannelAbilityTask Channels: holds its stage for its duration, in its caster's time, read as it starts at its ability's level, a critical section, as a cast bar fills. It kept a cast bar's calls commented out, which nothing drew. ChargesAbilityComponent Charges: how many uses an ability holds, each spending a charge that comes back as its Recharge says: its ability's cooldown model, an ICooldownModel, which the Cooldown check asks and the ability spends through. Without one, an ability has one charge, its single cooldown. An ability holds one at most. CheckRangeValidation Check Range: the Cast Range component's check, its target within the component's range of its caster, among the ability's Target Checks while the ability holds the component. The component enforces it, refusing a target or a point handed beyond it and ending targeting that picks one, so this passes: it's the range's place among the checks, and comes and goes with the component. It read its range from a tag's weight or the ability's Local Data before the component held it. ClampStage The value's size kept between two numbers read for the hit, its sign as it was. ClampedScaler A number kept between a floor and a ceiling: damage worked out from a target's missing health, capped. What it clamps and both bounds are numbers of any kind, read with the scaler as their owner, so its ceiling can be twice its floor, and its floor can scale by level. CombatLog An entity's combat log: the entries the project subscribes to, its last as many as the project keeps, oldest first; a test reads it as the game does, and the Debugger shows it. CombatLogSettings A project's combat log: what each entity's writes, which the project subscribes to, and how many entries each keeps, its last. CommitSave One retention group's committed total on an attribute. CompareCondition Whether one number compares with another: "Caster's Health > 2 × Target's Health". Each is any kind, read with the condition as its owner. ComponentStates What a holder's components keep for it: an object for each component, made the first time it's asked for. CompositeTargetingTask Runs multiple targeting tasks in sequence, accumulating all their results into the same data packet. Each sub-task runs to completion before the next begins. Common use cases: Select a target entity, then select a position (teleport target to location) Select multiple distinct targets across phases Auto-target self + select an enemy (buff self, then apply debuff) If any sub-task fails and StopOnFailure is true, the entire composite fails. ConditionValidation A rule that holds while its condition does, as an effect's requirements and an On Hit read theirs: a tag, an attribute, a level, a comparison of numbers, or any condition of your own. It's read against the activation, its caster and its ability's level and Local Data, with the entity its list hands it as the target: the target among the Target Checks, and the caster itself among the Caster Checks. With no condition, it holds. ConditionalScaler One number where a condition holds, and another where it doesn't: "−0.1 × Target's Health (base) if Target's Health < 0.3 × Target's Health (base), else 0". The condition is a class read against the number's context, so a project adds its own (GameplayCondition), and each branch is a number of any kind, read with the scaler as its owner. With no condition, it reads its False branch. ConstantImpacter A precomputed-magnitude impacter. Used for synthetic deltas where there's no scaler pipeline to evaluate — e.g. auto-scale propagation, tracked-impact reversal on container removal, or external systems that just want to push a number into the attribute aggregator while still being a first-class carrier. Construct one impacter per (operation, slot) pair you want to contribute. To express a (current=+10, base=+5) Add delta as a single carrier, hand that carrier two ConstantImpacters — one per slot. ConstantScaler Returns a constant value regardless of level. Useful for fixed bonuses or base values. ConsumeItemTask Uses up items its caster holds, as a potion's use does: the Healing Salve's ability ends with it, after its heal, and the last one used, the item and its ability go. Its item system's Item Consumed hears it, so a game's own bookkeeping, as a shop's stock, follows. ContainedSeries An effect another contains, read level by level, with when it lands. CooldownValidation A Caster Check that passes while the ability has a use in hand, as its cooldown model says: with the single cooldown, while its caster doesn't carry its Cooldown's asset tag; with Charges, while one is in hand. A component that waives the cooldown passes it. Its refusal is told as Cooldown. CostValidation A Caster Check that passes while the caster can pay the ability's cost: what its Cost effect spends would leave each attribute at 0 or more, and its Attribute Costs can be paid, the caster holding each attribute. A component that waives the cost, as a Toggle turning off does, passes it. Its refusal is told as Cost. CreateMonoProcessAbilityTask Spawns mono processes, as a projectile, as the ability runs. What it spawns takes the ability as its origin, so the effects it applies are the caster's at the ability's level, and its attributes can start as the caster's. It spawns the processes the activation's data holds under DataTag, or, where the data holds none or InternalIsOverride is on, its own. CrowdControlRule One crowd control rule: while its holder carries a tag, it can't use what the rule stops. CrowdControlRules Crowd control: the rules an entity's abilities follow, each a tag and what it stops, so no ability has to list Stunned among the tags it avoids. While its holder carries a rule's tag, an ability the rule stops is refused, and one running is interrupted, as a stun breaks a channel; an ability can ignore a rule by its tag. An entity names its rules, or takes the project's. CueLibrary A project's cue library: what each cue tag plays. A Cue Tag cue, listed on an effect or a Cues component, plays the library's route for its tag: the tag's own, or else its nearest parent's, and a route that doesn't override plays its parent's too, as Unreal's GameplayCueManager routes its GameplayCue tags. An entity's Cue Receiver plays a tag its own way first. The project names its library in its settings, or code gives one to Library. CuePackets The data a cue's process or sequence runs with, loaded for what raised it. An ability's cue starts from its activation's packet: its targets, its targeting data and the numbers its caller set. On it go the cue itself (CUE), its asset (ASSET) and its spec (SPEC), its source, the one it plays on as its target where the packet names none, where it plays, and its owner's clock; then the asset's Local Data, its numbers read for the cue, as at its level; then the cue's own Data list. Each step's keys take the place of an earlier step's, so the cue's own data has the last word. CuePlacement Where a cue places what it plays: on the one it's on, its source, an ability's target or each of its targets, or at the cue's point; at a socket of theirs, as a hand; moved by an offset in their space and scattered by a random amount; following them or not; and facing their way, the cue's normal, or from or toward its source. CuePoolInstantiator Makes a MonoBehaviour process's object from the cue pool, ForgeCuePool, and gives it back as the process ends, as a pooled Process cue's: an object of the process's prefab waiting there is handed out, else one is made, placed where the process's packet says. Give it to a registration with InstantiatedBy(AbstractMonoProcessInstantiator). CueReceiverEntityComponent Cue Receiver: plays cue tags its own way for its entity, as a golem's hits, before the project's cue library does, as Unreal's actors handle cues through their GameplayCue interface. Its own routes play first; where it plays nothing for a tag, or passes it through, the library's route plays, its Variant's where the library has one, as Cue.Hit.Golem for Cue.Hit. An entity holds one at most. CueRoute A cue tag's route: the handlers that play for it, and whether they play in place of its parent's. CuesAbilityComponent Cues: what an ability shows and sounds at its moments, on its caster: as an activation starts, as it pays its cost and starts its cooldown, while it's active, as it ends, and as one is refused. A stage's exact moment plays through a Play Cue task. An ability holds one at most. CuesEffectComponent Cues: what an effect shows and sounds at its moments, on the one it's on: as it lands, as an application it takes in lands, as each of its ticks executes, as an impact it deals lands, as it comes off, while it lasts, as an application of it is refused, and as its stacks change. An effect holds one at most. CuesEntityComponent Cues: what an entity shows and sounds at its moments: as it comes into the game, dies and comes back, and, While Tagged, for as long as it holds a tag, as stars over its head while it's Stunned. An entity holds one at most. CuesItemComponent Cues: what an item shows and sounds on its holder: as it's equipped, while it's equipped, and as it's used, as an ability it lends is. A load that puts an equipped item back begins its lasting cues and plays no burst. An item holds one at most. CustomScaler A scaler made of two delegates, one run as a carrier initializes it and one that works out its value, as IScaler.Generate makes. It isn't an AbstractScaler, so a number field can't hold it. DashTask Moves its caster toward its ability's target, or away from it, over a moment, as Tumble's roll. Its distance and duration are read as it starts, at its ability's level; it moves along the ground by its caster's time, a critical section, holding its caster's own mover, where it has one, while it moves. A caster with no object in the scene doesn't move. DataWrapper One entry of an asset's or an entity's Local Data: a value under a key. Its value is a class, a kind of its own: a number that can scale, a whole number, a string, a bool, a tag, an attribute, an effect, an ability, an entity, an object, a MonoBehaviour or a ScriptableObject; or a kind of your own, as a point or a colour, a [Serializable] class made from LocalDataValue<T> or LocalDataValue, which is offered beside them. Each entry saves its own value alone. DeathAction The deferred action that kills its entity as its turn comes, at Critical priority: the entity is marked dead, which its callbacks, its components, its effects and its killer hear, and it ends, or stays dead, at its frame's end, as its Death says. It's dropped where the entity is dead already; a death watcher and the Health role's watch queue it. DeathWatcherAnalysisWorker An analysis worker that kills its entity as an attribute reaches its threshold, as Health reaching 0: a Threshold whose firing queues the entity's death, after its effects and its event where it has them. An entity that holds one dies by it alone, not by its project's Health role reaching 0. DeferredContextSystem The base of the subsystems of an entity that queue work for its end of frame, its attribute, ability and item systems and its analysis worker cache: it holds the entity's action queue and frame summary, which the GAS hands it through SetDeferredContext as it initializes. DelayTask Waits: holds its stage for its delay, in its caster's time, read as it starts at its ability's level. DelegateSequenceInjection An injection that does what a function of your own says: applyFunc is handed the run's runtime and returns whether it applied, as one that adds to a count on a key press or jumps to a stage by name. With no function it applies nothing. DelegateSequenceTask Wraps a delegate as a sequence task. DelegateSyncTask Wraps a delegate as a sync-first sequence task implementing the unified ISequenceTask. Step is the primary execution path; Execute bridges by looping Step with per-frame yields. DeriveScalerName When placed on a Scaler field inside a ScalableFloat, the scaler drawer will look up the parent property's ScalerOperationKeyword attribute and use "{Keyword} Scaler" as the display name. DisjointAbilityTask A stage task that makes its caster disjoint, as in Dota: each homing shot aimed at it whose data marks it disjointable loses it, flies on to where the caster stood and lands on nothing. A skill shot, which aims at no one, isn't touched. DisjointProxyTaskBehaviour A disjoint, as in Dota: the shots already aimed at an entity lose it, fly on to where it stood, and land on nothing. A shot is found through the intent it registers with its target, which only a homing shot does (AbstractTargetedMonoProcess), and only one whose data marks it IS_DISJOINTABLE is disjointed. A skill shot, one that hits whatever it crosses, registers no intent, and lands as usual. DisjointTarget The placeholder a disjointed shot is aimed at instead of its entity. It stays where the entity stood, has no tags, and takes no effects, so the shot lands on nothing. DurationChange Changes how long it lasts: its time multiplied, then more added. Its ticks spread over the time it has. EachChargeRecharge Each spent charge comes back on a cooldown of its own, run alongside the others: the default. EffectArea An effect's area: as the effect lands on its target, it lands on each the area takes near that target too, as Storm Hammer stuns everyone near the one it hits. Each is found by its position, on either hub, with no collider needed; an effect that lands by an area spreads no further. EffectChanges What modifiers changed of one application: the effect's own reads take these in, its contained effects, its impacts' numbers, its overflow, its time, its stacks, its chance and its granted tags. Null on a spec no modifier changed, so an effect nothing modifies costs nothing more. EffectConditions An effect's conditions, beside the tags of each phase of its requirements: those that must hold for it to land, those that keep it going, and those that take it off, as Attribute Shift stops at its floor. A phase passes only when its tags pass and its conditions all hold; the Ongoing and Removal ones are checked at each frame's end while it lasts, as no tag needs to change for an attribute a condition reads to. EffectJournal An effect journal: each application, refusal (by requirement, immunity or chance), tick, impact and removal of an effect on the entities it listens to, with its number's trace as it lands, and each worker that ran for it, by its hook and its side, with the actions it queued and whether they ran. It keeps its last Keep entries, oldest first. It records only while it listens, and an entity no journal listens to pays nothing: the Creator Lab's bottom panel and the Debugger's Timeline read one. EffectJournalAction An action a worker queued, as a journal keeps it: what it said it was, and whether it ran. EffectJournalEntry One entry of an effect journal: when, of what kind, on whom, the effect and who applied it, and what the kind says: why it was refused, how many ticks, the change it made, or which worker ran, at which of its effect's moments, on whose side, with the actions it queued. EffectLevelSeries One effect evaluated across a level range: duration, ticks, and impacts. EffectModifier A modifier shared between assets: a rule that an item's, an ability's, an effect's or an entity's modifier entry names in place of its own, as a Value Pipeline is shared. Its class has a file of its own name, which an asset needs to find its script: in EffectModifiers.cs, an Effect Modifier saved as an asset came back with no script, and a search by its type found none. EffectModifierEntry A modifier an item, an ability, an effect or an entity holds: its own rule, or a shared Effect Modifier's, which it names in place of its own. EffectModifierRule What a modifier changes, and of which effects: the effects it picks, by tag, its direction and a condition, and its changes to each effect as it's made, which last as long as that application does. EffectModifierSet The modifiers an entity holds now: its own, its items' while they're equipped, its abilities' while it knows them, and its effects' while they last. Each holds as often as it's given, as two of an item modify twice. EffectModifiers Gives a holder the modifiers it has, takes them back, and applies them to each effect as it's made. EffectPurge A purge: its strength, a tier of the project's purge levels, taking the effects at that tier or under it; only those of the kinds it names, by their tags, as Status.Debuff; only those applied by whom it says, against the one purged; and only those its filters take. EffectSave An effect on the entity's shelf, with what applied it and its clock: its stacks, its duration and period, and each stack's time left and to its next tick. A clock has one of each, unless its stacks have their own durations. EffectScopedAction Base class for actions scoped to an effect's lifecycle. Automatically invalidates if the effect is removed. EffectStacksScaler The stack count of the effect's own container: 1 for an effect that doesn't stack. With Multiply With Scaler, a stacking effect's change grows by the stack, as a sunder of −5 armor a stack does, and a Continuous change reads the count again as it changes. Only a scaler written for it read an effect's stack count. EffectSystemComponent The effect shelf — apply / tick / re-apply / remove for gameplay effects, shared by BOTH RuntimeGameplayAbilitySystem and the MonoBehaviour GameplayAbilitySystem (the twin-drift class of bugs ends here; the GAS classes keep only thin delegating wrappers). Lifecycle under the two-kind impact model: Apply (durational): shelve container → RegisterModifier per Continuous entry → app workers → commit OnApply entries; TickOnApplication? then Periodic ones once Tick: commit Periodic entries per execute tick Remove: container.OnRemove() → UnregisterModifier per Continuous entry. Commits are permanent — there is no rollback path. Instant: commit OnApply entries — no shelf, no removal phase. EffectTagRequirements Tag requirements for effect application, ongoing, and removal phases. Each phase can have its own set of required and avoided tags. EffectWorkerGroup Several effect workers as one: at each of its effect's moments its workers hear, as it lands, ticks, comes off and hits, it runs each of its workers in turn and returns their actions together. EntityClock An entity's own time: the game's, as ForgeTime reads it, scaled by the entity's TimeScale: the scale code sets, as a hit-stop's, times the one its Time Scale attribute gives, as a slow's or a haste's, so the two compose. The entity's effects tick by it, its cooldowns among them, and so do its abilities' sequences and waits. Every entity ran on Unity's one clock, so nothing could slow one entity and not the rest. A scale of 0 holds the entity's time still; it isn't a pause, which ProcessControl's is, and processes keep their own bookkeeping on the game's clock. It's a clock as any other is, so a sequence that isn't an ability's runs on an entity's time with its packet's Clock set to it. EntityDeath What an entity does as it dies and as it revives: a MOBA hero, or anyone who dies and comes back, keeps its entity while its body goes. Where it stays: the effects its death ends, by tag, as buffs; the effects it takes as it dies, as a respawn timer; the effects it takes as it revives, as its health back; and its body, a MonoBehaviour process it spawns where it is, as it starts and as it revives, and ends as it dies. A runtime entity takes its position from its body. EntityIdentity An Entity asset: one kind of entity, as the hero or a goblin, and its starting setup: its sides and tags, its level range, its abilities and items and their limits, its attribute set and time scale attribute, its workers, modifiers and components, its crowd control rules and what its death does. Many entities can share one. A GAS hub reads it as it initializes, the GameplayAbilitySystem component that names it or a RuntimeGameplayAbilitySystem whose identity is made from it: the hub gives the entity its workers, registers its level under the asset's tag, gives its starting abilities, builds its attributes from its set and gives its starting items, then applies its tags. EvadeStage An evade: on its chance, nothing of the effect lands, as a dodge. ExceptTaggedPurgeFilter Spares the effects carrying one of its tags, as their asset tag or a context tag, as a purge that leaves stuns. ExecuteStage An execute: a hit that would leave the one hit with less than a share of its attribute's base takes the rest, as Culling Blade does below its threshold. FacingValidation Facing: the target lies within an angle in front of its caster, or the caster within an angle behind its target, as a backstab wants; each facing its targeting packet's, along the ground. An angle of 360 takes anywhere. FlatVariance Up or down by an amount, as 5 for a hit of 20 landing from 15 to 25. FloatingTextCue Floats a text where its placement says, above the one the cue is on by default: a hit's damage from an effect's On Hit, the gold a kill gave, a status's name as it lands. It says its Text, where {value} is its number, written as its Value says, {name} the name of what raised it, as an effect's, and {tag} its cue tag; it moves, fades and scales as its Motion says, looks as its Look says, and merges, staggers and caps as its Stacking says. Its texts come from ForgeCuePool and go back to it. FloatingTextLook How a floating text looks. FloatingTextMotion How a floating text moves and fades over its life. FloatingTextStacking How the floating texts on one entity merge, stagger, and how many show. FloatingTextValue A floating text's number, and how it's written. ForgeAssetCatalog Names the assets a save refers to, attributes, effects, abilities and items, by IDs that last across sessions, as a reference doesn't. A save names each by its ID here, and a load finds it by that. In the editor, Add Every PlayForge Asset, in the catalog's menu, names each PlayForge asset in the project by its GUID, which lasts as the asset is renamed or moved. A game can add its own as it runs. A ForgeProject is the catalog the Create menu makes, of the assets in its folder, which it keeps current as they're made, moved in and deleted; a catalog made before goes on naming what it names. ForgeAuras Gives a holder an aura, and takes it back: what each Aura component does in its own hooks, and a game's code may do for an aura of its own. An entity's auras are its AuraSet, a service it steps. ForgeAuthoringSettings How The Forge makes a Forge Project's assets: where each type's new assets go, each type's defaults, and the effects a new Cost or Cooldown copies. They were the whole Unity project's, in ProjectSettings/PlayForgeSettings.asset; each game keeps its own now. A game's build ignores them. ForgeChance Every chance PlayForge rolls goes through here: a number of the chance, the caster's luck, and, where the chance is pseudo-random, the caster's streak for it, kept by the chance's key. ForgeCombatLog The current project's combat log settings, which each entity's log reads as it writes. ForgeContext The contexts a tag is offered in: one per kind of tag, what a tag is rather than where it's used. A tag field names the kinds it takes with [ForgeTagContext], and its picker offers the tags of those kinds: those assets use in such a field, those a Tag Library declares for them, and those code exposes with [ForgeTagExposed]. Usage: [ForgeTagContext(ForgeContext.Granted)] public Tag Stunned; Each constant is its value without its spaces. A project's own contexts, made in a contexts field's New Context…, stand beside these. ForgeCounters PlayForge's counters in Unity's Profiler, in its PlayForge category, which the PlayForge Processes and PlayForge GAS modules chart. A frame's counts start from 0 each frame, and count every world's work, a headless run's within the frame among them. A level holds until it changes: the scene's ProcessControl gives the process levels as its LateUpdate loop ends, and the others follow what starts and ends. Unity compiles them out of release builds, so they count in the editor and development builds. A ProfilerRecorder reads one by its name in the category, as "Effects Applied". The markers time PlayForge's work; these say how much of it there is. ForgeCuePool The pools pooled Prefab cues take their objects from: one per prefab, its idle objects put away under a root that outlives a scene, in place of an object made and destroyed each time a cue plays. ForgeCueRoutes Plays a cue by its tag, as a Cue Tag cue raises it: the entity's own Cue Receiver first, its own way; then, where the receiver plays nothing for it or passes it through, the library's route for the tag, the receiver's variant's where the library has one. ForgeCueSink What a world asks once for each raise of a list of cues, before any of them plays: whether it plays here. The default plays everything; a network layer's says what a server plays, what it sends on, and what a client has played ahead. Give a world one of its own with UseSink(ProcessWorld, ForgeCueSink). ForgeCues Where every cue plays, whatever raised it: an effect's, an ability's, an entity's, an item's, or a game's own code, as sparks at a ray's hit. A handler that throws is reported and the rest play on: what something shows mustn't stop what it does. And what PlayForge's cues reach in the game: the camera shaker the game gives. ForgeEffectTemplateAttribute Marks a GameplayEffect field as template-able. The drawer will show an "Import from Template" option when a template is configured. ForgeEntities Every live entity, on both hubs: each joins as its core initializes and leaves as it ends. An area search goes through it, as Auto Target and Auto Target by Affinity do: with no range they searched the scene for MonoBehaviour entities alone, so a runtime entity was never found; and with a range they searched with physics alone, which finds no runtime entity, as it has no collider. ForgeEvents Sends a gameplay event to an entity as the core sends its own: only where an ability of the entity listens for it, queued for its frame's end where it has a queue, its data the source and the subject given. ForgeFloatingText A text a Floating Text cue floats: it moves, fades and scales over its life by its cue's motion, on the game's clock or in real time, faces the camera where asked, and goes back to its pool as its life ends. A number merged into it starts its life again. ForgeFrameCosts A frame's costliest processes, which go into the Profiler's capture as the frame's metadata while the Profiler records, for the PlayForge Processes module to list. The costs go under Tag, the costliest first, and each one's type's name, in UTF-8, under the tags after it in the same order, so a saved capture still names them. The scene's ProcessControl puts them in as its frame ends; while the Profiler doesn't record, nothing is timed for them. ForgeHelper Helpers the framework's code shares, many of them extension methods: an asset's texture under a tag, the sign of a change and checks of it, tag requirement and query checks, tag matching by hierarchy, attribute arithmetic by operation, a magnitude joined with its scaler, list helpers (RandomChoice, Shuffle, WeightedSample, SafeAdd), and random points in a circle or a sphere. ForgeInput The input click targeting reads: the project's own, unless Use(IForgeInput) puts another in. Targeting read the Input Manager's mouse and Camera.main itself, so a game on the Input System, with a camera of its own or a test couldn't stand in, and a scene with no main camera threw at the click. A source-scanning test keeps Unity's input out of the rest of the runtime. ForgeLifesteal Lifesteal's one rule, an effect's and a holder's. ForgeLog Level-gated logging for PlayForge: all the runtime says goes through here, and this file alone writes to Unity's console, so a project sets how much it hears in one place: Preferences → PlayForge → Logging in the editor, kept and put back on a domain reload, or MinimumLevel from code. Each message is of a system, effects, abilities, workers, numbers, processes, sequences and the rest, and a system can take a level of its own, SetLevel(ESystem, ELevel?), as the Creator Lab's log does; Logged hears each message let through, with the entity it's about where it names one. What's said only when asked, a debug tool's output (TagCache.LogWeights, the Threshold Debugger worker, LogAction), ProcessControl's logs while its inspector's toggles are on, and a sequence's injection or chain logging, is information: the toggle decides whether it's made, and the level whether it's shown. Its methods are marked to hide in the Console's stack, as the Console's Strip Logging Callstack hides them, and a double-click on a message it wrote opens the code that logged it, not this file. ForgeMenuAttribute Files a kind in the pickers that offer it, an ability task's, a worker's, a component's, a cue's, a number's and the rest: under the submenus its path names, a slash between each, as "Effects" or "Effects/Damage"; with a name to show in place of its class's; and with a description the picker's Context says while it's highlighted. A path holds for the classes made from the one that names it, unless one names its own, "" for the picker's top; a kind that names only a name or a description keeps its base's path. A name and a description are a kind's own. A picker lists a menu's submenus in name order, then its kinds; its search finds a kind whatever its submenu. It replaces ForgeCategory, the ability tasks' one level of groups, and the Category of a number's kind and of a condition, each of which filed one family alone. [Serializable] [ForgeMenu("Effects/Damage", Description = "Deals its damage to each target, once")] public class StrikeTask : AbstractAbilityTask { ... } ForgeProfiler PlayForge's markers in Unity's Profiler, so what it runs shows there by its own name: the step loop at each timing, a process's step, under one of its type's too, a GAS's step and its end of frame, an effect's application, an ability's activation, a tag compile, an attribute's recompute and a stage's start. Runtime had none, so PlayForge's cost showed only as its callers'. Each is a sample in the Scripts category, which a ProfilerRecorder can read by its name, as "PlayForge.ApplyEffect". ForgeProject A Forge Project: a set of PlayForge assets of its own, those under the folder its asset is in. The Forge shows the active project's assets alone, and makes new assets in it. A project's folder can hold another project's, and an asset is in the innermost project whose folder holds it. It's an asset catalog too, of its own assets, for saves, which it keeps current as they're made, moved in and deleted; Add Its Assets names them by hand. ForgeProjectSettings A Forge Project's settings: what its game reads as it runs, its attributes' roles and the crowd control rules an entity follows where it names none of its own. A running game finds them through its GameRoot. ForgePurge What purges an entity's effects: those a purge takes, by the current project's purge levels, each coming off as a removal does. ForgeRandom The random numbers PlayForge's runtime draws: Unity's, unless Use(IForgeRandom) puts another source in, as SeededRandom. The runtime drew from UnityEngine.Random in five files, so a roll could be repeated only by seeding the whole game's random numbers. ForgeReach What reads an ability's reach, its first IAbilityReach component's: how far it reaches, and whether a target or a point lies beyond it, from its caster. An ability with none reaches anywhere. Each read that takes a reach reads that one, as a component of more than one reach asks its own. ForgeResolveOrder The project's resolve order: the order an area's effects land on those it takes, by the tags they carry, so specific behaviour can be coded. An ability's Apply Effects and Apply/Remove Effects, an effect's Area, with its target among those it takes, and an aura's check follow it; code of your own can too. ForgeRoles The attributes playing roles in the current project: PlayForge's features read the roles it ships, as ROLE_HEALTH, and a game's code reads its own by their tags. ForgeSave Saves an entity at rest and loads it back. Nothing captured an entity's state, so a game couldn't keep a battle between sessions. Capture(IGameplayAbilitySystem, ForgeAssetCatalog, IForgeEntityIds) takes what lasts on an entity into a ForgeSnapshot: its attributes' permanent commits, its levels, the abilities it knows, its items with their stacks, worn or not, its effects with their time left, its loose tags and its time scale. Modifiers aren't saved: they come back with the effects that carry them. Restore(IGameplayAbilitySystem, ForgeSnapshot, ForgeAssetCatalog, IForgeEntityIds) ends what's running, lets go of what the entity has, and puts back what the save had, on the entity it was taken from or a fresh one of its kind. A restore tells nothing as it goes. No effect is told as applied or removed, no attribute as changed, and nothing of an effect's application runs again: its workers, its commits on application, its contained effects. It tells OnRestored once, as it ends, for a listener to read the entity afresh. ForgeShowWhenAttribute Shows a field in its inspector only while another field of the same object holds one of the values given, as a randomized scaler's multipliers show only for its Multiplier mode. The inspector reads it; nothing at runtime does. The other field is an enum or a bool. A field can carry several, and shows while every one holds, as an Asset Part number's worker key shows only for an effect's Worker Value. ForgeSnapshot An entity at rest, as Capture(IGameplayAbilitySystem, ForgeAssetCatalog, IForgeEntityIds) takes it and Restore(IGameplayAbilitySystem, ForgeSnapshot, ForgeAssetCatalog, IForgeEntityIds) puts it back: its attributes' permanent commits, its levels, abilities, items and effects, its loose tags and its time scale. Plain serializable types, so a game writes a save where it likes, through JsonUtility or its own serializer. Assets are named by their IDs in a ForgeAssetCatalog and tags by name, which last across sessions as a reference doesn't. ForgeTagContext The kinds of tag a tag field takes, which its picker offers: one context per kind, as ForgeContext names them, or a project's own. Usage: [ForgeTagContext(ForgeContext.Granted, ForgeContext.AssetTag)] public Tag Required; Or with string literals: [ForgeTagContext("Granted", "Asset Tag")] public Tag Required; ForgeTagDefault Specifies a default tag value for a field if none is set. ForgeTagExcludeUniversal Controls whether Universal tags are included when filtering by context. By default, Universal tags are always included. ForgeTagExposed Exposes a tag written in code to the editor's tag pickers, on a static Tag property or field, a project's own as PlayForge's in Tags: only a code tag marked so is offered, so a project chooses which of its tags its designers see. Its contexts say which fields offer it; with none, it's under Code. It was ForgeContextDefault, which a property alone could carry. ForgeTagGroup Groups related tag fields together in the inspector. ForgeTagLibrary A project-authored tag catalogue: tags that exist by declaration rather than by being referenced somewhere in an asset. The Forge's Create tab writes entries here, and the editor tag registry (ForgeTagRegistry) scans every library asset so declared tags appear in tag pickers under their chosen contexts — even before any asset uses them. Multiple libraries may exist (e.g. one per feature); all are scanned. ForgeTagLibrary.Entry A tag a Tag Library declares, which tag pickers offer under its contexts before any asset uses it: its Name, the full dotted path; its DisplayName, where it reads otherwise, as a unique tag's; the Contexts it's declared for, Universal where it names none; and a Note on what it's for. ForgeTagLockedCountAttribute Attribute to mark a Tag list field as having locked items determined by count. Tags at indices less than LockedCount are locked. ForgeTagLockedIndicesAttribute Attribute to mark specific indices in a Tag list as locked. ForgeTagNoCreate Prevents creating new tags from this field's dropdown. ForgeTagPrefix Specifies that this tag field should only accept tags matching specific prefixes. ForgeTagReadOnly Marks a tag field as read-only in the inspector. The tag can still be set programmatically. ForgeTagRequired Validates that a tag field is not empty when the asset is saved. ForgeTagTooltip Provides a custom tooltip for the tag field. ForgeTick The fixed-rate tick. With ProcessControl's tick rate set, the game steps in ticks, each a fixed step of its time, a number of them a frame: every process steps once a tick, its end of frame with it, and a sequence waits for the next tick where it waited for the next frame. So a run comes out the same at any frame rate. Off, as it is by default, a wait is Unity's next frame, as it was. A world of its own has a tick of its own, in force while it steps or moves a process, so its sequences wait on its steps. The ticks run on the game's time and stand with it, so a sequence on a clock that runs while it stands, as UnscaledClock does, waits for Unity's frames. ForgeTickSource A tick: the waits for its next one, which it lets go as it ticks, and how many it has run. The scene has one, which ProcessControl's tick rate turns on, and each world of its own has its own, which ticks as its owner steps it. ForgeTime The clock PlayForge's runtime reads: Unity's, unless Use(IForgeClock) puts another in. The runtime read Unity's Time in a dozen files, so nothing could step it to a clock of its own, as a deterministic replay, a server or a test needs. A source-scanning test keeps Time out of the runtime. ForgeTurnToFace What turns an activation's caster to face its target or its point before its first stage, as an entity's Turns To Face and an ability's Turn To Face do. ForgeUtils Extension methods for a list: IndexMin and IndexMax give the index of the element whose selected value is lowest or highest, the first where several tie, and 0 for an empty list. ForgeWorkerNames A worker's kind in a word or two, as a journal or a log names it: "Math" for a MathAttributeWorker. FrameSummary Captures all modifications and events that occurred during a frame for a single GAS. Impact tracking is split by perspective: • Impact RECEIVED — indexed by ISource (who attacked me) • Impact DEALT — indexed by ITarget (who I attacked) A self-impact (source == target on the same system) is recorded on both sides. FrameSummarySnapshot A frame's summary as its listeners read it. The one OnFrameComplete hands a listener is its entity's own and is refilled each frame, so it holds that frame only during the call. CreateSnapshot(int) makes one to keep. GameClock The game's time, as the clock in force reads it: ForgeTime's own, or a world's or a tick's while one steps. It reads that clock each time it's asked, so it can be kept and handed on: a sequence on it runs by the game's time whatever its packet's owner's is, as an ability's caster's. GameClockChoice The game's time, whatever an ability's caster's is: a slowed caster's sequence on it isn't slowed. GameRoot The game's own entity, a Mono hub every scene has one of, which ProcessControl hands any registration that names no handler. It runs as its Forge Project's Game Root entity: the project a scene's Bootstrapper plays, or else its own, or else the entity it names. It keeps through scene loads. GameplayAbilitySystem A GAS on a GameObject. What makes it a GAS lives in FarEmerald.PlayForge.GASCore, which it builds as it initializes and forwards to. What stays here is the asset it is made from, its place in the scene, and how it goes away. GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks Callbacks for the GameplayAbilitySystem level events. These are frame-level and cross-system events, distinct from AbilitySystemCallbacks (ability events) and AttributeSystemCallbacks (attribute events). GameplayCondition A condition read against a number's context: whether something holds where the number is read, as "the target's Health is below 0.3 of its base". A Conditional scaler reads one to choose its branch. It is a class, so a project adds its own as it adds a kind of number: override Evaluate(in NumberContext), and name it, file it and say what it reads with GameplayConditionAttribute: [Serializable] [GameplayCondition("Target Is Caster", Reads = NumberReads.Caster | NumberReads.Target)] public class TargetIsCaster : GameplayCondition { protected override bool Evaluate(in NumberContext context) => ReferenceEquals(context.Caster, context.Target); public override string Describe() => "the target is the caster"; } Where the context lacks what a condition reads, as a target's tag where there's no target, it doesn't hold, and it logs once. A condition's own numbers read with the condition as their owner. Its fields draw in the inspector with no editor code, with [Tooltip] and [ForgeShowWhen]; it is saved by its class's name, as a [SerializeReference] value is, so renaming the class needs Unity's [MovedFrom]. GameplayConditionAttribute Names a condition in the condition menu and says what it reads of a number's context. Its place in the menu is its ForgeMenuAttribute's: it named a Category of its own. Without it, a condition takes its class's name without "Condition", and is read everywhere. GameplayEffect A Gameplay Effect asset: a change to an entity, as damage, a heal, a timed buff, a poison, a cost or a cooldown. Abilities, items and code apply it to a target: Generate, through the target's GenerateEffectSpec, makes a GameplayEffectSpec for one application, which ApplyGameplayEffect lands. Its duration's Policy decides how long it lives: an Instant effect makes its change once, and a Durational or Infinite one goes on the target's effect shelf until its time runs out or something removes it. Its impacts change attributes, each a commit that stays or a modifier reversed as the effect ends; it can also grant tags and abilities, apply contained effects, run workers and carry components, and its requirements and conditions say whether it lands, goes on and comes off. It has no level of its own: it takes its origin's. GameplayEffectDefinition An effect's identity: its Name, which gives its asset tag, its Description, its Visibility, a tag a UI can read to decide whether to show it, its Textures, whether its icon is its origin's (Inherit From Origin, by Origin Texture), and the Retention Group its changes count toward unless an impact names its own. GameplayEffectDuration An effect's duration section: its Policy and Duration, the clock it runs by, its periodic ticks, Tick On Application and Additional Executions, what it does as it's applied to a target that has it already, and how its stacks count. As a lasting effect lands, it makes the container the application lives in on the shelf and sets its clock, reading its numbers for that application. GameplayEffectImpact An effect's impact section: its first impact, the attribute it changes, the operation and the value it changes, its magnitude, pipeline and impact types, whose delivery the duration gives it; its Additional Impacts, each with a delivery of its own; its affiliation check, its chance to apply and its contained effects. On every GameplayEffect.Generate, RebuildEntries derives the first impact's entry, which is never saved, and appends the additional ones after it: Entries is what an application commits and registers. GameplayEffectSpec One application of a Gameplay Effect: the effect, its origin, its source and its target, as the target's GenerateEffectSpec makes it and ApplyGameplayEffect lands it. It keeps what belongs to that application alone: magnitudes set by its caller, where it hit (WithHit), what modifiers changed of it, its workers' and components' state, what it has dealt, and, while it lasts, the container that holds it on the shelf. Its impacters, built once from its effect's entries, are what the attribute system evaluates for each delivery. GameplayPipelineConfiguration The base of an effect's stack behaviours: a Name, and a Priority that orders the behaviours as they apply, lowest first, so the highest has the last word. A kind can fix its own with ConfigPriority, as Stack Bounds applies last and Starting Stacks first. GrantTagsChange Adds tags it grants while it's on, as its own granted tags are. GrantTagsTask Grants tags to its caster or its target while its stage runs, as a charge's State.Charging: on as it starts, off as the stage ends, however it ends. Each is a loose tag, counted as a grant is, so two runs at once each give and take back their own. GroupImpactKind One retention group's part of an attribute, on the caster or the target, current or base: an attribute's value is the sum of its groups' parts, so 2 × Caster's Strength (Bonus) deals more for the Strength items give and nothing for the hero's own. An entity with no such attribute, or no part in the group, reads 0. GroupProcess A container process that other processes can register into. Members are still their own processes in ProcessControl — they move through Running/Waiting/Terminated as normal. The group adds coordinated lifecycle management, shared data, member-cap enforcement, and group-level operations. Usage: // Registration auto-creates the group if it doesn't exist: ProcessControl.RegisterWithGroup(myGroupTag, someProcess, out relay); // Or create the group manually for configuration: var group = new GroupProcess("Buffs", maxMembers: 5, overflowPolicy: EGroupOverflowPolicy.EvictOldest); ProcessControl.RegisterGroup(myGroupTag, group, out groupRelay); ProcessControl.RegisterWithGroup(myGroupTag, someProcess, out relay); HasEffectValidation A check that passes while the checked entity has an effect on: its Effect, or any effect tagged Tagged or a tag under it, by its asset tag, a context tag or a tag it grants; with Without, while it has none of it. Naming neither, it passes. HoldsItemValidation A check that passes while the checked entity holds its Item, or, with Equipped, wears it. Naming no item, it passes. HomeRespawnPlace Where the entity stood as it registered: its spawn. Where it never stood anywhere, where it died. ImpactSeries Per-level evaluation of one impact entry: the magnitude the entry contributes at each level, and the total delivered over the effect's lifetime (ticks × magnitude for Periodic delivery). ImpactWorkerCache Cache for impact workers, indexed by impacted attribute. Supports both inline and deferred execution modes. ImpactWorkerGroup Several impact workers as one: given to an entity, it gives it each of its workers, and each runs for the changes it takes as it would on its own; taken back, it takes them back. IndependentDurationsContainer The container of Stacks Have Independent Durations: each stack keeps its own timer and ticks and comes off as its time runs out, so the effect lasts as long as its longest stack. Refresh restarts its oldest stack's time, and Extend adds a stack. InitializationOperation The stack behaviour Starting Stacks: the stacks a new container of the effect is given as it's made, a number read at the effect's level; the application that makes it adds its own amount after. It applies first of the behaviours, and leaves the amount an application adds as it is. InjectAbilityTask A stage task that sends its Injection, an interrupt unless it's set to another, as a skip or a jump to a stage, into its ability's running activations, and ends at once. InputSystemPointerInput The Input System's pointer, a mouse, a pen or a touch, aimed through a camera: the one given, or else Camera.main. A mouse presses each of its three buttons, and a pen or a touch the primary. InterruptSequenceInjection Interrupts the entire sequence. IsAliveValidation A check that passes while the entity it checks isn't dead: the caster among the Caster Checks, the target among the Target Checks, each list's default. Its refusal of the caster is told as Dead. Item ScriptableObject defining an item that can be added to an entity's inventory. Items can grant effects, abilities, and tags when equipped. Supports level scaling for linked effects and abilities. ItemDefinition An item's Definition: its Name, Description and Textures; its Visibility tag, which a game's UI can filter by and the runtime doesn't act on; and its MaxStackSize, how many of it one inventory slot holds, read at the item's level, 1 or less making each its own slot (StackSizeOf). ItemSave An item the entity holds. ItemSpec Runtime specification for an item instance. Contains the item's current state, level, and provides level information for linked effects/abilities. ItemSpecContainer Container that manages an item instance's lifecycle. Tracks equipped state, applied effects, abilities, and granted tags. Handles equip/unequip operations with proper cleanup. ItemStacksScaler The stack count of the item that applied the effect: 1 for an item that doesn't stack, and 1 for an effect no item applied. With Multiply With Scaler, an item's effect grows by the stack, as a relic of +10 a stack does. Nothing read an item's stack count. ItemSystemCallbacks Callbacks for item system events. Used for monitoring item lifecycle without modifying behavior. ItemSystemComponent An entity's inventory: the items it holds, each in a slot (an ItemSpecContainer) with its level and stacks, and which of them it wears. GiveItem, EquipItem, UnequipItem, RemoveItem and ConsumeItem change it, within its entity's item limits and duplicate rules; a worn item puts on its Granted Effects and Granted Tags, lends its Active Ability and adds its workers, and takes them back as it comes off. Code reaches it through the entity's hub, GetItemSystem(), and hears each change through its Callbacks. ItemTags An item's Tags: its AssetTag, made from its Name, which its holder carries while the item is in its inventory, worn or not, and keeps the item's level under; its ContextTags, which the changes its effects make carry as context; and its Granted Tags (PassiveGrantedTags), on its holder while it's equipped. JumpToStageInjection Jumps to a specific stage by index. LambdaAction Simple action that executes a lambda. Use sparingly. LazyMonoProcess The Lazy process is a process (typically self-terminating) that runs until Waited or Terminated. LazyRuntimeProcess A runtime process whose run lasts until it's paused or ended: its RunProcess waits a tick at a time while it's active, so what it does goes in its steps and hooks, WhenUpdate and the rest. The base of most runtime processes, a group, a runtime GAS and a task sequence's process among them; its constructor takes a name, a step priority, a timing and a lifecycle. LegacyPointerInput The Input Manager's mouse, aimed through a camera: the one given, or else Camera.main. LevelCondition Whether the level compares with a number: the level itself, or how far up its range it is, from 0 at its least to 1 at its most. LevelSave A level the entity keeps: its own, or an ability's or an item's, under that one's asset tag. LevelSystemCallbacks Callbacks for level system events. Used for monitoring level changes without modifying behavior. LevelerEffectOrigin An origin that stands for an entity at a level of its own: a SourceEffectOrigin whose GetLevel gives the Level it holds, not the entity's. A leveler carrier reads its numbers through one, and a save puts one back where an effect's origin was one; IEffectOrigin.GenerateLevelerDerivation makes one. LevelerImpactDerivation A carrier to read numbers in at a level it's given, not its source's: its origin is a LevelerEffectOrigin at that level, and it carries no change of its own. An entity reads its Max Abilities, Max Items and Max Equipped Items at its level through one, and AbilityInspector reads an effect's numbers level by level through one with no source; IAttributeImpactCarrier.GenerateLevelerDerivation makes one. LifestealImpactWorker The Lifesteal worker: it heals its holder a share of each workable loss it deals another, the value of its holder's Share, the attribute it names, which an effect on the holder raises while it should. The losses that count are to its Receives attribute, and it heals its Heals attribute, each the Health role's where it names none. An effect has no lifesteal of its own. Only hits of the impact types it names count, as attacks, so a second worker on another attribute makes a spell vamp. A project gives it to every entity through its Forge Project's Workers, and an entity can hold one of its own; one that holds two heals a hit once. It allocates nothing, healing or not. LineOfSightValidation Line of Sight: nothing on the layers it names blocks a line from the caster to its target, run at a height above each, so the ground under them doesn't. The two ends' own colliders don't block it. The line runs between their targeting packets, so it's drawn for an entity of either hub, and 3D physics colliders block it. LinkedSourceAttribute Attribute to mark fields that should use the LevelProviderDrawer. Apply to ScriptableObject fields that should only accept ILevelProvider types. LocalAbility An ability. LocalAttribute An attribute. LocalBool A bool. LocalDataKind A value in Local Data, under a key, as a hero's attack range: in what the number belongs to (the ability's or the item's asset, or an entity's own Local Data, where the number is the entity's), or in the caster's or the target's Local Data as the entity holds it at runtime. An entry that holds a float or a whole number reads as that number; where there's no number under the key, it reads its Default. LocalDataStructure An entity's Local Data as its GAS holds it at runtime, a value under each key tag: loaded from its identity's rows as it initializes (Init), then written with Set and read with TryGet, or with GetOrInit, which adds a value where the key has none. A hub's GetLocalDataStructure gives it. LocalDataValue A Local Data entry's value. A kind holds its value as Held gives it, gives it as a packet takes it with Read(in NumberContext), a number read where it's used, and says whether it's a number with TryReadNumber(in NumberContext, out float), as a Local Data number and a tag rule read one. Most kinds hold one value, a LocalDataValue<T>'s. LocalDataValue<T> A Local Data value that holds one T, its Value, as most kinds do. LocalEffect An effect. LocalEntity An entity's identity. LocalFloat A number that can scale, read where it's used: at the level and with the caster it's read for. LocalInt A whole number that can scale, read where it's used. LocalMonoBehaviour A component on a prefab, as a process to spawn. LocalObject Any asset, as a prefab or a material. LocalScriptableObject A ScriptableObject asset. LocalString A string. LocalTag A tag; one left empty is none. LogAction A deferred action that writes its text through ForgeLog, at Info, as its turn comes: at Cleanup priority unless it's given another, and only where its validity check, if it's given one, holds. A Threshold with no effects and no event queues one as it fires. MagnitudeSave A magnitude a caller set under a tag. MainThreadSequenceTask Task that executes a synchronous action on the main thread. Forces non-async execution by only accepting Action delegates. MathAttributeWorker Performs math operations on attribute changes relative to another attribute. This is an INLINE worker because it modifies the ChangeValue directly. ModifyAttributeAction Deferred action to modify an attribute. One the system makes for itself, such as a rescale or a lifesteal's heal, is used again once the queue has run it, so a listener handed one reads it during the call. MonoWrapperProcess The wrapper ProcessControl holds a mono process in, passing each hook and step to its object and reading its lifecycle, timing and priority from it. It gets the process's object as it registers: from the registration's instantiator, else its handler's where the process uses its handler's, else the process's own, else a clone of its prefab, or the scene object itself; as the process ends, what made the object takes it back, or the object is destroyed. MultiplierVariance The value times a multiplier between its Min and its Max, as 0.9 to 1.1. MultiplyStage The value times a number read for the hit: a bonus, × Caster's Damage Amplification read as 1 + x; a reduction, × Target's Damage Resistance read as what's left; an armor curve; a bonus that reads the target, as Crowbar's above 90%. NeverCondition A condition that never holds. NewAssetSettings Where a type's new assets go. A new asset's file is its name alone: the file prefix and suffix are gone. NonStackingEffectContainer The container of an application with no stacks, which Add Another makes for each application of its effect: its own clock, its ticks executing once each. Refresh restarts its time and its tick, and Extend adds to its time. NotCondition Whether its condition doesn't hold. Where that condition can't be worked out, neither can this, so it doesn't hold either: not having a target's tag doesn't hold where there's no target. NullTargetingPacket A targeting packet that points at nothing: a StaticTargetingPacket with no entity and no transform, its position, rotation and scale left unset. NumberComparison A comparison between two numbers, as a condition makes one, and how a line writes it. NumberContextAttribute Says what a number field's context provides, which kinds its kind menu then offers, and which the Problems window flags. A targeting task's range has no target yet, as the target is what it looks for: [NumberContext(NumberReads.Level | NumberReads.Caster | NumberReads.Caller | NumberReads.LocalData)]. A field without it offers every kind but one that reads its owner, as an effect's numbers have everything else. An owner is given only by the code that reads the field, Max.Evaluate(context, this), so a field whose code gives one says so, [NumberContext(NumberReads.All)], and Relative to a Field joins its menu. It also takes the field's unit: a field whose unit is "%" stores 0.3 and shows and takes it as 30%. NumberKind A kind of number of your own: one class with one method. Override Evaluate(in NumberContext) to work out the kind's value from what the context offers, and Describe() for the field's one-line summary. Name it, file it and say what it reads with NumberKindAttribute, and the kind menu offers it in every number field whose context provides what it reads: [Serializable] [NumberKind("Distance to Target", Reads = NumberReads.Caster | NumberReads.Target)] [ForgeMenu("Space", Description = "How far the target is from the caster")] public class DistanceToTarget : NumberKind { [Tooltip("Along the ground, leaving height out")] public bool Flat = true; protected override float Evaluate(in NumberContext context) { var from = context.Caster.GetTargetingPacket().position; var to = context.Target.GetTargetingPacket().position; if (Flat) from.y = to.y = 0f; return Vector3.Distance(from, to); } public override string Describe() => "the distance to the target"; } A kind is a scaler, so it also works wherever a scaler does: inside a Group, a Conditional or a Clamped, and in an effect's magnitude. The base answers the scaler's carrier methods by building a NumberContext and calling yours. It reads no values per level. Its fields draw in the inspector with no editor code, as a scaler's do, with [Tooltip] and [ForgeShowWhen]. A kind is saved by its class's name, so renaming the class needs Unity's [MovedFrom], as any [SerializeReference] value does. Test one without an effect through For(ISource, ITarget, int, int). NumberKindAttribute Names a kind of number in the kind menu and says what it reads of a field's context. Its place in the menu is its ForgeMenuAttribute's, as every kind's is: it named a Category of its own. The inspector offers the kind only in fields whose context provides what it reads, and the Problems window flags it where it's found in one that doesn't. Without it, a kind takes its class's name, as a scaler does, and is offered everywhere. NumberMaxAttribute The most a number field's constant takes in the inspector: [NumberMax(10)]. With NumberMinAttribute beside it, the field takes what lies between the two. See NumberMinAttribute for what a limit reaches. NumberMinAttribute The least a number field's constant takes in the inspector, as Unity's [Min] is for a float: [NumberMin(0)] public ScalableFloat Duration = 2f; A number field takes these in place of Unity's [Min] and [Range]. Unity gives a field that has one of its own to that attribute's drawer, which draws "Use Min with float, int or Vector" where the number was, so the console names a number field that has one as scripts load. The limit is the inspector's, as Unity's is: it keeps the constant typed in. A number of a kind is worked out as the game runs, so where what it reads must stay inside limits, give it the Clamped kind, or clamp what the code reads. On a field whose unit is "%" the limit is in what the field stores: [NumberRange(0, 1)] is 0% to 100%. A whole-number field takes the whole numbers inside the limits. NumberRangeAttribute A number field whose constant is set on a slider between two values, as Unity's [Range] is for a float: [NumberRange(0, 1)] public ScalableFloat Chance = 0.5f;. See NumberMinAttribute for what a limit reaches. NumberSiblingFieldAttribute Marks the string field that names a relative number's sibling, which the inspector picks from a menu. NumberText A number's one-line summary, as its field shows it under its row: "0.3 × Target's Health (base)", "Fire Duration + 2", "the caller's Data.Damage". A kind of your own gives its part through Describe(). A field whose unit is "%" reads its numbers as percentages: "30% × Target's Health (base)". NumberTrace A number's read, explained: a tree of its parts, each with what it read and what it gave. A charged hit reads −180 because its Group adds its caster's Attack Damage, 100, to a Conditional that gives 80, as the caster's Combo Charges, 4, are above 0. A part whose context lacks what it reads says what it needs, "the target", and gives its fallback, so a read in the editor with no entities says where it would change in play. Each part reads as the number does, through the same context, so the parts and the read agree. A read that rolls, as a Randomized scaler's, rolls again for its parts. A trace allocates, and is for the editor, tools and tests. A kind or a condition of a project's own explains its parts by overriding Explain(in NumberContext, NumberTrace) or Explain(in NumberContext, NumberTrace) and adding them: trace.Add(Min, context, this, "Min"). NumberWorkers The workers on each entity that answer numbers, and the way to ask them or an effect's workers. A worker group installs its workers that answer as it gives them to an entity, and takes them back with them; code that gives an entity a worker of its own can do the same with Provide(ITarget, INumberWorker). OnHitEntry Effects that an item, an ability or an effect applies as its holder's hits land, or on the hit that kills: Desolator's armor, a dagger's bleed, a boon's Weak, a barrier on a kill. A hit is a loss to its Attribute, as Health, that the holder deals another entity: only of its impact types, where it names any, so a bleed's ticks, typed apart from attacks, set off nothing; and only while its condition holds. Each effect's own Chance to Apply rolls as it lands, and its hits set the entry off no more, so a shock it applies doesn't shock again. An item's hold while it's equipped, an ability's while it's known, an effect's while it lasts. OnHits Gives a holder the On Hits it has, and takes them back. OriginSave What applied an effect: an entity, or one of its abilities or items. Entity is empty for the entity the save is of, and otherwise the ID an IForgeEntityIds gives the other. PercentageVariance Up or down by a share of the value, as 0.1 for 10% either way. PipelineConfigRegistry A static store of GameplayPipelineConfiguration lists, kept per source and per asset tag, and cleared as play starts. Nothing in the package registers or reads one, and Register adds only to a list a source and a tag already hold, which nothing makes. PipelineConfigRegistry.ConfigPipeline A class with no members, which nothing in the package uses. PlayCueTask Plays its cues' bursts at a stage's exact moment, as a sword's arc or a spell's release: on its caster, on its activation's target, or at its activation's point. A cue there hears the activation's data, and a magnitude read as it plays, for a cue to scale with. An ability's lifelong moments play through its Cues component. PointRespawnPlace A point in the world. PrefabCue Places a prefab where its placement says: a burst as its moment comes, gone after its Lifetime, or, in a Cues component's list of lasting cues, as an effect's While Active, for as long as its cue lasts. Its placement puts it on the one the cue is on, its source, an ability's target or each of its targets, or at the cue's point, as a hit's: at a socket, moved and scattered, following them while it lasts or as it says. Pooled, it takes its objects from ForgeCuePool and gives them back, as Unreal recycles its cue actors. ProcessAttribute An attribute a gameplay mono process carries of its own, as a projectile's speed: the attribute it is, the role the process reads it by, and where its value starts. It changes as the process runs. ProcessControl The scene's scheduler of processes: every process, a GAS, a projectile, an ability's sequence, registers with it, and it steps each from Unity's player loop, in Update, LateUpdate or FixedUpdate as the process's timing asks, moves it between its states as its lifecycle says, and ends it. A Bootstrapper brings it up as the one Instance, and it then registers the scene's own mono processes, as its Collect On Awake says. ProcessControl.Register(process).HandledBy(handler).With(data).Run() registers a process and starts it, and its result holds the process's relay, which pauses, resumes and ends it; RegisterGroup and RegisterWithGroup hold runtime processes in a group by a tag. Its control state (SetControlState) pauses, closes or ends every process at once; its Fixed Tick Rate, above 0, steps every process at fixed steps of game time, so a run comes out the same at any frame rate; and its Callbacks hear every process register, change state and go. Its bookkeeping is its World, a ProcessWorld, which code can also own and step with no scene. ProcessControlBlock Represents a managed process instance with state tracking and lifecycle management. ProcessControlCallbacks Callbacks fired by ProcessControl for high-level observers (debuggers, recorders, GAS-aware observers, etc.). These are in addition to the per-process ProcessWatcher system — watchers subscribe to a specific ProcessRelay, whereas callbacks fire for every process managed by ProcessControl. ProcessCue Runs a MonoBehaviour process where its placement says: a burst's runs its own course, and one in a list of lasting cues runs for as long as its cue lasts, as a shield's that ends as the shield goes. Each runs with a data packet loaded for the cue (CuePackets), its Data list last, so the process reads the cue's entity, its asset and its numbers. Pooled, its objects come from ForgeCuePool through CuePoolInstantiator, and each goes back as its process ends. ProcessDataPacket ProcessDataPackets (and subclasses) contain data pertaining to processes and abilities Example usage: An ability, Cast, fires a ball that homes in on its target Cast is the ability and via implicit data and/or targeting tasks assigns some data to the packet The Ball is a MonoProcess and is created via ProcessControl Before initializing the MonoProcessWrapper is passed the data packet and its initial values are set After initializing the MonoProcess is passed the data packet It is responsible for procuring data from the data packet E.g. procuring the target transform via Data.TryGetPayload[Transform](Target, GameRoot.TransformParameter, Primary, out Transform value) This procures the Transform value under the Target classification stored under the key GameRoot.TransformParameter ProcessHandlerUtil Extension methods for a process handler: MassDataAction runs an action on the data packet of each process it handles, and returns false where it handles none. ProcessHierarchy Manages hierarchical relationships between MonoProcesses. Parent actions cascade to children, but not vice versa. Hierarchy Rules: Processes on the SAME GameObject are "siblings" (treated as a group) Processes on CHILD GameObjects are "children" Only the FIRST ancestor with processes counts as the "parent" ProcessHierarchy.HierarchyNode Represents a node in the process hierarchy. A node corresponds to a GameObject that has one or more processes. ProcessRelay Provides external access to ProcessControlBlock data without exposing internal state management. ProcessTaskUtil Extension methods an ability's tasks use on a data packet: the targeting packet under a tag (GetTargetingPacket, which interrupts a sequence's run where there's none, SetTargetingPacket and SetTargetingPackets), and the effects loaded under a tag, applied to a target with the magnitudes the caller set (TryApplyEffects) or read back (GetLoadedAssets). Its async loops, WhileAsync, DoWhileAsync and DoWhile, wait a tick between rounds. ProcessWorld The processes of one world and how they're stepped: every process's block, its step groups, the watches, the groups, which processes each GAS owns, the control state and its transitions, and the callbacks. A scene's ProcessControl wraps one and steps it from Unity's loop, and code can own one and step it itself, as a headless run does. It was ProcessControl itself, so no process ran without a ProcessControl in a scene. ProjectileMonoProcess A projectile: it flies at its target at its speed, the ProjectileSpeed role, and applies its effects as it lands. Its speed is an attribute it carries, or its origin's. PurgeLevels A project's purge levels: tiers of tags, weakest first, an effect at the first whose tag its asset tag or a context tag matches; a purge of a tier takes the effects at it or under it, and an effect at none is never purged, but by death. And the categories a death keeps whatever their tiers. PurgeTier A tier of a project's purge levels: the tag an effect carries to be at it, and whether a death keeps it. RandomizedScaler Adds random variance to level-based scaling. Useful for damage ranges, proc chances, etc. Its variance is a class: by a share of its value, by an amount, between two multipliers, or a way of your own, as dice. A variance's numbers are of any kind, read with the variance as their owner, so a share can widen by level and a Max multiplier can be 3 × its Min. RelativeOperationContextImpactWorker Impact worker that applies effects relative to the impact (e.g., lifesteal). Can be configured as INLINE (immediate) or DEFERRED (end-of-frame). RelativeToFieldKind Another number field of the same object: the number joins it as its Combine says, times it or plus it, so a Clamped scaler's Max can be 2 × Min and a stack bound's Max Min + 3. The field is a number (ScalableFloat or ScalableInt), read in the same context, so a relative Max follows a Min that scales by level, or a plain float or int. It reads its object through the owner its object's own code gives as it reads its numbers, MaxValue.Evaluate(context, this), and a field whose code gives one declares Owner in its NumberContextAttribute. With no owner, with a field name its object no longer has, or in a loop of numbers that read each other, which stops 8 deep, its number reads its own value and logs once. It finds its field by name through an accessor made once for each type and field, so a read allocates nothing after the first. RemoveEffectAction Deferred action to remove an effect. RepeatUntilSkippedPolicy Stage repeats infinitely until explicitly skipped, interrupted, or broken. Maintained stages with this policy will continue repeating. Use BreakStageRepeatInjection to exit the repeat loop gracefully. RequirementTemplate A reusable tag requirement configuration that can be shared across multiple assets. Usage: Create a RequirementTemplate asset (Create > PlayForge > Templates > Requirement Template) Configure the required/avoided tags in the template Reference this template from any requirement field using the "Link Template" button Changes to the template will propagate to all linked requirements when they sync Note: Linked requirements can "break" the link to make local modifications. ResolveOrderEntry One entry of a project's resolve order: those carrying its tag, or one under it, resolve at its Order among an area's hits, lower first. RespawnEntityComponent Respawn: revives an entity that stays as it dies a while after, in its own time, at its home, where it died, a point, or a place of your own, as a hero comes back at its fountain. Its Death's On Revive effects land as it does, as any revive's do; a revive before its time, as a buyback, ends the wait. The wait is its entity's RespawnTimer, a service a HUD can read. An entity that ends as it dies has nothing to revive, which the Problems view says. An entity holds one at most. RespawnTimer An entity's wait to revive, as its Respawn starts it: the time left, by the entity's own clock, and where it revives, at the end of the frame its time runs out. A revive before its time, as a buyback, ends the wait. A service of the entity, so a HUD reads it as gas.FindService<RespawnTimer>(). RetentionGroups Which retention groups' parts an attribute read takes.
