An attribute's value is the sum of its groups' parts: the base its set gives, what items add in their group, what a buff adds in its. × Attribute, an Attribute condition, a Math worker's Relative To and a Threshold worker read the whole value unless they say otherwise: only these groups, as a bonus of the items' strength reads their group; or all but these, as a bonus of a hero's own damage leaves its items' out. A group names the groups under it too. Group Impact reads one group's part, as it did. ReturnDamageAttributeWorker Damage return: a share of each workable loss its attribute takes from another goes back to the one who dealt it, typed Returned, so no return returns it again and no lifesteal heals from it, as Blade Mail. ReviveOnRemovalEffectWorker Revives the entity its effect is on as the effect ends: a respawn timer, as a staying entity takes as it dies, whose duration is the time it waits. It revives where the entity was, or at a point. An entity revived already, as by a buyback, takes nothing from it. RunProcessTask A stage task that runs its Processes as its stage starts, each registered for the caster, and waits while any still runs, up to MaxDuration seconds read at the ability's level, counted by its run's clock or, with UseUnscaledDeltaTime, unscaled; as the stage ends, it ends those still running. RunSequenceTask A stage task that runs a task sequence, or a chain, and waits for it to end: the one the static [TaskSequenceMethod] method its Sequence names makes, called for each activation, or, for an ability built in code, a fresh run of its Definition. It runs as a process in the caster's world, by the Clock picked where one is, and ends as the activation is cancelled; a critical stage in the sequence makes the task critical, and the ability lets its claim go as the sequence's critical section ends. RuntimeAttribute An attribute made in code, with no asset behind it: a name, an abbreviation and a description where it's given them, and textures AddTexture adds. AttributeRegistry.GetByName makes one for a name it doesn't know, where it's asked to, and an entity's attribute system takes one with ProvideAttribute(attribute, value). RuntimeEntityIdentity An entity's settings as a RuntimeGameplayAbilitySystem reads them: the Entity asset's fields in a plain class. Made from an Entity asset, it takes the asset's values, sharing its lists rather than copying them, and Asset names the asset; made in code, it describes an entity no asset does, and Asset is null. Two runtime entities can share one. RuntimeGameplayAbilitySystem Runtime (non-MonoBehaviour) version of GameplayAbilitySystem. Instantiated at runtime as a plain class. Derives from LazyRuntimeProcess and implements the same IGameplayAbilitySystem interface as the MonoBehaviour version. What makes it a GAS lives in FarEmerald.PlayForge.GASCore, which it builds in its constructor and forwards to. Usage: var gas = new RuntimeGameplayAbilitySystem(entityData); var relay = ProcessControl.Register(gas).With(dataPacket).Run().Relay; RuntimeWrapperProcess The wrapper ProcessControl holds a runtime process in: it passes each hook and step to the process, reads its lifecycle, timing and priority from it, and marks it ended as it terminates, so it can be registered again. ScalableFloat An authored gameplay number. It is a plain number by default, and it can also be one of the kinds the inspector's kind menu offers: a value by level, a multiple of an attribute, a value its caller sets, any scaler, or a kind a project writes (NumberKind). It is the magnitude field it grew from, under a new name, with the same saved fields: its number (Magnitude), its scaler, and how the two combine (RealMagnitude). So every magnitude saved before it loads as it was. A float converts to one, so public ScalableFloat Range = 20f; and effect.Range = 5f; compile. There is no conversion back, as it would drop the kind: a read is Evaluate(in NumberContext), once, at the site's natural moment, as an effect as it's applied or a task as it starts. ScalableInt A whole gameplay number: ScalableFloat for counts, as an effect's ticks or a stack's size. It takes every kind a ScalableFloat does, and rounds what it reads as Rounding says, so a kind is written once. It is the whole-number magnitude field it grew from, with the same saved fields. ScaledClock A time scale of its own over another clock, its source: a sequence on it runs at its scale, as a finisher's slow motion or a flourish at double speed, and the sequences that share one slow, speed up or stop together as it's set. Its source is the clock given, or, with none, the clock in force: the game's, or a world's or a tick's while one steps. ScaledClockChoice A pace of its own over another clock, as a finisher's slow motion at half or a flourish at double: a ScaledClock of its scale, made for each run, over the clock its Of picks, or the caster's. ScalerAsset A scaler kept as an asset of its own, which scaler fields reference through a SharedScaler. Editing it changes every field that uses it, so nothing propagates; a field adjusts it only through its own Magnitude, as in Fire Duration × 1.5. It was the Scaler Template, whose link code had no callers, so reuse meant copying a scaler into each field and propagating edits by hand. ScalerDisplayName Explicitly sets the display name for a Scaler field. Takes precedence over DeriveScalerName. ScalerGroup Several numbers joined as one: each member is a scaler or a kind of number, and says how it joins the others. Members that add are added up; that sum is multiplied by each member that multiplies and divided by each that divides; then each flat bonus is added on. So (5 + Caster's Strength) × 2 + 3 is one number, a wind-up's 1.7 ÷ Caster's Attack Speed another, and a curse's 5 + what its worker answers is one magnitude. A member that overrides gives the group's value alone. Where several override, OverrideMemberCollisionPolicy picks among them: the highest, the lowest, their average, the first or the last; Ignore sets them aside, and the other members join as they would without them. Each member reads in the number's own context, so a member that is a kind reads all the field's context gives, and a member that is a scaler evaluates against the effect, or against the carrier the context fills where there's no effect. Joining its members allocates nothing. It reads its members alone, so it has no values per level. With no members, or none that holds a kind, it is no kind at all (IsEmpty): its field reads its number, as a field with no kind does. It read values per level of its own, which its inspector hid. ScalerImpacter The default impacter shape — wraps a ScalableFloat (the editor-authored magnitude + scaler + RealMagnitude triplet that already lives on GameplayEffectImpact) and exposes it through the impacter contract. One ScalerImpacter per GameplayEffectImpact is the current shape. ScalerOperationKeyword Specifies a keyword that customizes labels in ScalableFloat and ScalableInt property drawers. The keyword is used to: Set the magnitude label to "Base {Keyword}" or "Additional {Keyword}" Set the operation label to "Real {Keyword}" or "Use {Keyword}" Set the scaler label to "{Keyword} Scaler" (via DeriveScalerName) ScalerRootAssignment Put on a scaler field, it narrows the kinds the field's Kind menu offers: those deriving from RootType alone, where it names one, and none deriving from AvoidType, where it names one. An attribute set element's sides take the cached kinds alone so, and a number field every kind but those. SeededRandom Random numbers of their own, from a seed, which nothing else draws from: two runs from one seed draw the same numbers, whatever else in the game draws from Unity's. SelectDirectionTargetTask Interactive targeting task: click to define a direction from the caster. Raycasts from the camera to determine the world position clicked, then computes a normalized direction from the caster to that point. Stores the direction in Tags.TARGET_POS as a Vector3 and the clicked world position in Tags.POSITION. Useful for skill shots, dashes, line attacks, etc. SelectGasOrPositionTargetTask Interactive targeting task: raycast to select either a GAS target or a world position. Prioritizes GAS targets (ITarget) — if the hit object has no ITarget component, falls back to using the hit position. Tag requirements apply only to GAS targets. SelectGasTargetInRangeTask Interactive targeting task: click to select a GAS target within range. Like SelectGasTargetTask, but adds a maximum distance check from the caster to the clicked target. Invalid targets outside range trigger retry or failure. Useful for melee abilities, short-range spells, or any ability where the player must select a target within a specific radius. SelectGasTargetTask Interactive targeting task: raycast to select a GAS target (ITarget). Waits for the player to click on a valid target in the world. Validates the hit object has an ITarget component and passes tag requirements. SelectPositionTargetTask Interactive targeting task: raycast to select a world position. Waits for the player to click on a valid surface in the world. Stores the hit position in the data packet under Tags.POSITION. SendEventTask Sends a gameplay event to its caster, or to each of its activation's targets, as a combo's hit tells its next stage it connected, or as an ability sets off another's trigger. The event's data holds its caster as Source and the one it's sent to as Event Subject, with the activation's caller's magnitudes; it's sent at once, and the abilities it triggers try to activate as a trigger's do. SequenceAnnotation Declarative annotation of what a sequence DOES — the introspection channel for code-driven sequences. Sequence bodies are opaque async lambdas; annotations let the author state gameplay intent so AbilityInspector can decipher abilities built on RunSequenceTask (tooltips, the Forge analysis tab, debugging). The load-and-apply pattern: an asset-loader task (e.g. SetEffectsTask) puts effects into the data packet under a tag, and the sequence applies them via data.TryApplyEffects(target, tag). Annotating with that tag (AppliedEffectsTag) lets the inspector connect the loaded effect assets to this sequence's application — including how many times (MaxApplications, e.g. Chain Lightning's 4 jumps). SequenceCondition A condition that triggers an injection when met. SequenceCue Runs a task sequence on a data packet loaded for the cue (CuePackets), its Data list last, so the sequence reads the cue's entity, its asset and its numbers: a burst's runs its course, and one in a list of lasting cues runs until its cue ends, as a shield's flicker that stops as the shield goes. It runs in the world of the one it plays on, by the clock its Clock picks, else the sequence's own, else its owner's. SequenceDataPacket Extended ProcessDataPacket for TaskSequence execution. Provides direct access to sequence, stage, and chain control. All TaskSequence builder methods use this type for delegates. SequenceInfo A code-driven sequence referenced by a RunSequenceTask, with its declared behavior. SequenceMetadata Optional metadata for the sequence. SequenceStage A stage within a TaskSequence containing tasks and/or sub-stages. SequenceStageMetadata Optional metadata for a stage. SequenceTaskBase Base class for async-first sequence tasks. Execute is abstract (must implement). Step defaults to instant completion (returns true). If you need your task to work in synchronous sequences, override Step. SequenceTaskLibrary Reusable async building blocks for common gameplay operations. Designed to be awaited inside TaskSequence .Task() lambdas where the caller has access to the data packet and cancellation token. Usage: .Task(async (d, t) => { var target = d.GetPrimary<Transform>(Tags.TARGET); await Seq.MoveTo(target, Vector3.zero, 1.5f, t, easeCurve); }) All timed methods: Accept an optional AnimationCurve for easing (null = linear) Snap to the final value after completion to avoid float drift Respect CancellationToken for interrupt/skip/timeout support Handle zero/negative duration by snapping immediately Hold while their sequence is paused, given the token the task was handed. ArcForce can't: physics moves the body whatever the sequence is doing SequenceTimeout A time limit on a sequence or a stage: once its Seconds have passed by the run's clock, its Injection applies, a skip of the stage by default. WithTimeout on a builder or a stage adds one, as a packet's SetStageTimeout does to the current stage from a task, and an OnTimeout handler is handed the one that ran out. SetAbilitiesTask An asset loader that puts its Abilities, Ability assets, in the activation's data under its Tag, Abilities by default. SetAssetsTask An asset loader that puts its Assets, PlayForge assets of any kind, in the activation's data under its Tag, Assets by default. SetAttributeSetsTask An asset loader that puts its AttributeSets in the activation's data under its Tag, Attribute Sets by default. SetAttributesTask An asset loader that puts its Attributes in the activation's data under its Tag, Attributes by default. SetBonusItemComponent Set Bonus: an effect its holder has while it has enough of a set's pieces equipped, as two pieces of a set giving fire resistance and four a flame aura. Each piece names its set by a tag and carries the set's bonuses; the holder's equipped pieces count each item once, and a bonus holds while they're as many as it needs, once for the holder however many pieces carry it. An item holds one for each of its set's bonuses. SetByCallerScaler A value the caller passes in under a tag, as Unreal's SetByCaller is: code that knows the amount as it applies an effect or activates an ability sets it, and the number reads it. What it checks: whether the context it's read in holds a value under exactly Key. A context holds the values set on what it was built from: an effect's spec (spec.SetByCaller(tag, value), before it's applied), an ability activation's data (data.SetByCaller(tag, value), which each effect the ability makes takes as it's made, and which the ability's tasks read), or the data that spawned a process. Only the key itself matches: a value set under a tag above or below it in the tag tree doesn't. A value set to 0 is a value, and is read. Where the context holds no value under the key, or holds no values at all, as an entity on its own, it reads Default. It is a number kind, so it reads from any context that holds values: it read only an effect spec's, so a task's or a process's number read its default. Its default is a number of any kind, read with the scaler as its owner, so where nothing is set it can read a value by level. SetEffectsTask An asset loader that puts its Effects in the activation's data under its Tag, Effects by default, for a later task to apply, as a sequence does with data.TryApplyEffects(target, tag). SetEntitiesTask An asset loader that puts its Entities, Entity assets, in the activation's data under its Tag, Entities by default. SetTagsTask An asset loader that puts its Tags in the activation's data under its Tag, Tags by default. SharedCachedScaler An attribute set's reference to a shared ScalerAsset whose scaler is one of the cached kinds: it reads the asset's scaler as the entity's values change, so an edit to the asset reaches every element that uses it. It keeps no values of its own. SharedScaler A field's reference to a shared ScalerAsset: it reads the asset's scaler, so an edit to the asset reaches every field that uses it, with nothing to propagate. It keeps no values of its own; the field's Magnitude adjusts what it reads, as in Fire Duration × 1.5. ShownWhenAttribute A kind's field shown only while another field of the same object says so: a toggle that's on, or, given values, an enum or a whole number that's one of them, as a targeting task's Detection Layers under Use Physics. A kind field, as a task's or a scaler's, draws its object's fields with this read, hiding one where it doesn't apply; it shows again as the field it reads changes. SideChangeEffectComponent Side Change: while its effect lasts, its target's sides are its caster's, as they are as it lands, a mind control, or those it names, as a pacify's Neutral. Of several on one entity, the highest Priority holds, a tie going to the latest, and the entity's own come back as the last ends. One that interrupts breaks what its target runs as it changes the side, landing or ending. An Instant effect doesn't last, so it changes nothing. An effect holds one at most. It was a field of the effect's own, with a switch. SideSet The side changes an entity is under, each from an effect that lasts: the sides the highest Priority gives, a tie to the latest, or none, where its own hold. SimpleScaler Simple level-based scaler that evaluates based on relative level. Uses the level values array for easy configuration. SingleCooldown The single cooldown, an ability's cooldown model where none of its components gives another: one use, spent as its Cooldown is applied, and back as the Cooldown ends, as its caster no longer carries the Cooldown's asset tag. SingleDurationEffectContainer The container of Stacks Share One Duration: one timer and one tick for every stack, which a stack added leaves as they are; each tick executes once for each stack. SkipAndMaintainInjection Skips the current stage but maintains it running in background. SkipStageInjection Skips the current stage and moves to the next. SoundCue Plays a sound where its placement says, as its moment comes, in whichever list it's in: on the one the cue is on, its source, an ability's target or each of its targets, or at the cue's point; attached, it follows them as it plays. SourceAttributeImpact The carrier of a change no effect's spec carries: a raw delta, an attribute's root value, a transfer's two sides, a rescale or a returned blow. It names its source, its attribute, its impact types and its retention group; one made over another carrier gives that one's origin, definition and context tags. IAttributeImpactCarrier.GenerateSourceDerivation makes one, and a change made every frame keeps one and hands the attribute system a new value over it each time, which allocates nothing. SourceEffectOrigin An origin that stands for an entity itself, for an effect the entity applies with no ability or item behind it: its source, definition, context tags, asset tag, level and sides are the entity's, and it's always active. IEffectOrigin.GenerateSourceDerivation makes one, as in gas.ApplyGameplayEffect(IEffectOrigin.GenerateSourceDerivation(gas), effect). SpreadEffectComponent Spread: spreads its effect, or another it names, from the one it's on to those near them, at the moments it names: as it lands, each tick, as it ends, or as the one it's on dies, as a plague jumps from its victim to the enemies near it. Each it takes gets the effect from the same origin, its caster's, so its modifiers and its chance to land are its own. A landing by spread spreads on only so far as its Hops allow. StackAmountOperation The stack behaviour Scaled Stack Amount: the stacks each application adds, the amount the behaviours before it settled on, from the effect's Stack Amount, combined with its Scaler, read against the effect, as its Operation says, and made whole by its Rounding. With no scaler, the amount stands. StackBoundsConfig The stack behaviour Stack Bounds: a Min and a Max of stacks, each read at the effect's level. A new container is given the Min as it's made, and no application takes the effect past the Max, more where a modifier raises it: one that would overflows, its Overflow Effects landing from its origin on the target or the caster, as Overflow Lands On says, with Deny Refresh On Overflow and Clear Stacks On Overflow saying what becomes of the effect's time and stacks. It applies after the other behaviours, so its bounds have the last word. StackQueueEffectContainer The container of Duration Taken From One Stack: one stack's timer runs at a time, and each time it runs out a stack is lost and the timer restarts, so its time left counts the stacks still waiting. Each tick executes once for each stack, and a stack added restarts the timer. StackingCurveKind A count through a stacking curve, then a number added: an item's stacks, an effect's stacks or an attribute, read as its curve says. Risk of Rain's items stack this way, and Dota's armor, so a number that reads stacks or armor needs no worker of its own. Plus 1 makes a share a multiplier. StacksChange Changes its stacks: more it can hold at most, and more a landing gives. StageBuilder Builds one stage of a sequence, handed to the action given to a builder's Stage, a stage's SubStage, or a branch's If and Default: its tasks (Task, Do, SyncTask, the delays and waits) and sub-stages, its policy (WhenAll, WhenAny, WhenN), its repeats, time limits and conditions, the injections it allows, whether it's critical, its name, and its handlers, OnInit, OnRepeat, OnTimeout, OnTerminate and the rest. StandardWorkerGroup A named group of workers that can be attached to entities, abilities, items, or attribute sets. Workers are disbursed to the appropriate subsystems when the owning asset is applied. StartingItemContainer One of an entity's Starting Items: the item, given as the entity's GAS initializes, and whether it's equipped as it's given. StaticTargetingPacket A targeting packet that holds its own position, rotation and scale, set as it's made and changed only through it: a point a click picked, a runtime entity's place, which whoever drives the entity keeps current, or a snapshot of a transform, or of another packet, whose entity, transform and direction it keeps. StopMaintainedAllInjection Stops all maintained stages. StopMaintainedAtIndexInjection Stops the maintained stage at a stage index. A stage that isn't maintained, the current one among them, is left alone. StopMaintainedLastInjection Stops the oldest maintained stage. SyncSequenceStage A stage containing one or more ISequenceTask instances driven synchronously. All tasks Step in parallel each frame; stage completes per its policy. SyncSequenceTaskBase Base class for sync-first sequence tasks (per-frame stepping). Step is abstract (must implement). Execute bridges automatically by looping Step with per-frame yields. SyncSequenceTaskLibrary Reusable synchronous building blocks for common gameplay operations. Each method returns an ISequenceTask that advances per-frame via Step(). Also usable in async sequences — the DelegateSyncTask.Execute bridge loops Step automatically. Designed for use with TaskSequenceBuilder. Usage: var runner = TaskSequenceBuilder.Create("Chase") .Stage(s => s .Task(SyncSeq.MoveTowards(chaser, target, 5f)) ) .BuildSyncRunner(); All timed tasks: Accept an optional AnimationCurve for easing (null = linear) Snap to the final value on completion to avoid float drift Handle zero/negative duration by completing immediately All tracking tasks (MoveTowards, LookAtTracking, etc.): Re-sample the target each frame for dynamic following Complete based on distance/condition, not duration SyncedTaskSequence Drives a list of synchronous sequence stages frame-by-frame. Uses the unified ISequenceTask interface (calls Step on each task). Designed to be called from a process's WhenUpdate. Usage: var runner = TaskSequenceBuilder.Create("MyRunner") .Stage(s => s.Task(...)) .BuildSyncRunner(); // In WhenUpdate, a step of its clock, or of a time given: if (runner.Step(data)) relay.Terminate(); SystemLevelsComponent An entity's levels, each under a tag: its own, under its identity's asset tag, and each of its abilities' and items', under theirs, registered as they're given. TrySetLevel and TryModifyLevel set or change one, as a hub's SetLevel and ModifyLevel do, and its Callbacks hear each change; an effect that reads a level reads it again as it changes. A hub's LevelSystem gives it. TagCache Manages tag state and tag workers for an entity. Supports hierarchical tag matching with O(1) exact lookups and O(n) hierarchical lookups. Tag worker activation/resolution is deferred to end-of-frame. TagCondition Whether the caster or the target holds a tag: counted by weight, so a tag granted twice counts twice, on either side. It reads the side it looks at, so a target's tag doesn't hold where there's no target. TagCue Plays what a cue tag routes to, in place of naming what it shows: the entity's own Cue Receiver's way, or the project's cue library's, as Unreal's GameplayCue tags play their notifies. Each burst, beginning and end it hears plays the tag's. TagListener A listener on one tag of an entity and the tags under it, as Listen(Tag, Action<TagChange>, ETagChangeKind) makes: it hears Status.Burning when it listens to Status. Dispose stops it. TagQuery Represents a query condition for a tag, with support for hierarchical matching. Used to validate whether an entity has/doesn't have certain tags. TagRegistry Runtime registry for hierarchical tags. Provides O(1) lookups for parent/child relationships by maintaining cached mappings. Thread-safe for read operations. Usage: Tags are automatically registered when created via Tag.Generate() Use TagHierarchy.GetChildren(), GetDescendants(), etc. for fast hierarchy queries Call TagHierarchy.Initialize() at game start to pre-populate from known tags TagRegistry.TagUtil Makes the names of unique tags. GenerateDeterministicTag makes a tag of a prefix and a text, padded to a fixed length of 32 to 64 characters from their SHA-256 hash, or cut to it, so the same text always gives the same tag, which reads as the text; Tag.GenerateAsUnique makes its tags so. GenerateUniqueRandomTag makes a random name that no registered tag has. TagWeightValidation A check that compares the checked entity's weight of its Tag with Weight, read at the ability's level, by Comparison, as combo points or stacks; an entity without the tag holds it at 0. Either list offers it. TagWorkerActivateAction Deferred action to activate a tag worker. TagWorkerRequirements A tag worker's requirements: its packets, each a tag and a weight the entity's must reach or stay under. The worker is active while every packet holds, and always where it has none. TagWorkerResolveAction Deferred action to resolve (deactivate) a tag worker. TaggedCueWatch An entity's While Tagged cues: each step, a tag the entity has taken on begins its cues, and one it has let go of ends them; as the entity ends, every one still playing ends. TaggedCues The lasting cues an entity plays while it holds a tag. Tags PlayForge's own tags, grouped by kind. Each is its text padded to 64 characters by a hash of it, a name every asset that uses the tag stores, so a text changed is another tag; a test pins each one's name and kind. Each is exposed to the editor's pickers for its kind. TargetAttributeCondition A single attribute condition used to filter auto-targeting candidates. Checks the target's current attribute value against a threshold. TargetAttributeRatioThresholdEffectWorker A threshold on an attribute's ratio, its Current to its Base, as below half its health: the ratio against Threshold's Current, whatever Target says, as a ratio has no other side. Its Base target compared Base to Base, which is always one; and with no Base there's no ratio, so no threshold is met. TargetAttributeThresholdEffectWorker The base of an effect worker that acts on each hit of its effect where an attribute meets a threshold: TargetAttribute on its context's System, which for a hit is the dealer, the effect's caster, its Current, its Base or both as Target says, compared with Threshold by Policy. Derive from it and override OnThresholdMet for the actions it queues; CanCompare and MeetsThreshold can be overridden too. TargetingPacket A targeting packet that follows a Transform: its position, rotation and scale are the transform's, read as they're asked for, and setting them moves it. The GameplayAbilitySystem component's GetTargetingPacket gives one on its own transform, with itself as the target. TaskSequence A reusable async task sequence that can be executed with a data packet. Wraps a TaskSequenceDefinition with execution capabilities. TaskSequenceBuilder Fluent builder for creating TaskSequence definitions. All delegate methods use SequenceDataPacket for direct sequence/stage control. TaskSequenceChain A chain of sequences that execute sequentially with shared data. Supports chain-level conditions, repeat, and interrupt. TaskSequenceDefinition The complete definition of a TaskSequence. Immutable after building. Can be reused across multiple runs. TaskSequenceMethodAttribute Marks a static method as a TaskSequence/TaskSequenceChain provider. TaskSequenceProcess Wraps a TaskSequence or TaskSequenceChain for execution via ProcessControl. Supports both async (SelfTerminating/RunThenWait) and sync (Synchronous) lifecycles. Async mode: RunProcess executes the sequence via Execute path. Sync mode: RunProcess is skipped; WhenUpdate drives the SyncedTaskSequence runner via Step path. Uses SequenceDataPacket for direct sequence/stage control. TaskSequenceRuntime Manages the runtime execution state of a TaskSequence. Created per-run, handles stage progression, injections, and cancellation. TemplateListSnapshot Stores the element identifiers of a list property at the time of last template sync. Used to detect additions/removals in the template for list merge logic. TextureItem One of an asset's Textures: a texture under a tag of the Texture Slot context. The texture under Primary is the asset's icon, and with none there, the first texture is. ThresholdAnalysisWorker Analysis worker that triggers callbacks based on attribute thresholds. ThresholdDebuggerEffectWorker An effect worker for debugging: on each hit of its effect where its threshold is met, as TargetAttributeThresholdEffectWorker checks it, it queues an action that logs so, with the effect's spec, through ForgeLog at Info. ThresholdScaler Returns values based on level thresholds. Useful for tier-based progression (e.g., Bronze/Silver/Gold ranks). Each tier's value and its default are numbers of any kind, as a share of the caster's attribute. A tier reads its number where the scaler is read, and the default with the scaler as its owner. ToggleAbilityComponent Toggle: an effect an ability turns on its caster with one use, paying its cost, and off with the next, starting its cooldown. It applies its ability's usage in the ability's place, waives the cost and the cooldown while its effect is on, so it can always turn off, and claims its effect as a Toggle's for a purge. As its holder forgets the ability, the effect comes off, where it stayed on. An ability holds one at most. TrackedImpact What a carrier's impacts came to: their total, the last of them, and how many. It kept a node for every impact on a list nothing walked, so an effect that ticked kept an allocation for every tick for as long as it lasted. TrackedImpactKind What an effect has dealt: its last impact, its total, or how many impacts, as each effect spec tracks them once they land, after workers, so a blow reads as it landed, after the target's armor. Whose: this effect, the one whose number it is, as a burn that grows each tick by its own count; an effect on the caster or the target, by its asset, its containers summed, as a combustion consuming a burn's total; or every effect there tagged with a tag, summed. An impact is signed, so damage is negative; BySize reads it as a size, as a heal of half a blow wants. Where nothing is tracked, as an effect that isn't on the target, it reads 0. At its first application an effect has dealt nothing: its last impact and total are 0, and so is its count. An effect's magnitude is worked out as it's applied and again at each tick, so a number on its own count reads the ticks so far. A save restores an effect's time and stacks but not what it has dealt, so after a load its tracked impact starts again at 0. TransferEffectComponent Transfer: moves an amount from an attribute of its effect's caster or target to one of either, as the effect lands, each tick, or while it lasts, giving back as it ends; only what the giver has moves. An effect holds as many as it moves, each its own. TurnToFaceAbilityComponent Turn To Face: how this ability turns its caster to face its target or its point before its first stage, in place of its entity's Turns To Face; or, with Turns off, that it doesn't, as a cast behind the caster doesn't. An ability holds one at most. TurnToFaceSettings How an ability's activation turns its caster to face its target or its point before its first stage. TurnsToFaceEntityComponent Turns To Face: every ability of the entity with a target or a point turns it to face it before its first stage, which starts once it's within the Start Angle; the turn goes on to the Facing Angle after. An ability with a Turn To Face of its own turns its own way, or not at all. An entity holds one at most. TypeDefaults A type's defaults: the asset a new one starts as a copy of, and the assets Import lists first. UnityClock Unity's time, the clock PlayForge reads unless another is put in. UnityEventAbilityTask A stage task that invokes its Events, each UnityEvent in turn, and ends at once. UnityRandom Unity's random numbers, the source PlayForge reads unless another is put in. UnscaledClock The game's time without its time scale, as the clock in force reads it: a sequence on it runs while the game is slowed or stopped, as a pause menu's or a hit-stop's own effects do. Its sequences wait for Unity's frames where the game's ticks would stand with the game's time. UnscaledClockChoice The game's time without its time scale: a sequence on it runs while the game is paused. UsesItemComponent Uses: how many times an item's ability can be used, each use one that paid what it costs, as a potion's sips or a wand's charges. With none left, one of the item goes: a stack of it, its uses whole again for the next, or the item with its last. A load gives its uses whole. An item holds one at most. ValidationSideAttribute Says which of an ability's checks a rule kind belongs among, and its picker offers it there alone. A kind that says none belongs among either. ValueBreakdown A run's stages, each with the value it took and gave and a note: what a combat log, a debugger and a test read of a hit. One is kept for each effect spec and filled again by each run. ValuePipeline A value through ordered stages as it lands. An effect names one as its impact's calculation, as an Unreal effect names its execution calculation, so each hit goes through the stages a project writes once: the caster's bonuses, those that read the target, a critical roll, the target's reductions, a barrier; and what comes out lands. A new item that changes every hit is a stage, not an edit to each attack. Generic: the value is any number an impact lands with, a blow, a heal, a drain. It isn't a Scaler asset. A scaler is a number worked out from its context, read wherever a number is; a pipeline transforms a value it's given, once, as it lands, with both sides known, and its stages can do what a number can't: roll once for the hit and keep it, route a part of it into a barrier, say what each did. It runs for what an impact commits: an instant impact's hit, each tick of a periodic one. A lasting impact's value is read again as its attribute changes, so nothing runs it. WaitForAttributeTask Waits for an attribute of its caster or its target to cross a value, as a berserk's next stage waits for its Health to fall under half. The value is read as it starts, at its ability's level; the attribute each step. WaitForEventTask Waits for a gameplay event sent to its caster or its target, by its tag or one under it, as a combo's next stage waits for its hit to connect. The core's own events, as Impact Taken, come while it waits, as the core sends them where anything listens. WaitForTagTask Waits for its caster or its target to gain a tag, or to lose it, as a stage waits for a stun to wear off. A tag already held counts as gained, and one not held as lost, so it waits for the state, not a change. WhenAllStagePolicy Stage completes when ALL tasks complete. WhenAnyStagePolicy Stage completes when ANY task completes. Cancels remaining tasks. WhenNStagePolicy Stage completes when N tasks complete. Cancels remaining tasks. WhereItDiedRespawnPlace Where the entity died. WorkerNumberKind A value a worker answers under a key: the number asks, and a worker that implements INumberWorker answers from what it knows, as how much health its effect's target has lost since the effect began. So work a number can't do alone goes to a worker, and the number reads the result: a curse whose every fourth tick deals a share of the damage its target took since it landed is one effect, with one worker. It asks the workers of the effect whose number it is, about that application of the effect, or the caster's or the target's own workers. The first worker that answers the key gives the value. Where none answers, as where the number isn't an effect's or the entity has no such worker, it reads its Default. Structs AbilityCallbackStatus What an ability system's callback is handed: the activation's Data and the ability it runs (Ability, its spec); for a stage's or a task's callback, the Stage and its Tasks, Task being the one a task's callback tells of; for an injection's, the Injection; and Success, which at an end says whether the task or the stage got there without being cancelled or failing, and for an injection whether it was taken. AbilityComponentContext What an ability's component hears a moment of its ability with. AbilitySystemComponent.AbilityActivationRequest A request to activate the ability in one slot of an entity's ability system, which CreateActivationRequest makes and TryActivateAbility takes: its slot (Index); the When Busy it's asked under (Policy), as its ability says unless the request names another; the Data it hands the activation, as a target an AI picked or set-by-caller magnitudes; how long it may wait in the input buffer (BufferWindow), below 0 for its ability's Buffer Window; and whether an ability still choosing its target gives way to it (CancelsTargeting), on as a player's press is, and off for a trigger's request and Activate At Start's. ActivationRefusal A refused activation: the ability, its slot, why, for a check, which, and in the check's own words, why. ActivationResult What came of a request to activate an ability: it started, waits in the input buffer, starts in the next frame, or was refused, and why. It reads as true where it wasn't refused. AttributeOverflowData Bounds policy for an attribute's Current and Base slots. The same instance is used both at runtime (via ApplyBounds()) and authoring time (the AttributeSetElement drawer clamps user input live) — all clamping flows through Clamp(AttributeValue) / the per-slot min/max helpers so policy semantics are defined once. Per-policy semantics: • Unlimited — no bounds. • ZeroToBase — Current ∈ [0, Base]; Base unbounded. • FloorToBase — Current ∈ [Floor.Current, Base]; Base ∈ [Floor.Base, +∞). • ZeroToCeil — Current ∈ [0, Ceil.Current]; Base ∈ [0, Ceil.Base]. • FloorToCeil — Current ∈ [Floor.Current, Ceil.Current]; Base ∈ [Floor.Base, Ceil.Base]. AttributeValue An attribute's two values as a pair: Base, the value it's measured against, and Current, the value in play, as a pool's maximum and what's left of it. An entity's attribute reads as one, and so do a change, a bound and a threshold; its operators work on both values at once, two are equal where each value is approximately, and Ratio, ClampedRatio and LerpedRatio read Current against Base. AvoidRequireTagGroup.ValidationResult Result of detailed validation showing which requirements failed. CachedMagnitudeModifierGroupMember One member of a cached Group, which joins an attribute set's kept numbers: its Calculation, a cached scaler, and how it joins the others, its RelativeOperation: added up, multiplied into the sum, dividing it, added on after as a flat bonus, or overriding them all. ChangeStep One step a change to an attribute took between being made and landing: an attribute worker's, before its commit or after it, inline or queued; a barrier's soak; or a gain's scaling; with the change before it and after. CombatLogEntry One entry of an entity's combat log: when, what kind, who else, the effect behind it, the attribute, the value before and the change, its run through its pipeline, its change as made and each step it took to land, and, for a hit, whether it killed. CompositeBehaviourPacket One application of a composite behaviour, an AbstractProxyTaskBehaviour, in one value: its Command tag, the Behaviour, the Caller that applies it, as an entity, and the User it acts on, as a shot aimed at that entity. Generate makes one. ContainedEffectPacket One of an effect's contained effects: the effect, the moment it lands at, as this one is applied, on each of its execute ticks or as it's removed, and whom it lands on, this one's target or its caster. It lands from this one's origin, with its set-by-caller magnitudes. ContainedEffects The contained effects of one policy, read from the packets as they are walked. ContainedEffects.Enumerator Walks the contained effects of one moment in place, each packet whose moment it is, as a foreach over ContainedEffects does; it allocates nothing. CueContext What a cue plays for: the entity it plays on, what raised it and why, and where. An effect's cue has its spec, and for a tick, how many executed; another's has its origin, as an ability's spec or an item's, and the activation's data where there is one. A lasting cue's beginning and its end share a key. CuePlace One place a cue plays at: where, which way, what it follows, and the entity it's at. CueRaise One raise of a list of cues, as a sink is asked of it: the cue, and what the list belongs to. CueSource What a raise's list of cues belongs to: an effect, an ability, an entity or an item, by its asset; a cue tag; or a game's own code. A network layer names it by the asset's ID, or the tag's, in place of the cues themselves. DataValue<T> The entries of one type under a data packet's key, as GetAll and TryGetAll give them: the first (Primary), the Last, one at random (Any), All of them or each once (AllDistinct), or by an EDataTarget, and it enumerates them. IsValid where it holds any. EffectChanges.ImpactStage A Value Pipeline stage a modifier's Change Impact adds to one application: the attribute whose impacts take it, every one where it names none, and the stage. An impact that commits runs it after its own pipeline; a lasting one takes it on its magnitude. EffectChanges.Packet An effect a modifier adds to one application: the moment it lands at, the effect, the rule that added it, which won't change it again, and whom it lands on, the target or the caster. An application's changes hold one for each contained effect a modifier adds, and one for each overflow effect, which lands as the application overflows. EffectComponentContext What an effect's component hears a moment of its effect with. EffectDurationRemaining How long an entity's effect under a tag has left: its total duration and the time remaining, and whether one was found, as GetLongestDurationFor gives them for the one of the longest duration that has the tag as its asset tag or grants it. An Infinite one gives float.MaxValue for both; Ratio is the share of it left. EffectWorkerContext Context for effect workers. EffectWorkerRun An effect's worker hearing one of its effect's moments, as the entity it ran on tells it. Told only where something listens, so a worker no one hears costs nothing more. EntityComponentContext What an entity's component hears a moment of its entity with. ForgeAssetCatalog.Entry One row of an Asset Catalog: the Id a save names an asset by, and the Asset. Where an ID or an asset repeats, the first row holds. ForgeLogEntry One message ForgeLog let through: its level, its system, the message, and whom it's about. ForgeProcessCost One of a frame's costliest processes in the Profiler's capture: its process ID, and the time its steps took in the frame, every timing's. GameplayEffectTags An effect's tags: its Asset Tag, by which the effect system finds it as it's applied again or removed, and which its target carries while it lasts; its Context Tags, which describe it and go with each change it makes, never applied to the entity; its Granted Tags, applied to its target while it's on; and the tags it cleanses (Removes Effects Tagged) and makes its target immune to (Blocks Effects Tagged). Names says whether an effect is tagged with a tag, or a child of one, by any of the three. GroupContribution One group's slice of an attribute's ActiveValue (see GetBreakdown()). ImpactData A change as it landed on an attribute: the Target it landed on, the Attribute, the SourcedModifier that made it, whose carrier names its source and its effect, the RealImpact, what the attribute's Current and Base changed by after workers, bounds and rounding, and the OldValue before it. Attribute callbacks, impact workers, an effect's Impact hook and the frame summary are each handed one; Ends marks a lasting modifier coming off, a change but no hit. ImpactDerivationContext The context tags a change carries, which workers can filter by: its origin's, OriginTags, and its effect's own, DerivationTags; All gives them in that order. A carrier with no effect behind it gives its source's alone. ImpactWorkerContext Context for impact workers. ImpactWorkerRun One of a hit's dealer's impact workers, run for the hit, as the dealer tells it. IntValuePair A whole value and a maximum, unclamped, as a level and its max level: SetLevel sets a level an entity keeps under a tag to one, and ModifyLevel adds one to it, the max first in each, so a level raised past the old max takes it. ToClamped gives it as an IntValuePairClamped. IntValuePairClamped A whole number held between a minimum and a maximum: every level PlayForge keeps is one, an entity's, an ability's or an item's under its tag, and so is the level an origin gives and a number reads. Setting CurrentValue clamps it, and moving a bound clamps it again; Ratio says where it stands between the two. ItemCallbackStatus What an item system's callback is handed: the item's slot (Container) and Spec, the item system, and whether what it tells succeeded (Success), as equipping an item already worn doesn't; Index, Item, Level and IsEquipped read the slot. ItemComponentContext What an item's component hears a moment of its item with. LevelCallbackStatus What a change to one of an entity's levels did, as its level system's callbacks and a hub's SetLevel and ModifyLevel report it: the level under its key, the level and max level before, and whether it took. IsLevelUp, IsLevelDown and the deltas compare before with after; Success is false where no level is under the key or nothing changed. LevelThreshold One tier of a Threshold number: the Level it starts at, the Value it reads from that level up, a number of any kind, and an optional TierName. Of the tiers at or below a level, the highest gives the value. MagnitudeModifierGroupMember One member of a Group number: its Calculation, a scaler or a kind of number, and how it joins the others, its RelativeOperation: added up, multiplied into the sum, dividing it, added on after as a flat bonus, or overriding them all. ModifiedAttributeValue A change to an attribute's Current and Base as two deltas, with no carrier behind it: SourcedModifiedAttributeValue.ToModified gives one. Combine, Negate and Multiply work on both deltas at once. NumberContext What a number is read against: what its site has. A kind of number reads it; it is the whole of a kind's API, so adding to it later breaks no kind. It offers the caster, the target and the level; the carrier, where there is one, and what it has dealt; the caller's magnitudes and Local Data, each by key; an attribute's value or a retention group's part of it, on either side, and through SystemOf(NumberSide) the effects there; the activation's data, where a task reads it; and the owner, the object the field belongs to. Has(NumberReads) says which of these this site provides. A site builds one with Of, from an effect spec, a container, an activation's data, a worker's context, an entity, a cue or a process, and reads its numbers through it: Range.Evaluate(NumberContext.Of(data)). A test builds one with For(ISource, ITarget, int, int). It is a struct, and a number read through it allocates nothing. ProcessRegistration A process's registration with ProcessControl, built a step at a time: what handles the process, the packet it carries, the ProcessControl that takes it, and, for a MonoBehaviour process, what makes its object. Register(AbstractRuntimeProcess) and its siblings start one, and Run() registers the process and starts it, as registering always has: var result = ProcessControl.Register(projectile).HandledBy(gas).With(data).Run(); if (!result) Debug.Log(result.Refusal); What isn't given takes its default. The handler follows the packet's run-time type: an ability's packet hands the process to its source, and any other to GameRoot, or to none in a world of its own, which reaches for nothing of the scene's. ProcessControl had 28 static Register overloads, and the argument's static type picked the handler, so an ability's packet passed as a SequenceDataPacket filed its sequence under GameRoot, and the sequence didn't end with its entity. Those overloads are wrappers of this now, marked obsolete, and go before the first Asset Store submission. ProcessRegistrationResult What a registration did: the relay of the process ProcessControl took, or why it refused it. It reads as true when the process was taken. A refused call returned false and a null relay, and said nothing of why. PurgeContext What a purge's filter reads an effect with. ReadOnlyListView<T> A read-only view of a list that foreach walks without allocating, through the list's own struct enumerator. Walked as an IEnumerable<T>, as any list's, the enumerator is boxed. SequenceEventContext Context passed to sequence event callbacks. SourcedModifiedAttributeValue A change to an attribute on its way through the attribute system: a Current and a Base, and the carrier it comes from, which names its source, its target, its impact types and its retention group. Code changes an attribute directly with one, through the entity's TryModifyAttribute: GenerateSimple makes a raw delta with no impact type, which workers take as they take an effect's change, and GenerateUnworkable one the system makes on its own account, unworkable, as ImpactIsWorkable says, so it counts as no hit. Over an effect's spec, the spec's impacters say what commits, and these values only travel with them. SystemComponentData A target's ability system and attribute system, each found once, as its ToGASComponentData gives them; a gameplay mono process keeps its origin's source's so. Either is null where the target has none. Tag Represents a gameplay tag with hierarchical support using dot notation. Example: "Status.Debuff.Burn" where "Status" is the root, "Debuff" is a child, and "Burn" is the leaf. TagAttributePair A role and the attribute it reads on a gameplay mono process's origin: one row of the process's Attribute Pairs, as ProjectileSpeed read from the caster's Projectile Speed. The process's own attribute in that role comes first (TryGetRole). TagChange A tag's weight on an entity changing: the tag, and its weight before and after, 0 when it isn't held. An event carries one as it happens; a compile, which rebuilds the tags from their sources, carries only what it changed. TagWorkerRequirementPacket One of a tag worker's requirements: a tag, whether the entity must carry it, Require, or must not, Avoid, and the weight that decides, read at the entity's level. Require holds while the tag's weight is at least RequiredWeight; Avoid while it's below. TaskSequenceReference Serializable reference to a TaskSequence method. ValueRun What a stage reads in a run: the hit's carrier, its number context, and the breakdown, if one's kept. ValueStep One stage's part of a run: what it took and what it gave, and a note. WorkerContext Context passed to workers during validation and execution. Provides access to the system, attribute cache, and current change value. Interfaces IAbilityProxyStagePolicy How a stage's tasks end it: the compiler maps each to a sequence's stage policy, Any to the first task's end and All to every task's (AbilitySequenceCompiler). The legacy execution that awaited one itself is gone. IAbilityReach How far from its caster an ability's target may be: a capability an ability's component implements, as Cast Range does. The targeting tasks that search from their caster, the Creator Lab's bots and a game's own code ask an ability's reach through ForgeReach, never the component, so a reach of your own is asked as Cast Range is. A component that reaches enforces its reach itself, as Cast Range refuses a target beyond it. IAbilityValidationRule A rule an ability's activation keeps, for its source or its target. It took the generic IValidationRule, which nothing else took; it declares its own Validate. A rule is a question, asked as often as the activation needs it answered: as it's requested, each frame a buffered request waits, and again once targeting has found its target, as the caster may have changed meanwhile. So a rule changes nothing and draws nothing: one that rolled a chance rolled it each time it was asked. Validate checks the entity getSource hands it: the caster among an ability's Caster Checks, the target among its Target Checks. Refused, it says why in error, as "Hale's Health, 80, isn't < 50". A kind says which of the two it belongs among with ValidationSideAttribute. IActiveSequence A sequence as code runs it, a TaskSequence or a TaskSequenceChain: Run runs it with a data packet, TryRun also says whether it finished, and IsCriticalSection whether its run is in a critical stage now. A TaskSequenceReference's GetActiveSequence gives one. IAffiliated What has sides: GetAffiliation gives its affiliation tags, as an entity's team or faction. Every target and every effect origin has them, and an effect's Affiliation compares its origin's with its target's. IAnalysisUser What holds analysis workers: GetAnalysisCache gives the cache a worker group gives its analysis workers to. Every GAS hub is one. IAttribute An attribute as the attribute system knows it: a name, a description and an icon, an abbreviation and its textures. The Attribute asset is one and a RuntimeAttribute made in code is another; an entity's attributes, an effect's impacts and workers each name one. IAttributeImpactCarrier Attribute impact carriers are sources of attribute impact (impact carriers) IAttributeImpacter A single magnitude-evaluation unit owned by an IAttributeImpactCarrier. One carrier may expose many impacters; the cached attribute aggregator walks them and applies their contributions in op-precedence order: Add — summed first → DirtyValue. Multiply — composed via MultiplyBehaviour. FlatBonus — added after multiplies. Override — wins (resolved by SortOrder). Reversal under recompute model — retained carriers reverse automatically when removed (Recompute simply walks the new shorter retention list). One-shot committed contributions persist via CachedAttributeValue.committedOneShotDelta and are reversed only by an explicit synthetic-carrier rollback (see GameplayEffectImpact.ReverseImpactOnRemoval). IAuraComponent A component that holds an aura: its holder's effect on those near it. ICameraShaker The game's camera, which a camera shake cue asks to shake. ICarrierApplication The "applicable" facet of a carrier — duration, container generation, contained effects, worker phases, validation. ITarget exposes its application surface against this interface (not against a concrete GameplayEffectSpec) so any future carrier kind that participates in the apply-shelf pipeline can plug in without subclassing the spec. Plain IAttributeImpactCarriers — synthetic deltas, leveler snapshots, nullified markers — intentionally do NOT implement this interface. They are identity + magnitude only; forcing them to expose duration policy or worker hooks would be lying about their lifecycle. IComponentValidationRule A check an ability's component stands behind, whatever the component's kind. ICooldownModel How an ability's uses come back: how many it holds, how many are in hand, and what a use spends. A capability an ability's component implements, as Charges does; with none, an ability has SingleCooldown, one use, back as its Cooldown ends. The Cooldown check asks it what's in hand, an ability spends a use through it as it commits, and a HUD reads it through CooldownModel, whatever the ability's components are. IEffectOrigin Sources of Gameplay Effects IForgeClock A source of time, which PlayForge's runtime reads instead of Unity's Time. The default reads Unity's; a test, a replay or a server puts one of its own in with Use(IForgeClock). A sequence or a packet can name one of its own too (Clock, WithClock(IForgeClock)), as a menu's runs on UnscaledClock. IForgeEntityIds Names the entities a save refers to besides the one it's of: the source of an effect another entity applied. A game keeps IDs that last across sessions, as a reference doesn't. IForgeInput What click targeting reads of the player's input: whether a pointer's button went down this frame, and the ray the pointer aims along. The defaults read a mouse, a pen or a touch through a camera; a game with a gamepad's reticle, a controller's ray or input of its own puts its own in with Use(IForgeInput). The Creator Lab and the task sequence libraries' waits read the keys and the pointer through it too. IForgeMover A game's own mover, as the Creator Lab's units are, which PlayForge's movement tasks tell what they do: a Dash holds it while it moves its entity, and a Blink stops it after it puts its entity elsewhere, so it drops the path it was on. A component on the entity's object that implements it hears; an entity without one moves as the task puts it. IForgeRandom A source of random numbers, which PlayForge's runtime reads instead of UnityEngine.Random. The default reads Unity's, so Random.InitState still seeds it; SeededRandom is one of its own. IForgeTurner A game's own turner, on an entity's object: it turns its character itself, by its animation or its controller, as each step of a turn PlayForge orders asks, in place of PlayForge, which sets the entity's facing straight. PlayForge reads how far is left to turn from the entity's facing, its object's rotation, so that's what the turner turns. IGameplayAbilitySystem An entity's gameplay ability system as code meets it, whichever hub runs it: the GameplayAbilitySystem component on a GameObject or a RuntimeGameplayAbilitySystem made in code. Through it code reaches the entity's attribute, ability, item and effect systems, its tags, levels and effects, its callbacks, clock, services and Local Data, and its turning, death and revival; ToGASObject gives the component, where there is one. Code that works with any entity takes one. IGameplayProcess A process as ProcessControl runs it: the packet and relay it's handed as it registers (SendProcessData), its hooks as it initializes, waits, terminates and is destroyed, its steps at its timing (WhenUpdate, WhenLateUpdate, WhenFixedUpdate), the run ProcessControl awaits (RunProcess), and whether it keeps its run through a pause (TryHandlePause, TryHandleResume). It's a process handler too, so the processes registered under it end with it. AbstractMonoProcess and AbstractRuntimeProcess implement it, and a process of your own derives from one of them. IGameplayProcessHandler What a process is registered under, its handler: what the process belongs to, as a GAS hub, ProcessControl, a data packet or another process. It keeps the relays of the processes it handles (GetRelays), which ProcessControl subscribes as each registers and voids as each is removed, and gives the instantiator that makes the object of a mono process that uses its handler's (GetInstantiator). A process, a hub among them, ends what it handles as it ends. IHasIntentToTarget What can be aimed at a target and turned to another, as a homing projectile, AbstractTargetedMonoProcess, is: SetTarget gives it the target and its targeting packet. A disjoint turns the shots aimed at an entity, through it, to where the entity stood. IHasReadableDefinition What has a name, a description and an icon to show: GetName, GetDescription and GetDefaultIcon. Every PlayForge asset, an attribute, a tag and every target, a GAS hub among them, is one, and an origin or a carrier gives the one behind it through GetReadableDefinition, as a combat log names what dealt a hit. IHasTextures What holds textures under tags, as an asset's Textures: an ability, an item, an effect, an entity or a running one. An effect that inherits its texture takes its origin's under a tag. ILevelProvider Interface for assets that can provide level information to linked effects. Implemented by Ability and EntityIdentity to support "Lock to Source" level mode. When a GameplayEffect is linked to an ILevelProvider, the effect's modifiers can derive their MaxLevel from the provider, ensuring consistent scaling. Common use cases: Ability Cost effect linked to its parent Ability Ability Cooldown effect linked to its parent Ability Entity-specific effects linked to EntityIdentity ILocalDataSource What holds Local Data rows, which GetLocalData gives: every PlayForge asset, and a runtime entity's identity. A GAS loads its identity's rows into a store of its own as it initializes, and a number that reads Local Data reads the rows of what it belongs to. ILocalDataUser What keeps Local Data of its own at runtime, as a GAS hub does: InitLocalData loads a source's rows, SetLocalData and TryGetLocalData write and read a value by its key, and GetLocalDataStructure gives the store itself. Code and workers read and write an entity's Local Data through it, as a threshold analysis worker notes there that it has fired. IManagerial Marks PlayForge's managers, ProcessControl and GameRoot, which a Bootstrapper brings up: Bootstrap makes the one it's called on the one instance, or destroys it where another is already. A manager that is a GAS, GameRoot, isn't one of the game's entities: area searches pass it by, and the Mono Entities counter leaves it out. INumberWorker A worker that answers numbers: a number of the Worker kind, or an Asset Part number's Worker Value, asks it for a value under a key, and it answers from what it knows, as how much health its effect's target has lost since the effect began. Any worker can implement it: an effect's workers answer about their effect, and an entity's workers, those its worker groups give it, about the entity. Every number field can ask, so a worker can drive an effect's magnitude, a task's range, a threshold or a cue's parameter. The context it's asked in is what it's asked about: for an effect's worker, the effect's own context, whose Carrier is the effect's spec, where its state for that application is (GetWorkerState<T>(AbstractEffectWorker)); for an entity's worker, the asking number's context. It answers false for a key it doesn't know, and the asker reads its default. IPooledCue What a pooled cue object does as its pool hands it out and takes it back, as Unreal's cue actors recycle: a MonoBehaviour on the prefab resets itself here, as a particle system that plays again from the start. IProxyTaskBehaviourCaller The system calling the composite behaviour IProxyTaskBehaviourUser What a composite behaviour, an AbstractProxyTaskBehaviour, acts on: something with a process's data (Data), which the behaviour reads, as a disjoint reads whether a shot aimed at its caster is marked disjointable. Every IProxyTaskBehaviourCaller, which applies a behaviour to others, is one: the processes made from AbstractMonoProcess and AbstractRuntimeProcess, and each GAS hub. IRootAction Interface for deferred actions that execute at end-of-frame. Actions can be invalidated (e.g., effect removed) before execution. IScaler What works out a number for a carrier, an effect's spec or another: Initialize as the carrier is made, which can capture what the number needs, then Evaluate each time it's read. Every AbstractScaler is one, and a carrier keeps what a scaler captures under the scaler. Generate makes a CustomScaler from two delegates, or, given none, one that reads how far up its range the origin's level is, from 0 to 1. ISequenceInjection An action that can modify sequence execution at runtime. ISequenceStagePolicy Determines how a stage completes based on its tasks. ISequenceTask Unified interface for tasks that can be executed within a TaskSequence. Supports both async execution (via Execute) and synchronous per-frame stepping (via Step). Task authors implement whichever path(s) their task will be used under. ISource An entity as the source of what it does: a target that is also an effect origin of its own and a handler of the processes it runs, with the tag cache, action queue and frame summary its workers use. Every GAS hub is one, and an effect's source is the entity behind its origin. SetLevel and ModifyLevel change a level it keeps under a tag, its own under its asset tag, and GetLongestDurationFor reads how long its longest effect under a tag has left, as a cooldown. ITagHandler The tag side of an entity, as a GAS hub's: the tags it holds (GetAppliedTags), how many times a tag is granted (GetTagWeight, which a hub gives as −1 for a tag it doesn't hold), whether a tag query holds of it (QueryTags), and a rebuild of its tags from what grants them (CompileGrantedTags). Every target is one, and a tag worker checks its requirements against it. ITagSource What grants tags: GetGrantedTags gives the tags it grants the entity that holds it, as an ability held grants its passive tags and, while it runs, its active ones. Every PlayForge asset is one, as are the containers of an entity's effects and abilities; an entity's tags are built from what its sources grant. ITarget What an effect can land on: an entity, with its sides, its tags and a definition to show. It makes, applies and removes effects (GenerateEffectSpec, ApplyGameplayEffect, RemoveGameplayEffect), reads and changes its attributes, reads its levels, finds its subsystems, and says whether it's dead. Every GAS hub is one, and so is a stand-in, as the placeholder a disjointed shot is aimed at. IWorkerGroupSource What gives an entity workers through its worker group: InitWorkers gives them, and RemoveWorkers takes them back. An entity's identity and its attribute set give theirs as it initializes, an ability while the entity has it, and an item while it's equipped. Enums AbstractAttributeWorker.EChangeEventTiming Timing options for attribute workers. CreateMonoProcessAbilityTask.ESpawnPoint Where a spawned process appears. EAbilityActivationPolicy What an activation does while another ability holds its claim, the When Busy the inspectors show. Activate Anyway (AlwaysActivate) starts at once; Refuse (ActivateIfIdle) is refused, as Busy, while another ability asked under Refuse holds its claim; Queue (QueueActivationIfBusy) waits in the input buffer, for up to its Buffer Window, while a Queue ability holds its claim or a running stage blocks it. Whatever the choice, an ability with critical tasks can't start while another with critical tasks holds its claim. An entity's When Busy is one, and so is each activation request's Policy. EAbilityActivationPolicyExtended An ability's When Busy as its Definition holds it: Entity's Policy (UseLocalPolicy), the default, takes its entity's When Busy, and the others are the EAbilityActivationPolicy choices, Activate Anyway, Refuse and Queue. TryActivateAbility and CreateActivationRequest can name one in place of the ability's. EAbilityEffectRole How an effect participates in an ability. EAbilityEnd How an ability's activation ended. EAbilityLinkMode Defines how an ability is linked to its level provider. EAbilityPart What an Asset Part number reads of an ability. EAbilityStageConditionSubject Where a stage's condition looks for its tag. EAbilityTriggerSource What sets an ability off on its own. EActionStatus How a composite behaviour's run on one user came out, as its Status reads it: Success; Pending, not yet done; Failure, refused by its checks, as a shot not marked disjointable; Error, as with a caller that isn't an entity; NoData, nothing recorded for the user; or NoOp, nothing done, as for a shot whose data says nothing of being disjointable. EActivationRefusal Why an activation was refused, or None where it wasn't: it activated, waits in the input buffer, or starts next frame. A refused activation said only false. EActivationStatus What came of a request to activate an ability. EAddBehaviour How an Add impacter combines with the others on its attribute. EAffiliationFilter Whom a search or a check takes, by how each stands to its caster, or to an aura's holder: an enemy shares none of its sides, an ally shares one, and the caster itself is an ally of itself and no one's enemy. The one choice an Area Effect, an effect's area, a spread, an aura, the auto-target tasks and an Affiliation check make. A caster with no sides takes every other one as its ally and its enemy alike. EAffiliationPolicy Which targets an effect may land on, by their affiliation tags against its origin's: Always Allow, the default, takes any; Affiliated, those that share the origin's sides; Unaffiliated, those that don't; Use Affiliation List, those that carry the effect's own Affiliations. The impact's Comparison says whether one tag matching does or every tag must, and a target it doesn't take refuses the effect. EAnyAllPolicy How a list of tags is matched against another: Any passes where one of its tags is in the other, All only where every one is. An effect's Affiliation Comparison is one, and so is the Context Matching Policy of a focused attribute worker and of a context impact worker. EApplyTickRemove The moment in an effect's life another effect lands at: as it's applied (On Apply), on each of its execute ticks (On Tick), or as it's removed (On Remove). A contained effect and an effect a modifier adds each name one; an Instant effect has no ticks and no removal, so only its On Apply ones land. EAreaCentre Where an area search is measured from. EAssetPartAmong How an Asset Part number reads one value from several that match. EAssetPartOf What an Asset Part number looks for on an entity. EAttributeChangeWhat What an Attribute Change worker answers about its attribute. EAttributeElementCollisionPolicy An attribute set element's Collision: the group it joins where its attribute appears in more than one element across a set and its sub-sets. One group decides the attribute's root, the first there is of Use Set Collision Setting, Use This, Combine and Use Existing, and the other groups' elements are passed over: Combine adds its elements' values up, and each other group picks one, or averages them, by the Resolution Policy of the set the entity names. EAttributeOverflowPolicy The bounds an attribute set element holds its attribute's values in, with its Floor and Ceiling, each a Current and a Base: Zero To Base holds Current between 0 and Base; Floor To Base, Current between the Floor's Current and Base, and Base at or above the Floor's Base; Zero To Ceil, each between 0 and the Ceiling's; Floor To Ceil, each between its Floor and its Ceiling; Unlimited, none. They hold only while the element's Auto Clamp is on. EAttributeRead How × Attribute reads its attribute. EAttributeRole What an attribute is, which sets how bonuses to it add up and how a number reads it by default, as how several effects' Damage Amplification adds up and how an attack's scaler reads it. An effect's impact can add up its own way, and a number can read it its own way. EAttributeRoundingPolicy How an attribute set element rounds its attribute's Current and Base, after its bounds, each time the value changes: None; To Floor, down; To Ceil, up; Round, to the nearest; Snap To, to the nearest multiple of its Snap Interval. Rounding can make a change bigger or smaller than its effect asked for. EAttributeSetLinkMode Defines how an AttributeSet's level range is sourced. EAttributeTarget Which of an attribute's two values a change goes to: its Current, its Base, or both. An effect's impact names one with its operation, as Add to Current or Multiply Base, and a transfer's Slot and a threshold effect worker's Target choose by it too. EAttributeTargetBinary The part of an attribute's value something reads: its Current, its Base, what's missing of it (base − current), or its share (current ÷ base), as AttributeParts.Read reads it. A Threshold, a wait, the Attribute condition and an attribute-backed number read through it; some fields, as a tracked impact's part or a retention group's, read Base under Base and Current otherwise. EAttributeTargetExpanded Which of an attribute's values a change must touch for a worker to take it: Current, Base, Current And Base, or Current Or Base. A focused attribute worker's Target Modification and a context impact worker's Impact Target choose by it; with their exclusive switch on, a change to Current or to Base must touch that one alone. EAttributeTargetLimited A narrower EAttributeTarget, of the two choices that change Base: Current and Base together, or Base alone. ForgeHelper.Translate gives the EAttributeTarget it names. EAutoTargetMode How an auto-targeting task, Auto Target or Auto Target By Affinity, orders the entities it finds before it takes its Max Targets, the first being its primary target: Nearest or Farthest first, measured from where its range is, or in a Random order; All leaves them as found. Max Targets still holds under All, and 0 takes every one. ECalculationOperation How a change applies its magnitude to an attribute's value: Add adds it, Multiply multiplies by it, FlatBonus adds it after the multipliers, so they don't scale it, and Override sets the value to it. An attribute's lasting modifiers apply in that order, and of several overrides of one value the lowest order wins. An effect's impact chooses one as its Operation, and some workers do. ECaptureAttributeWhen When a × Attribute scaler reads its attribute: OnCreation captures it once, as the effect's spec is made, and reads that snapshot after; OnApplication reads the live value each time the scaler is read. EChangeStepKind What a step of a change to an attribute was. ECombatLogKind What a combat log entry is. ECombatLogRecords What an entity's combat log writes, as the project subscribes to it. EComparisonOperator How one number compares with another: less than, less or equal, equal, not equal, greater or equal, or greater than. A tag query compares the tag's count with its number by it, and conditions, validation rules, waits, auto-targeting and the threshold effect worker compare their numbers by it. ECrowdControlStops What a crowd control rule stops. ECueAt Whom a cue places what it plays on. ECueAttach Whether what a cue places follows what it's placed at. ECueEvent How a cue plays: a burst, or a lasting cue's beginning or its end. ECueFacing Which way what a cue places faces. ECueMoment What raised a cue: one of an effect's moments, an ability's, an entity's or an item's, or a game's own code. ECueSource What a raise's list of cues belongs to. ECurveTangentMode Runtime-safe mirror of the editor tangent modes used by scaler curves. EDataTarget Which entry under a data packet's key a read takes where the key holds several: Primary, the first; Any, one at random; or Last, the last. EDeathPolicy What an entity's death does. EEffectCategory The kinds of effect a death can keep whatever their tiers. EEffectDurationPolicy How long an effect lives: Instant, the default, makes its change once and is done; Durational stays on the target's shelf for its Duration; Infinite stays until something removes it. It gives the effect's first impact its delivery: on applying for an Instant effect, and for a lasting one while it lasts, or on each tick where it ticks. EEffectInteractionPolicy What a lasting effect on the target does with its time as it takes in an application under Do Nothing, Replace Existing or Stack Existing: Do Nothing, the default, leaves it; Refresh Duration restarts it; Extend Duration adds the new application's duration to it, or, where stacks keep their own durations, adds a stack. Refresh and Extend run Tick On Application again. EEffectJournalKind What an effect journal's entry tells. EEffectLinkMode Defines how an effect is linked to its level provider. EEffectPart What an Asset Part number reads of an effect. EEffectReApplicationPolicy What a Durational or Infinite effect does as it's applied to a target that has it already, matched by its asset tag whoever applied it: Add Another, the default, adds a container of its own; Do Nothing takes nothing new in; Replace Existing gives the old container the new application's values and modifiers, keeping its stacks and past commits; Stack Existing adds stacks to it. All but Add Another then do with its time as the effect's EEffectInteractionPolicy says. EEffectRecipient Whom an effect another lands lands on: a contained effect, an overflow's, or one a modifier adds. EEffectRefusal Why an effect didn't land on an entity, as the entity's callbacks tell it. EEffectStackPolicy How the stacks of an effect whose Re-application is Stack Existing keep time: Stacks Share One Duration, the default, runs one timer for all, which a stack added doesn't reset, each tick executing once for each stack; Stacks Have Independent Durations gives each stack its own timer and ticks, so they drop off one at a time; Duration Taken From One Stack runs one stack's timer at a time, a stack lost and the timer restarted each time it runs out. EEffectTargetScope Who an effect application lands on, as statically determinable. EEffectWorkerHook The moment of its effect an effect worker heard. EEventRecipient Whom a Send Event task sends to: its caster, or each of its activation's targets. EFacingCheck Which way a Facing check looks. EFloatingValue Where a floating text's number comes from. EFromSelfSource Where a relative attribute worker reads its relative attribute: From Self, on the entity whose attribute changes; From Source, on the source of the change. EGroupOperation How a Group's member joins the others: an impact's four operations, in their order, so a member saved before keeps its meaning, and Divide. EGroupOverflowPolicy What happens when a new member tries to join a full group. EImpactDelivery How an impact entry rides its carrier's lifecycle. Delivery IMPLIES the contribution kind — there is deliberately no independent "retained?" switch to get wrong: Continuous → Modifier (transient, derived). Registered while the carrier is present, re-evaluated on every recompute, reversed automatically and exactly when the carrier is removed. Only valid on durational/infinite carriers. OnApply → Commit (permanent). One commit at application time. Never reversed. This is what an Instant effect is. Periodic → Commit (permanent) once per execute tick. Never reversed. Requires a carrier with periodic ticks enabled. EItemLinkMode Defines how an item is linked to its level provider. EItemPart What an Asset Part number reads of an item.
