EJournalActionState Where an action a worker queued stands. ELevelConfig The level range a scaler's values spread over, where they spread: the level provider's (LockToLevelProvider, Provider's Levels), the scaler's own Max Level (Unlocked, Own Max Level), or the provider's up to that Max Level (Clamped, Clamped to Provider), so the values reach their last at the lower of the two. ELocalDataFrom Whose Local Data a Local Data number reads. EMagnitudeOperation How a field joins its number with its scaler, its Combine: Multiply With Scaler, the scaler times the number; Add Scaler, the scaler plus the number; Use Magnitude, the number alone; Use Scaler, the scaler alone. A number field, an attribute set element's sides, an effect's clock and Scaled Stack Amount each combine by it. EMathApplicationPolicy How a value is used as a factor: AsIs as it is, OnePlus as 1 + x, and OneMinus as 1 − x, so a 30% bonus multiplies by 1.3 and a 30% reduction by 0.7. An Attenuate scaler behaviour's Policy turns its value so, and a Math attribute worker's Operation Policy the attribute it changes by. EModifierDirection Which effects a modifier changes: those its holder applies, those landing on it, or both. EMultiplyBehaviour How a Multiply impact combines with the other multiplies on the same value of its attribute: Multiplicative, the default, compounds them, ×1.5 and ×1.5 making ×2.25; Additive Bonus adds each one's bonus, its value less 1, and multiplies once, +50% and +50% making ×2.0. It's apart from stacking, which decides how one effect applied again stacks against itself. EOnHitTo Whom an On Hit's effects land on. EProcessAttributeStart Where a process's own attribute starts. EProcessControlState What ProcessControl does as a whole: Ready takes new processes and runs them; Waiting takes them and holds every process where it is; Closed takes no more and runs those it has; ClosedWaiting takes no more and holds those it has; Terminated ends every process, a running one as its run ends, and TerminatedImmediately ends them all at once, and neither takes more. SetControlState sets it, and leaving a waiting state sends back what it held; the inspector's Start State is the one it starts in. EProcessLifecycle How a process starts and what follows its run: SelfTerminating starts running and ends as its run is done, as a projectile; RunThenWait starts running and waits when its run is done, to run again, as an ability; RequiresControl starts waiting and runs only when told, as an ability on a key; and Synchronous starts running with no run to await, stepped at its timing for as long as it lasts, as a health bar. EProcessRegistrationRefusal Why ProcessControl refused a registration, or None when it took the process. EProcessState Where a registered process is in its life: Created, as it's registered and set up, before its first move; Running; Waiting, paused or waiting to run again; and Terminated, ended and cleaned up. A relay's State reads it, and the process's lifecycle and ProcessControl's state decide each move. EProcessStatus Whether a process is stepped or its run awaited, as its wrapper's Status says: Synchronous for a process of the Synchronous lifecycle, Asynchronous for any other, and Unknown where the wrapper doesn't say. EProcessStepPriorityMethod Where a process steps among the others of its timing: First, at priority 0; Last, after every other; or Manual, at its own step priority. Lower priorities step first, and ProcessControl registers a scene's own processes by it too, parents before their children. EProcessStepTiming Which of Unity's loops a process is stepped in while it runs, each step calling its WhenUpdate, WhenLateUpdate or WhenFixedUpdate: one of Update, LateUpdate and FixedUpdate, two of them, all three, or None, never stepped. A GAS hub steps in Update and LateUpdate: Update ticks its effects, and LateUpdate runs its end of frame. Under ProcessControl's Fixed Tick Rate, each tick steps the Update and LateUpdate processes. EPurgeRelation Whom a purge takes the effects of, by who applied each, against the one purged. ERequireAvoidPolicy Which way a tag worker's requirement holds: Require, while the tag's weight on the entity is at least the required weight; Avoid, while it's below it. ERetentionGroupRead Which of an attribute's retention groups a read takes. ERoundingOperation How a whole-number field, a ScalableInt, makes a value read through its scaler whole: Floor rounds it down, Ceil up, and Round to the nearest, a half away from zero. Scaled Stack Amount rounds its stacks by it too. ESavedOrigin The kinds of origin a save tells apart. EScalerInterpolation How a scaler whose values spread over levels reads a level between two of its points: Constant steps from one to the next (Steps), Linear goes in a straight line (Straight Line), and Smooth along a smooth curve (Smooth Curve). EScalerParts The parts of every scaler a kind reads, which its inspector draws (Parts). EScalerRelativeOperation How a cached attribute-backed scaler joins the attribute it captures with its own value at the level: Add adds them, Multiply multiplies them, and UseAttributeValue and UseScalerValue take one alone. ESideSource Whose sides a side-changing effect gives its target. ESignPolicy The sign of a change or a value: Positive, Negative, ZeroBiased, 0 from values that cancel out, or ZeroNeutral, 0 from nothing at all. ForgeHelper.SignPolicy reads it from magnitudes and an attribute change's SignPolicy gives it; a context impact worker takes impacts of one sign (Impact Sign) and gives its own change one (Work Sign Policy). ESignPolicyExtended A sign policy with Any, which every sign matches: a focused attribute worker's Sign Policy, the sign of the changes it watches, is one. ESourceTarget Which side's attribute is read: the Source, whose effect or impact it is, or the Target. A × Attribute scaler's Capture From chooses one, as does a RelativeOperationContextImpactWorker's With Respect To. ESpreadMoment The moments a Spread component spreads at. EStackBoundsOnMaxPolicy What Stack Bounds does as an application finds the effect at its Max: Do Nothing, the default, keeps to the one effect, held at its Max; Append New Container stacks it into a container of the effect under its Max, or else a new one, which stacks again. EStackingCurve How a stacking curve turns a count into its number, with its a. EStopImpacts What a Block or Evade stage can stop. ESyncStagePolicy Completion policy for synchronous stages. ETagChangeKind What a tag listener hears. ETagMatchMode Mode for matching tags in queries. ETagWait What a Wait For Tag task waits for: its tag gained, or lost. EThresholdComparison How a Threshold analysis worker compares what it reads with its threshold while its Crossing is While It Holds: less than, less than or equal, greater than, greater than or equal, or equal, within 0.001. EThresholdCrossing As a threshold fires. EThresholdSource Whom a threshold's effects come from. ETrackedImpactOf Whose impacts a Tracked Impact number reads. ETrackedImpactPart What a Tracked Impact number reads of what effects have dealt. ETriggerImpactSign Which way an impact goes, for a trigger that takes impact events. ETriggerTarget What an ability a trigger sets off targets. ETurnTooLong What a turn to face a target does when reaching its Start Angle takes longer than its Max Wait. EUsageCheck The checks of an ability's use a component may waive, Waives(AbilityComponentContext): its cost, as the Cost check asks, and its cooldown, as the Cooldown check asks. EValidationSide Which of an ability's checks a rule belongs among: its Caster Checks, its Target Checks, or either. EValueCollisionPolicy Which value stands where several claim one result: the highest (UseMaximum), the lowest, their average, the first or the last, or none of them (Ignore). A Group's policy picks among its overriding members, Ignore setting them aside so the rest join as they would; an attribute set's Resolution Policy picks among the elements that give one attribute, Ignore keeping the first. EWhileTargeting What an ability still choosing its target does as another of its entity's abilities activates, past that one's own checks, on a request that cancels targeting (CancelsTargeting), as a player's press does: the While Targeting the inspectors show. Entity's Rule (EntitysRule) does as its entity's Targeting Yields says; Yields gives way, its targeting cancelled, nothing of it paid, and its claim let go at once, so the other starts; Holds keeps its claim until its target is chosen or it's cancelled, and the other does as its When Busy says. EWorkerExecution Defines how a worker executes during the modification pipeline. EWorkerNumberFrom Whose workers a Worker number asks. EWorkerSide Whose side a worker ran on: the entity its effect is on, or the one that dealt the hit, as an effect's workers hear its hits on their dealer's side and impact workers run for their dealer. ForgeLog.ELevel How much a message matters: Verbose, chatty lifecycle traces, then Info, Warning and Error. A message is let through at its system's level or above, and None, as a level, lets nothing through, framework errors included. ForgeLog.ESystem The part of PlayForge a message is of, each able to take a level of its own. NumberReads What a number field's context provides: what a site has for its numbers to read, which Has(NumberReads) tests, what a kind needs (Reads), and what a field declares (NumberContextAttribute). NumberSide Which of a context's two entities a read is about. SyncedTaskSequence.ERunnerState Where a synced runner is, as its State says: Ready, built or reset and not stepped since; Running; Completed, every stage done; or Interrupted. A step of a Completed or Interrupted runner does nothing and returns true, and a repeating runner goes back to Ready after each round. Delegates AbilitySystemCallbacks.AbilityRefusedDelegate A refused activation, with why it was refused. AbilitySystemCallbacks.AbilitySystemCallbackDelegate The handler of an ability system's callbacks on its abilities' runs, handed an AbilityCallbackStatus: OnAbilityActivate as an activation takes its claim, before its targeting; OnAbilityClaimReleased as it lets the claim go; OnAbilityEnd as it ends; OnAbilityStageActivate and OnAbilityStageEnd for each stage; OnAbilityTaskActivate and OnAbilityTaskEnd for each task; and OnAbilityInjection for an injection sent into it. AbilitySystemCallbacks.GameplayEventDelegate A gameplay event the entity was sent, with its data. ActionQueue.ActionCallback A listener of an action in the queue, handed the action: OnActionQueued hears it as it's queued, OnActionExecuted as it runs, and OnActionInvalidated as it's dropped unrun. An action the system makes for itself, as a rescale, is used again once the queue has run it, so read it during the call. ActionQueue.ActionFailedCallback A listener of an action that failed: its IsValid or its Execute threw error. AttributeSystemCallbacks.AttributeChangeDelegate A change on its way through the pipeline. It's reused once its commit is done, so read it during the call or copy its Value; don't keep it. AttributeSystemCallbacks.AttributeDelegate A listener of an attribute coming or going, handed the attribute: OnAttributeRegister hears each attribute the entity's attribute system takes, as its set is built, and OnAttributeUnregister each it removes. AttributeSystemCallbacks.AttributeImpactDelegate A listener of a change that has landed on an attribute, handed its ImpactData: the entity, the attribute, what it changed by after workers, bounds and rounding, its value before, and the change that did it. OnAttributeChanged, OnAttributeIncreased and OnAttributeReduced take one. AttributeSystemCallbacks.AttributeStateDelegate A listener of an attribute's Current emptying or filling, handed the attribute: OnAttributeCurrentZero hears a change to its Current that leaves it at 0, and OnAttributeCurrentFull one that leaves it at its Base, each as its share of its Base reads. AttributeSystemCallbacks.AttributeValueChangeDelegate A listener of an attribute's value changing, handed the attribute and its value before and after the change: OnAttributeBaseChanged hears each change that moves its Base. ForgeCues.CuePlayedDelegate A listener of ForgeCues.Played, invoked as each cue plays, after its handler, handed whether it bursts, begins or ends, the handler, and the cue's context: what raised it, who's behind it and where it plays. GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.ActionFailedDelegate Invoked when an action fails as its turn comes: its IsValid or its Execute threw. It's written to the Console too, and the rest of the queue runs on. GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.ActionQueuedDelegate Invoked when an action is queued for deferred execution. An action the system makes for itself, such as a rescale or a lifesteal's heal, is used again once the queue has run it, so read it during the call. GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.ChangeStepDelegate A step a change to one of this entity's attributes took, as it was taken: an attribute worker's, a barrier's soak or a gain's scaling. GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.DeathDelegate The handler of an entity's OnEntityDied and OnEntityRevived callbacks, handed the entity's hub: invoked as it's marked dead, before its frame ends, and as a staying entity revives. GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.EffectDelegate Invoked when an effect is applied. GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.EffectRefusedDelegate An effect that didn't land on this entity, and why. GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.EffectTickDelegate Invoked when an effect ticks. GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.EffectWorkerDelegate An effect's worker heard one of its effect's moments on this entity: its own, or a hit it dealt. GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.FrameCompleteDelegate Invoked at the end of each frame after all deferred actions are processed. Provides a complete summary of all modifications that occurred. The summary is the entity's own and is refilled each frame, so read it during the call, or copy what you need. GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.ImpactDelegate The handler of an entity's impact callbacks, handed the ImpactData of an impact as it's recorded: its target, its attribute and the change that landed. OnImpactDealt hears those the entity dealt and OnImpactReceived those it took, OnImpact either, and OnReductionDealt, OnIncreaseDealt, OnReductionReceived and OnIncreaseReceived a loss or a gain alone. GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.ImpactWorkerDelegate One of this entity's impact workers ran for a hit it dealt. GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.SystemDelegate Invoked when the system is initialized. GameplayAbilitySystemCallbacks.TagWorkerDelegate Invoked when a tag worker is activated. ItemSystemCallbacks.ItemConsumedDelegate Items used up, as a Consume Item task's, the item and how many went. ItemSystemCallbacks.ItemSystemCallbackDelegate The handler of an item system's callbacks, handed an ItemCallbackStatus: OnItemGiven and OnItemRemoved, as an item comes into the inventory or a slot leaves it; OnItemEquipped and OnItemUnequipped; OnItemEffectsApplied and OnItemEffectsRemoved, once for each effect a worn item puts on or takes off; and OnItemAbilityGranted and OnItemAbilityRevoked, for the ability it lends. LevelSystemCallbacks.LevelSystemCallbackDelegate A handler of a level system's events, invoked as a level is registered or unregistered (OnLevelRegistered, OnLevelUnregistered) and as one is set or changed (OnLevelChanged, OnMaxLevelChanged, OnLevelUp, OnLevelDown), and handed the LevelCallbackStatus of that change. ProcessControlCallbacks.ControlStateDelegate A handler of OnControlStateChanged, ProcessControl's callback, invoked as ProcessControl's own state changes, and handed the state it left and the state it entered. ProcessControlCallbacks.GASProcessDelegate A handler of OnGASProcessRegistered and OnGASProcessUnregistered, ProcessControl's callbacks, invoked for a process a GAS owns, one registered with the GAS as its handler or with an ability's packet whose caster is the GAS, as it registers and just before it's removed, and handed the GAS, the process's relay and its data packet. ProcessControlCallbacks.ProcessDelegate A handler of OnProcessRegistered and OnProcessUnregistered, ProcessControl's callbacks, invoked for every process once it has registered and initialized, and just before it's removed, and handed its relay and its data packet. ProcessControlCallbacks.ProcessStateDelegate A handler of OnProcessStateChanged, ProcessControl's callback, invoked as any process moves from one state to another, and handed its relay, the state it left, the state it entered and its data packet.

api/index.html.title: API Reference | PlayForge
api/index.html.summary: API Reference Every public type of PlayForge: its runtime, the Creator Lab, its editor and its test kit, read from the comments in its source. Each type's page says which guide sections name it, or which guide covers its area, and the guides link each type they name in code to its page. The contents group the types by area, as the package's folders do. Everything in the runtime is in the namespace FarEmerald.PlayForge, the Creator Lab's in FarEmerald.PlayForge.Lab, the editor's in FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor and the test kit's in FarEmerald.PlayForge.Testing. guides/abilities/activation.html.title: Activation | PlayForge
guides/abilities/activation.html.summary: Activation The Activation section sets how the ability starts: when it may start, what sets it off, what it costs and how it picks its target. sequenceDiagram autonumber participant G as Caller participant A as AbilitySystemComponent participant S as AbilitySpec participant K as AbilitySpecContainer participant P as AbilityProxy participant W as ProcessWorld of the caster participant R as TaskSequenceRuntime participant T as Task participant X as Target G->>A: TryActivateAbility(Ability, Tag or request) Note over G,A: also triggers, the input buffer and ActivateImmediateAbilities A->>A: AbilityDataPacket.GenerateFrom(spec, request, ...) A->>S: SourceRefusal: tags, crowd control, rules, CanStart A->>A: level zero, while-active, Blocks, ChanceToActivate alt refused A-->>G: a Refused ActivationResult, OnAbilityRefused(ActivationRefusal) end A->>A: CancelAbilitiesCancelledBy alt the request CancelsTargeting, as a press does, not a trigger or an activation at start A->>A: YieldTargetingTo: another ability still choosing its target gives way where its While Targeting yields, cancelled, nothing paid, its claim let go end A->>A: then the activation policy A->>K: ActivateAbility(data) K->>A: ClaimActive: OnAbilityActivate, components Start K->>P: TakeProxy, or GenerateProxy, which compiles K->>P: ActivateTargetingTask(token, data) P->>W: Register(CompiledTargeting).HandledBy(caster).With(data).In(world).Run() W->>T: the targeting task's Prepare, Activate, Clean T-->>W: TARGET packets through SetTargetingPacket W-->>P: relay.WhenTerminated K->>S: PickRefusal: a component's CanTakeTarget, as Cast Range's K->>K: ResolveTarget(ImplicitTag) into TARGET_REAL K->>S: TargetRefusal(target, data), the target checks alt targeting cancelled or failed, or its pick or target refused K-->>A: the activation ends Cancelled, nothing paid, a refused pick or target told through OnAbilityRefused end K->>K: WindUp: its entity's and its components' wind-ups, as Turn To Face K->>S: ApplyUsageEffects(data), unless a stage takes it Note over K,S: a component's ApplyUsage in their place, as Toggle's, else a cooldown or a charge through its CooldownModel, the Cost effect, the attribute costs K->>K: components Commit, CompileGrantedTags() Note over K,P: The claim is released here, unless a stage is critical K->>P: Activate(token, data) P->>P: the asset loaders run inline P->>W: Register(CompiledSequence).HandledBy(caster).With(data).In(world).Run() W->>R: its TaskSequenceProcess runs the stages loop each stage R->>R: a Branch skips it when its AbilityStageCondition fails R->>R: OnInit, OnAbilityStageActivate R->>T: Prepare, Execute (task.Activate), Clean T->>X: GenerateEffectSpec(data.EffectOrigin, effect) T->>X: ApplyCarrier(spec) R->>R: WhenAll or WhenAny, OnTerminate, OnAbilityStageEnd end W-->>P: relay.WhenTerminated K->>A: CleanHandle: release the claim, EndActivation, OnAbilityEnd K->>K: components End, the lent item's Used, CompileGrantedTags() Note over A,R: Interrupts: Inject(InterruptSequenceInjection.Instance) cancels the run. CancelAbilitiesTask and CancelledBy spare critical stages From the request through the checks, targeting, usage, stages and tasks to the end. Each activation is two processes HandledBy the caster, in ProcessWorld.Of(caster). Property Description When Busy What happens when the ability is asked to activate while another ability is busy. See When Busy. While Targeting Whether the ability gives way, while its targeting waits for the player, as another of the entity's abilities activates. See While Targeting. Buffer Window and Buffer Priority The input buffer's window and priority, under Queue. See The input buffer. Activate At Start When the ability is one of the entity's Starting Abilities, it tries to activate once, as the entity's GAS starts. An ability that an item or code grants later doesn't try it. Triggers What sets the ability off on its own. See Triggers. Chance to Activate How likely an activation is to start, from 0 to 1, rolled once for each, a player's or a trigger's, after its other checks. A miss is refused with Chance. Activation Roll Makes Chance to Activate pseudo-random or lucky. It shows for a chance that can miss. Proc Coefficient What its effects' hits carry for on-hit effects, where an effect sets none of its own. Ignores Crowd Control The crowd control rules the ability ignores, by their tags, as Black King Bar's Avatar ignores Silenced; a tag ignores the rules under it too. The other rules still stop it, and still interrupt it as it runs (see Crowd Control). Cost and Cooldown Gameplay effects applied to the caster as the ability starts, or by the stage that takes them. See Cost and Cooldown. Attribute Costs What the ability spends of attributes as it's used, beside its Cost effect. See Attribute Costs. Targeting The task that picks what the ability acts on. See Targeting. Use Implicit Targeting Records the caster as the activation's target before targeting. See Implicit targeting. In this section How an ability starts: One activation of an ability goes through these steps Requesting an activation: Code asks for an ability in one of three ways, and each returns an ActivationResult. Refusals: Each form of request can say why it was refused, through its result's Refusal or an out ActivationRefusal. When Busy: When Busy sets what happens when the ability is asked to activate while another ability is busy. While Targeting: While Targeting sets whether the ability, while its targeting waits for the player, gives way as another of the entity's abilities activates. Triggers: Triggers are what set the ability off on its own. Cost and Cooldown: Cost and Cooldown are gameplay effects (Effects) that the ability applies to its caster. Targeting: Targeting is the task that picks what the ability acts on, such as an entity the player clicks, or the caster itself. Click targeting: Click targeting waits for a press and aims along the game's input, ForgeInput.Current. Auto targeting: Auto targeting takes the entities within a range.

guides/abilities/activation/auto-targeti.title: Auto targeting | PlayForge
guides/abilities/activation/auto-targeti.summary: Auto targeting Auto targeting takes the entities within a range. Its tasks are Auto Target and Auto Target By Affinity. Each task picks its targets in three steps: It takes the entities within its Range, or within its ability's Cast Range when all of these hold: the ability has a Cast Range; the range is measured from the caster; Use Cast Range is on. It sorts them by its Mode. It keeps up to Max Targets, or every one at 0. Each is a target of the activation. The first, the nearest for Nearest, is its primary. A Target row and the Target Checks check the primary. Apply Effects and Apply/Remove Effects reach each target. They do so in the project's resolve order unless their Use Resolve Order is off (Effects: Workers: Resolve Order). So an area ability is Auto Target and then Apply Effects. Auto Target From Data with Primary Only off takes each target its key holds. Finding entities Each entity is found by its position, on either hub, with no collider needed. Property Description Around Where the range is measured from: the caster, the activation's target (as an AI hands it, or a task before it in a Composite picks it), or its point. Flat On by default: measures along the ground. Off, it measures a sphere. Use Physics Finds entities with physics instead, by collider on its Detection Layers, as it did. A runtime entity is still found by its position. Detection Layers The layers its physics search finds colliders on. They show under Use Physics alone. Takes Whom each takes, by how each stands to its caster. Takes offers its Enemies, its Allies (itself among them), its Other Allies, Self, All But Self or Everyone. Auto Target takes All But Self to start, and Auto Target By Affinity its Enemies.

guides/abilities/activation/click-target.title: Click targeting | PlayForge
guides/abilities/activation/click-target.summary: Click targeting Click targeting waits for a press and aims along the game's input, ForgeInput.Current. Its tasks are the Select tasks: Position, Direction, GAS Target, GAS Or Position and GAS Target In Range. Input and cameras By default, the game's input is the Input System's pointer, a mouse, a pen or a touch, where its package is in and on. Otherwise it's the Input Manager's mouse. Each is aimed through Camera.main, and with no camera, a press aims nowhere. To aim another way: For a camera of your own, give the default one: new LegacyPointerInput { Camera = camera }, or InputSystemPointerInput. For a gamepad's reticle or a controller's ray, write an IForgeInput. Put either in with ForgeInput.Use(input). Targets handed in the data An activation that already holds its target, under TargetReal, or its point, under Position, takes it with no click, as an AI's does. This holds unless the task's Take Target From Data is off. A handed target the task can't take, out of range or failing its requirements, fails the targeting at once. Prompts While a click targeting task waits, its slot's IsTargeting is true. The task's Prompt gives the words to ask with, as "Click a target", for a game's own screen. The Creator Lab and the Demo show them this way (The Creator Lab).

guides/abilities/activation/cost-and-coo.title: Cost and Cooldown | PlayForge
guides/abilities/activation/cost-and-coo.summary: Cost and Cooldown Cost and Cooldown are gameplay effects (Effects) that the ability applies to its caster. They apply as the ability starts, after its targeting, so a cancelled targeting pays nothing. A stage that takes them applies them instead (see Stages). Property Description Cost Usually an Instant effect that lowers a resource such as Mana. Cooldown Usually a Durational effect. While it is active, the caster carries its asset tag, and the Cooldown check refuses the ability. Attribute Costs Shown after Cost: what the ability spends of attributes as it's used, beside its Cost effect. See Attribute Costs. Each field has tools of its own: A line under each field says how its effect takes its levels. Link makes it take this ability's. New, beside an empty field, makes an effect linked to this ability. If Project Settings → PlayForge names a Cost or Cooldown effect, the field's right-click menu copies it or uses it. Attribute Costs Attribute Costs are what the ability spends of attributes as it's used. They're paid as well as its Cost effect. Property Description Attribute The attribute it spends. Role Where it names no attribute, a role whose attribute in the project it spends (Attributes: Roles). Amount How much it spends, a number that can scale by level. The ability is refused with Cost while its caster has less than they come to, lacks the attribute, or no attribute plays the role. They're paid where a Cost is: as the ability starts, or as its stage applies usage. The section's line says them, as "30 Mana".

guides/abilities/activation/how-an-abili.title: How an ability starts | PlayForge
guides/abilities/activation/how-an-abili.summary: How an ability starts One activation of an ability goes through these steps: The caster's tag requirements and Caster Checks are checked (see Requirements), and so is the ability's level (see Leveling). The Targeting task runs, if there is one. If targeting found a target, every check and requirement is checked again, the target's included. The activation winds up. It waits for what its components and its entity's wait for before it starts, such as a turn to face its target (see Turn To Face). The Asset Loaders run (see Stages). The Stages run, one after another. An interrupt during the wind-up cancels the activation. Its cost and cooldown, paid after the wind-up, aren't paid. These steps start inside the call that asks for the ability, AbilitySystemComponent.TryActivateAbility, and run until a task waits. So an ability whose tasks all finish at once has ended, and its callbacks have fired, by the time the call returns. An ability asked for again while that call still runs starts in the next frame instead. That holds whether it's asked for from its own callbacks or from those of another ability that it started. When the entity ends, its running abilities end with it, critical or not, and it takes no more activations.

guides/abilities/activation/refusals.htm.title: Refusals | PlayForge
guides/abilities/activation/refusals.htm.summary: Refusals Each form of request can say why it was refused, through its result's Refusal or an out ActivationRefusal. The refusal holds: Field Description Reason Why it was refused, such as Cooldown, Cost, Requirements, Blocked or Busy. Rule For another caster check, that check's name. For Crowd Control, the rule's tag, such as Stunned. Detail Where a check or a component refused it, why, in the check's own words, such as "Its caster's Mana, 10, can't pay 50". The ability system's OnAbilityRefused callback tells each refusal as it happens. A request that waits in the input buffer isn't refused, and isn't told again as the buffer retries it. Refusals after targeting A check on the target comes after targeting, and ends the activation instead, with nothing of it paid. The request said nothing was refused, as the activation had started. So the callback tells it, as Target, with Rule naming the check and Detail saying why. A component that refuses the target its targeting picked is told the same way, as a Cast Range refuses one beyond it. It's told as the kind its RefusedAs says, Range for a Cast Range, with its reason in Rule and Detail.

guides/abilities/activation/requesting-a.title: Requesting an activation | PlayForge
guides/abilities/activation/requesting-a.summary: Requesting an activation Code asks for an ability in one of three ways, and each returns an ActivationResult. Request How By slot With a request from CreateActivationRequest. By asset TryActivateAbility(ability). By tag TryActivateAbility(tag) activates the first ability, by slot, whose asset tag or one of whose context tags is that tag or under it. The result's Status says what came of the request: Status Meaning Started It started, inside the call. Buffered It waits in the input buffer. NextFrame It was asked for while its own activation call still ran, so it starts in the next frame. Refused It was refused. See Refusals. The result reads as true where the request wasn't refused, so if (abilities.TryActivateAbility(ability)) asks whether it was taken. Passing magnitudes The request's data can carry magnitudes for the effects the ability applies, set with data.SetByCaller(tag, magnitude). A Set By Caller scaler on each effect reads them (see Effects). So a caller that knows the damage as it casts passes it in, and one effect serves every strength.

guides/abilities/activation/targeting.ht.title: Targeting | PlayForge
guides/abilities/activation/targeting.ht.summary: Targeting Targeting is the task that picks what the ability acts on, such as an entity the player clicks, or the caster itself. Targeting holds the activation's claim. If the task fails while its Break Runtime On Invalid is on, or it doesn't finish, the activation ends. Leave Targeting empty to skip this step. PlayForge's targeting tasks come in two kinds: Kind Tasks Click targeting The Select tasks: Position, Direction, GAS Target, GAS Or Position and GAS Target In Range. See Click targeting. Auto targeting Auto Target and Auto Target By Affinity. See Auto targeting. Numbers in targeting tasks A targeting task's numbers can scale by level or read an attribute. They're read as its activation starts, at its ability's level. They include its Range, its Max Targets, a pointer task's Max Distance and an attribute condition's value. A pointer's Mouse Button picks one of three, so it stays a choice. Implicit targeting Implicit targeting records the caster as the activation's target before targeting runs. Property Description Use Implicit Targeting Off by default. Before targeting, it records the caster as the activation's target, under Implicit Tag. Implicit Tag The tag the caster is recorded under (default Target). It shows while Use Implicit Targeting is on. A targeting task that sets a target replaces it. The Passive preset turns it on, as a passive gives its holder its effects.

guides/abilities/activation/triggers.htm.title: Triggers | PlayForge
guides/abilities/activation/triggers.htm.summary: Triggers Triggers are what set the ability off on its own. Each trigger tries the ability as a request would, so its checks and its When Busy still hold. Trigger What sets it off Gameplay Event Code sends the entity an event under the trigger's tag, or a tag under it, with SendGameplayEvent(tag, data). The ability gets the event's data, its target among it. Tag Added The entity gains the trigger's tag, or one under it, that it didn't have. More of a tag it holds sets off nothing. Core events The core's own events are sent only where an ability listens for them. Event Sent to Impact Dealt The dealer, as an impact lands between two entities. Impact Taken The one hit, as an impact lands between two entities. Kill The killer: the source of the last blow the one who died took. Died The one who died. Revived A staying entity, as it revives. Blocked One that stops an effect by a Block stage. Evaded One that stops an effect by an Evade stage. Hit Blocked The dealer of an effect that was blocked. Hit Evaded The dealer of an effect that was evaded. Their data hold the instigator as Source, the entity it was done to as Subject, and an impact as Impact. Trigger properties Each trigger can narrow what sets it off, and say what the ability targets. Property Description Attribute For an impact event, the trigger takes only impacts on this attribute. Sign For an impact event, it takes only a Loss or only a Gain. Impact Types For an impact event, it takes only impacts of these types. Chance Rolls once for each event, as Counter Helix's 20%. Chance Roll Makes the Chance pseudo-random or lucky (Effects: Requirements). Target What the ability targets: the ability's own targeting, as an area spin finds the enemies round it; the event's Instigator, as a counterattack; or its Subject, as an on-hit ability targets the one hit. An ability set off by Died runs on a dead entity only if its rules don't ask that its caster be alive. Problems view The Problems view checks an ability's triggers: It notes a Gameplay Event trigger on an event that neither the core nor an asset in the project sends, as only code can send it. An asset sends one as a threshold's Event or a stop stage's does. It warns of an Impact Dealt or Impact Taken trigger's impact type that no effect deals, which never matches.

guides/abilities/activation/when-busy.ht.title: When Busy | PlayForge
guides/abilities/activation/when-busy.ht.summary: When Busy When Busy sets what happens when the ability is asked to activate while another ability is busy. An activation is busy, or holds its claim, while its targeting and its critical tasks run. A critical task is one that must not overlap another ability's critical work, such as an attack animation. The inspector marks critical tasks and stages Critical. Which claims an ability waits on depends on its choice and its tasks: An ability waits on the claims of abilities that use the same choice. An ability with critical tasks also waits on any ability with critical tasks that holds its claim, whatever its choice. Option What it does Entity's Policy (default) Uses the entity's When Busy, set in the Entity asset's Abilities section. Activate Anyway Starts at once. It is refused, as Critical, only when it has critical tasks and another ability with critical tasks holds its claim. Refuse Starts only when no Refuse ability holds its claim; otherwise the request is refused, as Busy. With critical tasks, it is also refused, as Critical, while another ability with critical tasks holds its claim. Queue Waits in the input buffer while it can't start, for up to Buffer Window seconds of the caster's time, then lets go. See The input buffer. Whatever the choice, an ability can't start again while its own activation holds its claim. The input buffer Under Queue, a request waits in the input buffer when any of these holds: A Queue ability holds its claim. The ability has critical tasks, and any ability with critical tasks holds its claim. A running stage blocks this ability (see Stages). The request waits for up to Buffer Window seconds of the caster's time, then lets go. The buffer holds one request for each ability. A new press replaces it, with its window afresh. As a claim is released, and each frame, the request with the highest Buffer Priority that can start does. Of equals, the newest starts. While the entity is paused or its time is stopped, as in a hit-stop, the windows wait too. A request can name a window of its own (CreateActivationRequest's bufferWindow). Property Description Buffer Window How long a request waits in the input buffer, in seconds of the caster's time (default 0.3 s). A window of 0 doesn't wait, so the request is refused. Buffer Priority Which waiting request starts first: the highest (default 0). Each is a number field read at the ability's level. They show under Queue and under the entity's policy, which may be Queue, and are hidden under the others.

guides/abilities/activation/while-target.title: While Targeting | PlayForge
guides/abilities/activation/while-target.summary: While Targeting While Targeting sets whether the ability, while its targeting waits for the player, gives way as another of the entity's abilities activates. A player who starts one ability's targeting and presses another's key means the other. Option What it does Entity's Rule (default) Follows the entity's Targeting Yields, set in its Abilities section, on by default. Yields Its targeting is cancelled, nothing of it paid, and its claim lets go at once. So the other starts, ahead of anything waiting in the input buffer. Holds It keeps its claim until its target is chosen or it's cancelled. The other does as its When Busy says. An ability that yields gives way only to an activation that passes its own checks. So a press of an ability on cooldown leaves it be. An activation that a trigger or Activate At Start makes doesn't cut a choice short, as the player didn't ask for it. Code that activates for the game rather than the player says the same of its request: CancelsTargeting = false.

guides/abilities/built-in-kinds.html.title: Built-in kinds | PlayForge
guides/abilities/built-in-kinds.html.summary: Built-in kinds The kinds PlayForge ships for this guide's pickers, each with its menu and what it does, as its picker says. A project's own kinds join them in the same pickers. In this section Components Tasks Targeting tasks Requirements Charge recharges Stage policies

guides/abilities/built-in-kinds/charge-r.title: Charge recharges | PlayForge
guides/abilities/built-in-kinds/charge-r.summary: Charge recharges Kind Menu What it does AllAtOnceRecharge — Every charge comes back at once, after the last one is spent. EachChargeRecharge — Each spent charge comes back on a cooldown of its own.

guides/abilities/built-in-kinds/componen.title: Components | PlayForge
guides/abilities/built-in-kinds/componen.summary: Components Kind Menu What it does AuraAbilityComponent — Gives those near the holder an aura's effects while it knows the ability. CastRangeAbilityComponent — How far from the caster the ability's target may be. ChargesAbilityComponent — How many uses the ability holds, each coming back as it recharges. CuesAbilityComponent — Shows and sounds the ability's moments: as it activates, commits, ends or is refused, and while it's active. ToggleAbilityComponent — Turns an effect on with one use and off with the next. TurnToFaceAbilityComponent — Turns its caster to face its target or its point before its first stage, its own way, or not at all where its entity's Turns To Face would.

guides/abilities/built-in-kinds/requirem.title: Requirements | PlayForge
guides/abilities/built-in-kinds/requirem.summary: Requirements Kind Menu What it does AbilityLevelValidation (Ability Level) — Activates only where the ability's level compares with a number, as a form it unlocks at a rank. AffiliationValidation (Affiliation) — Activates only on a target that stands to its caster as it says: an enemy, an ally, itself, or anyone else. AttributeValidation — Activates only where an attribute of the checked entity, or its share of its base, compares with a value. CheckRangeValidation (Check Range) — The Cast Range component's check: its target within the component's range of its caster. It comes and goes with the component. ConditionValidation — Activates only while its condition holds: a tag, an attribute, a level, or any other condition. CooldownValidation — Activates only where the ability isn't cooling down, or with its charges counted, has one in hand. CostValidation — Activates only where the caster can pay the cost. FacingValidation (Facing) — Activates only where its target lies within an angle in front of its caster, or its caster within an angle behind its target. HasEffectValidation (Has Effect) — Activates only where the checked entity has an effect on, by asset or by tag; or, with Without, where it hasn't. HoldsItemValidation (Holds Item) — Activates only where the checked entity holds an item; or, with Equipped, wears it. IsAliveValidation — Activates only while the checked entity lives: the caster among the Caster Checks, the target among the Target Checks. LineOfSightValidation (Line of Sight) — Activates only where nothing on the layers given blocks a line from the caster to its target; 3D physics colliders block it. TagWeightValidation (Tag Weight) — Activates only where the checked entity holds a tag at a weight that compares with a number, as combo points or stacks.

guides/abilities/built-in-kinds/stage-po.title: Stage policies | PlayForge
guides/abilities/built-in-kinds/stage-po.summary: Stage policies Kind Menu What it does AllProxyStagePolicy — The stage ends as its last task does. AnyProxyStagePolicy — The stage ends as its first task does.

guides/abilities/built-in-kinds/targetin.title: Targeting tasks | PlayForge
guides/abilities/built-in-kinds/targetin.summary: Targeting tasks Kind Menu What it does AutoTargetByAffinityTask Automatic Targets the entities in range of an affiliation, as the nearest ally to heal or every enemy in reach. AutoTargetFromDataTask Automatic Targets the entity the ability's data holds under a key, as a trigger's subject. AutoTargetSelfTask Automatic Targets the caster itself, checked against the task's tag requirements. AutoTargetTask Automatic Targets the entities in range that pass its tag requirements and conditions. CompositeTargetingTask — Runs several targeting tasks in turn, each adding its targets, as an entity and then a point. SelectDirectionTargetTask Picked The player clicks a direction from the caster. SelectGasOrPositionTargetTask Picked The player clicks an entity, or else a point on the ground. SelectGasTargetInRangeTask Picked The player clicks an entity within range of the caster. SelectGasTargetTask Picked The player clicks an entity. SelectPositionTargetTask Picked The player clicks a point on the ground.

guides/abilities/built-in-kinds/tasks.ht.title: Tasks | PlayForge
guides/abilities/built-in-kinds/tasks.ht.summary: Tasks Kind Menu What it does ApplyEffectsAbilityTask Effects Applies its effects to the ability's targets. ApplyRemoveEffectsAbilityTask Effects Applies its effects as its stage starts and takes them off as the stage ends. ApplyToCasterTask Effects Applies its effects to the caster, whatever the ability targets. AreaEffectTask Effects Applies its effects to each entity of the sides it takes within a radius of the caster, the target or a point. BlinkTask Movement Puts the caster at the target at once: at the point within its reach, or behind the entity. CancelAbilitiesTask Events and Tags Cancels the caster's running abilities tagged with one of its tags. ChannelAbilityTask Waits Holds its stage for a duration nothing interrupts, as a cast bar fills. ConsumeItemTask Items Uses up items the caster holds, as a potion is drunk. CreateMonoProcessAbilityTask Process Spawns a process, as a projectile, whose effects are the caster's at the ability's level. DashTask Movement Moves the caster toward the target, or away from it, over a moment. DelayTask Waits Waits a while before its stage goes on. DisjointAbilityTask Process Makes every disjointable shot homing on the caster lose it, as a dodge. GrantTagsTask Events and Tags Grants tags to the caster or the target while its stage runs. InjectAbilityTask Sequence Sends a command into the ability's own run, as an interrupt. PlayCueTask (Play Cue) Cues Plays its cues at this moment of the stage: on the caster, the target or the point. RunProcessTask Process Runs processes for the caster and waits for them, up to a time. SendEventTask Events and Tags Sends a gameplay event to the caster or to each target. SetAbilitiesTask Asset Loaders Puts abilities in the ability's data under a key, for its later tasks. SetAssetsTask Asset Loaders Puts assets in the ability's data under a key, for its later tasks. SetAttributeSetsTask Asset Loaders Puts attribute sets in the ability's data under a key, for its later tasks. SetAttributesTask Asset Loaders Puts attributes in the ability's data under a key, for its later tasks. SetEffectsTask Asset Loaders Puts effects in the ability's data under a key, for its later tasks. SetEntitiesTask Asset Loaders Puts entities in the ability's data under a key, for its later tasks. SetTagsTask Asset Loaders Puts tags in the ability's data under a key, for its later tasks. UnityEventAbilityTask Utility Invokes UnityEvents, for objects in the scene to answer. WaitForAttributeTask Waits Waits for an attribute of the caster or the target to cross a value. WaitForEventTask Waits Waits for a gameplay event sent to the caster or the target. WaitForTagTask Waits Waits for the caster or the target to gain a tag, or to lose it.

guides/abilities/components.html.title: Components | PlayForge
guides/abilities/components.html.summary: Components An ability's components are features it carries, each a class with hooks into its life, added with the list's +. A kind that makes no sense twice is offered only while the ability holds none of it. Component What it does Cast Range The one range the ability has. Charges How many uses the ability holds. Toggle An effect the ability turns on and off on its caster. Turn To Face How the ability turns its caster to face its target or its point before its first stage. Auras An effect on those near its holder, while the entity knows the ability. Cues What the ability shows and sounds at its moments. To write a component of your own, see Component hooks, Writing a component and Components in code. In this section Cast Range: A Cast Range component is the one range the ability has: how far from its caster its target or its point may be. Charges: A Charges component says how many uses the ability holds, each use spending a charge. Toggle: A Toggle component holds an Effect the ability turns on and off on its caster, as a mana shield. Turn To Face: A Turn To Face component says how this ability turns its caster to face its target or its point before its first stage. Auras: An Aura component holds an effect on those near its holder, while the entity knows the ability, as a banner that inspires the allies round its bearer. Cues: A Cues component plays what the ability shows and sounds at its moments, on its caster. Component hooks: A component hears its ability's life through hooks, each a no-op unless the component overrides it. Writing a component: A component of your own derives from AbstractAbilityComponent and overrides the hooks it needs, each a no-op otherwise. Components in code: Code finds a component by what it does, not by its class.

guides/abilities/components/auras.html.title: Auras | PlayForge
guides/abilities/components/auras.html.summary: Auras An Aura component holds an effect on those near its holder, while the entity knows the ability, as a banner that inspires the allies round its bearer. Property Description Effect The effect it holds on each it takes while they're near. Radius How far it reaches from its holder. Flat Measures the radius along the ground; off, a sphere. Takes Whom it takes, by how each stands to its holder, its holder too or not. Interval How often it checks who's near. For how auras work, see Effects: Components: Auras.

guides/abilities/components/cast-range.h.title: Cast Range | PlayForge
guides/abilities/components/cast-range.h.summary: Cast Range A Cast Range component is the one range the ability has: how far from its caster its target or its point may be. Property Description Range How far from its caster the target or point may be, a number that can scale by level. 0 reaches anywhere. Flat The range is measured along the ground unless Flat is off. How the range is enforced: An activation handed a target or a point beyond it, under TargetReal or Position, as an AI's is, is refused as Range. So nothing of it is paid, and an AI can walk closer and ask again. Targeting that picks a target beyond it, whichever task picked it, ends the activation before its stages, told as Range too. Where the range is used: The auto-targeting tasks measured from the caster, and Select GAS Target In Range, search within it where their Use Cast Range is on, as it is by default. Their own range is set aside. The Creator Lab's units attack from their attack's Cast Range. Its bots cast an ability once their foe is within its Cast Range, where it has one (The Creator Lab). It's the ability's reach, an IAbilityReach. Code reads it through ForgeReach, as ForgeReach.TryRead(caster, ability, out range), and a reach of your own takes its place in each of these. While the ability holds it, its Target Checks show its Check Range, locked, saying the range (see Requirements). An ability holds one at most.

guides/abilities/components/charges.html.title: Charges | PlayForge
guides/abilities/components/charges.html.summary: Charges A Charges component says how many uses the ability holds, each use spending a charge. Property Description Charges How many uses the ability holds, a number that can scale by level. With 1 it is an ordinary cooldown. Recharge How spent charges come back: Each Charge (the default), All At Once, or a recharge of your own. With more than one charge, the Cooldown check refuses the ability only with none in hand. Recharge What it does Each Charge (default) Starts the Cooldown for each charge spent, a container of its own whatever the effect does when applied again. Each brings its charge back as it ends, so three spent a second apart come back a second apart. All At Once Starts the Cooldown only as the last charge is spent, and its end brings them all back. A recharge of your own Write a recharge of your own by extending AbstractChargeRecharge: Override InHand: how many are in hand. Override Spend: what a use does. Use AbilityCharges' Max, Spent, Cooldowns and StartCooldown. One of your own counts even a single charge, unless its CountsASingleCharge says not. Charges in code Charges are the ability's cooldown model (see Components in code). So code reads what's in hand of any ability as spec.CooldownModel.InHand(spec). The component itself, spec.Find<ChargesAbilityComponent>(), holds its Charges and Recharge. Its ChargesOf(spec) gives the ability's charges on its caster, an AbilityCharges. Charges in the editor The section's line counts them, as "3 charges". A warning under the Components list, as in the Problems view, says where built-in charges have no Cooldown to bring them back, so they never run out. An ability holds one at most.

guides/abilities/components/component-ho.title: Component hooks | PlayForge
guides/abilities/components/component-ho.summary: Component hooks A component hears its ability's life through hooks, each a no-op unless the component overrides it. Hook What it does Granted Hears the ability granted to an entity. Removed Hears the ability removed from it. CanStart Is asked whether an activation may start. A reason it gives refuses the activation, named by it, as the kind its RefusedAs says, Rule unless it says otherwise. CanTakeTarget Is asked whether the target its targeting picked may be taken. A reason it gives ends the activation there, before anything of it is paid, told as the kind its RefusedAs says. WindUp Is waited on as an activation winds up, after its target checks and before its cost, as a turn to face its target is. Start Hears an activation start. Commit Hears the activation commit its cost and cooldown. End Hears the activation end, by how it ended: done, cancelled or failed. ApplyUsage As the activation's usage applies, it may apply it in the ability's place, as a Toggle does. It composes its own from the spec's PayCosts and SpendCooldown. Waives May waive the Cost and Cooldown checks while it says so. CategoryOf Claims the categories of the effects its ability puts on for a purge, as a Toggle claims its effect a toggle's.

guides/abilities/components/components-i.title: Components in code | PlayForge
guides/abilities/components/components-i.summary: Components in code Code finds a component by what it does, not by its class. Find<T>(), on an ability, its spec, an effect, an item and an entity, gives the first of its components that is a T, a kind or an interface it implements. Capability What it is Implemented by IAbilityReach An ability's reach. Cast Range ICooldownModel How an ability's uses come back. Charges Reach The targeting tasks, the Creator Lab's bots and your own code read an ability's reach through ForgeReach. So a component of your own that implements IAbilityReach is asked as a Cast Range is. Cooldown model An ICooldownModel says how many uses the ability holds, how many are in hand, what a use spends, and why the Cooldown check refuses it with none. An ability with none has SingleCooldown: one use, back as its Cooldown ends. The Cooldown check asks it, the ability spends through it, and a HUD reads it as spec.CooldownModel. Component state A component's state that needs its holder, as a Charges component's charges need their ability, is kept with spec.ComponentStates.TryGet and Keep. No shortcuts The built-in components are written on this API alone, and PlayForge's core names none of them. So a component of your own reaches as far as they do. None has a shortcut: code reads one through Find<T>() or the component itself. For example, spec.Find<ToggleAbilityComponent>()?.IsOn(spec) says whether a Toggle is on.

guides/abilities/components/cues.html.title: Cues | PlayForge
guides/abilities/components/cues.html.summary: Cues A Cues component plays what the ability shows and sounds at its moments, on its caster. Property Description On Activate Plays as an activation starts. On Commit Plays as it pays its cost and starts its cooldown. While Active Lasts from its start to its end. A Prefab cue here lasts until the activation ends. On End Plays as it ends, however it ended. On Refused Plays as one is refused, nothing of it paid. Each list holds cues as an effect's does (Effects: Cues), a Cue Tag among them. A stage's exact moment, as a sword's arc, plays through a Play Cue task. An ability holds one at most.

guides/abilities/components/toggle.html.title: Toggle | PlayForge
guides/abilities/components/toggle.html.summary: Toggle A Toggle component holds an Effect the ability turns on and off on its caster, as a mana shield. Property Description Effect The effect the ability turns on and off on its caster. Use What happens Used while off It puts the effect on where its usage would be paid, paying its Cost and Attribute Costs and starting no cooldown. Used again, while on It takes the effect off, paying nothing and asking no cost, and starts its Cooldown, or spends a charge. Neither its cost nor its cooldown stops it turning off. It counts only the effect it put on. One another put there leaves it off. A purge counts its effect a Toggle's, as a death that keeps toggles keeps it. As its holder forgets the ability, the effect comes off; it stayed on. The Problems view warns where it toggles an Instant effect, which is never on. Code asks the component, spec.Find<ToggleAbilityComponent>(). Its IsOn(spec) says whether its effect is on, and its Effect is the effect. It's written on the components' hooks alone: it applies the usage in its ability's place, waives the cost and the cooldown while it's on, and claims its effect. An ability holds one at most.

guides/abilities/components/turn-to-face.title: Turn To Face | PlayForge
guides/abilities/components/turn-to-face.summary: Turn To Face A Turn To Face component says how this ability turns its caster to face its target or its point before its first stage. It does so in place of its entity's Turns To Face (Entities: Components: Turns To Face). Property Description Turns Whether the ability turns its caster. Off, it doesn't turn at all, as a cast behind its caster doesn't. Turn Speed How fast it turns, in degrees a second of its own time. 0 faces at once. Start Angle How close to facing its target, in degrees, it turns before the first stage starts. Facing Angle How close to facing its target it goes on turning once the stage has started. If Too Long What happens when reaching the Start Angle takes longer than Max Wait: No Limit, Start Anyway or Cancel. Max Wait How long, in seconds of its own time, it waits to reach the Start Angle, where If Too Long sets a limit. The Target Checks come before the turn. So a Facing check that wants its target in front of its caster reads the caster's facing before it turns. An ability holds one at most.

guides/abilities/components/writing-a-co.title: Writing a component | PlayForge
guides/abilities/components/writing-a-co.summary: Writing a component A component of your own derives from AbstractAbilityComponent and overrides the hooks it needs, each a no-op otherwise. It's the ability's, shared by everything that holds it. So what it keeps for one entity's ability it keeps through its context: ctx.GetState<T>(this). Describe says what it does in one line with its numbers, as a Cast Range's "Range 600". The Components section's line, The Forge's summary and the ability's breakdown say it beside its name. DescribeUsage says what it adds to the ability's use, as Charges' "3 charges". The Activation section's line says it after its cost and cooldown. Editor rules A component's rules in the editor derive from ForgeComponentRule<T>, in the editor's assembly, with a public constructor that takes nothing. The Problems view runs each on every asset that holds a component of its kind. The ability's inspector says what it finds under its Components list, as it says the Charges'.

guides/abilities/identity.html.title: Identity | PlayForge
guides/abilities/identity.html.summary: Identity The Identity section names the ability, describes it and sets its icon. Property Description Name The ability's display name. It also gives the asset tag, so renaming the ability changes its tag. Description Free text for your UI. The inspector header shows it. Asset Tag Read-only, made from the Name: punctuation is dropped, and each word is capitalised and joined. The tag is stored when you edit the Name. Textures Icons, each paired with a tag. The texture tagged Primary is the ability's icon; without one, the first texture is used. If the stored tag differs from the one the Name gives, the Asset Tag shows in warning text with an Update button that stores the new one. Note Renaming an ability changes its asset tag. Update anything that names the old tag.

guides/abilities/index.html.title: Abilities | PlayForge
guides/abilities/index.html.summary: Abilities An Ability asset describes one thing an entity can do, such as a fireball, a dash or a heal. AbilityDataPacket and a pooled AbilityProxy that compiles lazily. An entity learns an ability in one of three ways, and keeps it until the ability is removed: from its Entity asset's Starting Abilities; from an equipped Item; from code, with AbilitySystemComponent.GiveAbility. Each time the ability activates, the GAS checks that it may run, lets a targeting task pick a target, then runs the ability's stages of tasks. The ability's cost and cooldown are gameplay effects, assets that change an entity, which it applies to its caster. Abilities run as processes under ProcessControl, so the scene needs one. Tags are names, such as State.Stunned, that an entity carries and that requirements check. Each asset stores a tag made from its Name: Fire Ball gives Ability.FireBall. The entity carries this tag while it has the ability, and keeps the ability's level under it. Each section below matches the inspector section of the same name. The inspector's header shows the ability's one line, as The Forge's Summary column does. The line gives each effect the ability applies, by its first impact across its levels, then its costs and its cooldown, as "-450/-600/-750 Health; 280/420/680 Mana; 70/60/50 s". A number that reads what the editor can't give it, such as the target, is marked *. In this guide Identity: The Identity section names the ability, describes it and sets its icon. Leveling: An ability has its own level on each entity that learns it, kept under the ability's asset tag. Tags: An ability's tags describe it, and some of them are applied to its entity while it has the ability or while it runs. Activation: The Activation section sets how the ability starts: when it may start, what sets it off, what it costs and how it picks its target. Stages: The Stages section sets what the ability does once it has started. Requirements: Requirements are what an activation must pass. Components: An ability's components are features it carries, each a class with hooks into its life, added with the list's +. Workers: Workers are reusable behaviours, picked from a list, that react to what happens to an entity. Local Data: Local Data is a list of named values stored on the asset. Used By: The Used By section lists the PlayForge assets that refer to this ability, each with its type icon. Built-in kinds: The kinds PlayForge ships for this guide's pickers, each with its menu and what it does, as its picker says.
