guides/abilities/leveling.html.title: Leveling | PlayForge
guides/abilities/leveling.html.summary: Leveling An ability has its own level on each entity that learns it, kept under the ability's asset tag. Effects the ability applies take this level, so their scalers can pick per-level values. A scaler is a value source, such as a table with one value per level. A level provider is an asset whose level range another asset follows. Property Description Link Mode Standalone (default) keeps the ability's own range. Linked To Provider takes the range from a level provider instead. Starting Level The bottom of the ability's own range (default 1). An entity's Starting Abilities begin at the Starting Level, and the ability's level never goes below it. Max Level The top of the ability's own range (default 4). Level Provider Shown while linked: the asset the range comes from, an Entity, Ability, Effect, Item or Attribute Set. Right-click the field to pick from one type. Ignore When Level Zero On by default: the ability can't activate while its level is 0. With a Starting Level of 0, the entity must raise the ability's level before it can use it. Link Cost & Cooldown Links this ability's cost and cooldown effects to it, so their per-level values follow its range. Unlink Cost & Cooldown Removes the links that point at this ability. Under Linked To Provider: A link that would make a loop is refused, with an error in the Console. While no provider is set, a warning says the ability uses its own range. While linked, Starting Level and Max Level show the range in use, read-only. Link Cost & Cooldown and Unlink Cost & Cooldown each ask first, and one Undo takes it back. Code changes an ability's level through the entity's GAS, with SetLevel or ModifyLevel and the ability's asset tag. An ability that an Item grants starts at the item's level, kept within this range. Note The link serves the inspector and the tooltips that AbilityInspector builds. At runtime, the ability's level stays within its own Starting Level and Max Level, even while it is linked.

guides/abilities/local-data.html.title: Local Data | PlayForge
guides/abilities/local-data.html.summary: Local Data Local Data is a list of named values stored on the asset. Each row has a Key (a tag) and a value of a kind. The kinds are: PlayForge's: Float, Int, String, Bool, Tag, Attribute, Effect, Ability, Entity, Object, MonoBehaviour or ScriptableObject. A kind of your own: a [Serializable] class made from LocalDataValue<T>, as a point or a colour. The row's kinds offer it beside PlayForge's. A row saves its own value alone. Object fields take project assets, not scene objects. Code reads a value with ability.TryGetLocalData(key, out var data). The first row with that key wins. Code then reads the value by its type, data.TryGet(out float range) or data.TryGet(out MyPoint point). A number, a Float or an Int, which can scale, reads with data.Value.TryReadNumber(context, out float number). A tag check of your own, extending AbstractTagValidationRule, reads its tag's value with GetValue. The value is the tag's weight on the entity it checks or, where that entity holds none of it, the ability's Local Data under the tag.

guides/abilities/requirements.html.title: Requirements | PlayForge
guides/abilities/requirements.html.summary: Requirements Requirements are what an activation must pass. If one fails, the ability doesn't run. Requirement What it checks Tag requirements The tags of the caster, of the caster while the ability runs, and of the target. See Tag requirements. Caster Checks The caster, before targeting and again after it. See Caster Checks and Target Checks. Target Checks The target, after targeting. See Caster Checks and Target Checks. Crowd control Rules that hold for every ability at once. See Crowd Control. In this section Tag requirements: The tag requirements table holds tag checks, a row for each side. Caster Checks and Target Checks: An ability's checks are rules it runs on its caster and on its target. Check types: PlayForge's check types are grouped below by the list that offers them. Failed checks: A failed check refuses or ends the activation, and says why. Writing your own check: A check of your own implements IAbilityValidationRule. Crowd Control: Crowd control holds for every ability at once, so no ability has to list Stunned among the tags it must not have.

guides/abilities/requirements/caster-che.title: Caster Checks and Target Checks | PlayForge
guides/abilities/requirements/caster-che.summary: Caster Checks and Target Checks An ability's checks are rules it runs on its caster and on its target. You pick each check's type from a list. List When it runs Defaults Offers Caster Checks When the ability is asked to activate, before targeting, and again after targeting. Cooldown, Cost and Is Alive. The caster's types, and those that check either side. Target Checks After targeting. If targeting found no target, they are skipped. Is Alive. The target's types, and those that check either side. A check a component stands behind shows under its list, locked, as Check Range does under the Target Checks while the ability holds a Cast Range. No list holds it: it comes and goes with its component, which enforces it. The section's line counts it among the checks.

guides/abilities/requirements/check-type.title: Check types | PlayForge
guides/abilities/requirements/check-type.summary: Check types PlayForge's check types are grouped below by the list that offers them. Caster check types Check What it does Cooldown Passes when the ability isn't cooling down, or, with its charges counted (see Charges), has one in hand. Cost Passes when the ability has no cost, or the cost would leave each attribute it spends at 0 or more, and its Attribute Costs can be paid. The caster must have each attribute. Ability Level Compares the ability's level with Level, using Comparison, as a form it unlocks at a rank. It starts at 2 or more. Check types for either list These check the caster among the Caster Checks, and the target among the Target Checks. Check What it does Is Alive Passes when the checked entity isn't dead. Attribute Compares the checked entity's Current value of Attribute with Value, using Comparison. With Share Of Base, it compares its share of its base, from 0 to 1, as "below half its health". Tag Weight Compares the checked entity's weight of Tag with Weight, using Comparison, as combo points or stacks. It starts at 1 or more; an entity without the tag holds it at 0. Has Effect Passes when the checked entity has Effect on, or any effect tagged Tagged or under it, by its asset tag, a context tag or a tag it grants. With Without, it passes when it has none of it; naming neither, it passes. Holds Item Passes when the checked entity holds Item, or, with Equipped, wears it. Naming none, it passes. Condition Passes while its condition, When, holds: a tag, an attribute, a level, a comparison of numbers, or a condition of your own (see Scalers). With none, it passes. A Condition check reads its condition as an effect's requirements and an On Hit read theirs. It's read against the activation, with the checked entity as its target, so among the Caster Checks its target is the caster. Target check types Check What it does Affiliation Passes when the target stands to its caster as Target says, as a search's Takes does. Line of Sight Passes when nothing on the Blocking layers blocks a line from the caster to its target. The line runs Height above each, so the ground under them doesn't block it. Facing Passes when the target lies within Angle in front of its caster. With Behind Target, it passes when the caster stands within the angle behind its target, as a backstab wants. Check Range The Cast Range component's check, which no list offers. It shows while the ability holds a Cast Range, saying its range, and passes, as the component enforces the range (see Cast Range). Affiliation's Target offers these choices: Option Passes for Enemies A target that shares none of the caster's sides. Allies A target that shares one, the caster itself among them. Other Allies An ally, leaving the caster out. Self The caster alone. All But Self Anyone else. Everyone Anyone. A caster with no sides takes anyone as either. Line of Sight: 3D physics colliders block it. Triggers and the two ends' own colliders don't. Facing: the caster and the target each face as their targeting packet does, along the ground. An Angle of 90 takes 45° to either side, and 360 anywhere.

guides/abilities/requirements/crowd-cont.title: Crowd Control | PlayForge
guides/abilities/requirements/crowd-cont.summary: Crowd Control Crowd control holds for every ability at once, so no ability has to list Stunned among the tags it must not have. A Crowd Control Rules asset (Create → PlayForge → Crowd Control Rules) holds its rules. Each rule has these properties: Property Description Tag The tag the caster carries, as Stunned. Stops What the rule stops: Every Ability, as a stun, or Abilities Tagged. Ability Tags Under Abilities Tagged, the rule stops the abilities whose asset tag or a context tag is one of these or under it. So Silenced stops spells and Disarmed attacks. An entity's abilities follow its own Crowd Control (Entities: Abilities), or, where it names none, its Forge Project's (Attributes: Roles). While the caster carries a rule's tag, or one under it: An ability the rule stops is refused with Crowd Control, the refusal's Rule naming the tag. One that runs is interrupted as the tag lands, as a stun breaks a channel. An ability's Ignores Crowd Control (see Activation) opts it out of the rules it names. Code asks with rules.Stopping(ability, tags), which gives the first rule that stops the ability, or null.

guides/abilities/requirements/failed-che.title: Failed checks | PlayForge
guides/abilities/requirements/failed-che.summary: Failed checks A failed check refuses or ends the activation, and says why. Check What a failure does Caster Check Refuses the activation as the kind its RefusedAs says: Cooldown, Cost or Dead for the Cooldown, Cost and Is Alive checks, which name none, and Rule, naming the check, for any other. Target Check Ends the activation after targeting, told as Target, naming the check (see Refusals). Each says why in Validate's error, which the refusal carries as its Detail, as "Its caster's Mana, 20, can't pay 30".

guides/abilities/requirements/tag-requir.title: Tag requirements | PlayForge
guides/abilities/requirements/tag-requir.summary: Tag requirements The tag requirements table holds tag checks, a row for each side. Row What it checks Caster The caster, with the Caster Checks. While active The caster, for as long as the ability runs. When it fails, the ability is interrupted, and while it fails, the ability can't activate. Target The target, the same way, after targeting. For example, a channel whose While active row must not have State.Stunned ends as a stun lands. Each row has two cells: Cell Description Requires The tags the entity must have. Must not have The tags it must not have, such as State.Stunned, or None. A row passes when the entity has every tag it requires and none it must not have. So an empty row always passes. Click a cell to edit its list under the table, with the row's Template and Sync With Template (see Effects). Each entry is a tag query: a Tag, a Match mode such as Include Children, and a comparison with a number. Greater Than 0 means "the tag is present". Note The section's Clear button empties the tag requirements and leaves the checks, since an ability without them would skip its cost and cooldown.

guides/abilities/requirements/writing-yo.title: Writing your own check | PlayForge
guides/abilities/requirements/writing-yo.summary: Writing your own check A check of your own implements IAbilityValidationRule. Member What it does Validate Says whether the activation passes, and why not. GetName Names the check. RefusedAs The kind its refusal of the caster is told as, Rule unless it says otherwise. So an ammunition check can say Cooldown, as the built-in does. [ForgeMenu] Names and describes it in the list. [ValidationSide] Says which list offers it, Caster or Target. Without it, both do. A component stands behind a check by overriding its TargetCheck or CasterCheck with an AbstractComponentValidationRule<T> of its own kind. The check shows under the list while the ability holds the component, and the component enforces it, in CanStart.

guides/abilities/stages.html.title: Stages | PlayForge
guides/abilities/stages.html.summary: Stages The Stages section sets what the ability does once it has started. Property Description Asset Loaders Run once per activation, after targeting. Each loader adds assets to the activation's data under a tag. Cancelled By Abilities that cancel this one as they activate. See Cancelling and blocking. Blocks Abilities that can't activate while this one runs. See Cancelling and blocking. Stages The ability's stages, which run one after another. See Stage properties. A Set Effects loader, for example, adds effects under Effects. Code-driven tasks read them from there. In this section Stage properties: Each stage starts all its tasks together, and the next stage starts when it ends. Tasks: A stage's Tasks are its work, such as Apply Effects, Delay or Run Sequence. Built-in tasks: PlayForge's own tasks sit under these categories in the task picker. Stage conditions: A stage's Condition sets when the stage runs, by a tag. Cancelling and blocking: An ability's Cancelled By and Blocks lists name other abilities, by asset tag or a context tag, or a child of one. Critical stages: A stage that holds a critical task is critical: it commits the ability to the stage.

guides/abilities/stages/built-in-tasks.h.title: Built-in tasks | PlayForge
guides/abilities/stages/built-in-tasks.h.summary: Built-in tasks PlayForge's own tasks sit under these categories in the task picker. Category Tasks Effects Apply Effects, Apply/Remove Effects, Area Effect and Apply To Caster. Asset Loaders The Set tasks. Process Create Mono Process, Run Process and Disjoint. Sequence Run Sequence and Inject. Waits Delay, Channel, Wait For Event, Wait For Tag (gained or lost) and Wait For Attribute (crossing a value). Events and Tags Send Event, Grant Tags and Cancel Abilities. Movement Dash and Blink. Items Consume Item. Cues Play Cue. Utility Unity Event. What some of them do: Area Effect applies its effects to each it takes within its radius of its caster, its target or its point. Where the activation has neither a target nor a point, it measures from its caster. It finds them by position on either hub, or with physics. Wait For Event, Wait For Tag and Wait For Attribute wait on the caster or the target. Each has a Timeout, and a Record As for a later stage's Condition. While a Wait For Event waits for one of the core's own events, the core sends it. Send Event sends an event to the caster or the targets. Grant Tags grants loose tags while its stage runs. Cancel Abilities cancels the caster's running abilities by tag, except one in a critical stage. Dash and Blink tell a mover of the game's own: an IForgeMover on the caster's object, as the Creator Lab's units have. Consume Item is heard by its item system's Item Consumed. Play Cue plays its cues at the stage's moment, on the caster, on the target or at the point. Apply Effects' Record Landed As tags the activation's data as an effect lands on a target, for a later stage's Condition. Dash, Blink, Area Effect, Apply To Caster and Consume Item were the Demo's own.

guides/abilities/stages/cancelling-and-b.title: Cancelling and blocking | PlayForge
guides/abilities/stages/cancelling-and-b.summary: Cancelling and blocking An ability's Cancelled By and Blocks lists name other abilities, by asset tag or a context tag, or a child of one. List What it does Cancelled By The abilities it names cancel this one as they activate. The ability is interrupted, then the other starts. Blocks The abilities it names can't activate while this one runs. Each stage that names none of its own takes the ability's lists, and targeting takes its Cancelled By too. A critical stage is committed, so nothing cancels it. A blocked activation is refused, unless When Busy is Queue: then it waits in the input buffer for the block to lift. A stage's own Cancelled By and Blocks hold while it runs. A heavy attack's recovery can name the specials that cut it short, and its windup none.

guides/abilities/stages/critical-stages..title: Critical stages | PlayForge
guides/abilities/stages/critical-stages..summary: Critical stages A stage that holds a critical task is critical: it commits the ability to the stage. The stage list shows Critical on the stage's row. A critical stage is committed, so nothing cancels it. The activation keeps its claim until its last critical stage ends. With no critical stage, it lets the claim go as the stages start. A critical stage that's skipped lets the claim go as the next stage starts (see Stage conditions).

guides/abilities/stages/stage-conditions.title: Stage conditions | PlayForge
guides/abilities/stages/stage-conditions.summary: Stage conditions A stage's Condition sets when the stage runs, by a tag. With no tag, the stage always runs. Otherwise it runs only while the tag is there, or, with When Missing, only while it isn't. A stage whose condition fails is skipped. Property Description Looked For On Where the tag is looked for. The Activation: the activation's data, as Record Landed As fills it. Caster or Target: that entity's tags. When Missing Runs the stage only while the tag is missing. Both show once the condition names a tag. Two stages that name one tag, one wanting it and one wanting it missing, branch: a jab's hit recovery and its whiff. Tip A critical stage that's skipped lets the claim go as the next stage starts. So put a committed whiff before the hit's recovery, and the claim goes as that recovery starts.

guides/abilities/stages/stage-properties.title: Stage properties | PlayForge
guides/abilities/stages/stage-properties.summary: Stage properties Each stage starts all its tasks together, and the next stage starts when it ends. Property Description Completion All ends the stage when every task has finished. Any ends it when the first task finishes, and cancels the rest. A stage with no policy set behaves as All. Apply Usage Effects Applies the ability's cost and cooldown in this stage. They apply once per activation, in the first stage that does this. At Stage Start Under Apply Usage Effects. On, it applies them as the stage starts; off, as it ends, and only if it succeeded. Tasks The stage's work, such as Apply Effects, Delay or Run Sequence. See Tasks. Condition When the stage runs, by a tag. See Stage conditions. Cancelled By and Blocks The stage's own lists, which hold while it runs. See Cancelling and blocking. If no stage applies usage effects, the cost and cooldown apply as the ability starts, after its targeting. In the stage list: A stage folds to one line of what it holds, as "2 tasks · All · Applies usage effects". It shows Critical on its row while a task commits the ability to it. The list's − removes the selected stage. A stage keeps its fold as others are removed or dragged.

guides/abilities/stages/tasks.html.title: Tasks | PlayForge
guides/abilities/stages/tasks.html.summary: Tasks A stage's Tasks are its work, such as Apply Effects, Delay or Run Sequence. To add a task: Click the list's +. It adds an empty task. Pick a kind for it from the searchable picker, in which each task sits under its category (see Built-in tasks). A task's numbers, as Delay's milliseconds and Channel's duration, are numbers that can scale by level. They're read as the task runs, at its ability's level. A stage that holds a critical task is critical. Your own tasks in the picker A task of your own names its submenu with [ForgeMenu("Effects", Description = "...")]. A slash nests one submenu in another. A class's path holds for those made from it. A task that names no submenu sits after the submenus. A task's Description is what the picker's Context says while it's highlighted. Run Sequence Run Sequence runs the sequence a static method makes. You pick it in Sequence by name, from a searchable dropdown of the project's [TaskSequenceMethod] methods; where more than one class holds them, each class's sit under its name. For an ability built in code, it runs a fresh run of the sequence its Definition describes, which TaskSequenceBuilder makes. Its Clock picks the clock that sequence runs by. The ability's other tasks keep the caster's. Option Clock None The sequence's own, or the caster's. Caster's The caster's. Game's The game's. Unscaled Runs while the game is paused. Scaled A pace of its own.

guides/abilities/tags.html.title: Tags | PlayForge
guides/abilities/tags.html.summary: Tags An ability's tags describe it, and some of them are applied to its entity while it has the ability or while it runs. Property Description Context Tags Describe the ability, such as Spell or Melee, and are not applied to the entity. The changes made by effects this ability applies carry them as context, and workers can filter by them. Passive Tags Applied to the entity while it has the ability. Active Tags Applied to the entity while an activation of the ability is running.

guides/abilities/used-by.html.title: Used By | PlayForge
guides/abilities/used-by.html.summary: Used By The Used By section lists the PlayForge assets that refer to this ability, each with its type icon. They include an entity that starts with it, an item that grants it, or a cost linked to it. Click a row to select the asset. The list follows the project as it changes.

guides/abilities/workers.html.title: Workers | PlayForge
guides/abilities/workers.html.summary: Workers Workers are reusable behaviours, picked from a list, that react to what happens to an entity. This group is subscribed to the entity when it learns the ability, and removed when the ability is removed. Name labels the group. It holds four lists: List What its workers do Attribute Run before or after an attribute changes, for example to reduce incoming damage. Impact Inspect the changes this entity deals. Tag React when the entity's tags change. Analysis Examine the frame at its end, for example to detect death. Each list's + adds an empty worker to pick a kind for. The section's import button copies a worker group from another asset. In this section On Hit: On Hit, above the workers, holds the effects the entity's hits apply while it knows the ability, as a passive's. Modifiers: Modifiers, under On Hit, change other effects as they're made, while the entity knows the ability. Lifesteal: An ability gives its holder lifesteal by an effect that raises the holder's Lifesteal, as a passive applies it to its caster.

guides/abilities/workers/lifesteal.html.title: Lifesteal | PlayForge
guides/abilities/workers/lifesteal.html.summary: Lifesteal An ability gives its holder lifesteal by an effect that raises the holder's Lifesteal, as a passive applies it to its caster. Lifesteal is the attribute the project's Lifesteal worker names as its Share. The Lifesteal worker heals by it (Workers: Lifesteal). For example, a vampiric mask's Infinite effect of +0.15 Lifesteal heals its wearer 15% of each blow it deals. The ability's Lifesteal list is gone.

guides/abilities/workers/modifiers.html.title: Modifiers | PlayForge
guides/abilities/workers/modifiers.html.summary: Modifiers Modifiers, under On Hit, change other effects as they're made, while the entity knows the ability. They change either: its holder's own, as a boon that adds a burst to its holder's every Chill; or those landing on it, as a cloak that halves the stuns its wearer takes. Each entry is a rule of its own or names a shared Effect Modifier asset (Effects: Workers: Modifiers).

guides/abilities/workers/on-hit.html.title: On Hit | PlayForge
guides/abilities/workers/on-hit.html.summary: On Hit On Hit, above the workers, holds the effects the entity's hits apply while it knows the ability, as a passive's. Its entries are an item's (Items: Workers: On Hit). Each holds: an attribute; the effects, to the one hit or the holder; whether it applies only on a kill; impact types; a condition.

guides/attribute-sets/all-attributes.htm.title: All Attributes | PlayForge
guides/attribute-sets/all-attributes.htm.summary: All Attributes All Attributes is a table of each attribute the set gives an entity, its sub-sets' included, once each. It shows the value its Current starts at, at each level, and the range the set keeps it in. The values are the ones the elements show, in the set this set is previewed in. Hover over a value for its Current and Base at each level. Where several elements give an attribute, the hover also says whose value is used. The Entity inspector shows the same table under the entity's Attribute Set, at the entity's levels.

guides/attribute-sets/attributes.html.title: Attributes | PlayForge
guides/attribute-sets/attributes.html.summary: Attributes The Attributes section lists the set's elements, each of which sets up one attribute. Folded, an element shows one line: what its attribute starts at, and its range. Property Description Attribute The attribute asset, in the element's row. Starts At What the attribute starts at, at each of the set's levels. Base A magnitude field, as an effect's are: a number, or a cached scaler with how the number combines with it. Link Current to Base Current takes Base's number and scaler, and its own field hides. Current A magnitude field, as Base is. Bounds The range the values are held in, with the Floor and Ceiling the policy reads, each a Current and a Base. Auto Clamp Applies the Bounds. With it off, the Bounds are ignored at runtime. Scale With Base When Base changes, changes Current by the same share. A value of 80/100 that loses half its Base ends at 40/50. Rounding None, To Floor, To Ceil, Round, or Snap To with a Snap Interval, a number field read at its owner's level. Retention Group The group the root value counts toward. Groups split an attribute's value for queries and UI, such as base and bonus health; they never change the math. Collision What to do when this attribute appears more than once across the set and its sub-sets. See Collision Settings. One kind of cached scaler follows the entity's level. Another follows a different attribute, and this attribute is then worked out again whenever that one changes. The Base and Current fields' menus each copy the other side's number and scaler into the field. Rounding applies after the Bounds, each time the value changes. So it can make a change bigger or smaller than its effect asked for. In this section Starts At: Starts At shows what an element's attribute starts at, at each of the set's levels, with the levels on the right. Bounds: An element's Bounds set the range its values are held in, with the Floor and Ceiling the policy reads, each a Current and a Base. Preview In: Preview In shows a set's elements as part of a set that holds it.

guides/attribute-sets/attributes/bounds..title: Bounds | PlayForge
guides/attribute-sets/attributes/bounds..summary: Bounds An element's Bounds set the range its values are held in, with the Floor and Ceiling the policy reads, each a Current and a Base. Policy What it holds Zero To Base Current stays between 0 and Base. Floor To Base Current stays between the Floor's Current and Base. Base stays at or above the Floor's Base. Zero To Ceil Current stays between 0 and the Ceiling's Current. Base stays between 0 and the Ceiling's Base. Floor To Ceil Current and Base each stay between their Floor and Ceiling. Unlimited No bounds. Right-click a Floor or a Ceiling for No Floor or No Ceiling. A magnitude you type is kept within the bounds. A stored magnitude outside them, as after the bounds change, shows a warning, and the runtime clamps it. With Auto Clamp off, the Bounds are ignored at runtime.

guides/attribute-sets/attributes/preview.title: Preview In | PlayForge
guides/attribute-sets/attributes/preview.summary: Preview In Preview In shows a set's elements as part of a set that holds it. It appears above the list while another set holds this one as a sub-set. Choose This Set, or a set that holds it, directly or through another. An entity built from that set starts with these attributes as part of it. So the elements and All Attributes show their values there, with that set's collisions and the attributes it gives. The choice lasts until the editor closes.

guides/attribute-sets/attributes/starts-.title: Starts At | PlayForge
guides/attribute-sets/attributes/starts-.summary: Starts At Starts At shows what an element's attribute starts at, at each of the set's levels, with the levels on the right. One value a level, as "100/120/140/160". Current and Base apart, as "Current 50 · Base 80", when they differ. A range, past six levels. It's worked out as the runtime works it out: an entity at each level, built from the set, with its sub-sets, collisions, scalers, bounds and rounding, before any effect, item or worker acts on it. A note says when another element's value is the one used. A warning says when a scaler reads an attribute the set doesn't give, which reads 0.

guides/attribute-sets/collision-settings.title: Collision Settings | PlayForge
guides/attribute-sets/collision-settings.summary: Collision Settings These settings decide an attribute's root value when it appears in more than one element, across this set and its sub-sets. Property Description Resolution Policy How the deciding group picks a value, unless it's the Combine group. Use Maximum by default. The root value is decided in three steps: Elements are taken in order: this set's elements first, then each sub-set's in turn. Each element's Collision choice puts it in a group. One group decides, picked in this order: Use Set Collision Setting, Use This, Combine, Use Existing. Elements in the other groups are ignored. In the Combine group, the values are added up. Bounds, rounding and the retention group come from the first element. The other groups choose by the Resolution Policy: Policy What it picks Use Maximum (default) The element with the highest Base magnitude. Use Minimum The element with the lowest Base magnitude. Use Average The average of the elements' values. Bounds and rounding come from the first element. Use First and Use Last The first or the last element. Ignore The first element stands.

guides/attribute-sets/identity.html.title: Identity | PlayForge
guides/attribute-sets/identity.html.summary: Identity The Identity section names the set, shows its asset tag and holds its icons. Property Description Name The set's display name, which also gives the asset tag. Renaming the set changes its tag, so update anything that names the old tag. Description Free text for your UI. Asset Tag Read-only, made from the Name: punctuation is dropped, and each word is capitalised and joined. Textures Icons, each paired with a tag. The texture tagged Primary is the set's icon; without one, the first texture is used. The asset tag is stored when you edit the Name, and the inspector header shows it after the set's type. If the stored tag differs from the one the Name gives, it shows in warning text with an Update button that stores the new one.

guides/attribute-sets/index.html.title: Attribute Sets | PlayForge
guides/attribute-sets/index.html.summary: Attribute Sets An Attribute Set asset lists the attributes an entity starts with, and how each one starts: its Current and Base values, its bounds and its rounding. An entity is anything that runs a gameplay ability system (GAS), such as the player or an enemy. Its Entity asset names one set. When the GAS initializes, it builds every attribute in the set and in its sub-sets. Each element becomes its attribute's root value, the value before any effect. Gameplay effects then change the attribute on top of that root. A root can follow the entity's level or another attribute, through a cached scaler. It is worked out again whenever the attribute is recalculated. Tags are names, such as State.Stunned, that an entity carries and that requirements check. Each asset stores a tag made from its Name: Hero Stats gives AttributeSet.HeroStats. The entity carries the set's tag and the tags of its sub-sets. Each section below matches the inspector section of the same name. A collapsed section shows one line about what it holds, such as the level range or how many attributes the set gives. In this guide Identity: The Identity section names the set, shows its asset tag and holds its icons. Leveling: The Leveling section sets the level range the cached scalers on the set's elements are authored for. Attributes: The Attributes section lists the set's elements, each of which sets up one attribute. Sub-Sets: The Sub-Sets section lists other attribute sets this set includes. Collision Settings: These settings decide an attribute's root value when it appears in more than one element, across this set and its sub-sets. All Attributes: All Attributes is a table of each attribute the set gives an entity, its sub-sets' included, once each. Workers: Workers are reusable behaviours, picked from a list, that react to what happens to an entity. Local Data: Local Data is a list of named values stored on the asset. Used By: The Used By section lists the PlayForge assets that refer to this set, each with its type icon, such as an entity built from it or a set that holds it as a sub-set.

guides/attribute-sets/leveling.html.title: Leveling | PlayForge
guides/attribute-sets/leveling.html.summary: Leveling The Leveling section sets the level range the cached scalers on the set's elements are authored for. A cached scaler is a value source for an element, such as a table with one value per level. At runtime, those scalers follow the level of the entity that owns the set. Linking the set to that Entity asset gives the scalers one value per entity level. A level provider is an asset whose level range another asset follows. Property Description Link Mode Standalone (default): keeps the set's own range. Linked To Provider: takes the range from a level provider instead. Starting Level The start of the set's own range, 1 by default. Max Level The end of the set's own range, 4 by default. Cached scalers on its elements whose Level Configuration is Lock To Level Provider use it to size their per-level values. Level Provider Shown while linked: the asset the range comes from, an Entity, Ability, Effect, Item or Attribute Set. Right-click the Level Provider field to pick from one type. A link that would make a loop is refused, with an error in the Console. While no provider is set, a warning says the set uses its own range. While linked, Starting Level and Max Level show the range in use, read-only.

guides/attribute-sets/local-data.html.title: Local Data | PlayForge
guides/attribute-sets/local-data.html.summary: Local Data Local Data is a list of named values stored on the asset. Each row has a Key (a tag) and a value of a kind. Column Description Key A tag that names the row. Kind The kind of value: Float, Int, String, Bool, Tag, Attribute, Effect, Ability, Entity, Object, MonoBehaviour or ScriptableObject, or a kind of your own. Value The row's value. A row saves its own value alone. A kind of your own is a [Serializable] class made from LocalDataValue<T>, such as a point or a colour. The row's kinds offer it beside PlayForge's. Object fields take project assets, not scene objects. Code reads a value by its type, with data.TryGet(out float range) or data.TryGet(out MyPoint point). A number, a Float or an Int, can scale. Code reads it with data.Value.TryReadNumber(context, out float number). PlayForge doesn't read an attribute set's Local Data itself. Your code and workers can, with set.TryGetLocalData(key, out var data). The first row with that key wins.

guides/attribute-sets/sub-sets.html.title: Sub-Sets | PlayForge
guides/attribute-sets/sub-sets.html.summary: Sub-Sets The Sub-Sets section lists other attribute sets this set includes. Property Description Sub-Sets Other attribute sets this set includes, one a row. The entity gets their attributes as well, and those of their own sub-sets in turn. Their asset tags are applied to the entity, and their workers are subscribed with this set's. When an attribute appears more than once, Collision Settings decide which value it starts with. Only the Collision Settings of the set the entity names are used. All Attributes lists each attribute the set gives, sub-sets included. Note Don't let a set include itself, directly or through another set: nothing stops the loop.

guides/attribute-sets/used-by.html.title: Used By | PlayForge
guides/attribute-sets/used-by.html.summary: Used By The Used By section lists the PlayForge assets that refer to this set, each with its type icon, such as an entity built from it or a set that holds it as a sub-set. Click a row to select the asset. The list follows the project as it changes.

guides/attribute-sets/workers.html.title: Workers | PlayForge
guides/attribute-sets/workers.html.summary: Workers Workers are reusable behaviours, picked from a list, that react to what happens to an entity. This group is subscribed when the entity's GAS initializes, with each sub-set's group, and stays for the entity's lifetime. Property Description Name Labels the group. Attribute Workers that run before or after an attribute changes, for example to reduce incoming damage. Impact Workers that inspect the changes the entity deals. Tag Workers that react when the entity's tags change. Analysis Workers that examine the frame at its end, for example to detect death. Each list's + adds an empty worker to pick a kind for. The section's import button copies a worker group from another asset.

guides/attributes/identity.html.title: Identity | PlayForge
guides/attributes/identity.html.summary: Identity The Identity section names the attribute and says what it is. Property Description Name The attribute's display name. Give each attribute its own Name: some lookups compare attributes by Name, such as an attribute worker matching the attribute it watches. Abbreviation A short form, such as HP. The collapsed section shows it. Description Free text for your UI. Role What the attribute is, which says how bonuses to it add up and how a number reads it. Gains Scaled By An attribute that multiplies each workable gain to this one's current, on the same entity. Textures Icons, each paired with a tag. The texture tagged Primary is the attribute's icon; without one, the first texture is used. An attribute that plays one of its project's roles says so in this section, as "Plays Health in Arena". In this section Role: An attribute's Role says what it is: how bonuses to it add up, and how a number reads it. Barrier: A Barrier attribute is a shield before another attribute, such as Health. Gains Scaled By: Gains Scaled By names an attribute that multiplies each workable gain to this one's current, on the same entity.

guides/attributes/identity/barrier.html.title: Barrier | PlayForge
guides/attributes/identity/barrier.html.summary: Barrier A Barrier attribute is a shield before another attribute, such as Health. While the Role is Barrier, the Identity section shows its settings. Property Description Absorbs For The attribute it absorbs for. Each workable loss to that one comes off the barrier first, as much as it holds, and the rest goes on. Decay Per Second A number field, read at its holder's level, that takes the barrier down by its holder's own time: a number a second. Topaz Brooch's barrier fades so. Decay As Share Of Base Reads Decay Per Second as that share of the barrier's base. Fades With Effect Fades what a lasting effect gives the barrier to 0 by the time that effect ends. Two hits in a frame soak no more than it holds. What it soaks comes off it at the frame's end. A hit the barrier soaks whole is no loss to the other attribute, so an On Hit counting it doesn't go off.

guides/attributes/identity/gains-scaled-.title: Gains Scaled By | PlayForge
guides/attributes/identity/gains-scaled-.summary: Gains Scaled By Gains Scaled By names an attribute that multiplies each workable gain to this one's current, on the same entity. Health's gains are scaled by Healing Received, so a curse at 0.5 halves heals and Ice Blast's 0 blocks them. A loss passes it by. A gain to the base, such as more maximum, passes it by too.

guides/attributes/identity/role.html.title: Role | PlayForge
guides/attributes/identity/role.html.summary: Role An attribute's Role says what it is: how bonuses to it add up, and how a number reads it. Value is every attribute's role unless it says otherwise. Role How bonuses add up How a number reads it Value Bonuses add and multiply as each effect says. As it is. Bonus Share, such as Damage Amplification at 0.2 for 20% Bonuses add: +20% and +30% make 0.5. × Attribute reads it as a multiplier, 1 + x, so an attack of 100 that reads it deals 150. Multiplier, such as Damage Dealt at 1 As a Value. As it is. Resistance, a share taken off or a chance, such as Damage Resistance Bonuses stack with diminishing returns, each on what's left: two of 30% make 51%, and none takes it past 1. × Attribute reads what's left, 1 − x. Barrier, such as a shield before Health It absorbs losses for the attribute its Absorbs For names. — For a Resistance, the lasting bonuses diminish. A permanent change, which an instant or periodic impact commits, adds as it is. A role sets the defaults, which an effect or a number can override: An effect's impact can add its own way, with its Add Behaviour: as the attribute's role says, a plain Sum, or Diminishing. A number can read its own way, with × Attribute's Read As.

Object fields take project assets, not scene objects. Code reads a value by its type, with data.TryGet(out float range) or data.TryGet(out MyPoint point). A number, a Float or an Int, can scale. Code reads it with data.Value.TryReadNumber(context, out float number). PlayForge doesn't read an attribute's Local Data itself. Your code and workers can, with attribute.TryGetLocalData(key, out var data). The first row with that key wins.

guides/attributes/roles.html.title: Roles | PlayForge
guides/attributes/roles.html.summary: Roles A game's settings live on its Forge Project, the asset at the root of its folder that The Forge's projects are. Among them are its Roles: the part each attribute plays in the game, each a role tag and the attribute that plays it. PlayForge's own features read the roles it ships, and a game's code reads its own by their tags, so no attribute's name is built in. Role Tag What reads it Health Tags.ROLE_HEALTH What an entity dies of as it reaches 0, where no death watcher of its own watches for its death and its Death doesn't say otherwise (Entities: Death). What On Hit counts, lifesteal heals and Execute reads, where they name no attribute. Whose loss names the killer, for Kill and Died. Luck Tags.ROLE_LUCK It's read on the caster of every chance that gives no luck of its own. Movement Speed Tags.ROLE_MOVEMENT_SPEED What the Creator Lab's units walk at, where its rules name none. A role of your own Any tag, such as Role.Energy, in the same list Code reads it with ForgeRoles.AttributeFor(tag), and an ability's attribute cost can spend it (Abilities: Activation). An entity whose set has no attribute in the Health role doesn't die of it. Each role is optional, and an empty one leaves things as they were. In this section Project Settings: Project Settings → PlayForge shows the active project's settings under Forge Project. The project a game reads: A running game reads its settings from ForgeProject.Current. What the Problems window checks: The Problems window checks attribute costs, roles and deaths against each asset's project.

guides/attributes/roles/project-settings.title: Project Settings | PlayForge
guides/attributes/roles/project-settings.summary: Project Settings Project Settings → PlayForge shows the active project's settings under Forge Project. Fill Roles by Name fills each of PlayForge's roles that no attribute plays yet with the project's attribute of its name. Create Forge Project makes the default project, where there's none. The settings also hold the project's default Crowd Control (Abilities: Requirements: Crowd Control).

guides/attributes/roles/the-project-a-ga.title: The project a game reads | PlayForge
guides/attributes/roles/the-project-a-ga.summary: The project a game reads A running game reads its settings from ForgeProject.Current. That's the project code sets with ForgeProject.Use(project), as a test or a game with no GameRoot does, or else the one its GameRoot names in its Project field. A build has the project because the GameRoot names it. Play mode reads it as a build does, not The Forge's active project. In the editor, the inspectors and the Problems window read each asset against its own project: the one whose folder holds it.

guides/attributes/roles/what-the-problem.title: What the Problems window checks | PlayForge
guides/attributes/roles/what-the-problem.summary: What the Problems window checks The Problems window checks attribute costs, roles and deaths against each asset's project. It warns of: an ability's attribute cost that spends nothing, or one that spends a role no attribute plays in its project; an entity whose starting abilities spend attributes its set doesn't give; an entity that stays when it dies whose set lacks the Health role's attribute, with no death watcher of its own.

guides/attributes/used-by.html.title: Used By | PlayForge
guides/attributes/used-by.html.summary: Used By The Used By section lists the PlayForge assets that refer to this attribute, each with its type icon: the Attribute Sets that give its starting values; the Gameplay Effects that change it; the validation rules and ability costs that check or spend it. Click a row to select the asset. The list follows the project as it changes.

guides/creator-lab/battle.html.title: Battle | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/battle.html.summary: Battle The Battle mode fights teams of bots. In this section Setting up a battle: You set up a battle in the Lab panel's Battle section. How bots fight: A bot takes the nearest foe it can target, casts what's ready, and otherwise attacks with its attack.

guides/creator-lab/battle/how-bots-fight.title: How bots fight | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/battle/how-bots-fight.summary: How bots fight A bot takes the nearest foe it can target, casts what's ready, and otherwise attacks with its attack. Its order and its moments are its rules', read from Local Data under these keys (The lab's rules): Rule Description Cast Order Key The Local Data key an entity's order is under, as "W Q E": the letters of its abilities other than its attack, in its entity's order. With none, it casts each in turn. Cast When Key The key for when it casts an ability. Reach Key The key for an ability's reach, 0 for anywhere, where it has no reach of its own, as a Cast Range. An ability that has one reaches as far as that does. An ability's Cast When Key names one of these moments: Moment The bot casts the ability InRange (the default) With its foe in reach. Hurt Below 60% health. Low Below 35%, away from its foe, as an escape. Stunned While something stops it. FoeLow With its foe below half. Low on health, a bot backs off a moment once in a while. The Demo's AI hero is a bot, its roster giving the keys.

guides/creator-lab/battle/setting-up-a-b.title: Setting up a battle | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/battle/setting-up-a-b.summary: Setting up a battle You set up a battle in the Lab panel's Battle section. Pick an entity and a side at the top of the Lab panel. Pick a level in Level. Select Add bot. Each side stands in a line of its own: Side Its line Blue To the south Red To the north Green To the west Gold To the east The section's other buttons run the battle: Button What it does Quick battle Makes Blue against Red, with as many bots on each side as A side sets. Each bot is the entity selected in the library, or one picked at random from the project's. Play Starts the fight and the lab's time. Reset Makes every bot anew where it started, at full, with the items and abilities you gave it since, and their levels. The line under the buttons says who stands, and who won, or that no one stands.

guides/creator-lab/dropping-assets.html.title: Dropping assets | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/dropping-assets.html.summary: Dropping assets You give assets to units by dragging them from the library and dropping them on the space. Dropped On What happens An effect A unit It lands on the unit, from the selected unit, or from the lab's caster. An ability A unit, or the ground The selected unit, or the lab's caster, casts it there. An item A unit It's given to the unit, equipped. An entity or an attribute set The ground A test dummy of it is put down, on the side the Lab panel's picker names. When you drop an ability: Its target goes in the activation's data, as click targeting takes it with no click. A unit that doesn't know the ability learns it first. An ability that needs more than the point waits for a click, which Esc cancels.

guides/creator-lab/in-code.html.title: In code | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/in-code.html.summary: In code The lab can be made, driven and read from code. Note A build can leave the lab out by defining PLAYFORGE_NO_LAB. The Demo uses the lab's units, so it goes too. In this section Making and driving a lab: CreatorLab.Create(library, rules, panels) makes a lab, as the tests do. Libraries: A lab's library, the assets it plays, is an ILabLibrary. Your unit in code: The lab's members for your unit match its Your unit section. Showing its working in code: What the lab shows of its working is its Showing, a LabShowing.

guides/creator-lab/in-code/libraries.htm.title: Libraries | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/in-code/libraries.htm.summary: Libraries A lab's library, the assets it plays, is an ILabLibrary. Library Where What it holds EditorLabLibrary The editor Every asset of the project. ListLibrary Code The assets given. ListLibrary.Of(project) A game's own build The assets its Forge Project's catalog names. The lab plays it where no editor gives it a library. A library offers projects to switch between through ILabLibrary.Projects, Project and UseProject, which have defaults.

guides/creator-lab/in-code/making-and-dr.title: Making and driving a lab | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/in-code/making-and-dr.summary: Making and driving a lab CreatorLab.Create(library, rules, panels) makes a lab, as the tests do. Its calls are the panels': For Calls Units AddUnit and AddDummy Assets ApplyEffect, CastAt and GiveItem Dropping Drop (at a point of the screen) and DropAt (on a unit or a point) The lab Select, SetMode, ResetDummies and Clear Its time Step, Paused, Speed and StepFrame

guides/creator-lab/in-code/showing-its-w.title: Showing its working in code | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/in-code/showing-its-w.summary: Showing its working in code What the lab shows of its working is its Showing, a LabShowing. Member What it is Journal An EffectJournal over every unit. Stops Its stops, added with Add(stop). As one fires, StoppedBy and StoppedFor say which and what fired it. Resume() lets it go, and StepTick() steps on as Step Tick does. Watches Its watches, pinned with Pin(watch). Log ForgeLog's messages.

guides/creator-lab/in-code/your-unit-in-.title: Your unit in code | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/in-code/your-unit-in-.summary: Your unit in code The lab's members for your unit match its Your unit section. The unit you control is ControlledUnit, given by PutDownOwnUnit, TakeControl and ReleaseControl. Its camera is set by Follow. The lab's controls are its Controls, a LabControls, whose Driver comes before its rules'. A game's own player can be a LabControls too, as the Demo's is: its unit set on it, or its ControlledUnit() overridden.

guides/creator-lab/index.html.title: The Creator Lab | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/index.html.summary: The Creator Lab The Creator Lab is a space for trying a project's own assets. You put units down, give them abilities, effects and items, cast, and watch the numbers move. The Creator Lab: a quick battle with the Demo's heroes, a unit selected. To open it, choose Window → PlayForge → Creator Lab. It opens in a new scene and plays. The scenes open before are saved first, if you want them saved. The lab plays every PlayForge asset in the project's own folders. In this guide The space: The space is the scene the lab plays in: its ground, its camera, its units and the lab's caster. The panels: The lab's panels sit at the edges of the screen. Dropping assets: You give assets to units by dragging them from the library and dropping them on the space. Test dummies: A test dummy is a unit that stands and counts what it takes. Battle: The Battle mode fights teams of bots. Your unit: In either mode you can play a unit of your own, with the Demo's controls. Time: The lab's units live in a world of the lab's own (ProcessWorld), which the lab steps by its own time. Showing its working: The bottom panel's pages show what happens as the lab plays. The lab's rules: The lab's rules tell it a few things about a project: which attribute is a unit's health, which it walks at, which tags stop, hide or shield it, and which ability is its attack. In code: The lab can be made, driven and read from code. In the API The types of this guide's area: CreatorLab, CreatorLabMenu, EditorLabLibrary, ELabStopKind, ELabWatchKind, ILabLibrary, ILabRules, ILabUnitDriver, LabAssetKind, LabAssets, LabBlow, LabBodyDriver, LabBot, LabCamera, LabControls, LabDriver, LabDriverEditor, LabDummy, LabEffects, LabMode, LabPanels, LabRules, LabRulesEditor, LabRulesExtensions, LabSeat, LabShowing, LabSide, LabSides, LabStop, LabSummary, LabUnit, LabUnitSpec, LabWatch, ListLibrary.

guides/creator-lab/showing-its-working.h.title: Showing its working | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/showing-its-working.h.summary: Showing its working The bottom panel's pages show what happens as the lab plays. Each records only while the lab runs. In this section Journal: The Journal page is the lab's effect journal over every unit, newest first. Combat: The Combat page is the selected unit's combat log, newest first. Stops: The Stops page holds a list of what pauses the lab's world. Watches: The Watches page pins numbers on the selected unit, and draws each over time. Log: The Log page shows PlayForge's messages as ForgeLog lets them through, by system, newest first.

guides/creator-lab/showing-its-working/c.title: Combat | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/showing-its-working/c.summary: Combat The Combat page is the selected unit's combat log, newest first. Each hit has its steps under it, as "-30 as made → Math -30 → -15 (inline) → landed -15". The project's combat log writes it (Project Settings → PlayForge → Combat Log).

guides/creator-lab/showing-its-working/j.title: Journal | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/showing-its-working/j.summary: Journal The Journal page is the lab's effect journal over every unit, newest first. It records: each effect landing, with its number traced; each effect refused, and why; each effect ticking, hitting and coming off; each worker that ran, by its hook and its side, with the actions it queued and whether they ran. It shows what happened on the selected unit or, with Selected unit off, on any. Click an entry to see its parts: a number's, a hit's breakdown, or a worker's actions.

guides/creator-lab/showing-its-working/l.title: Log | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/showing-its-working/l.summary: Log The Log page shows PlayForge's messages as ForgeLog lets them through, by system, newest first. Control What it does Selected unit While it's on, the page shows only the messages about the selected unit. System and Level Give a system a level of its own, which the Console keeps too. As all Gives the system back the Logging preference's level.

guides/creator-lab/showing-its-working/s.title: Stops | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/showing-its-working/s.summary: Stops The Stops page holds a list of what pauses the lab's world. A stop fires when: an effect lands, is refused or has a worker run; an attribute crosses a value; a tag comes or goes; an ability is refused. Each stop watches the selected unit or any. It names an effect, an ability, a tag or an attribute where it asks for one, and Any for an effect or an ability takes any. As one fires, the world pauses, and the page says which stop fired and what fired it. Button What it does Go Plays on. Step Frame Goes one frame. Step Tick Goes on until an effect ticks on the selected unit, or on any, up to ten seconds, or until a stop fires.

guides/creator-lab/showing-its-working/w.title: Watches | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/showing-its-working/w.summary: Watches The Watches page pins numbers on the selected unit, and draws each over time. You can pin: an attribute's current or base value; a tag's count; an effect's stacks or time left; a Scaler asset read on the unit. Each shows as a line over the last minute of the lab's time, in its own color and scaled to its own range, with its value now.

guides/creator-lab/test-dummies.html.title: Test dummies | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/test-dummies.html.summary: Test dummies A test dummy is a unit that stands and counts what it takes. The Lab panel's Test dummies section puts down a dummy of any entity or attribute set, on a side: Blue, Red, Green, Gold or Neutral. Button What it does Add Puts down a dummy of the entity picked, on the side picked. Reset Puts each dummy back where it was put, at full. Clear Takes every unit out. A dummy: counts what it takes: its damage a second, the last blow by its impact types and the effect it came from, and a short history, which the Selected panel shows; doesn't die unless asked: falling, it's revived where it stands, at full; mends to full when it's left alone for three seconds. Changing assets as the lab plays An asset you change while the lab plays takes effect the next time it's read. An effect or an entity changed in the inspector or The Forge as the lab plays is read on its next application, as every asset is. What a unit was made from, its attribute set and its starting abilities, shows on a new unit.

guides/creator-lab/the-labs-rules.html.title: The lab's rules | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/the-labs-rules.html.summary: The lab's rules The lab's rules tell it a few things about a project: which attribute is a unit's health, which it walks at, which tags stop, hide or shield it, and which ability is its attack. With no rules given, the lab: takes the attributes playing the project's Health and Movement Speed roles (Attributes: Roles), or else finds the attributes named Health and Movement Speed (or Move Speed); walks a unit without a speed at 4 a second. Lab Rules properties To say more, you give the lab a Lab Rules asset. Make one with Create → PlayForge → Lab Rules. Give it to the lab's CreatorLab component. Property Description Health The attribute that is a unit's health. Left empty, it's the project's. Movement Speed The attribute a unit walks at. Left empty, it's the project's. Walk Speed How fast a unit walks where it has no Movement Speed. Stops Tags that stop a unit moving, as Stunned. Hides Tags under which the other side can't see or target it, as Invisible. Shields Tags under which no one can target it. Attack Range Key The Local Data key a unit's attack range is under. Attack Range An attack range for every unit, in place of the key. Attack Slot Which of an entity's starting abilities is its attack, from 0, or −1 for none. Driver The project's Lab Driver, which the unit you control is ordered about through (Your unit). A unit whose attack has a reach of its own, as a Cast Range, attacks from as far as it reaches. The rules also hold the bots' keys: Cast Order Key, Cast When Key and Reach Key (Battle). The Demo's roster is the Demo's rules: its units, camera and dummy are the lab's, so the two can't drift.

guides/creator-lab/the-panels.html.title: The panels | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/the-panels.html.summary: The panels The lab's panels sit at the edges of the screen. The middle of the screen is the space's. Panel Where What it holds Library Left The active Forge Project's assets, by kind. Selected Right, over the Lab panel What's selected. It's shown as something is selected. Lab Right, under Selected The mode, the test dummies, the camera and the lab's time. Log Bottom A page for each way the lab shows its working. It's collapsed until you open it. The status Top, between the panels What a cast waits for, what's selected, and the keys for what you can do now. Each panel but Selected collapses to a tab at its edge with its − button. In this section The Library panel: The Library panel, on the left, lists the active Forge Project's assets by kind, each kind by name. The Selected panel: The Selected panel shows what's selected: an asset from the library, or a unit in the space. The Lab panel: The Lab panel, on the right under the Selected panel, holds the mode, the test dummies, the camera and the lab's time. The Log panel: The Log panel, at the bottom, shows the lab's working as it plays. The status: The status runs along the top of the screen, between the panels, and says what's going on.

guides/creator-lab/the-panels/the-lab-pa.title: The Lab panel | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/the-panels/the-lab-pa.summary: The Lab panel The Lab panel, on the right under the Selected panel, holds the mode, the test dummies, the camera and the lab's time. Section What it does The mode buttons Pick the mode (Modes). Entity and Side Pick the entity and the side a dummy, a bot or your unit is put down as. Test dummies Puts down dummies, in the Dummies mode (Test dummies). Your unit Puts down a unit for you to control, or takes one (Your unit). Battle Adds bots and runs a fight, in the Battle mode (Battle). Camera Its Distance and Tilt sliders, and Reset view (The camera). Time Pause, Step and Speed (Time).

guides/creator-lab/the-panels/the-librar.title: The Library panel | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/the-panels/the-librar.summary: The Library panel The Library panel, on the left, lists the active Forge Project's assets by kind, each kind by name. The kinds are abilities, effects, items, entities, attribute sets, attributes and scalers. While the project has no Forge Project, the panel lists every asset of the project. A kind's color shows in its icon alone. Control What it does Project Switches the active project, as The Forge does. It also follows The Forge's switch. The search box Filters the assets. Refresh Lists the assets again, after you make or delete one. Click an asset Shows its numbers in the Selected panel. Drag an asset Drops it on the space (Dropping assets).

guides/creator-lab/the-panels/the-log-pa.title: The Log panel | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/the-panels/the-log-pa.summary: The Log panel The Log panel, at the bottom, shows the lab's working as it plays. It's collapsed until you open it. It holds a page for each way the lab shows its working (Showing its working): Page What it shows Journal The lab's effect journal. Combat The selected unit's combat log. Stops What pauses the lab's world. Watches Numbers pinned on the selected unit, over time. Log PlayForge's messages.

guides/creator-lab/the-panels/the-select.title: The Selected panel | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/the-panels/the-select.summary: The Selected panel The Selected panel shows what's selected: an asset from the library, or a unit in the space. It sits on the right, over the Lab panel, and shows as something is selected. Its Lab tab sets it aside, the selection kept. The Lab panel's Selected tab brings it back, as each selection does. Selected What the panel shows An asset, clicked in the library Its numbers level by level, as "−80/−120/−160 Health". Open in The Forge opens it there. A unit, clicked in the space Its attributes, its tags, its effects with their stacks and time left, its abilities with their levels and cooldowns, and its items. For a unit, the panel has these controls: Control What it does − and + Change an ability's level. × Takes an ability or an item. Remove Takes the unit out. Take control Makes the unit yours (Your unit). Release Lets it go. A test dummy's count of what it took shows here too (Test dummies).

guides/creator-lab/the-panels/the-status.title: The status | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/the-panels/the-status.summary: The status The status runs along the top of the screen, between the panels, and says what's going on. Line What it says What a cast waits for The cast's wait, in its targeting's words, as "Bolt: Click a target · Esc or a right-click cancels". The lab's state What's selected, whom you control, and whether the lab is paused. The keys The keys for what you can do now. Clicks go through the status to the space.

guides/creator-lab/the-space.html.title: The space | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/the-space.html.summary: The space The space is the scene the lab plays in: its ground, its camera, its units and the lab's caster. Part Description The ground A plane in the middle of the scene, lit from above. The camera Looks down at an angle (The camera). Units Each a body and a GameplayAbilitySystem (Units). The lab's caster A unit of the lab's own, on no side, with no body. It's the source of what you drop while no unit is selected. In this section The camera: The lab's camera looks down at the space at an angle. Units: Each of the lab's units is a body and a GameplayAbilitySystem. Modes: The mode sets what the space holds.

guides/creator-lab/the-space/modes.html.title: Modes | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/the-space/modes.html.summary: Modes The mode sets what the space holds. You pick it with the buttons at the top of the Lab panel. Mode What the space holds Dummies Test dummies you put down (Test dummies). Battle Teams of bots that fight (Battle). None An empty space, where abilities still cast and effects still land. The lab starts in Dummies. Each mode starts with its units cleared.

guides/creator-lab/the-space/the-camera..title: The camera | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/the-space/the-camera..summary: The camera The lab's camera looks down at the space at an angle. Control What it does Scroll Pulls the camera back, or brings it in. Drag with the middle button Pans the camera. The right panel's Distance and Tilt sliders Set its distance and tilt. Reset view Puts the camera back.

guides/creator-lab/the-space/units.html.title: Units | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/the-space/units.html.summary: Units Each of the lab's units is a body and a GameplayAbilitySystem. Its body is a capsule, with a nose to show where it faces. A ring at its feet is in its side's color. A bar over it shows its name and health. A unit walks in a straight line where it's sent, and attacks what it's set on. A walk or a stop ends a turn to face that its abilities ordered, as a game's move would. Note PlayForge has no movement of its own, so the lab's movement is its own. A project's game moves its units its own way.

guides/creator-lab/time.html.title: Time | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/time.html.summary: Time The lab's units live in a world of the lab's own (ProcessWorld), which the lab steps by its own time. So its time stands still or runs faster without touching Unity's. Control What it does Pause Stops the lab's time. Step Goes one frame (a sixtieth of a second) while the lab is paused. Speed Runs the lab's time from a quarter to four times as fast. The camera and the panels go on while the lab is paused.

guides/creator-lab/your-unit.html.title: Your unit | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/your-unit.html.summary: Your unit In either mode you can play a unit of your own, with the Demo's controls. In this section Taking control: The Lab panel's Your unit section gives you a unit of your own to control. Controls: You control your unit with the mouse and the keys, as in the Demo. Drivers: Your unit's orders go through a driver.

guides/creator-lab/your-unit/controls.ht.title: Controls | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/your-unit/controls.ht.summary: Controls You control your unit with the mouse and the keys, as in the Demo. Input What it does Right-click the ground Walks there. Right-click a foe Attacks it. Right-click an ally Walks to it. Q, W, E and R Cast its abilities past its attack, in its entity's order. 1 to 6 Cast its items' active abilities. S Stops it. Left-click Picks the target of an ability that waits for one. Esc Cancels an ability that waits for its target. An ability that needs a target waits for a left-click. While it waits: a ring on the ground shows its reach, its Cast Range or its Reach; another ability's key casts that one instead; a right-click order lets it go; Esc cancels it. The click that picks a target selects nothing. The keys are the Lab Controls' own, as the status says them, and the ring's colors, width and material are its too. They read PlayForge's input, ForgeInput, so a game's own input or a test's stands in.

guides/creator-lab/your-unit/drivers.htm.title: Drivers | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/your-unit/drivers.htm.summary: Drivers Your unit's orders go through a driver. The lab's driver walks a unit in a straight line, and casts as the lab's units do. A project whose units move and cast their own way gives a driver of its own: Make a Lab Driver asset (Create → PlayForge → Lab Driver) of a class of your own. In that class, override the orders your game gives its own way: MoveTo, Attack, Cast and Stop. Each does as the lab's does unless overridden. Name the asset on your Lab Rules' Driver.

guides/creator-lab/your-unit/taking-cont.title: Taking control | PlayForge
guides/creator-lab/your-unit/taking-cont.summary: Taking control The Lab panel's Your unit section gives you a unit of your own to control. Button What it does Put down Puts down a unit of the entity picked above, on the side picked, where the camera looks, and gives you control of it. Take control Takes the unit selected. Release Lets your unit go. Follow Has the camera follow your unit. A bot you take over stops fighting until you let it go. A new fight passes it over. Reset keeps you on its seat's new bot. The line under the buttons says whom you control.

guides/cues/built-in-kinds.html.title: Built-in kinds | PlayForge
guides/cues/built-in-kinds.html.summary: Built-in kinds The kinds PlayForge ships for this guide's pickers, each with its menu and what it does, as its picker says. A project's own kinds join them in the same pickers. Cue handlers Kind Menu What it does CameraShakeCue — Shakes the camera as its moment comes. FloatingTextCue — Floats a text, as a hit's damage, the gold a kill gave or a status's name, where its placement says. PrefabCue — Places a prefab where its placement says, for a moment or for as long as the cue lasts. ProcessCue (Process) — Runs a MonoBehaviour process where its placement says, with a data packet loaded for the cue. SequenceCue (Sequence) — Runs a task sequence on a data packet loaded for the cue. SoundCue — Plays a sound where its placement says as its moment comes. TagCue (Cue Tag) — Plays what the project's cue library has for its tag, or the entity's own Cue Receiver's.

guides/cues/data-packets.html.title: Data packets | PlayForge
guides/cues/data-packets.html.summary: Data packets A cue that runs a process or a sequence hands it a data packet of its own, loaded for what raised the cue: CuePackets.For(cue, data). The packet loads in four steps. Each step's keys take the place of an earlier step's: An ability's activation: an ability's cue starts from a copy of its activation's packet, with its targets, its targeting data and the numbers its caller set. The cue's context: the cue itself under Tags.CUE, a CueContext; its asset under Tags.ASSET: the effect, the ability, the item, or the entity's identity; its spec under Tags.SPEC: the effect's, the ability's or the item's; its source under Tags.SOURCE; the one it plays on under Tags.TARGET_REAL, where the activation named no target; where it plays under Tags.POSITION and Tags.ROTATION, and what it follows under Tags.TRANSFORM; its owner's clock: the activation's for an ability's cue, else that of the one it plays on. The asset's Local Data: each row under its key, its numbers read for the cue, as at its level. The cue's own Data list, last, so it has the last word. A row with no value puts nothing. A process or a sequence reads it as it reads any packet: data.TryGetFirst(Tags.CUE, out CueContext cue).

guides/cues/floating-text.html.title: Floating text | PlayForge
guides/cues/floating-text.html.summary: Floating text A Floating Text cue floats a text where its Placement says, 2 units above the one the cue is on by default. It shows a hit's damage, the gold a kill gave, or a status's name as it lands. Property Description Text What it says. {value} is its number, {name} the name of what raised it, as an effect's, and {tag} its cue tag. Value Its number, and how it's written. Look How it looks. Motion How it moves and fades. Stacking How its texts on one entity merge and stagger, and how many show. Its Text can be +{value} gold, for example, or {name} for a status. Its Value gives its number and writes it: Property Description From Where its number comes from: the cue's magnitude, as a hit's value from an effect's On Hit, or its Number. Number Its number, read as it plays, as a Tracked Impact's for the gold an instant effect gave. Decimals The most decimals it's written with. Absolute Writes it without its sign, as damage shown as 35. Plus Sign Writes a plus before a number above 0. Abbreviate Shortens it past a thousand, as 1.2k. Hide Zero Writes nothing for a number of 0. Its Look sets how it shows: Property Description Color Its colour. By Sign Colours it by its number's sign: its Color for 0 and above, its Negative Color below 0. Negative Color Its colour below 0, where By Sign is on. Size, Font and Bold Its size and font, and whether it's written in bold. Outline Its outline. Face Camera Turns it to the camera: ForgeCues.Camera, or else the main camera. Sorting Order The order it draws in among others. Prefab A prefab holding a TextMeshPro text, which shows it in place of the cue's own. Its font, size and outline are the prefab's own. Its Motion sets how it moves: Property Description Lifetime How long it floats. Velocity How it moves. Random Velocity A random amount of velocity, either way on each axis. Gravity and Drag Gravity for an arc, and drag to slow it. Fade Its opacity over its life. Scale Its scale over its life, as a pop. Game Time On, it floats on the game's clock. Off, in real time. Its Stacking sets how its texts on one entity share the space: Property Description Merge Within A number within this many seconds of the last adds to it, which shows the sum and floats again, as a burn's ticks. Stagger Each text floats this much above the one below it, in the lowest place free. Max Shown At most this many float at once, the oldest going first. Its texts come from ForgeCuePool and go back to it. Tip For damage numbers, put one in an effect's On Hit. It plays as each impact the effect deals lands, on the one it lands on, told the value it changed.

guides/cues/handlers.html.title: Handlers | PlayForge
guides/cues/handlers.html.summary: Handlers Each cue in a list is a handler, its kind picked from the list. A handler plays at each moment whose list holds it. In a list of lasting cues, as a While Active, it plays from its beginning to its end. PlayForge ships the handlers below, and you can write your own. In this section Camera Shake cue: A Camera Shake cue shakes the camera as its moment comes. Sound cue: A Sound cue plays its clip where its Placement says (Placement). Prefab cue: A Prefab cue places its prefab where its Placement says. Floating Text cue: A Floating Text cue floats a text where its Placement says, as a hit's damage, the gold a kill gave or a status's name. Process cue: A Process cue runs a MonoBehaviour process where its Placement says, on a packet loaded for the cue. Sequence cue: A Sequence cue runs a task sequence on a packet loaded for the cue, with its Data list last. Cue Tag cue: A Cue Tag cue plays what its tag routes to (Routes). Writing your own handler: Write a handler of your own by deriving from AbstractCueHandler.

guides/cues/handlers/camera-shake-cue.ht.title: Camera Shake cue | PlayForge
guides/cues/handlers/camera-shake-cue.ht.summary: Camera Shake cue A Camera Shake cue shakes the camera as its moment comes. Property Description Strength How hard it shakes. Duration How long the shake lasts, in seconds. It shakes through the shaker the game gives ForgeCues.Shaker, an ICameraShaker. With none, it shakes nothing. Its Strength and Duration are read for what raised it.

guides/cues/handlers/cue-tag-cue.html.title: Cue Tag cue | PlayForge
guides/cues/handlers/cue-tag-cue.html.summary: Cue Tag cue A Cue Tag cue plays what its tag routes to (Routes). Property Description Tag The cue tag whose route plays. Each burst, beginning and end it hears plays the tag's route.

guides/cues/handlers/floating-text-cue.h.title: Floating Text cue | PlayForge
guides/cues/handlers/floating-text-cue.h.summary: Floating Text cue A Floating Text cue floats a text where its Placement says, as a hit's damage, the gold a kill gave or a status's name. Property Description Text What it says. Value Its number, and how it's written. Placement Where it floats: 2 units above the one the cue is on, by default. Look How it looks. Motion How it moves and fades. Stacking How its texts on one entity merge, stagger, and how many show. Floating text describes each field. Every burst floats it, whatever raised it: the list it's in says when. A lasting cue floats it as it begins, as a status's name as it lands.

guides/cues/handlers/prefab-cue.html.title: Prefab cue | PlayForge
guides/cues/handlers/prefab-cue.html.summary: Prefab cue A Prefab cue places its prefab where its Placement says. Property Description Prefab The prefab it places. Placement Where it's placed, on whom, and which way it faces (Placement). Lifetime How long a burst's prefab stays, in seconds. 0 keeps it. Pooled Takes its objects from a pool and gives them back, in place of making and destroying one each time. Preallocate How many objects its pool makes ahead, as the cue first plays. A burst's prefab stays for its Lifetime. As a lasting cue, its prefab stays until its cue ends (Pooling).

guides/cues/handlers/process-cue.html.title: Process cue | PlayForge
guides/cues/handlers/process-cue.html.summary: Process cue A Process cue runs a MonoBehaviour process where its Placement says, on a packet loaded for the cue. Property Description Process The process it runs: a prefab with a MonoBehaviour process on it. Placement Where its process runs (Placement). Pooled Takes its objects from the cue pool, and gives each back as its process ends (Pooling). Preallocate How many objects its pool makes ahead, as the cue first plays. Data Data its process runs with, loaded last (Data packets). A burst's process runs its own course. A lasting one's runs until its cue ends (Pooling).

guides/cues/handlers/sequence-cue.html.title: Sequence cue | PlayForge
guides/cues/handlers/sequence-cue.html.summary: Sequence cue A Sequence cue runs a task sequence on a packet loaded for the cue, with its Data list last.
