presentation, modifiers that change other effects, and purges. Add a component with the Components list's +. A kind that makes no sense twice is offered only while the effect holds none of it. Component What it does Aura Holds an effect on those near the one it's on, while it lasts. Area Lands the effect on those near its target as it lands. Transfer Moves an amount from one attribute to another. Side Change Changes the target's sides while the effect lasts. Spread Spreads the effect from the one it's on to those near them. Cues Shows and sounds the effect's moments. In this section Auras: An Aura component holds an effect on those near the one it's on, while it lasts. Area: An Area component lands the effect on those near its target as it lands, as Storm Hammer stuns everyone near the one it hits. Transfers: A Transfer component moves an amount from one attribute to another, as Essence Shift steals Agility or Attribute Shift moves Agility into Strength. Side Change: A Side Change component changes the target's sides while the effect lasts. Spread: A Spread component spreads its effect, or the Effect it names, from the one it's on to those near them, as a plague jumps from its victim to the enemies near it. Component hooks: A component hears its effect's moments through hooks, at the moments its workers do. Custom components: A component of your own derives from AbstractEffectComponent and overrides the hooks it needs.

guides/effects/components/area.html.title: Area | PlayForge
guides/effects/components/area.html.summary: Area An Area component lands the effect on those near its target as it lands, as Storm Hammer stuns everyone near the one it hits. Property Description Radius How far from the target it reaches, read as it lands. A Radius of 0 is no area. Flat Measures along the ground. Off, it measures in a sphere. Takes Whom it takes, by how each stands to its caster. Max Targets The most it takes besides the target, the nearest first. At 0, it takes every one. Use Resolve Order Lands on its target and those it takes in the project's resolve order. On by default. Takes chooses among its Enemies, its Allies (itself among them), its Other Allies, Self, All But Self or Everyone. A caster with no sides takes everyone as its allies and enemies. Each is found by its position, with no collider. Each takes the effect from the same origin, so its modifiers and its chance to apply are its own. An effect that lands by an area spreads no further. It lands on its target and those it takes in the project's resolve order, its target among them, unless its Use Resolve Order is off (see Resolve Order). An effect holds one at most. Without one, it lands on its target alone.

guides/effects/components/auras.html.title: Auras | PlayForge
guides/effects/components/auras.html.summary: Auras An Aura component holds an effect on those near the one it's on, while it lasts. Property Description Effect The effect it holds. Radius How far from its holder it reaches, read at each check. Flat Measures along the ground. Off, it measures in a sphere. Takes Whom it takes, by how each stands to its holder. Its Allies, itself among them, to start. Interval How often it checks who's near, by its holder's own time. 0.25 s by default. It puts its effect on each that comes near, from an origin of its own. It takes the effect off as they leave, die or end, as its holder dies or ends, or as the aura goes. An effect of its that ends on its own, a durational one, goes on again at its next check. An Infinite effect holds as long as they're near. Two of an item hold two, as their effect's stacking says. A purge counts an aura's effect Lent. Items, abilities and entities have an Aura component too, each its own kind. Each gives its aura in its own hooks: an effect's as it lends (see Component hooks); an ability's as it's granted; an item's as it's equipped; an entity's as it registers. An entity's auras are its AuraSet, gas.GetService<AuraSet>(), a service it steps (Entities: Components: Services). ForgeAuras.Provide(entry, holder) and Remove give one of your own.

guides/effects/components/component-hook.title: Component hooks | PlayForge
guides/effects/components/component-hook.summary: Component hooks A component hears its effect's moments through hooks, at the moments its workers do. Hook When the component hears it Land As the effect lands on the entity it's on. Tick Each period, as a tick executes. Hit As an impact the effect deals lands. End As it comes off: an instant effect at once, a lasting one as it's removed. Death As the one it's on dies while it's on them, whether the entity stays or ends, before what the death ends comes off. Lend A lasting effect only: as it starts to last, to lend what it gives while it lasts. TakeBack A lasting effect only: as it stops lasting. Reapply As an application it takes in lands, as a stack or a refresh. Refused As an application of it is refused, with why, on the one it was aimed at. StacksChanged As its stacks change while it lasts, with the counts before and after. A lasting effect's components hear Lend as it starts to last: as it lands, before its Land; as it takes another's place under its tag; as a load or a move puts it back, where it doesn't land again. They hear TakeBack as it stops: as it comes off, before its End; as another takes its place; as a load clears it or a move takes it away. An Aura lends its aura so. A component hears a tick only as one executes: one its ongoing condition stops isn't heard.

guides/effects/components/custom-compone.title: Custom components | PlayForge
guides/effects/components/custom-compone.summary: Custom components A component of your own derives from AbstractEffectComponent and overrides the hooks it needs. Each hook is a no-op otherwise. A component is the effect's, shared by everything that holds it. What it keeps for one application of the effect, it keeps through its context: ctx.GetState<T>(this). Describe says what it does in one line with its numbers, as an Area's "Lands on enemies within 300". The Components section's line and The Forge's summary say it beside its name.

guides/effects/components/side-change.ht.title: Side Change | PlayForge
guides/effects/components/side-change.ht.summary: Side Change A Side Change component changes the target's sides while the effect lasts. Property Description Source Whose sides it gives: Caster: its caster's, as they are as it lands, as a mind control. Named: the Sides it names. Sides Shown under Named alone. The sides it gives, as a pacify's Neutral. Priority Of several on one entity, the highest holds, read as it lands. A tie goes to the latest. Interrupts Breaks what the target runs as the change lands or ends. As the last one ends, the entity's own sides come back. Its tags follow, so whom effects and areas take changes with it. Interrupts acts where it changes the sides, not where a change of higher priority keeps them. An Instant effect doesn't last, so it changes nothing. An effect holds one at most. It was a field of the effect's own, Side Change in its Tags section, with a switch.

guides/effects/components/spread.html.title: Spread | PlayForge
guides/effects/components/spread.html.summary: Spread A Spread component spreads its effect, or the Effect it names, from the one it's on to those near them, as a plague jumps from its victim to the enemies near it. Property Description When The moments it spreads at, any of them: Land: as the effect lands. Tick: each tick. End: as it comes off, however it ends. Death: as the one it's on dies. Effect The effect it spreads. With none, it spreads its own effect. Radius How far from the one it's on it reaches, read at the effect's level. Flat Measures along the ground. Off, it measures in a sphere. Takes Whom it takes, by how each stands to its caster, as an Area's. Its Enemies to start. Max Targets The most it takes each time, the nearest first. At 0, it takes every one. Hops How far a landing it made spreads on. Skip Holders Passes over those who have the effect it spreads already. On by default. Use Resolve Order Lands on those it takes in the project's resolve order. On by default. Each takes the effect from the same origin, its caster's, so its modifiers and its chance to land are its own. A landing it made spreads on only so far as its Hops allow. At 0, it spreads only from where the effect landed of its own. At 1, it spreads once more from each it spread to, and so on. An effect holds as many as it has moments to spread at, each its own.

guides/effects/components/transfers.html.title: Transfers | PlayForge
guides/effects/components/transfers.html.summary: Transfers A Transfer component moves an amount from one attribute to another, as Essence Shift steals Agility or Attribute Shift moves Agility into Strength. Property Description Delivery When it moves. From Who gives: the effect's caster or its target. From Attribute The attribute it gives. To Who gets: the effect's caster or its target. To Attribute The attribute it gets. Slot Which values move: Current, as a pool's Mana; Base; or Current And Base, as a stat's Strength. Amount How much it moves. It can scale by level. Delivery When it moves On Apply Once, as the effect lands, for good. Periodic Each tick, for good. Continuous As the effect lands, and holds while it lasts, a modifier on each side. It gives back as the effect ends, as a load or a move takes it, or as the entity it's on goes. Each side is its own, so an entity can give to itself. Only what the giver has moves, so one with 3 of a steal of 5 gives 3, and nothing is made. A Continuous transfer is read again only where a stack or a level changes its amount. Each side's change is exact: no worker takes it for a hit, no barrier soaks it and nothing scales it. So the getter gets what the giver gave, as far as its own bounds let it. What its maximum can't hold is lost, as an overheal is. An effect holds as many as it moves, each its own. The Problems view warns of a transfer whose Delivery the effect's duration can't make, as it does an additional impact's. It also warns of one that names no attribute to give or get. Each is numbered among the effect's transfers.

guides/effects/cues.html.title: Cues | PlayForge
guides/effects/cues.html.summary: Cues What the effect shows and sounds, apart from what it changes, plays from its Cues component. Add it from the Components list's +. An effect holds one at most. The component has a list for each of the effect's moments: Moment When its cues play On Apply As the effect lands. On Reapply As an application it takes in lands, as a stack or a refresh. On Tick As each tick executes. On Hit As an impact it deals lands, on the one it lands on. Its magnitude is the value it changed, as for a damage number. On Remove As a lasting effect comes off. While Active While it lasts: from as it lands, or a load puts it back, to as it comes off. Where another application replaced it, it ends as it began. On Refused As an application is refused, as by an immunity, on the one it was aimed at. On Stack Change As its stacks change while it lasts. Its magnitude is the stacks it has. A cue plays at each moment whose list holds it. A sound on each tick is a Sound in On Tick, and one as the effect lands as well is in On Apply too. An applier can say where an application hit, spec.WithHit(point, normal, magnitude), and its cues play there (Cues: Raises and sinks). A save's load ends each While Active cue and begins it again as the effect leaves and comes back, and plays no burst. Cues brings cues together: where each is raised, the library's routes, what each tag plays, and pooling. In this section Cue kinds: A cue's kind decides what it plays. Playing cues from code: Every cue plays through ForgeCues, an effect's as any other's. Cue Tag routing: A Cue Tag cue plays what its tag routes to, in place of naming what it shows.

guides/effects/cues/cue-kinds.html.title: Cue kinds | PlayForge
guides/effects/cues/cue-kinds.html.summary: Cue kinds A cue's kind decides what it plays. Each list holds its cues as the Workers list holds workers, each cue's kind picked from the list. Kind What it plays Camera Shake Shakes the camera through the shaker the game gives ForgeCues.Shaker, an ICameraShaker. With none given, it shakes nothing. Sound Plays its clip where its Placement says, at the target by default (Cues: Placement). Prefab Places its prefab where its Placement says, at the target by default, for Lifetime seconds. Floating Text Floats a text where its Placement says, as a hit's damage or a status's name (Cues: Floating text). Process Runs a MonoBehaviour process where its Placement says, on a data packet loaded for the cue, as a shield's while it lasts (Cues: Data packets). Sequence Runs a task sequence on a data packet loaded for the cue, as a flicker while the effect lasts (Cues: Handlers). Cue Tag Plays what its tag routes to (Cues: Routes). A Camera Shake's Strength and Duration are number fields read for its effect as it plays, as are Prefab's Lifetime and Sound's Volume. A Prefab cue has more to it: In While Active, it stays for as long as the effect lasts, following the target. A cue raised at a point, as a Play Cue task's, places it there. With Pooled, it takes its objects from a pool, ForgeCuePool, and gives them back. The pool makes Preallocate of them ahead as it first plays. An IPooledCue on the prefab resets it as it's taken and given back. Write a cue of your own by deriving from AbstractCueHandler and overriding the moments it plays at. Or override Burst to play every burst one way, reading the moment that raised it from cue.Moment.

guides/effects/cues/cue-tag-routing.html.title: Cue Tag routing | PlayForge
guides/effects/cues/cue-tag-routing.html.summary: Cue Tag routing A Cue Tag cue plays what its tag routes to, in place of naming what it shows. So an effect, an ability and an entity can each raise Cue.Hit.Fire, and one place says how it looks. The project's Cue Library, an asset its settings name, plays the route for the tag, or else for its nearest parent. A route that doesn't Override plays its parent's after it. An entity's Cue Receiver component plays a tag its own way first, in place of the library's, or before it with Pass Through. The receiver's Variant plays the library's route under its name, as Cue.Hit.Golem for Cue.Hit, where the library has one.

guides/effects/cues/playing-cues-from-co.title: Playing cues from code | PlayForge
guides/effects/cues/playing-cues-from-co.summary: Playing cues from code Every cue plays through ForgeCues, an effect's as any other's. A game's own code raises one there too, as sparks where a ray hit: ForgeCues.Burst(sparks, new CueContext(entity, ECueMoment.Raised, point: hit.point)). A cue's context says what raised it, who's behind it and where it plays. For a lasting cue, it also holds the key its beginning and its end share. ForgeCues.Enabled = false silences every cue, as on a server or while a simulation runs ahead. ForgeCues.Mute(entity, true) silences one entity's, as one off screen. A lasting cue that began still ends. ForgeCues.Played hears each cue as it plays, for a debugger or a recorder.

guides/effects/duration.html.title: Duration | PlayForge
guides/effects/duration.html.summary: Duration The Duration section sets how long the effect lasts, how it ticks, and what another application of it does. Its fields show as the Policy uses them. Property Description Policy Instant (default) makes the change once. Durational stays for a set time. Infinite stays until something removes it. Duration Durational only. The effect's length in seconds, with its scaler. Periodic Ticks Durational and Infinite. A tick makes the effect's change again, as a new commit. Ticks Durational, with Periodic Ticks. How many ticks fit in the duration, evenly spaced. Tick Every Infinite, with Periodic Ticks. The seconds between ticks. Tick On Application Durational and Infinite. Runs one tick as soon as the effect is applied, before the first periodic tick. Additional Executions While it ticks. Adds to the number of times each tick executes the change. Real Delta Time Durational only. With a scaler, combines the scaler and the frame time. Multiply With Scaler, for example, slows the clock down or speeds it up. Delta Time Scaler Durational only. Changes how fast the effect's clock runs. With no scaler, the clock follows Unity's frame time. Re-application Durational and Infinite. What happens when the effect is applied to a target that already has it. Then All but Add Another. What the old container does with its time as it takes in the application. Stacking, Stack Behaviours, Stack Amount Stack Existing only. How the stacks keep their time, the rules they follow, and how many each application adds. In this section Ticks: A tick makes a lasting effect's change again, as a new commit. Re-application (Durational and Infinite): Re-application decides what happens when the effect is applied to a target that already has it. Stacking (Stack Existing only): Stacking sets how a Stack Existing effect's stacks keep their time, and how many stacks each application adds. Moving an effect to another entity: An effect on one entity can move to another, as a possession hands a body's effects over.

guides/effects/duration/moving-an-effect.title: Moving an effect to another entity | PlayForge
guides/effects/duration/moving-an-effect.summary: Moving an effect to another entity An effect on one entity can move to another, as a possession hands a body's effects over. gas.GetEffectSystem().MoveTo(effect, other) moves each of the effect's containers on the entity onto another. Each container keeps its stacks, its time left and what applied it. A move is neither a removal nor an application. None of either's workers, commits or contained effects run, and neither is told. Its lasting changes, its granted tags, the abilities it lends and its lasting cues go with it.

guides/effects/duration/re-application-d.title: Re-application (Durational and Infinite) | PlayForge
guides/effects/duration/re-application-d.summary: Re-application (Durational and Infinite) Re-application decides what happens when the effect is applied to a target that already has it. Each application on the shelf lives in a container. The effect is matched by its asset tag, whoever applied it. Re-application offers four choices: Choice What it does Add Another (default) Adds a separate container, and both apply. Do Nothing Adds nothing new. Replace Existing Gives the old container the new application's values and modifiers, and keeps its stack count. Past commits stay. Stack Existing Adds stacks to the old container (see Stacking). Then (all but Add Another) applies as the old container takes in the application: Choice What it does Do Nothing (default) Leaves its time alone. Refresh Duration Restarts its time. Extend Duration Adds the new duration to its time. Refresh and Extend also run Tick On Application again.

guides/effects/duration/stacking-stack-e.title: Stacking (Stack Existing only) | PlayForge
guides/effects/duration/stacking-stack-e.summary: Stacking (Stack Existing only) Stacking sets how a Stack Existing effect's stacks keep their time, and how many stacks each application adds. Property Description Stacking How the stacks keep their time. Stack Behaviours Optional stacking rules, such as Stack Bounds Config and Starting Stacks. Stack Amount With its scaler, the stacks each application adds. 0 counts as 1. Stacking offers three choices: Choice What it does Stacks Share One Duration (default) Runs one timer for all stacks. Adding a stack doesn't reset it. Stacks Have Independent Durations Gives each stack its own timer and ticks. Stacks drop off one at a time, and the effect lasts as long as its longest stack. Duration Taken From One Stack Runs one stack's timer at a time. Each time it runs out, one stack is lost and the timer restarts. Stack behaviours Stack behaviours are optional rules that the stacks follow. Stack Bounds Config keeps the stack count between a Min and a Max. Starting Stacks sets the stacks a new effect starts with. The Min, the Max and Starting Stacks are each a number field read at the effect's level. Starting Stacks is a single number field, where a number, a scaler, a combine and a rounding of its own were once written out. An application that would take the effect past the Max overflows: Its Overflow Effects land, from the same origin, as a bleed's fourth stack hemorrhages. They land on the target, or, with Overflow Lands On set to Caster, on its caster, as a frenzy. Deny Refresh On Overflow keeps that application from refreshing or extending the effect. Clear Stacks On Overflow takes the effect's stacks off. Reading the stack count A change reads the stack count through an Effect Stacks scaler (Scalers). A magnitude of −5 with Multiply With Scaler takes 5 a stack. A Continuous change updates whenever the count changes. A Periodic change already lands once for each stack. One that also reads its stacks counts them twice, so 3 stacks hit 9 times as hard as 1. The Problems view warns of it. Its quick fix, Count Stacks Once, gives the number one stack gives.

guides/effects/duration/ticks.html.title: Ticks | PlayForge
guides/effects/duration/ticks.html.summary: Ticks A tick makes a lasting effect's change again, as a new commit. Ticks (Durational) spaces its ticks evenly over the duration. The last falls as the duration ends, so 5 ticks over 10 seconds tick every 2 seconds. Tick Every (Infinite) sets the seconds between ticks. Tick On Application runs one tick as soon as the effect is applied, before the first periodic tick. It runs again when re-application refreshes or extends the effect. Use Tick On Application with Periodic Ticks. On its own, it is a shape that the Problems view flags. Additional Executions applies while the effect ticks. Each tick executes the change a number of times, N plus this, combined with its scaler. N comes from the effect's container and is normally 1. A stacking container that shares one duration, or takes it from one stack, uses its stack count. A tick only executes while the While On requirements hold (see Requirements).

guides/effects/identity.html.title: Identity | PlayForge
guides/effects/identity.html.summary: Identity The Identity section names the effect, gives its asset tag, and holds what your UI shows of it. Property Description Name The effect's display name. It also gives the asset tag, so renaming the effect changes its tag. Description Free text for your UI. Asset Tag Read-only, made from the Name: punctuation is dropped, and each word is capitalised and joined. The tag is stored when you edit the Name. Visibility A tag your UI can read to decide whether to show the effect, such as Always Visible or Not Visible. The Forge lists it, but the runtime doesn't act on it. Textures Icons, each paired with a tag. The texture tagged Primary is the effect's icon; without one, the first texture is used. Inherit From Origin Takes the effect's icon from its origin, the ability, item or entity that applied it. Origin Texture Shown under Inherit From Origin. A tag, Primary to start, that names the origin's texture to take. Note Renaming an effect changes its asset tag. Update anything that names the old tag. If the stored asset tag differs from the one the Name gives, it shows in warning text with an Update button that stores the new one. The effect system finds an effect by its asset tag when it is applied again or removed, whoever applied it. While a Durational or Infinite effect is active, its target carries the tag. Cooldowns work this way: an ability's Cooldown check looks for the cooldown effect's tag on the caster. With Inherit From Origin on, the effect's icon is the origin's texture under Origin Texture. Where the origin has none under that tag, the effect's own stands. A spec reads the icon with spec.GetIcon(), as the Demo's bar and the Additional Content's status bar do. An origin holds textures through IHasTextures, as abilities, items, effects, entities and both hubs do.

guides/effects/impact.html.title: Impact | PlayForge
guides/effects/impact.html.summary: Impact The impact is the change the effect makes to an attribute. The first fields are its first impact, whose delivery the duration gives it. Additional Impacts change more attributes, or the same one again, each with a delivery of its own. Property Description Attribute The attribute to change. Leave it empty for an effect that only grants tags, applies other effects or runs workers. Operation How the impact changes the attribute, and which of its values, in one choice, such as Add to Current or Multiply Base. See Operations. Multiply Behaviour Multiply only. How this multiply combines with other multipliers. Add Behaviour Add only, shown where it matters. How this add combines with others on the attribute. Magnitude The amount. See Magnitude. Pipeline The calculation each hit of the impact goes through as it lands, a Value Pipeline: the caster's bonuses, the target's reductions, a critical roll, a barrier. It runs for an instant impact's hit and each tick of a periodic one (Value Pipelines). Delivery Read-only. When the impact lands, which the duration gives it. See Delivery and commits. Commits Read-only, for a periodic impact. How many times it lands. Impact Types Tags that label the kind of change, such as Damage.Fire. Workers can accept or skip changes by type. Affiliation Which targets the effect can be applied to. See Affiliation. Comparison All but Always Allow. Whether one affiliation tag matching is enough, or every tag must match. Affiliations Use Affiliation List only. The tags the target is compared with. A target that lacks the attribute isn't changed. Never Allow, as an impact type, hides the change from workers that check types. Always Allow passes every type check. The section also holds the effect's Retention Group (Retention Group) and its Proc Coefficient (On Hit). In this section Operations: The Operation sets how the impact changes the attribute, and which of its values it changes. Magnitude: The Magnitude is the amount the impact applies. Delivery and commits: The read-only Delivery and Commits rows say when, and how often, the first impact lands. Affiliation: Affiliation decides which targets the effect can be applied to. Additional Impacts: Each additional impact changes an attribute of its own, or the same one again, with a delivery of its own. Contained Effects: Contained effects are other effects this one applies, with the same origin. Retention Group: The Retention Group is the group this effect's changes count toward (default Ignore), unless an impact names its own.

guides/effects/impact/additional-impacts.title: Additional Impacts | PlayForge
guides/effects/impact/additional-impacts.summary: Additional Impacts Each additional impact changes an attribute of its own, or the same one again, with a delivery of its own. One effect can lower Armor while it lasts and burn Health on each tick. Add Impact adds one with a delivery the duration can make: Continuous on a Durational or Infinite effect, On Apply on an Instant one. While it's folded, an impact shows one line, such as "Mana −10 · Continuous", and its trash button removes it. Property Description Attribute, Operation, Multiply Behaviour, Add Behaviour, Magnitude, Pipeline As for the first impact (Impact). Delivery When the impact lands. It offers what the duration can make. Commits Read-only, for a Periodic impact, as for the first impact. Order Override only. Among overrides of one attribute, the lowest order wins. Retention Group The group the change counts toward. Empty, it takes the effect's. Impact Types As for the first impact. Delivery When it lands Continuous While the effect lasts. Then it reverses. On Apply Once, as the effect is applied. Periodic On each tick, and as the effect is applied when Tick On Application is on. An Instant effect makes only On Apply impacts, and Periodic needs ticks. If the duration changes so that an impact's delivery can't happen, a warning under it says so, and the impact never applies. An impact with no Attribute changes nothing. The Cost check counts every attribute a cost spends (see Abilities).

guides/effects/impact/affiliation.html.title: Affiliation | PlayForge
guides/effects/impact/affiliation.html.summary: Affiliation Affiliation decides which targets the effect can be applied to. If the check fails, the effect isn't applied. An entity's affiliation tags are its team or faction, set on its Entity asset. Choice What it allows Always Allow (default) Any target. Affiliated Targets that share the origin's affiliation. Unaffiliated Targets that don't share it. Use Affiliation List Compares the target with the Affiliations list instead. Comparison (all but Always Allow): Any (default) needs one tag to match. All needs every tag to match.

guides/effects/impact/contained-effects..title: Contained Effects | PlayForge
guides/effects/impact/contained-effects..summary: Contained Effects Contained effects are other effects this one applies, with the same origin. Each row pairs a moment with an effect, and says whom it lands on: Column Description Moment On Apply (when this effect is applied), On Tick (on each execute tick) or On Remove (when this effect is removed). Effect The effect to apply. Lands on The Target, this effect's, as it always did, or the Caster, as a lifesteal's heal or a curse's rebound as it ends. An Instant effect has no ticks and no removal, so only its On Apply rows run. An effect that is asked to apply again while it is still applying is refused, with a warning. So an effect that contains itself doesn't loop forever.

guides/effects/impact/delivery-and-commi.title: Delivery and commits | PlayForge
guides/effects/impact/delivery-and-commi.summary: Delivery and commits The read-only Delivery and Commits rows say when, and how often, the first impact lands. The duration gives the delivery: Delivery reads For When the impact lands On applying An Instant effect Once, as it's applied. While the effect lasts A Durational or Infinite effect with no ticks As a modifier while the effect is active. Each tick A Durational or Infinite effect with periodic ticks Once per tick. It reads "Each tick, and on applying" when Tick On Application is on. A note says when Tick On Application alone keeps a multiply or override as a modifier, so it reverses as the effect ends. Commits, for a periodic impact, says how many times it lands at the effect's first level, as in "7 over 6 s, level 1". For an Infinite effect, Commits says how far apart the ticks are. Note The inspector no longer shows Reverse On Removal. A Continuous modifier always reverses when the effect ends, and a commit never does, so the flag changes nothing. The Problems view still flags a periodic effect that sets it.

guides/effects/impact/magnitude.html.title: Magnitude | PlayForge
guides/effects/impact/magnitude.html.summary: Magnitude The Magnitude is the amount the impact applies. It is a Constant number, or, by its kind, a scaler's value at the origin's level, such as a By Level table of values per level. Combine joins the scaler and the number (Scalers). A Continuous modifier works its magnitude out again whenever the attribute is recalculated. A commit works it out once. Set By Caller A Set By Caller scaler reads a magnitude that your code sets, under a tag, as it applies the effect. You set it in one of two places: on the spec, with SetByCaller(tag, magnitude); on an ability activation's data, which each effect the ability applies takes as it's made, its cost, cooldown and contained effects among them. Only the tag itself matches. Where none is set, the scaler reads its Default. Other kinds A magnitude can also read what the effect has dealt, a part of another effect, ability or item on either side, or what a worker answers. SCALERS.md lists each kind.

guides/effects/impact/operations.html.title: Operations | PlayForge
guides/effects/impact/operations.html.summary: Operations The Operation sets how the impact changes the attribute, and which of its values it changes. Base is the value the attribute is measured against, and Current is the value in play. For Health, Base is the maximum and Current is what is left. Operation What it does Add Adds the magnitude. Use a negative magnitude to subtract. Multiply Multiplies by the magnitude. Override Sets the value to the magnitude. Flat Bonus Adds too, but as a modifier it lands after the attribute's multipliers, so they don't scale it. Multiply Behaviour Multiply Behaviour (Multiply only) sets how a multiply combines with other multipliers: Choice What it does Multiplicative (default) Compounds with other multipliers, so ×1.5 and ×1.5 give ×2.25. Additive Bonus Adds the bonuses first, so +50% and +50% give ×2.0. Add Behaviour Add Behaviour (Add only, shown where it matters) sets how an add combines with the others on the attribute (Attributes): Choice What it does Attribute Role (default) As the attribute's role says: a Resistance's adds diminish. Sum A plain sum. Diminishing On what's left.

guides/effects/impact/retention-group.ht.title: Retention Group | PlayForge
guides/effects/impact/retention-group.ht.summary: Retention Group The Retention Group is the group this effect's changes count toward (default Ignore), unless an impact names its own. Groups split an attribute's value for queries and UI, such as base and bonus health. They never change the math.

guides/effects/index.html.title: Gameplay Effects | PlayForge
guides/effects/index.html.summary: Gameplay Effects A Gameplay Effect asset describes a change to an entity: damage, a heal, a timed buff, a poison, a cost or a cooldown. An effect can change attributes (numbers such as Health), grant tags, apply other effects and run workers. classDiagram class GameplayEffect:::asset { <<ScriptableObject>> +Definition : The Additional Impacts are authored entries, each with its own delivery. A spec's icon can come from its origin. An entity is anything that runs a gameplay ability system (GAS), such as the player or an enemy. Abilities and items apply effects to a target entity, and so can your code. The ability, item or entity that applies an effect is its origin. The duration's Policy decides how long an effect lives. An Instant effect makes its change once and is done. A Durational or Infinite effect goes on the target's effect shelf, its list of active effects. It stays until its time runs out or something removes it. The kind of change follows from the Policy: Effect Delivery The change Instant OnApply one permanent commit, such as "take 30 damage" Durational or Infinite, no ticks Continuous a modifier while the effect is active, reversed exactly when it ends Durational or Infinite, periodic ticks Periodic one permanent commit per tick, such as "5 Health per second" A commit stays after the effect ends. A modifier doesn't. Effect & Attribute Pipeline has the full model. Tags are names, such as State.Stunned, that an entity carries and that requirements check. Each asset stores a tag made from its Name: Fireball Damage gives Effect.FireballDamage. Each section below matches the inspector section of the same name. In this guide Identity: The Identity section names the effect, gives its asset tag, and holds what your UI shows of it. Leveling: An effect has no level of its own. Tags: The Tags section sets what the effect grants its target while it's on, and which other effects it removes, purges or blocks. Purging: Purging takes effects off an entity by strength. Duration: The Duration section sets how long the effect lasts, how it ticks, and what another application of it does. Impact: The impact is the change the effect makes to an attribute. Levels: The effect's levels say what it does, level by level. Cues: What the effect shows and sounds, apart from what it changes, plays from its Cues component. Requirements: The Requirements section decides whether the effect lands, keeps working and comes off. Components: An effect's components are features it carries. Workers: The Workers section holds what runs for the effect beside its impacts. Local Data: Local Data is a list of named values stored on the asset. Used By: Used By lists the PlayForge assets that refer to this effect, each with its type icon, such as an ability whose cost it is or an item that grants it. Built-in kinds: The kinds PlayForge ships for this guide's pickers, each with its menu and what it does, as its picker says. guides/effects/leveling.html.title: Leveling | PlayForge
guides/effects/leveling.html.summary: Leveling An effect has no level of its own. At runtime it takes the level of its origin, and its scalers use that level to pick per-level values, such as 20/30/40/50 damage at levels 1 to 4. A scaler is a value source, such as a table with one value per level. A level provider is the asset whose level range an effect is authored for, normally its origin. Property Description Link Mode Standalone (default): the effect takes the level of what applies it, as a note says. Linked To Provider: the effect takes its range from a level provider. Level Provider Shown while linked. The asset the range comes from: an Entity, Ability, Effect, Item or Attribute Set. Link Contained Effects Shown while linked. Links every contained effect (see Contained Effects) to this effect's provider, so their per-level values follow its range. Unlink Contained Effects Removes the contained effects' links that point at the provider. Right-click the Level Provider field to pick from one type. A link that would make a loop is refused, with an error in the Console. While no provider is set, a warning says the effect takes the level of what applies it. While linked, Starting Level and Max Level show the provider's range, read-only. Link Contained Effects and Unlink Contained Effects each ask first, and one Undo takes it back. The link serves the inspector: a scaler set to Lock To Level Provider shows one value per level of the provider. An effect field in another inspector, such as an ability's Cost, says how the effect takes its levels. Its Link links the effect to that asset.

guides/effects/levels.html.title: Levels | PlayForge
guides/effects/levels.html.summary: Levels The effect's levels say what it does, level by level. Its line is its first impact by level, with an add signed, as "-10/-20/-30 Health" or "+20 Armor". The effect's header and The Forge's Summary column show it. The line reads at its provider's levels where it's linked to one, and at levels 1 to 5 where it isn't. ForgeAssetLines.Of(asset) gives any asset's line in the editor. The whole reading is code's, for a tooltip or a game's own screen. AbilityInspector.BuildEffectSeries(effect, 1, 5, caster, target) reads the effect at levels 1 to 5 against a caster and a target, either of which may be null. Member What it gives Magnitude, Total Each impact's magnitude and total at each level. Line Each impact's line, as its field's summary reads it. Parts Each impact's parts at each level. Needs What each impact needs. Duration, Ticks, Interval, Chance The effect's duration, ticks, interval and chance. Contained The effect's contained effects. Describe(level) What the effect does at a level, an impact to a line: "-15 Health each tick, 12 ticks over 12 s". NumberTrace.Of(number, context) explains any one number the same way, each part with what it read and what it gave: Health as it lands, level 2: -1 × (Caster's Attack Damage + 80 if Caster's Combo Charges > 0, else 0) = -100 Group = 100 Add: Caster's Attack Damage = 100 Add: Conditional = 0 When: Caster's Combo Charges > 0: doesn't hold False: 0 = 0 A read given no caster or no target gives, for a part that reads one, what its field falls back to. It says what it needs, as "the target". A kind or a condition of your own adds its parts by overriding Explain: trace.Add(Min, context, this, "Min").

guides/effects/local-data.html.title: Local Data | PlayForge
guides/effects/local-data.html.summary: Local Data Local Data is a list of named values stored on the asset. Property Description Key A tag that names the row. Value A value of a kind: Float, Int, String, Bool, Tag, Attribute, Effect, Ability, Entity, Object, MonoBehaviour or ScriptableObject, or a kind of your own. A kind of your own is a [Serializable] class made from LocalDataValue<T>, as a point or a colour. The row's kinds offer it beside PlayForge's. A row saves its own value alone. Object fields take project assets, not scene objects. Code reads a value by its type, data.TryGet(out float range) or data.TryGet(out MyPoint point). It reads a number, a Float or an Int, which can scale, with data.Value.TryReadNumber(context, out float number). PlayForge doesn't read an effect's Local Data itself. Your code and workers can, with effect.TryGetLocalData(key, out var data). The first row with that key wins.

guides/effects/purging.html.title: Purging | PlayForge
guides/effects/purging.html.summary: Purging Purging takes effects off an entity by strength. A project's Purge Levels, under Forge Project in Project Settings → PlayForge, rank its purges. Purge Levels holds the project's tiers, weakest first: Property Description Tier A tag, as Purge.Basic or Purge.Strong. An effect is at the first tier whose tag it carries, as its asset tag or a context tag, or a child of one. Kept On Death (on a tier) A death keeps the effects at this tier. Kept On Death (on Purge Levels) Categories a death keeps whatever their tiers. A project starts with an ability's cooldowns, lent effects and toggles. A purge of a tier takes the effects at that tier or under it, as a Strong dispel takes the Basic too. An effect at no tier is never purged, but by death. A purge, an effect's Purges or ForgePurge.Purge(entity, purge) in code, has these fields: Property Description Strength A tier's tag. The purge takes the effects at that tier or under it. Kinds Tags an effect must carry one of to be taken, as Status.Debuff. Where it names none, it takes any kind. Applied By Whom it takes the effects of, by who applied each, against the one purged: itself, its allies (its buffs) or its enemies (its debuffs). An applier sharing none of its sides is an enemy. Filters Filters of a project's own, each an AbstractPurgeFilter whose Takes says yes or no. Except Tagged spares the effects carrying the tags it names. An effect a purge takes comes off at the next tick, as a removed effect does. A purge never takes the effect doing it. ForgePurge.Purge(entity, strength) purges by a strength alone, of every kind. A staying entity's death purges its effects too, all but those it keeps (Entities: Death). Each tier's Kept On Death keeps the effects at that tier, and the categories in Purge Levels' own Kept On Death keep theirs whatever their tiers.

guides/effects/requirements.html.title: Requirements | PlayForge
guides/effects/requirements.html.summary: Requirements The Requirements section decides whether the effect lands, keeps working and comes off. It holds the effect's chance to apply, its tag checks on the target and the source, and its conditions. Property Description Chance to Apply How likely the effect is to land, from 0 to 1, which can scale by level. See Chance to Apply. Chance Roll How the chance rolls. It shows for a chance that can miss. On the target, On the source A switch between the two sides' tag tables. See Tag requirements. Apply Conditions, Ongoing Conditions, Removal Conditions Conditions for each phase. See Conditions. In this section Chance to Apply: Chance to Apply comes first: how likely the effect is to land, from 0 to 1, which can scale by level. Tag requirements: The tag requirements check tags on the effect's target, and on its source, the entity behind its origin. Conditions: Under the tag tables are the effect's Conditions for each phase.

guides/effects/requirements/chance-to-ap.title: Chance to Apply | PlayForge
guides/effects/requirements/chance-to-ap.summary: Chance to Apply Chance to Apply comes first: how likely the effect is to land, from 0 to 1, which can scale by level. It gates the whole application, as the Applying rows do. Each application draws once from PlayForge's random source (ForgeRandom). A miss is refused, so applying returns false, as an immunity's refusal does. The target's callbacks hear a miss, OnEffectRefused, with why (Entities: Effect Journal). 1, the default, always lands, and 0 never does. Neither draws, so an effect without a chance leaves the numbers others draw as they were. A contained effect draws its own: a strike with a bleed at 0.3 lands every time, and its bleed about one time in three. The section's summary shows a chance short of 1. Chance Roll Chance Roll, under it, says how the chance rolls, as every chance PlayForge rolls can. It shows for a chance that can miss. Property Description Pseudo Random Each miss raises the next roll's odds by a constant, and a hit starts them again. So streaks even out, and the chance over many rolls stays the same. Own Luck Uses a number of the chance's own, its Luck, in place of the luck attribute. Luck Shown under Own Luck alone. The chance's own luck. Pseudo Random works as Dota's pseudo-random distribution: a 25% chance's first roll has about 8.5%, its next about 17%, and so on. With Pseudo Random, each caster keeps its own streak for each chance. Without Own Luck, the luck is the attribute playing the project's Luck role (Attributes: Roles), read on the caster. Above 0, luck rolls that many more times and keeps the best. Below 0, it keeps the worst. A chance of 1 or more always comes up, and one of 0 or less never does. Neither draws. The same roll is on a trigger's Chance, the Chance stage of a Value Pipeline, an ability's Chance to Activate, and the Chance condition. The Chance condition holds on a roll of its number, as a critical strike chance read from an attribute. In a hit it rolls once and keeps the roll, so a hit read twice, its preview and its commit, reads the same.

guides/effects/requirements/conditions.h.title: Conditions | PlayForge
guides/effects/requirements/conditions.h.summary: Conditions Under the tag tables are the effect's Conditions for each phase. Each is a condition read in the effect's context, its caster's and its target's numbers in reach, as "the target below 30% Health". Property Description Apply Conditions Must each hold for the effect to land. Ongoing Conditions Pause the effect while one fails, as While On does. Removal Conditions Take the effect off once each holds, with its Removed By rows where it names any, as Attribute Shift stops at its floor. A phase passes only when its tags pass and its conditions all hold. The Ongoing and Removal conditions are checked at the entity's end of frame while the effect lasts, as no tag needs to change for an attribute they read to. They are checked before each tick as well.

guides/effects/requirements/tag-requirem.title: Tag requirements | PlayForge
guides/effects/requirements/tag-requirem.summary: Tag requirements The tag requirements check tags on the effect's target, and on its source, the entity behind its origin. The switch shows one side's table at a time: On the target first, then On the source. Each table has a row for each group: Row What it does Applying Must pass for the effect to be applied. The effect is also refused if its Removed By row is already met. While on While it fails, the effect stays, but its ticks don't execute. Its Continuous modifiers stay in place. Removed by When it's met, the effect is removed. Each row has two cells: Cell Description Requires The tags the entity must have. Must not have The tags it must not have, or None. A row passes when the entity has every tag it requires and none it must not have. Editing a row Click a cell to edit its list under the table, with the row's template settings: Property Description Template A shared Requirement Template for the row. Sync With Template Keeps the row's tags the same as its template's. A template's Category is a tag of its own context, Requirement Category, which groups templates. Each entry is a tag query: a Tag, a Match mode and a comparison with a number. Greater Than 0 means "the tag is present". When rows are checked Empty Applying and While On rows always pass. An empty Removed By row never removes anything. While On and Removed By are checked whenever an effect is applied to or removed from the target. While On is also checked before each tick.

guides/effects/tags.html.title: Tags | PlayForge
guides/effects/tags.html.summary: Tags The Tags section sets what the effect grants its target while it's on, and which other effects it removes, purges or blocks. Property Description Granted Tags Applied to the target while the effect is active. An Instant effect grants them only for the moment it applies. Granted Abilities Given to the target as the effect lands, each at the level of what applied it, and taken back as it comes off. Context Tags Describe the effect, such as Fire. They are not applied to the entity. Removes Effects Tagged Makes the effect a cleanse. Purges Makes the effect a purge, by the project's purge levels (Purging). Blocks Effects Tagged Makes the effect an immunity. A change of the target's sides while the effect lasts is a Side Change component (Side Change). A granted ability that's running as the effect comes off is interrupted. An ability the target can't take, such as one it knows already when duplicates aren't allowed, isn't lent, so the target keeps its own as the effect comes off. An Instant effect lends no abilities, as it's never on the target. Each change the effect makes carries its context tags and its origin's context tags, and workers can filter by them. As a cleanse lands, every other effect on the target tagged with one of its tags, or a child of one, comes off at the next tick, as a removed effect does. An effect counts as tagged by its asset tag, a context tag or a tag it grants. For example, Status.Debuff takes off Status.Debuff.Poison and Status.Debuff.Burn, and State.Burning takes off whatever grants it. As a purge lands, the effects on the target its strength reaches, of the kinds it names and applied by whom it says, come off. While an immunity is on the target and its ongoing requirements hold, an effect tagged with one of its tags, or a child of one, can't land. Tags match the same way as for a cleanse, and applying a blocked effect returns false. An immunity leaves the effects already on the target. Add the same tags to Removes Effects Tagged to clear them as it lands.

guides/effects/used-by.html.title: Used By | PlayForge
guides/effects/used-by.html.summary: Used By Used By lists the PlayForge assets that refer to this effect, each with its type icon, such as an ability whose cost it is or an item that grants it. Click a row to select the asset. The list follows the project as it changes.

guides/effects/workers.html.title: Workers | PlayForge
guides/effects/workers.html.summary: Workers The Workers section holds what runs for the effect beside its impacts. It also covers the project's resolve order. Part What it does Effect workers React to this effect's own events. Worker Group Gives the one the effect is on more workers while it lasts. On Hit Holds the effects that the hits of the one this effect is on apply while it lasts. Modifiers Change other effects as they're made. Resolve Order The order an area's effects land on those it takes. In this section Effect workers: Effect workers react to this effect's own events. Worker Group: Worker Group, after the effect workers, gives the one the effect is on more workers while it lasts, as an item's group does while it's equipped. On Hit: On Hit, above the effect workers, holds the effects that the hits of the one this effect is on apply while it lasts, as a poisoned blade or a boon's Weak. Modifiers: Modifiers, under On Hit, change other effects as they're made, for that application alone. Resolve Order: The project's Resolve Order, under Forge Project in Project Settings → PlayForge, decides the order an area's effects land on those it takes.

guides/effects/workers/effect-workers.ht.title: Effect workers | PlayForge
guides/effects/workers/effect-workers.ht.summary: Effect workers Effect workers react to this effect's own events. Event When the worker can act Application When the effect is applied. Tick When it ticks. Removal When it is removed. Impact When it deals a change to an attribute. Workers maps each, and on whose side it runs. Workers return actions, which run at the end of the frame. An Instant effect runs its apply and remove workers within its one application. A worker can also answer numbers. A magnitude of the Worker kind asks the effect's workers for a value under a key, and one that implements INumberWorker answers. For example, the Attribute Change worker answers how much health the target has lost since the effect began. What a worker keeps for one application of its effect goes in ctx.GetState<T>(this), since the worker itself is shared by every application (Scalers: Asking a worker).

guides/effects/workers/modifiers.html.title: Modifiers | PlayForge
guides/effects/workers/modifiers.html.summary: Modifiers Modifiers, under On Hit, change other effects as they're made, for that application alone. For example: a boon that adds a burst to every Chill its holder applies, a ring that makes its holder's debuffs last longer, or a cloak that halves the stuns landing on its wearer. An effect's modifiers hold on the one it's on while it lasts. An item's, an ability's and an entity's modifiers are the same entries. Each entry is a rule of its own, or names a shared Effect Modifier asset (Create → PlayForge → Effect Modifier), whose rule it uses in its place. A rule has: Property Description Direction Outgoing: its holder's own effects as it applies them, on another or itself. Incoming: the effects landing on its holder, whoever applies them. Both. Effect Tags The effects it changes: each with one of these among its asset tag and context tags, or a child of one. None picks every effect. When A condition read as the effect is made, its caster the caster and its target the target. Changes What it changes, each change of a kind. With Effect Tags, Status.Chill picks every Chill. Change What it does Add Contained Effect An effect that lands as this one lands, each tick, or as it ends. It lands on the target or, with Lands On set to Caster, on its caster. Change Impact A Value Pipeline stage its impacts on an attribute go through, of some impact types where it names any. Add Overflow Effect An effect that lands as an application would take it past its most stacks, on the target or its caster as its Lands On says. Clear Stacks takes its stacks off with it. Change Duration Its time multiplied, then more added. Its ticks spread over the time it has. Change Stacks More it can hold at most, where a stack bound of its own sets a most, and more a landing gives. Change Chance to Apply Its chance multiplied, then added to. Grant Tags More tags it grants while it's on. Under Change Impact, an impact that commits, a hit or a tick, runs the stage after its own pipeline, and its breakdown keeps it. A lasting impact, which no pipeline runs on, takes the stage on its magnitude, as Weak's −30% made −40%. Add Overflow Effect needs a stack bound of the effect's own to overflow. An effect a rule adds, and what that effect contains, isn't changed by that rule again. So a Chill that adds a Chill adds one. Two of an item modify twice.

guides/effects/workers/on-hit.html.title: On Hit | PlayForge
guides/effects/workers/on-hit.html.summary: On Hit On Hit, above the effect workers, holds the effects that the hits of the one this effect is on apply while it lasts, as a poisoned blade or a boon's Weak. Its entries are an item's (Items: Workers: On Hit): Property Description Attribute The attribute a hit lowers, as Health. Effects The effects it applies. To Whom they land on: the one hit or the holder. Only On Kill Applies them only on a kill. Impact Types Only hits of these impact types count. When A condition that must hold. An Instant effect doesn't last, so its On Hit does nothing. Another effect that replaces it under its tag takes it off, and a load puts it back once. Proc Coefficient Proc Coefficient, in Impact, is what the effect's own hits carry for On Hit effects. Property Description Own Proc Coefficient Uses the effect's own Proc Coefficient. Off, its ability's stands, or else 1, and Proc Coefficient is hidden. Proc Coefficient What the effect's hits carry. On Hit effects scale their chance and their duration by it. A damage over time at 0.25 sets them off a quarter as often, for a quarter as long, and 0 sets nothing off. Lifesteal An effect has no lifesteal of its own. What its hits heal its caster is the caster's Lifesteal. Lifesteal is the attribute the Lifesteal worker names as its Share, which the worker heals by (Workers: Lifesteal). The worker is the one the project gives every entity, or the caster's own. For hits that steal more, an effect raises its caster's Lifesteal while they should. For example, a lasting effect of +0.3 Lifesteal whose Removal condition takes it off, as a charged attack's buff comes off as its last charge is spent. The heal is a gain like any other, so Healing Received scales it. Damage a return sends back heals nothing.

guides/effects/workers/resolve-order.htm.title: Resolve Order | PlayForge
guides/effects/workers/resolve-order.htm.summary: Resolve Order The project's Resolve Order, under Forge Project in Project Settings → PlayForge, decides the order an area's effects land on those it takes. With it, specific behaviour can be coded, as a totem whose aura keeps its allies alive resolving after them. Property Description Tag One carrying the tag, or one under it, resolves at the entry's Order. Order Lower resolves first. One carrying none of the entries' tags is at 0. One carrying several tags takes the first entry it matches, so the list's order is its precedence. An entity carries a tag on its identity, as a totem always does, or while something grants it, as an aura can grant its holder one while it holds. The area's own order breaks ties. These land in the resolve order: Apply Effects and Apply/Remove Effects land on an ability's targets in it, though the targeting keeps its own order and its primary target. An effect's Area component lands on its target and those it takes in it, its target among them. An aura puts its effect on those that came near in it. The tasks' and the Area's Use Resolve Order, on by default, turns it off for that one. Code reads it through ForgeResolveOrder: OrderOf(target), Sort(targets), and TargetsOf(data) for an activation's targets in order. A death waits for its entity's end of frame, and an aura comes off a dead holder at its next check or as the holder ends. So one area's hits resolve together: a blow that kills the totem doesn't take its aura off the hero the same explosion strikes next. The order matters for what changes as each lands, as an effect that lands on the caster with each hit, or a transfer.

guides/effects/workers/worker-group.html.title: Worker Group | PlayForge
guides/effects/workers/worker-group.html.summary: Worker Group Worker Group, after the effect workers, gives the one the effect is on more workers while it lasts, as an item's group does while it's equipped. Property Description Attribute Workers Run before and after an attribute changes, as a debuff that changes how its target takes damage. Impact Workers Run on each impact the entity deals. Tag Workers Run as the entity's tags change. Analysis Workers Look over the frame's gathered data at its end. The impact, tag and analysis lists serve rules such as Ice Blast's debuff, which shatters its target, by a Threshold, as its Health falls below 13%. The effect takes its workers back as it goes. Two of the effect on one target give the group once, and the last of them to go takes it back. An Instant effect doesn't last, so its group does nothing.

guides/entities/abilities.html.title: Abilities | PlayForge
guides/entities/abilities.html.summary: Abilities The Abilities section sets the abilities the entity starts with, how many it can hold, and what its abilities do while another is busy. Property Description When Busy What one of the entity's abilities set to Entity's Policy does when it's asked to activate while another is busy: Activate Anyway starts it at once. Refuse starts it only when no ability under that choice is busy, and refuses it otherwise. Queue (default) makes it wait in a queue while one is busy. Targeting Yields On by default: an ability whose While Targeting is the entity's rule gives way, while it waits for its target, as another of the entity's abilities activates. Starting Abilities Abilities the entity learns when its GAS initializes, each at its own Starting Level. Those set to Activate At Start then try to activate. Max Abilities The most abilities the entity can hold, 99 by default. Its kind can make it a scaler, which changes the limit with the entity's level (Scalers). Allow Duplicates Lets the entity hold the same ability more than once. Off by default. Crowd Control The crowd control rules its abilities follow, such as a stun stopping every ability and Silenced stopping spells. Where it names none, the project's apply (Abilities: Requirements: Crowd Control). Abilities explains each When Busy choice, and Targeting Yields. A runtime entity's identity names its crowd control rules too.

guides/entities/attributes.html.title: Attributes | PlayForge
guides/entities/attributes.html.summary: Attributes The Attributes section names the entity's attribute set and the attribute its time runs at. Property Description Attribute Set The set the entity's attributes come from. Attribute Sets describes the set itself. Time Scale The attribute the entity's time runs at, 1 as the game's. Under the Attribute Set field, a table lists each attribute the set gives, its sub-sets' included, with the value it starts at and its range. When the GAS initializes, it: creates every attribute in the set and its sub-sets, each at its starting Current and Base values; applies the set's asset tags to the entity; subscribes the set's workers. Gameplay effects then change the values. An entity with no Attribute Set has no attributes. An effect that targets an attribute the entity lacks leaves it unchanged. Time Scale Time Scale names the attribute the entity's time runs at, 1 as the game's. The entity's effects, cooldowns, sequences and waits run by that time. An effect that lowers the attribute slows the entity. One that raises it hastes the entity. As each comes off, the entity's time is the game's again. Give the attribute a Current of 1 in the set. Code sets a scale of its own with GetClock().TimeScale, such as a hit-stop's 0. The clock reads the two multiplied, so a hit-stop holds under a slow. OwnScale is code's part, and AttributeScale the attribute's.

guides/entities/built-in-kinds.html.title: Built-in kinds | PlayForge
guides/entities/built-in-kinds.html.summary: Built-in kinds The kinds PlayForge ships for this guide's pickers, each with its menu and what it does, as its picker says. A project's own kinds join them in the same pickers. In this section Components Respawn places Local Data kinds

guides/entities/built-in-kinds/component.title: Components | PlayForge
guides/entities/built-in-kinds/component.summary: Components Kind Menu What it does AuraEntityComponent — Gives those near the entity an aura's effects while it lives. BountyEntityComponent — An effect the entity's killer takes as it dies, as gold or experience. CueReceiverEntityComponent — Plays cue tags its own way for this entity, before the project's cue library. CuesEntityComponent — Shows and sounds the entity's moments: as it spawns, dies and revives, and while it holds a tag. RespawnEntityComponent — Brings the entity back a while after it dies. TurnsToFaceEntityComponent — Its abilities turn it to face their target or point before their first stage.

guides/entities/built-in-kinds/local-dat.title: Local Data kinds | PlayForge
guides/entities/built-in-kinds/local-dat.summary: Local Data kinds Kind Menu What it does LocalAbility (Ability) — An ability. LocalAttribute (Attribute) — An attribute. LocalBool (Bool) — A bool. LocalEffect (Effect) — An effect. LocalEntity (Entity) — An entity's identity. LocalFloat (Float) — A number that can scale, read where it's used. LocalInt (Int) — A whole number that can scale, read where it's used. LocalMonoBehaviour (MonoBehaviour) — A component on a prefab, as a process to spawn. LocalObject (Object) — Any asset, as a prefab or a material. LocalScriptableObject (ScriptableObject) — A ScriptableObject asset. LocalString (String) — A string. LocalTag (Tag) — A tag.

guides/entities/built-in-kinds/respawn-p.title: Respawn places | PlayForge
guides/entities/built-in-kinds/respawn-p.summary: Respawn places Kind Menu What it does HomeRespawnPlace (Home) — Where the entity stood as it registered: its spawn. PointRespawnPlace (Point) — A point in the world. WhereItDiedRespawnPlace (Where It Died) — Where the entity died.

guides/entities/combat-log.html.title: Combat Log | PlayForge
guides/entities/combat-log.html.summary: Combat Log Each entity keeps a combat log of what happens to it. A test reads it as the game does, through gas.GetCombatLog(), and the Debugger shows it under the entity it has selected. In this section What the log writes: What a combat log writes is the project's to say, under Combat Log in Project Settings → PlayForge. Log entries: Each entry in a combat log is a CombatLogEntry. How a change landed: A combat log entry also tells how its change came to land.

guides/entities/combat-log/how-a-change-.title: How a change landed | PlayForge
guides/entities/combat-log/how-a-change-.summary: How a change landed A combat log entry also tells how its change came to land. Made is its change as made, before any step. ChangeSteps lists each step it took on the way: each attribute worker that heard it, with its Timing (before the commit or after), its Execution (inline, or the actions it Queued), and the change Before and After it; a barrier's soak; a gain's scaling, such as Healing Received's. StepsText reads them as a line: "-30 as made → Math -30 → -15 (inline) → Answering (queued 1, after) → landed -15". The steps are recorded only where the log keeps entries, or where something hears the entity's OnAttributeChangeStep.

guides/entities/combat-log/log-entries.h.title: Log entries | PlayForge
guides/entities/combat-log/log-entries.h.summary: Log entries Each entry in a combat log is a CombatLogEntry. Property Description Kind Taken, Dealt, Changed or Event. Time and Frame When it was written. Other The other entity: the dealer of a hit taken, the one a hit dealt struck, an event's source, or the one it names. Effect The effect behind it. Attribute The attribute it changed. Before and After The attribute's value before and after. Change The change. Steps The hit's steps through its pipeline. Killed Whether it killed. It's marked on the blow that killed, in both logs. An entry reads as a line: "Took -20 Health from Lina (Fireball)". The log's Entries run oldest first. Of(kind), By(effect) and With(entity) filter them. Total(kind, attribute) adds their changes up, such as the damage an entity took.

guides/entities/combat-log/what-the-log-.title: What the log writes | PlayForge
guides/entities/combat-log/what-the-log-.summary: What the log writes What a combat log writes is the project's to say, under Combat Log in Project Settings → PlayForge. Setting Description Records What it records: Hits Taken: a workable change another's effect makes to its attributes. Hits Dealt. Changes: its other changes, such as its own, a cost, regeneration or a transfer. Events The gameplay events it's sent, by tag or one under it, such as Died, Kill or your own. They're written though no ability listens for them. Keep How many entries each entity keeps, its last: 100 by default. 0 keeps none, as for a build.

guides/entities/components.html.title: Components | PlayForge
guides/entities/components.html.summary: Components An entity's components are features it carries, each a class with hooks into the entity's life. Add one with the list's +. A kind that makes no sense twice is offered only while the entity holds none of it. A component hears these moments: Hook When it runs Register As the entity registers, its systems set up. Death As the entity dies, whether it stays or ends. Its context's Killer is the one whose loss killed it, as the entity's Died event names. Revive As an entity that stays revives. End As the entity ends. WindUp As an activation of one of the entity's abilities winds up, before the ability's cost and first stage. The activation waits on it, as on a turn to face its target. In this section Auras: An Aura component holds an effect on those near the entity for as long as the entity lives, such as a captain's command aura. Bounty: A Bounty component gives the entity's killer an effect as the entity dies, such as gold or experience. Turns To Face: A Turns To Face component turns the entity to face the target, or the point, of each of its abilities before the ability's first stage. Respawn: A Respawn component revives an entity that stays as it dies, once a delay has passed. Cues: A Cues component plays what the entity shows and sounds at its moments, on the entity. Cue Receiver: A Cue Receiver component plays cue tags its own way for the entity, before the project's cue library. Writing your own component: A component of your own derives from AbstractEntityComponent and overrides the hooks it needs. Services: A service is a per-entity object that an entity's components share.

guides/entities/components/auras.html.title: Auras | PlayForge
guides/entities/components/auras.html.summary: Auras An Aura component holds an effect on those near the entity for as long as the entity lives, such as a captain's command aura. Property Description Effect The effect it holds on each one it takes while they're near. Radius How far it reaches from the entity, read at each check. Flat Measures along the ground, leaving height out. Off, it measures a sphere. Takes Whom it takes, by how each stands to the entity: Allies (the default, itself among them), Other Allies, Enemies, Self, All But Self or Everyone. Interval How often it checks who's near, by the entity's own time: 0.25 s by default. An entity that dies takes its auras' effects off. One that stays and revives holds them again. Effects: Components: Auras describes how an aura holds its effect.

guides/entities/components/bounty.html.title: Bounty | PlayForge
guides/entities/components/bounty.html.summary: Bounty A Bounty component gives the entity's killer an effect as the entity dies, such as gold or experience. Property Description Effect The effect the killer takes. It comes from the entity, so the effect reads the entity's level. Share Radius Where it's set, the killer's allies within this distance of the entity take the effect too, as an assist. It's read at the entity's level. Flat Measures the Share Radius along the ground. Off, it measures a sphere. A death no one dealt gives no bounty. An entity can hold several Bounty components, one for each bounty it gives.

guides/entities/components/cue-receiver..title: Cue Receiver | PlayForge
guides/entities/components/cue-receiver..summary: Cue Receiver A Cue Receiver component plays cue tags its own way for the entity, before the project's cue library. Property Description Routes Its own routes, which play for its cue tags before the library's. Pass Through Plays the library's route too, after its own, for a tag it plays. Variant Its variant, by its last name. The library's route under that name plays in place of the tag's own, such as Cue.Hit.Golem for Cue.Hit, where the library has one. Cues: Routes explains cue routes. An entity holds one Cue Receiver at most.

guides/entities/components/cues.html.title: Cues | PlayForge
guides/entities/components/cues.html.summary: Cues A Cues component plays what the entity shows and sounds at its moments, on the entity. Property Description On Spawn Plays as the entity comes into the game. On Death Plays as it dies, its killer behind the cue. On Revive Plays as it comes back. While Tagged Lasting cues, each under a tag, that play for as long as the entity holds the tag, such as stars over its head while it's Stunned. Each step, a tag the entity has taken on begins its While Tagged cues, and one it has let go of ends them. The While Tagged cues end with the entity. Each list holds cues as an effect's does (Effects: Cues), a Cue Tag among them. An entity holds one at most.

guides/entities/components/respawn.html.title: Respawn | PlayForge
guides/entities/components/respawn.html.summary: Respawn A Respawn component revives an entity that stays as it dies, once a delay has passed. Property Description Delay How long after it dies the entity revives, in seconds of its own time, read at its level. At Where it revives: Home: where it stood as it registered. Where It Died. Point: a point in the world. A place of your own, such as a checkpoint. A place of your own is a [Serializable] class made from AbstractRespawnPlace. It says Where from the entity's context and its home: a hero's fountain, for example. Its Death's On Revive effects land as it revives, as any revive's do. A revive before its time, such as a buyback, ends the wait. The wait is the entity's RespawnTimer, a service. A HUD reads gas.FindService<RespawnTimer>()'s Waiting and TimeLeft. An entity that ends as it dies has nothing to revive, which the Problems view says. A save keeps neither the entity's death nor its wait. An entity holds one at most.

guides/entities/components/services.html.title: Services | PlayForge
guides/entities/components/services.html.summary: Services A service is a per-entity object that an entity's components share. The auras an entity runs are one, AuraSet, and so is the wait a Respawn counts down, RespawnTimer. gas.GetService<T>() returns the entity's service of a kind, made the first time it's asked for. gas.FindService<T>() finds one without making one. The entity calls each service's hooks: Hook When it runs Step Each frame, by the entity's own time: after its effects, and before its turn and its barriers. Revive As the entity revives, before anything else of the revive. End As the entity ends. A service of your own derives from AbstractEntityService and overrides what it needs, such as a heat meter that cools by the entity's time. A save keeps no services.

guides/entities/components/turns-to-face.title: Turns To Face | PlayForge
guides/entities/components/turns-to-face.summary: Turns To Face A Turns To Face component turns the entity to face the target, or the point, of each of its abilities before the ability's first stage. Property Description Turn Speed How fast it turns, in degrees a second of the entity's own time. It's a number that can read a turn rate attribute; 0 faces at once. Start Angle The ability's first stage starts once the entity faces its target within this angle. Facing Angle The angle the turn goes on to after the stage starts, even after the ability has ended. The turn goes on until another turn, the entity's death or the game's word ends it. If Too Long What happens where reaching the Start Angle takes longer than Max Wait: No Limit (default): it waits as long as it takes. Start Anyway: it starts the stage, the turn going on. Cancel: it cancels the activation. Max Wait How long reaching the Start Angle may take, in seconds of the entity's own time, where If Too Long sets a limit. The ability's cost and cooldown are paid after the turn, so an interrupted turn pays nothing. A turn taken over before the stage starts, by another order or the game's word, cancels the activation. An ability with nothing to face, or with the entity for its target, turns nothing. An ability a trigger sets off turns as any does, so a counterattack turns to its attacker. An ability with a Turn To Face of its own turns its own way, or not at all (Abilities: Components: Turn To Face). An entity holds one at most. Turning from code Code turns an entity through its hub: gas.Face(target, degreesPerSecond, within) turns it to face a target, and follows the target as it moves. gas.Face(point, ...) turns it to face a point. gas.StopTurning() stops the turn, as when a move of the game's takes over. gas.AngleToFace says how far it has yet to turn. A turn sets the entity's facing, flat: its object's rotation, or a runtime entity's. A game that turns its characters itself, by animation or a controller, puts an IForgeTurner on the entity's object. The turner takes each step of a turn in PlayForge's place. The Creator Lab's units stop a turn as they walk or stop.

guides/entities/components/writing-your-.title: Writing your own component | PlayForge
guides/entities/components/writing-your-.summary: Writing your own component A component of your own derives from AbstractEntityComponent and overrides the hooks it needs. Each hook is a no-op otherwise. A component is the entity's, shared by everything that holds it, such as every entity made from one asset. So what it keeps for one entity, it keeps through its context: ctx.GetState<T>(this). Its context's Identity is the entity's settings, its Death among them.
