guides/workers/the-action-queue.html.summary: The action queue What a deferred worker returns, and whatever else is queued to an entity (GetActionQueue().Enqueue), waits in the entity's action queue for its end of frame. classDiagram class GASCore:::rt { <<internal sealed>> +EffectModifiers : EffectModifierSet +Sides : SideSet +CombatLog : CombatLog +Clock : EntityClock +LocalData : LocalDataStructure +IsDead : bool +MarkDead() +Revive(at) } class ActionQueue:::rt { +Enqueue(action, priority) +EnqueueRange() +ProcessAll(ISource) int +HasActions : bool +Clear() } class IRootAction:::ext { <<interface>> +Priority : int +IsValid : bool +Description : string +Execute(ISource) } class ActionPriority:::rt { Critical = 100 High = 50 Normal = 0 Low = -50 TagWorker = -100 Analysis = -200 Cleanup = -300 } class DeathAction:::rt { Critical, calls MarkDead } class LambdaAction:::rt { +ctor(Action~ISource~, desc, priority) } class ModifyAttributeAction:::rt class ApplyEffectAction:::rt class RemoveEffectAction:::rt class FrameSummary:::rt { one frame's impacts, effects and deaths +GetTotalReduction(attr) +GetNetImpact(attr) +GetImpactsDealtTo() +CreateSnapshot(n) FrameSummarySnapshot +Clear() } class EntityClock:::rt { <<sealed>> +TimeScale : float +DeltaTime : float +FixedDeltaTime : float +Time : float } class SideSet:::rt { +Count : int +Current : List~Tag~ +Changed } class AbstractEntityService:::ext { <<abstract>> one per entity, gas.GetService or FindService Step(dt) Revive() End() } class AuraSet:::rt { +Add() +Remove() +Step(dt) +Clear() } class RespawnTimer:::rt { +TimeLeft : float +ReviveIn(seconds, where) } class CombatLog:::rt { a ring buffer of CombatLogEntry +Entries +Of(kind) +By(effect) +Total(kind, attr) } class EntityDeath:::asset { <<Serializable>> +Policy : EDeathPolicy +DiesAtZeroHealth : bool +Purges +KeepsTiers +Body OnDeath and OnRevive effects } class EDeathPolicy:::rt { <<enumeration>> End Stay } class AbstractEntityComponent:::ext { <<abstract>> Register(ctx) Death(ctx) Revive(ctx) End(ctx) } class BountyEntityComponent:::rt { +Effect +ShareRadius +Flat } class RespawnEntityComponent:::rt { +Delay +At : AbstractRespawnPlace places: Home, WhereItDied, Point } class AuraEntityComponent:::rt GASCore *-- ActionQueue GASCore *-- FrameSummary GASCore *-- EntityClock GASCore *-- SideSet GASCore "1" *-- "many" AbstractEntityService : Services AbstractEntityService <|-- AuraSet AbstractEntityService <|-- RespawnTimer GASCore *-- CombatLog ActionQueue o-- IRootAction IRootAction ..> ActionPriority : Priority IRootAction <|.. DeathAction IRootAction <|.. LambdaAction IRootAction <|.. ModifyAttributeAction IRootAction <|.. ApplyEffectAction IRootAction <|.. RemoveEffectAction GASCore ..> EntityDeath : the identity's Death EntityDeath --> EDeathPolicy GASCore ..> AbstractEntityComponent : the identity's Components AbstractEntityComponent <|-- BountyEntityComponent AbstractEntityComponent <|-- RespawnEntityComponent AbstractEntityComponent <|-- AuraEntityComponent RespawnEntityComponent ..> RespawnTimer : ReviveIn classDef rt fill:#FFE86D,stroke:#CBB333,color:#574900 classDef ext fill:#A0C4FB,stroke:#6A8BBF,color:#14315E classDef asset fill:#B8ACFB,stroke:#7D6DD4,color:#231266 What GASCore keeps besides the subsystems, the ActionQueue its end of frame drains, and the identity's death rules and entity components. When it runs. Four passes run in each end of frame, in this order: The actions queued since the last end of frame. Those the tag workers' activations and resolutions queue. Those their ticks queue. Those the analysis workers, the Health watch and the effects' conditions queue. An action queued as a pass runs joins that pass. In what order. By priority, higher first (ActionPriority, from Critical's 100 down to Cleanup's −300), and in the order queued within one priority. Enqueue(action, priorityOverride) puts one at another priority. What's heard. Each action is heard as it's queued (OnActionQueued), then once more as it's done with: Outcome Event When Run OnActionExecuted It ran. Dropped unrun OnActionInvalidated Its IsValid said no as its turn came, it was taken off, or its entity had ended. Failed OnActionFailed, with what it threw Its IsValid or its Execute threw. It's written to the Console as well, and the rest of the queue runs on. The queue's events and the entity's callbacks both tell them. The frame's summary keeps the dropped and the failed, and an EffectJournal settles a worker's action as Ran, Dropped or Failed. Taken off. Remove(action) takes one off, RemoveWhere(match) every one it picks, and Clear() all of them. Each is heard as dropped, and the rest keep their order. An entity that ends. Its queue closes (IsClosed). What waited is dropped and heard, and an action queued to it after is dropped at once, so nothing waits on it for good. Another entity's queue. An action queued to another entity runs at that entity's end of frame. That's this frame if its end of frame is still to come, by the order the entities step in, or else the next. The guard. A pass runs 10,000 actions at most, so an action that queues another for good can't hold the frame. Those left past it wait for the next pass, and the queue writes an error.

guides/workers/the-map.html.title: The map | PlayForge
guides/workers/the-map.html.summary: The map The map shows, for each kind of worker, when it runs, whose system it runs on, and what its context holds. Kind Hook When it runs For whom: its context's System What its context holds Attribute Pre Change Before a change to one of the entity's attributes lands The entity whose attribute changes WorkerContext Attribute Post Change After the change lands The entity whose attribute changed WorkerContext Impact Validate, then actions As a change the entity dealt lands on another's attribute The dealer ImpactWorkerContext Tag Activate, Tick, Resolve At the entity's end of frame The entity The system Analysis Analyze At the entity's end of frame, after its tag workers The entity The system and its FrameSummary Effect Application, Tick, Removal As the effect lands, at each of its execute ticks, and as it comes off The entity the effect is on EffectWorkerContext Effect Impact As a change the effect made lands The dealer, the effect's caster EffectWorkerContext, with ImpactData Each kind has a page of its own below. In this section Attribute workers: An attribute worker runs as a change to one of its entity's attributes lands: before it, in Pre Change, or after it, in Post Change. Impact workers: An impact worker runs as a change its entity dealt lands on another's attribute, for the attribute the worker subscribes to. Tag workers: A tag worker acts while its entity's tags meet its requirements. Analysis workers: An analysis worker looks over its entity at its end of frame, after its tag workers. Effect workers: An effect worker runs for its own effect's events, as the effect lands, ticks, comes off and deals an impact.

guides/workers/the-map/analysis-workers..title: Analysis workers | PlayForge
guides/workers/the-map/analysis-workers..summary: Analysis workers An analysis worker looks over its entity at its end of frame, after its tag workers. Its hook is Analyze. Its context is the system and its FrameSummary, which holds: the frame's impacts dealt and received, by attribute, target and source; the effects applied and removed; the deaths. It returns actions, which the entity's action queue runs (The action queue).

guides/workers/the-map/attribute-workers.title: Attribute workers | PlayForge
guides/workers/the-map/attribute-workers.summary: Attribute workers An attribute worker runs as a change to one of its entity's attributes lands: before it, in Pre Change, or after it, in Post Change. A change is a commit, or a modifier registered or taken off. Its context, WorkerContext, holds: Member What it holds System The entity whose attribute changes. AttributeCache The entity's attribute cache. Change In Pre Change, the incoming change. In Post Change, what the attribute changed by. FrameSummary The frame's summary (Analysis workers). ActionQueue The entity's action queue (The action queue). In Pre Change, an Inline worker's edit to the incoming change is what commits, before bounds and rounding. A modifier's change it only reads. Inline or deferred. An attribute worker's Execution says how it acts: Execution How it acts Inline Runs inside the change, and can edit the change in Pre Change. It must not change attributes itself, which would run workers inside workers. Deferred Returns actions instead, as impact, analysis and effect workers do. The entity's action queue runs them at its end of frame, where they can change anything. A focused attribute worker, one that watches a single attribute, sets these among its fields: Property Description Timing When it runs: Pre Change, Post Change or both. Sign Policy The changes it takes: losses, gains or either. Allow Self Modification Whether it takes changes whose source and target are the same entity.

guides/workers/the-map/effect-workers.ht.title: Effect workers | PlayForge
guides/workers/the-map/effect-workers.ht.summary: Effect workers An effect worker runs for its own effect's events, as the effect lands, ticks, comes off and deals an impact. Hook When it runs Its context's System Application As the effect lands The entity the effect is on Tick At each of its execute ticks, with how many The entity the effect is on Removal As the effect comes off The entity the effect is on Impact As a change the effect made lands The dealer, the effect's caster, not the one it's on. The one hit is ImpactData.Target. Its context, EffectWorkerContext, holds: Member What it holds System The entity it runs on, as above. Carrier The effect's spec. FrameSummary The frame's summary. ActionQueue The action queue (The action queue). ExecuteTicks For a tick, how many ticks executed. ImpactData For the Impact hook, the change that landed. GetState<T>(worker) keeps what it counts for this application.

guides/workers/the-map/impact-workers.ht.title: Impact workers | PlayForge
guides/workers/the-map/impact-workers.ht.summary: Impact workers An impact worker runs as a change its entity dealt lands on another's attribute, for the attribute the worker subscribes to. Its hook validates the hit, then makes its actions. It runs for the dealer, not the one hit (Traps). Its context, ImpactWorkerContext, holds: Member What it holds System The dealer. The one hit is ImpactData.Target. ImpactData The hit: its Target, its Attribute, the sourced change, its RealImpact and its OldValue. FrameSummary The frame's summary. ActionQueue The action queue (The action queue). Property Description Accept Unworkable Impact Also takes unworkable changes (Workable and unworkable).

guides/workers/the-map/tag-workers.html.title: Tag workers | PlayForge
guides/workers/the-map/tag-workers.html.summary: Tag workers A tag worker acts while its entity's tags meet its requirements. Hook When it runs Activate As its tag requirements come to be met. Tick While they hold. Resolve As they no longer do. Each runs at the entity's end of frame. A tag worker is read in a frame the entity's tags changed, or every frame where its Evaluate Every Frame says. Its context is the system, the entity. Property Description Requirements Its tag requirements, each a tag, Require or Avoid, and a required weight. With none, it's always active. Tick Pause Frames between its ticks, read at its entity's level: 0 for every frame, or −1, the default, for none. Require holds while the tag's weight is at least the required weight, and Avoid while it's below.

guides/workers/traps.html.title: Traps | PlayForge
guides/workers/traps.html.summary: Traps These are the mistakes workers invite most often. An impact worker runs for the dealer. Its context's System is the dealer, and the one hit is ImpactData.Target. A worker that took System for the one hit applied its holder's effects to the target, and read the target's items for its holder's. An effect worker's Impact hook runs on the dealer's side too. Its System is the effect's caster. Its Application, Tick and Removal hooks' System is the one the effect is on. A stacking effect's periodic tick lands once for each stack, while its lasting change counts once. A number that reads the effect's stacks on each tick multiplies again. Hangover, which read its stacks, took 100 a tick where 20 was meant. Read the stacks in a lasting change, or leave them out of a periodic one. The Problems view warns of it. What a worker sets in motion waits for the frame's end. Deferred actions, deaths and the kills they give, and an aura's effect coming off a dead holder, all land at the entity's end of frame. One area's hits therefore resolve together (Effects: Workers: Resolve Order).

guides/workers/where-workers-come-from.h.title: Where workers come from | PlayForge
guides/workers/where-workers-come-from.h.summary: Where workers come from An entity holds workers from each of these sources: Source What the entity holds An attribute set's Worker Group The workers of the set it's built from, for as long as it lives. An entity's Worker Group The same, as the entity's own. The group is on its Entity asset. Its project's Workers The workers its Forge Project's settings list under Workers, in Project Settings → PlayForge. An item's, an ability's or an effect's Worker Group Their workers, while the item is equipped, the ability known, or the effect lasts on it. An effect's Workers Effect workers, which run for that effect's own events. Built in An impact worker, which an On Hit entry gives its holder. Every entity in a Forge Project holds its project's workers after its own, as it registers. A project starts with the Lifesteal worker, whose Share is yours to name. Two of an effect lasting on an entity give its group once.

guides/workers/workable-and-unworkable.h.title: Workable and unworkable | PlayForge
guides/workers/workable-and-unworkable.h.summary: Workable and unworkable A change is workable unless it says it isn't (SourcedModifiedAttributeValue.ImpactIsWorkable). An unworkable one is a change the system makes on its own account (GenerateUnworkable), as the pulse each attribute starts with, or a transfer's two sides. Only a workable change: reaches impact workers, unless a worker's Accept Unworkable Impact is on; is soaked by a barrier as a loss, and scaled by its attribute's Gains Scaled By as a gain, as Healing Received; sends the core's Impact Dealt and Impact Taken events; counts toward the kill: the killer is whoever dealt the last workable loss to the Health role's attribute; counts for lifesteal, and is returned by Return Damage; is written in the combat log as a hit, taken or dealt. Another change is written as a Change. Attribute workers run for every change, workable or not. One that cares reads ctx.Change.Value.ImpactIsWorkable.

index.html.title: PlayForge | PlayForge
index.html.summary: PlayForge PlayForge is a gameplay framework for Unity 6, modelled on Unreal's Gameplay Ability System. Every ability, effect, attribute, tag and item is an asset you build in the inspector, and one hub on each entity runs them all. Start here Getting Started sets PlayForge up in a project, makes an entity, and gives it an ability that changes an attribute through an effect. The guides Area Guides Gameplay Entities · Attributes · Attribute Sets · Effects · Effect & Attribute Pipeline · Value Pipelines · Scalers · Abilities · Items · Tags · Cues · Workers Running it Processes · Task Sequences · Time, Input and Logging · Saving and Loading · Spreadsheets Tools The Editor Tools · The Creator Lab · Testing Your Content Going further Extending PlayForge: a game's own components, workers, tasks, scalers, cues, rules and tools · Recipes: common rules built from PlayForge's own assets, field by field These guides are the ones the package ships in PlayForge/Documentation, each section here a page of its own, and each help button in PlayForge's inspectors opens its section. A guide's Built-in kinds page lists the components, tasks, workers, cues, scalers and the rest that PlayForge ships for its pickers, each with what it does. The API reference The API reference has a page for every public type of PlayForge: its runtime, the Creator Lab, its editor and its test kit, grouped by area. Each type's page links the guide to its area and the guide sections that name it, and each guide links the types it names to their pages.
